chapters.title: Chapter 301: Lord Vespera Vs. Lord Sky
paragraphs: Thor’s storm-blue eyes instantly widened to the size of saucers, her mouth watering as a boisterous thunderous grin split across her broad face.
"BY THE ANCESTORS!" Thor roared out in unrestrained delight.
Without waiting for silver forks or knives, Thor reached out her bare muscular hands and snatched a massive, four-foot-long roasted wyvern rib straight off the top of the pile.
She opened her jaw wide and bit directly into the thick, steaming meat!
CHOMP! CRUNCH!
Bone and meat shattered between her teeth with a terrifying rhythmic impact.
Thor chewed violently, swallowing half the rib in a single gulp, before reaching out with her other hand to grab an entire roasted wild boar by its hind leg.
GLUB! GLUB! GLUB!
She snatched a gallon jug of chilled dwarf-mead from a butler’s tray, chugging the entire jug down her throat in three seconds flat, letting the golden foam spill over her chin and singlet.
"GWAHAHAHA!" Thor laughed boisterously, wiping her mouth with the back of her forearm, her booming voice echoing off the pavilion walls! "Good! GOOD! Now THIS is a proper feast!"
She pointed a greasy meat-filled bone toward the royal-blue-haired Princess, nodding approvingly.

"I must say, Princess... you are far, far better than that overgrown green weed! That insufferable Druid would have given me a bowl of raw grass and lectured me about nature balance for three hours! You actually feed a warrior real meat!"
The Princess let out another soft, amused laugh, fanning herself gently as she watched the female Thor devour half a mountain of food in less than sixty seconds.
Thor didn’t even slow down.
She tore through roasted hydra legs, swallowed kraken tentacles whole, and smashed through silver platters, yelling out at the bowing butlers between massive mouthfuls.
"HEY! BRING SECOND SERVINGS! BRING THIRD SERVINGS! THIS TINY MOUNTAIN ISN’T GOING TO SATE ME AT ALL! I NEED TEN MORE BOARS AND A BARREL OF DWARF MEAD!"
The butlers bowed in sheer terror, sweating profusely as they ran off to the kitchens at top speed to fulfill her order.
The Princess watched Thor eat with a mixture of awe and playful exasperation, letting out a soft melodic sigh.

"Haah~ If I weren’t the Princess of the Lord World with access to the imperial treasury, and were just a regular person... a single meal with you would have put me into so much debt that I would have seriously considered dying."
Thor stopped eating mid-bite with a massive piece of hydra meat hanging from her jaw. She blinked her storm-blue eyes, processing the Princess’s words, then let out a loud hearty laugh.
"Gwahahaha! Well, I am bloody glad you’re a Princess then!" Thor declared cheerfully, swallowing the hydra meat whole.
DZZZZZT!
Suddenly, the golden holographic display in the center of the suite flashed brightly.
The glowing countdown timer hit zero!
[00:00:00 — BROADCAST LIVE SIGNAL ESTABLISHED!]
The floating screen automatically expanded, maximizing its display to cover the entire far wall of the private dining pavilion...
The live view count on the upper corner instantly exploded past three hundred and fifty million concurrent viewers!
Thor wiped her greasy hands on a silk napkin, leaning forward in her chair as her storm-blue eyes sharpened into those of an ancient battle god.
"Aha..." Thor grinned, her voice dropping into a low rumbling frequency. "The war has finally begun."
[Deep within the Umbral Basin, along the neutral border clearing...]
The morning air was thick with tension.
Over the past week, The Unmovable Wall had shifted its massive, multi-tiered steel treads forward, rolling three miles closer to the boundary of the Blessed Land.
The colossal mobile fortress sat parked on a long, wide, and flat clearing that had been completely leveled by heavy spells... forming a massive open battlefield spanning thousands of yards.
Up ahead, the divine, translucent fog that Eluned had cast to cover the Blessed Land was beginning to recede.
The green-tinted mist pulled back slowly, revealing the terrifying impenetrable perimeter of Silas’s territory.

Rising high above the tree line stood the newly upgraded Steel-Weave Perimeter Walls... reinforced with interlocked pitch-black Obsidian-Slate Stone and reinforced with tempered steel alloy plating that glinted coldly under the sun.
And towering fifty feet above the main gates was the Tier 3 Watchtower...
Stationed atop the high stone battlements were dozens of women... archers holding heavy composite longbows, and mages in arcanist robes with staffs held ready.
Their cold gazes stared straight down at The Unmovable Wall.
In front of his mobile fortress, Lord Sky took a deep, steadying breath.
"Haah~"

He was wearing his full-face, silver-and-black streaming helmet... the spatial disguise artifact forged by Thora’s father that completely concealed her true identity as a young, black-haired woman in a hoodie.

Hovering all around Sky were hundreds of sleek silver Streaming Drones. Every single optical sensor was active, tracking her physical movements, capturing panoramic battlefield angles, and transmitting ultra-high-definition video feeds to over three hundred million viewers watching live across the globe.
Sky was a master content creator... a veteran Classic Lord who knew exactly how to manipulate broadcast tension, farm viewer engagement, and build hype.
This single Lord War stream was going to elevate her career past anything the streaming industry had ever seen.
Sky took ten deliberate, confident steps forward onto the grassy battlefield, raising his gloved hand toward the central hovering drone.

"Welcome, everyone, to the official main event!" Sky announced with his voice amplified by his helmet’s audio transmitter, sounding boisterous and full of energy. "It’s been quite some time since I felt this level of raw excitement in my chest... Two territories, one battlefield and no holding back!"

On his internal HUD display, Sky could see millions of live comments cascading past at light-speed... but with a quick practiced flick of her fingers, Sky disabled the comment overlays on her main screen.
In a high-stakes territory war, distractions were lethal.
Sky turned his masked head back toward the lower gun decks of The Unmovable Wall, his tone dropping into a hard commanding military commander.
"All gun crews to your stations! Man the heavy mana cannons!"
CLANK! CLANK! CLANK!
From the iron gun ports lining the lower hull of the mobile fortress, thirty colossal, heavy-bore Mana Cannons extended their black steel barrels.
The runic artillery arrays hummed violently as high-density mana crystals loaded into the breech chambers.
In the Sovereign Realm, official Lord Wars operated under strict system-enforced victory parameters.
A victory could be achieved by depleting the enemy territory’s Structural Integrity from one hundred percent down to five percent or lower through continuous siege bombardment.
Alternatively, a victory occurred if the opposing Lord was physically captured, slain, or officially tapped out by declaring surrender on their system interface.
Sky stood on the grassy field, looking up at the high stone walls of the Blessed Land.
Behind her helmet, Sky’s sharp black eyes narrowed.
Even though her scouts had been wiped out earlier, her veteran instincts as a Classic Lord remained unshakeable.

’I’m up against a brand-new, unregistered Lord...’ Sky thought with sharp thoughts. ’She has high-tier Heroes, sure, but in terms of territory siege warfare, experience is everything. It’s really not that serious. A couple of heavy artillery salvos will force her barriers open...’
Sky drew his broad steel sword from his belt, pointing the gleaming blade straight toward the Blessed Land’s main gates.
"First Legion... FIRE!" Sky bellowed.
BOOOOOOOOOOM!
A deafening earth-shattering roar erupted from the front ten mana cannons.
The shockwave was so immense that the grass beneath the fortress was instantly vaporized into black ash.𝐟𝐫𝕖𝗲𝘄𝚎𝗯𝕟𝐨𝕧𝐞𝚕.𝕔𝕠𝐦
Ten colossal spheres of highly compressed, glowing red destructive mana shot through the sky, tearing across the clearing with whistling velocity.
FWOOSH! FWOOSH! FWOOSH!
The explosive cannonballs hurtled directly toward the main gates of the Blessed Land.
Sky fully expected a standard translucent magical barrier or an iron energy shield to manifest over the walls to absorb the impact.
’I can’t wait to see the hit...’
She raised his sword higher, executing a double-salvo tactic to overload the enemy’s energy reserves.
"Second Legion! Third Legion! Continuous fire!" Sky commanded!
BOOOOOOOOOOM! BOOOOOOOOOOM!
Twenty additional heavy mana cannons fired in rapid succession.
Twenty more blazing red-hot energy cannonballs tore through the air, creating a wall of flying explosive destruction heading straight for Silas’s territory.
Thirty heavy artillery rounds in total... enough firepower to flatten a regular mountain stronghold!
...However, just as the first wave of red cannonballs reached within fifty yards of the Blessed Land’s outer perimeter—
STEP!
A single cloaked figure casually stepped up to the very edge of the high stone wall, looking down at the incoming barrage.
It was Eluned.
The SSS-Rank Nature Goddess was wearing a flowing dark-green hooded cloak over her white robes.
Her long emerald hair drifted gently in the wind with her deep green eyes calm, unbothered, and utterly unimpressed by the thirty flying explosive rounds.
Eluned didn’t draw a staff.
She didn’t chant an incantation, hell she didn’t even raise her aura.
She simply raised her delicate, bare right hand... and made a casual, dismissive flick of her fingers.
HUMMM!
In that exact second... the entire front section of the Blessed Land’s Steel-Weave perimeter wall came alive!
BOOM! BOOM! BOOM!
Hundreds of colossal, thick, and impossibly dense Ancient Ironwood Roots erupted violently from the stone masonry.
The thick, thorned roots grew at light-speed, interweaving across the air like a sprawling, beautiful, and impenetrable botanical web.
The thirty blazing red mana cannonballs slammed directly into the dense root web...
...But they didn’t explode!
The moment the high-density mana cannonballs touched the divine nature-infused roots, the ancient flora didn’t absorb the impact.
Instead, the roots curled with fluid, spring-like elasticity, absorbing the momentum... and LAUNCHED ALL THIRTY CANNONBALLS DIRECTLY BACK AT LORD SKY’S TERRITORY!
VWOOSH! VWOOSH! VWOOSH!
The thirty blazing red cannonballs reversed direction instantaneously, flying back across the field toward The Unmovable Wall at double their original speed.
"WHAT?!" Sky gasped out, her composure completely shattering behind her helmet.
What kind of absurd god-tier strength was that?! Reflecting thirty heavy siege artillery rounds with a casual flick of a hand without losing a single point of structural integrity?!
Eluned didn’t even stay to watch the chaos.
She offered a soft, quiet scoff beneath her hood, turned on her heel, and casually slunk back down the battlements into the Keep.
Seeing their own thirty high-density cannonballs screaming back toward their front line...
FLASH!
From the front deck of The Unmovable Wall, one of Sky’s elite Hero combatants stepped forward!
It was a tall woman clad in heavy, pink-tinted tower armor, holding a massive tower shield.
She slammed her shield flat into the ground, unleashing every drop of her physical mana.
"DIVINE AEGIS WALL!" the Hero roared.
SHRRRRR!
A massive, semi-transparent pink barrier expanded across the entire front of Sky’s territory, forming a curved dome over the mobile fortress!
BOOOOOOM! BOOOOM! BOOOOM! BOOOOM!
All thirty reflected cannonballs slammed into the pink barrier simultaneously.
Violent blinding explosions of fire and shockwaves tore through the neutral clearing...

The absurd force of the impacts caused the pink barrier to shake violently, deep spiderweb cracks spreading across its surface as the Hero gasped out in pain with her boots sliding backward through the dirt.
"Haah~"
CRACK! CRACK!
The pink barrier barely held on, shattering into harmless pink spackles as the last explosion cleared.
The Hero collapsed to her knees, panting heavily with her mana reserves completely depleted from blocking her own territory’s reflected artillery.
Sky stood on the field, cold sweat pouring down her neck beneath her disguise helmet.
Before Sky could even process the absurdity of what had just occurred—
CREAK... HEAVE!
The massive reinforced front gates of the Blessed Land slowly swung open.
Through the open gates, a small tactical group stepped out onto the grass... led by Brida and Tamsin!
They weren’t rushing out in a reckless charge... they were casually fanning out across the clearing, establishing wide tactical angles.
Sky’s battle-trained mind instantly recognized the danger.
The high stone Watchtower towering above the gates was equipped with heavy defense turrets and long-range snipers.
If Sky kept her forces clustered together in front of the gate, those turrets would rain down hell upon his clustered troops.
Sky glanced up at the Watchtower.
Standing atop the highest platform of the Watchtower was Fenna... the sniper.
Fenna stood in a wide, stable archer’s stance.
She was holding a massive, four-foot-long composite longbow forged from dark star-iron.
Her sharp hazel eyes were completely calm, locked directly onto Lord Sky’s masked face across a distance of eight hundred yards.
Fenna reached back to her quiver, pulled out a single sleek black arrow, and notched it onto the bowstring.
SHRRRRR!
She drew the bowstring all the way back to her ear.
There was outwardly nothing special or flashy about that single arrow. There was no roaring fire magic, no crackling lightning, no glowing aura.
It appeared to be just a standard well-forged iron arrow.
THWIP!
Fenna released the string.
The single black arrow shot through the air with a soft, whistling whisper but Sky’s spatial senses flared wildly.

chapters.title: Chapter 302: Elm’s Sacrifice [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: Even though the arrow looked completely ordinary, Sky’s veteran combat instincts screamed in terror.
’The hell...’
The single black arrow wasn’t just flying in a straight trajectory... it was subtly altering its flight path mid-air, locking onto her helmet’s signal with terrifying automated homing magic.
Sky wasn’t going to take a single chance with anything coming out of that territory.
HUMMM!
Sky raised her right hand, unleashing a powerful, high-yield stream of Water Magic.
A roaring high-pressure jet of compressed water shot out from her palm, striking the incoming arrow mid-air four hundred yards away.
The moment Sky’s water stream touched the tip of the black arrow—
BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
An explosive detonation of mind-boggling magnitude erupted in the center of the battlefield.

A colossal, fifty-foot fireball exploded into the sky. The shockwave was so immense that it tore up thousands of pounds of dirt and grass, creating a massive, blinding wall of dark smoke and fire that completely obscured the entire field!
BOOM!
Sky stumbled back half a step, using her arm to shield her helmet from the flying dirt and heat!
Inside her disguise, Sky’s heart was hammering against her ribs like a trapped bird.
She had been in terrifying overwhelming positions like this before... facing high-tier Lords, getting cornered in Zones, and dealing with absurd enemy abilities.𝗳𝚛𝚎𝚎𝘄𝕖𝕓𝕟𝕠𝚟𝚎𝕝.𝗰𝕠𝐦
But Sky was a veteran Classic Lord! She knew how to survive, how to adapt, and most importantly... how to turn a dangerous situation into high-tier streaming content for her audience.
She was currently farming millions of viewers... The engagement metrics were going through the roof.
Sky lowered his arm, his eyes glinting behind his mask as he pointed his sword outward.
"SPREAD OUT!" Sky bellowed at the top of his lungs with his voice echoing through the smoke. "DISPERSE ACROSS THE ENTIRE FIELD! DO NOT GIVE THEM A CLUSTERED TARGET! CHARGE!"
Sky’s forces... dozens of heavy infantry warriors, speed-type combatants, and mercenary knights let out a roaring battle cry.
"RAHHHHHHHH!"
They broke formation instantly, fanning out across the vast clearing in every direction, running toward the open gates of the Blessed Land.
Sky offered a sharp confident smirk behind the mask.
By spreading his troops across a two-thousand-yard width single-target homing arrows and area-of-effect spells would be completely rendered useless.
...However, as the thick smoke from the initial explosion slowly began to vanish in the wind...
Sky looked up into the sky... and his jaw dropped completely open.
The smoke cleared... revealing NOT a single arrow... but DOZENS AND DOZENS OF IDENTICAL BLACK ARROWS floating in the upper atmosphere!
Fenna, standing atop the high Watchtower, was holding her composite bow horizontally.
Behind her, a massive, glowing blue Multi-Shot Volley spell was active.
Hundreds of sleek, black homing arrows were suspended in the sky above the battlefield with their glowing tips pointing straight down at Sky’s spreading army like a rain of dark meteors.
Sky stared at the sky, her black eyes widening in horror behind her helmet, as a single helpless word escaped her lips.
BOOOOOOOOOOM! BOOOOOOOOOOM! BOOOOOOOOOOM! BOOOOOOOOOOM! BOOOOOOOOOOM!
A deafening continuous cascade of apocalyptic explosions consumed the entire battlefield.
[A Bit Earlier...]

Deep beneath the massive, multi-tiered steel treads of The Unmovable Wall, far below the vibrating engine blocks and the deafening roar of the upper artillery decks, lay a hidden subterranean medical chamber.
The air down here was thick, frigid, and heavily saturated with the sharp chemical tang of distilled mana-salts, pressurized magic, and sterile life-support fluids.

The walls were lined with heavy iron plating, lit only by the soft sickly green luminescence of giant glass containment cylinders embedded directly into the foundational bedrock of the mobile fortress.
Submerged inside the largest, central glass cylinder was a woman.
She possessed long silky white hair that floated weightlessly around her shoulders in the thick, glowing green nutrient fluid like a halo of frost.
Her striking almond-shaped eyes were a pristine, crystalline silver, currently staring unblinkingly through the glass at the shadowy iron ceiling above.

Her slender, pale frame was clad in thin medical linen, and a flexible breathing apparatus was fitted tightly over her mouth and nose, venting a rhythmic steady stream of silver bubbles up toward the fluid’s surface.
Her name was Elm.

Once upon a time... long before The Unmovable Wall had ever acquired its giant, land-flattening steel treads, before it became a famous moving territory across the global networks, and long before Lord Sky had amassed hundreds of millions of followers on LordTube... Elm had been one of Lord Sky’s very first and most cherished Hero combatants.
She and Hiro had been summoned together into the Sovereign Realm during the territory’s earliest and most perilous days.

Side by side, the three of them had bled in the dirt, repelled wild monster swarms in the unforgiving wilderness, and carved out their tiny sanctuary in the Umbral Basin through pure grit and survival instinct.
She had been Lord Sky’s ultimate sword, her light and support magic turning hopeless battles into miraculous victories...
RUMBLE! RUMBLE! RUMBLE!
A colossal violent shockwave rattled the chamber.
Dust and iron shavings rained down from the ceiling girders, and the luminescent green liquid inside her glass cylinder sloshed violently, sending a cascade of bubbles turbulence around her body.
High above, the muffled thunderous impacts of heavy artillery and exploding spellcraft echoed through the iron foundations.
Deep within her chest, Elm’s spiritual core throbbed with a sharp agonizing ache.
Ever since she had suffered a catastrophic, near-fatal spatial core rupture during a desperate dungeon boss raid a long time ago, she had been confined to this nutrient tank.

Lord Sky had poured astronomical fortunes into her life support... buying rare high-grade medical catalysts, hiring alchemists, and diverting precious territory mana reserves just to keep her vital signs from fading into nothingness.
Yet, despite all those efforts, her damaged mana pathways had refused to mend.
There had been zero advancement in her physical recovery.
She was trapped in a agonizing state of static limbo... conscious, fully aware, yet utterly incapable of stepping onto the battlefield to swing her blade or cast a spell.

’Lord Sky...’ Elm thought, her silver eyes trembling behind the thick glass as she felt another heavy explosion shake the foundations. ’Lord Sky is out there right now... fighting for the very survival of our territory... fighting against a terrifying, unknown enemy... and here I am. Floating in a glass jar like a fragile, pathetic ornament.’
Tears of pure frustration welled in the corners of her silver eyes, dissolving instantly into the surrounding green liquid.
What made her a Hero if she couldn’t stand beside her Lord when everything was on the line?
What was the worth of holding a Hero title if she could only sit in the dark while her comrades and standard soldiers spilled their blood on the grass outside?
Elm’s lips pursed tightly beneath her breathing mask.
A sudden blinding spark of white-and-silver mana ignited deep within her shattered core, burning through the numbness of her body like liquid fire.
She remembered the private conversation she had shared with Lord Sky right before the broadcast signal went live this morning.
She remembered Lord Sky’s voice echoing through her chamber’s comm-speaker, sounding tired yet resolute.
’All’s fair in love and war, Elm...’
Those words meant everything to her.

Elm knew that Lord Sky, Hiro, and all the territory medics had repeatedly begged her to take it easy, warning her that unlocking her core before her pathways healed would permanently destroy her spiritual foundation.
However they had forgotten one thing...
She was The Unmovable Wall’s ultimate, hidden secret weapon and what good was a secret weapon if it sat rusting in the dark when its Lord needed it most?!

Elm opened her mouth beneath the breathing apparatus, blowing a cloud of silver bubbles into the green fluid, and channeled every single drop of her remaining life force directly into the base of her glass cylinder.
Through the thick pressurized liquid, her voice echoed out into the subterranean silence like a solemn divine command.
HUMMMMMMMMM!
The exact second the word left her lips, a colossal glowing white Four-Leaf Clover magical circle flared into existence at the bottom of her glass cylinder.

The brilliant silver-and-white light didn’t just illuminate the green fluid... it erupted outward, expanding through the bedrock and steel plating of The Unmovable Wall like an unstoppable blinding tidal wave.
The white clover spell shot through the iron hull, expanding across the entire two-thousand-yard width of the mobile fortress, and swept directly onto the open battlefield outside.
Out on the open, smoke-filled clearing...

Hundreds of Lord Sky’s vanguard soldiers, heavy armored knights, and speed-type combatants were sprinting across the trampled grass with their hearts gripped by paralyzing terror as they looked up at the sky.
Above them, Fenna’s Multi-Shot Volley had just released its apocalyptic payload.
Dozens upon dozens of sleek, black homing arrows were screaming down from the clouds like a rain of dark explosive meteors, their tips glowing with volatile destruction!
Lord Sky stood in the center of the field with his disguise helmet locked onto the incoming rain of black arrows and his teeth clenching as she braced for devastation.
"Fu—"
SWOOOOSH!
Before the black arrows could strike the dirt, a blinding ethereal wave of white-and-silver clover light swept across the entire battlefield from behind.
The glowing white light washed over every single soldier, hero, and knight in Sky’s army.
The second the silver clover magic touched their bodies, their physical forms underwent an instantaneous miraculous transformation.
Their muscles bulged beneath their plate armor, their skin hardened into adamantine density, and a blinding ten-fold aura of supercharged mana erupted from their bodies like pillars of light.
In front of the army, Lord Sky froze as the white light washed over the disguise armor.
[TERRITORY-WIDE SACRIFICIAL HERO SKILL ACTIVATED: FOUR-LEAF CLOVE]
[SOURCE: HERO UNIT ’ELM’]
+ ALLIED COMBAT POWER MULTIPLIER: 1000% (10x)
+ PHYSICAL DURABILITY & ARMOR HARDNESS: +900%
+ MOVEMENT SPEED & NEURAL REFLEXES: +900%
+ MANA OUTPUT & SPELL RESISTANCE: +900%
[WARNING: UNIT ’ELM’ IS CONSUMING VITAL LIFE ESSENCE TO MAINTAIN SPELL]
Behind his full-face disguise helmet, Sky’s eyes widened in heartbreaking shock.
’Elm...’ Sky thought with his heart clenching painfully in his chest. ’So... you actually did it, you stubborn fool...’
BOOOOOOOOOOM! BOOOOOOOOOOM! BOOOOOOOOOOM! BOOOOOOOOOOM!
At that exact second, Fenna’s dark homing arrows slammed into the battlefield.

A continuous, apocalyptic cascade of fifty-foot fireballs and shockwaves consumed the terrain, tearing up thousands of pounds of earth and obscuring the entire clearing in a blinding sea of fire and dark smoke.
On the global stream, over three hundred and fifty million viewers held their breath, expecting Lord Sky’s entire vanguard army to be wiped out in a single salvo!
...However, as the roaring flames raged—
"RAHHHHHH!"
"IS THAT ALL YOU’VE GOT, BLESSED LAND?!"
"WE ARE UNMOVABLE! CHARGE!"
A chorus of bloodthirsty, roaring battle cries erupted directly from the center of the inferno.
Through the blinding wall of fire and smoke, Sky’s soldiers didn’t fall...
Reinforced by Elm’s 10x stat multiplier, their armor held firm against the kinetic blasts.

They surged forward out of the burning craters like an unstoppable, golden-white tide of supercharged juggernauts with their physical speed doubling as they tore across the grass toward the open gates of the Blessed Land.
Sky’s face twitched beneath the mask. The overwhelming grief for Elm’s sacrifice turned into cold razor-sharp battle focus.
’I respect your sacrifice, Elm...’ Sky resolved in her mind, raising her steel sword high into the air. ’I won’t let your willingness to die be in vain!’
"KEEP MOVING!" Sky bellowed at the top of his lungs with his voice echoing across the battlefield! "PUSH THEM ALL THE WAY BACK TO THEIR TERRITORY!"
However, as her supercharged army roared forward, Sky’s veteran instincts remained sharply on guard.
She looked up at the Steel-Weave perimeter walls of the Blessed Land.
Something was deeply wrong.
Aside from the small vanguard squad that had stepped through the main gates earlier, Blessed Land had deployed zero additional reinforcements.
There were no secondary armies marching out, no grand elemental spell circles forming over the battlements, and the archers atop the Watchtower had suddenly stopped firing their homing salvos...
Why had they stopped? Had they run out of composite bows? Were their arrow quivers depleted? Or... did the Lord of the Blessed Land have something far more sinister waiting in the box?

’No...’ Sky analyzed rapidly with her mind racing. ’Blessed Land is a brand-new territory. Their total population and unit roster are significantly smaller than The Unmovable Wall. They’re trying to bide their time and conserve their high-tier units because they can’t afford a prolonged war of attrition!’

chapters.title: Chapter 303: Charge! [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: Sky decided not to give them that time. She was going to eliminate their primary combat threats one by one...
Sky turned his masked head toward two figures standing silently in the shadows behind the command vehicle.
They were two female Heroes clad in long pristine white cloaks adorned with glowing solar runes... Sky’s elite Light-Magic Specialists.
Sky offered them a firm decisive nod.
"Deal with her. Neutralize the shadow woman before she reaches our rear lines."
The two white-cloaked Heroes bowed silently in unison.
FLASH!
In a fraction of a second, both women dissolved into beams of pure blinding light, vanishing across the battlefield at high speed to intercept Tasmin.
’I’d like to see your move Vespera... come on, make things interesting.’
Out on the central battlefield, three hundred yards ahead of the open iron gates...
"Hahahahaha! We’re finally about to engage!" Brida roared out with boisterous bloodthirsty laughter.
The S-Rank Grand Titan Bastion stood in the center of the field, her six-foot three frame clad in armor.
She hoisted her massive, double-bitted Titan’s Cleaver onto her broad shoulder with her other arm bracing the towering Steel Aegis shield flat against the dirt.
A few paces behind her in the shadows, Tasmin, the S-Rank Shadow Commander shot Brida a flat unamused deadpan look.
"Calm down, Brida," Tasmin remarked smoothly, her twin shortswords spinning around her fingers with hypnotic speed. "You’re acting like you haven’t seen a fight in three years."
"I can’t help it!" Brida grinned savagely, her eyes burning with fanatical excitement. "I can’t wait to break some skulls and smash through their lines!"
Standing in a tight tactical formation alongside them were three other Vanguard warriors.
Gunnhild, holding her heavy ashwood spear with a confident smirk...
Hilda, adjusting her iron gauntlets and Fenna, who was wearing a dark traveler’s cloak over her sniper gear, her composite longbow slung over her back and her compact wrist-bow locked onto her arm.
There were exactly five members in this forward strike force: Tasmin, Brida, Gunnhild, Hilda, and Fenna.

Lord Silas had laid out the overarching battle strategy for them before they had stepped out through the gates this morning... and to be completely honest, every single girl in the squad loved their Lord’s plan.
Technically, if Silas wanted to end this Lord War instantly, all he had to do was send Eluned or Morwenna onto the field.
Eluned could sink The Unmovable Wall into a bottomless abyss with a single gesture, and Morwenna could slice the entire mobile fortress in half with her spatial magic.
The war would be over in less than five seconds!
...But Silas had explicitly forbidden them from taking the easy way out.
Relying entirely on SSS-Rank powerhouses would never help the girls to grow, evolve, or learn how to navigate high-stakes combat on their own.
Silas wanted his girls to become strong... strong enough to stand on their own two feet, face rival armies, and overcome adverse odds through sheer skill, teamwork, and tactical collaboration.

Their objective today was straightforward... Charge into the enemy vanguard, slaughter or neutralize Lord Sky’s frontline officers, clear a path through the infantry, and allow Fenna to destroy the remaining heavy mana cannons mounted on the fortress hull.
And, of course, as Silas had smirked and told them right before they marched out.
’Doing it this way will make you girls look infinitely cooler on the global broadcast.’
Tasmin’s lips twitched into a fond subtle smile as she recalled her Lord’s words.
’If My Lord says it will help us look cool...’ Tasmin thought with diehard devotion, ’...then it will help us look cool.’
"Don’t forget the plan, Brida," Tasmin reminded her smoothly, adjusting the Eclipse-Thread chains wrapped around her forearms.
"Yeah, yeah~!" Brida waved her hand dismissively, her red eyes fixed on the charging tide of supercharged soldiers. "I know my job! I’m the wall!"
Beside her, Gunnhild clutched her heavy ashwood spear, her knuckles turning white as she let out a excited breath.
"I can’t believe I’m back in action, baby! My spear hand has been itching for days!"
Fenna pulled her cloak hood over her head, her sharp hazel eyes narrowing as she calibrated her wrist-bow.
"I just need a clear line of sight to those upper gun decks. Give me five seconds of clear air, and I’ll silence those cannons permanently."
The roaring battle cries of Sky’s supercharged 10x-buffed army echoed loudly across the field, growing closer by the second.
Dozens of heavy knights, mercenary shock-troopers, and warriors were surging toward them like a tidal wave of golden-white mana.
Tasmin’s eyes narrowed into sharp cold slits. She raised her hand, issuing a crisp tactical command to the squad.
"Behind Brida. Now."
In a heartbeat, Gunnhild, Hilda, and Fenna smoothly shifted their positions, arranging themselves directly behind Brida’s towering mountain-like frame.
Far across the field, Lord Sky, her officers, and over three hundred and fifty million viewers watching the stream looked at the Vanguard’s bizarre formation in total confusion.
Why was the all-powerful terrifying shadow woman... Tasmin deliberately standing behind this broad, burly shieldmaiden?
Was this shield-bearing woman some sort of hidden God of War?!
Brida lowered her center of gravity, her hands gripping the handles of her Titan’s Cleaver and Steel Aegis.
She turned her head slightly, looking back over her shoulder at Tasmin with a wide feral grin.
"So really..." Brida chuckled, her voice deep and vibrating with raw power. "...I don’t have to hold back, right? Like... not even a little bit?"
Tasmin stepped up behind her, gently placing her gloved hand flat onto Brida’s reinforced shoulder plate.
Tasmin’s crimson eyes flashed with lethal shadow magic as she whispered.
"Give them hell, Brida."
"GWAHAHAHA! WITH PLEASURE!" Brida roared out.
BOOOOOOOOOOM!
Brida took a single violent step forward onto the grass!
The moment her boot struck the soil, a colossal tremor erupted across the terrain.
The ground for fifty yards in every direction shattered and vibrated wildly, kicking up dirt, rocks, and grass into the air.
[PASSIVE SKILL ACTIVATED: Unyielding Bedrock Body]
Brida’s muscle and bone density expanded to adamantine, mountain-like levels.
Her physical form radiated an aura of unshakeable gravity, rendering her completely immune to knockback, stagger, or displacement.
She brought her massive Steel Aegis shield flat in front of her chest, her red eyes burning like twin suns through her visor.
"COME ON, YOU BASTARDS!" Brida bellowed at the top of her lungs.
[ACTIVE SKILL ACTIVATED: Aegis Charge]
BO-BO-BO-BOOM!
A blinding blood-red crimson aura erupted from Brida’s body.
She surged forward across the battlefield like a runaway, five-hundred-ton armored locomotive.
Her boots tore three-foot-deep trenches into the dirt as she accelerated to high speeds, generating a massive boom around her shield!
The supercharged 10x-buffed vanguard of Sky’s army reached her position at that exact second—
KABAAAAAAM!
The impact was utter apocalyptic carnage.
The moment Brida’s Steel Aegis shield slammed into the frontline of Sky’s heavy knights, the laws of physics ceased to exist.
Even with Elm’s ten-fold physical durability buff, the mind-boggling kinetic force behind 5,000 Vitality moving at high speeds was completely incomprehensible!
"TAKE THIS BITCH!"
The first person struck... a massive six-foot-six heavy knight in full plate mail was completely crushed upon contact.
His steel chestplate flattened like paper, his bones pulverized instantly, and a spray of crimson blood erupted across the broad face of Brida’s Aegis shield!
"AHHHHHHH!"
"WHAT IS THIS MONSTER?!"
"MY LEGS! MY ARMOR IS CRUSHED!"
Screams of horror-filled agony echoed across the field as Brida plowed straight through the center of Sky’s army but she didn’t slow down.
She tore a gory, twenty-yard-wide breach directly through their dense infantry lines, spraying blood, shattered shields, and broken swords across her Aegis like a bloody snowplow.

"HAHAHAHAHA! MORE! GIVE ME MORE!" Brida laughed boisterously, sweeping her Titan’s Cleaver in massive horizontal arcs as she tore through their rear ranks, leaving a wide trail of destruction and groaning soldiers in her wake.
Behind her, the charging army was left completely shattered, disoriented, and paralyzed in terror!
Stepping out from the wake of dust and blood left behind by Brida’s charge, Gunnhild stepped forward.
Gunnhild rolled her shoulders, her hands gripping her heavy ashwood spear. Her sharp eyes scanned the confused, trembling stragglers who had survived Brida’s initial impact.
A cool confident smirk touched Gunnhild’s lips as her eyes ignited with a bright, swirling gale-force mana.

"Alright, boys and girls..." Gunnhild spoke smoothly, her voice echoing over the groans of the wounded as she casually whipped her heavy spear sideways in a wide sweeping arc. "...for your final act... you will now..."
The atmospheric pressure around her spear tip condensed to a terrifying density.
"...DISAPPEAR!"
BOOOOOOOOOOM!
A catastrophic wave of compressed, hurricane-force wind magic erupted outward from her spear blade.
The invisible wall of atmospheric pressure blasted forward in a broad thirty-meter cone.

Dozens of disoriented enemy soldiers were lifted clean off their feet, their armor tearing apart as the gale blasted them backward through the air, crashing into trees and rocks with bone-crushing impacts, killing several instantly.
Before the dust could even settle—
SWISH!
Fenna ran gracefully past Gunnhild, her traveler’s cloak fluttering in the wind as her boots touched the blood-stained grass.
Fenna sprinted forward, her sharp hazel eyes scanning the battlefield, and shouted back at Gunnhild.

"Try to keep killing the women to a minimum, Gunnhild! For the men here, you can do whatever you want... kill them or break their bones! But the female soldiers are going to be our new territory sisters after we win this war!"
Suddenly, from the cloud of dust on her left—
"DIE, YOU BITCH!"
A massive burly mercenary officer who had lost his right arm and his left eye from Brida’s initial charge let out a desperate bloodthirsty roar.
He had somehow tanked Gunnhild’s wind blast, and was now diving straight toward Fenna with his broadsword held in a two-handed overhead execution strike.
Fenna didn’t even flinch and she didn’t draw her longbow.
’I still don’t know why I was chosen... My Lord said I’m special... me...?’
As the massive officer plummeted down toward her head, Fenna smoothly dropped her hips, sliding flat on her back across the damp grass directly beneath his open legs!
While sliding under his falling body, Fenna raised her left forearm.
CLICK! THWIP!
’I’m not special but I’ve been trusted... and for that reason...’
The compact high-pressure wrist-bow mounted on her left forearm fired a single, three-inch micro-bolt point-blank through the bottom of the officer’s chin!
THWACK!
The steel micro-bolt penetrated cleanly through his skull, exiting out the top of his helmet in a spray of grey matter.
’I will fight for my Lord until the day I die.’
The massive officer’s eyes went completely life-less mid-air with his heavy body crashing face-first into the dirt behind her with a dull sound.
THUD!
Fenna smoothly popped back up onto her feet, dusting off her cloak, and muttered with a quiet deadpan huff.
"No offense... but I’d like to be touched by only my Lord."
Standing near the edge of the clearing, Tasmin observed the team’s seamless execution with a satisfied calm nod.
’This is okay...’ Tasmin evaluated in her mind. ’We’re making exceptional progress.’
She looked at the massive cloud of dust left behind by Brida’s charge.
The thick haze was hanging heavy in the air, significantly reducing optical visibility across the central battlefield.

Of course, Lord Sky’s high-tech streaming drones were equipped with thermal and mana-line sensors, so the viewers watching on the stream could still see through the dust and catch every single detail clearly...
Suddenly, Tasmin’s ears twitched beneath her pigtails.
From the dust haze directly to her left and right, two blinding, superheated pillars of pure Light Magic cut through the air, closing in on her position at light-speed!
It was the two white-cloaked Hero assassins sent by Lord Sky.
’I knew it...’
Light magic was the polar-opposite elemental counter to Shadow magic... capable of burning through shadow-submersion, illuminating dark stealth seams, and disrupting void-bleed effects.
If a standard shadow mage were caught between two high-tier Light Specialists, they would struggle immensely, get overwhelmed, and be forced onto the defensive.
...However, Tasmin was NOT a standard shadow mage. She was the Shadow Commander of the Blessed Land!
Instead of retreating into the safety of Brida’s Bastion barrier, a dark wicked, and utterly terrifying grin broke across Tasmin’s face.
HUMMMMMM!
[ACTIVE SKILL ACTIVATED: Shadow Strengthening]
Dense murky void magic erupted from Tasmin’s core.
Her shadow beneath her boots expanded, rising up and wrapping around her body like a suit of living, writhing dark armor.
Her physical stats doubled instantly, and dark terrifying shadow tendrils flared out from her shoulders like demon wings.
Tasmin turned her head toward Fenna and Gunnhild, her crimson eyes glowing with absolute, murderous thrill.
"Follow Brida and advance," Tasmin ordered smoothly.
Fenna paused, looking back at her through the dust.
"Why, Tasmin? Those two are Light Specialists... their magic is designed to counter your shadow!"
Tasmin’s grin widened, revealing her sharp fangs as shadow tendrils whipped violently around her blades.
"Why?" Tasmin chuckled darkly, her eyes locking onto the two incoming light-beams. "...Because I have bitches to kill."
Fenna looked at her, blinked her hazel eyes, and offered a flat deadpan nod.
"Fair enough," Fenna agreed instantly. She turned around, grabbing Gunnhild by the arm. "Gunnhild, let’s go! Keep up with Brida!"
"ON IT!" Gunnhild cheered.
With a sudden burst of speed, Fenna and Gunnhild dashed forward through the dust, following directly behind the continuous wave of devastation that Brida was carving through Sky’s army.

Left alone in the center of the dust haze, Tasmin slowly raised her twin void-blades, the Eclipse-Thread chains rattling against her wrists as the two solar light assassins burst out from the blinding glare.
Tasmin’s crimson eyes burned in the dark, and she whispered into the light.
"Let’s see if your light can outburn my shadow."

sentences.text: Sky decided not to give them that time.
She was going to eliminate their primary combat threats one by one...
Sky turned his masked head toward two figures standing silently in the shadows behind the command vehicle.

Sky’s elite Light-Magic Specialists.

The two white-cloaked Heroes bowed silently in unison.
FLASH!

Relying entirely on SSS-Rank powerhouses would never help the girls to grow, evolve, or learn how to navigate high-stakes combat on their own.

Charge into the enemy vanguard, slaughter or neutralize Lord Sky’s frontline officers, clear a path through the infantry, and allow Fenna to destroy the remaining heavy mana cannons mounted on the fortress hull.

I’m the wall!"

My spear hand has been itching for days!"

"I just need a clear line of sight to those upper gun decks.

Tasmin’s eyes narrowed into sharp cold slits.
She raised her hand, issuing a crisp tactical command to the squad.
"Behind Brida.
Now."
In a heartbeat, Gunnhild, Hilda, and Fenna smoothly shifted their positions, arranging themselves directly behind Brida’s towering mountain-like frame.
Far across the field, Lord Sky, her officers, and over three hundred and fifty million viewers watching the stream looked at the Vanguard’s bizarre formation in total confusion.
Why was the all-powerful terrifying shadow woman...
Tasmin deliberately standing behind this broad, burly shieldmaiden?
Was this shield-bearing woman some sort of hidden God of War?!
Brida lowered her center of gravity, her hands gripping the handles of her Titan’s Cleaver and Steel Aegis.
She turned her head slightly, looking back over her shoulder at Tasmin with a wide feral grin.
"So really..." Brida chuckled, her voice deep and vibrating with raw power.
"...I don’t have to hold back, right?
Like... not even a little bit?"
Tasmin stepped up behind her, gently placing her gloved hand flat onto Brida’s reinforced shoulder plate.
Tasmin’s crimson eyes flashed with lethal shadow magic as she whispered.
"Give them hell, Brida."
"GWAHAHAHA!
WITH PLEASURE!" Brida roared out.
BOOOOOOOOOOM!
Brida took a single violent step forward onto the grass!
The moment her boot struck the soil, a colossal tremor erupted across the terrain.
The ground for fifty yards in every direction shattered and vibrated wildly, kicking up dirt, rocks, and grass into the air.
[PASSIVE SKILL ACTIVATED: Unyielding Bedrock Body]
Brida’s muscle and bone density expanded to adamantine, mountain-like levels.
Her physical form radiated an aura of unshakeable gravity, rendering her completely immune to knockback, stagger, or displacement.
She brought her massive Steel Aegis shield flat in front of her chest, her red eyes burning like twin suns through her visor.

BO-BO-BO-BOOM!
A blinding blood-red crimson aura erupted from Brida’s body.
She surged forward across the battlefield like a runaway, five-hundred-ton armored locomotive.
Her boots tore three-foot-deep trenches into the dirt as she accelerated to high speeds, generating a massive boom around her shield!
The supercharged 10x-buffed vanguard of Sky’s army reached her position at that exact second—
KABAAAAAAM!
The impact was utter apocalyptic carnage.
The moment Brida’s Steel Aegis shield slammed into the frontline of Sky’s heavy knights, the laws of physics ceased to exist.
Even with Elm’s ten-fold physical durability buff, the mind-boggling kinetic force behind 5,000 Vitality moving at high speeds was completely incomprehensible!

The first person struck... a massive six-foot-six heavy knight in full plate mail was completely crushed upon contact.
His steel chestplate flattened like paper, his bones pulverized instantly, and a spray of crimson blood erupted across the broad face of Brida’s Aegis shield!
"AHHHHHHH!"

MY ARMOR IS CRUSHED!"

chapters.title: Chapter 304: "Faithful" 1 v 1 [I / Bonus - ]
paragraphs: High atop the obsidian battlements of the Blessed Land’s Steel-Weave perimeter wall, the morning air was cold and saturated with a beautiful scent.
Row upon row of women stood in rigid, disciplined military formation.

Clad in lightweight tactical armor under dark hooded cloaks that fluttered against the rising wind, the archers held their heavy composite longbows at forty-five-degree angles, while the mages kept their staffs planted firmly against the smooth stone floor.
Behind them, the massive Watchtower cast a long intimidating shadow across the battlements, its automated turret arrays humming with latent power.
Down below, on the blood-soaked smoke-filled clearing between the two territories, the frontline Shieldmaidens were already drawn up in tight overlapping defensive formations.
They were preparing for Phase Two of the grand battle strategy laid out earlier that morning by their Sovereign...
However, Phase Two could only be officially initiated once Tasmin, Brida, Fenna, Gunnhild, and Hilda brought Phase One to a definitive, overwhelming conclusion.
And even though every single woman standing on the battlements knew just how terrifyingly strong the frontline strike team was, a quiet prickling anxiety hung over the wall like a heavy shroud...
Not everyone was entirely convinced that five women... no matter how ridiculously skilled or level-advanced could hold off an entire supercharged enemy army indefinitely.
Even from here, they could tell that Sky’s vanguard was currently buffed by a ten-fold stat multiplier, numbering in the thousands and backed by a very powerful spellcaster.
Near the central arch of the wall, Vala stood leaning her shoulder against the dark stone crenellations.
Her right hand rested firmly on the polished silver pommel of her sheath.
Ever since Silas had utilized his System to upgrade her class into that of a Magic Swordsman, Vala’s physical presence on the battlefield had transformed completely.

The air immediately surrounding her body was subtly distorted with a flickering aura of condensed elemental mana which was a delicate blend of wind and blade aura that made her dark hair sway continuously.
She took a slow deep breath through her nose with her sharp blue eyes staring down into the lingering cloud of dust and fire on the field below.
Beside her, Elara slowly lowered her composite longbow, her fingers trembling slightly against the worn leather grip.
"Vala..." Elara spoke softly, her voice barely audible over the whistling wind.
She turned her head, her hazel eyes wide with mounting tension as she looked at the magic swordsman.

"Are... are you truly sure we shouldn’t march down there and support them? They’re down on that open field completely surrounded by a lot of buffed troops! What if Brida’s barrier collapses? What if they get flanked and overwhelmed by Sky’s Hero officers?"
Vala didn’t answer right away.
She kept her gaze fixed on the pommel of her sword, her thumb gently tracing the intricate runic engravings etched into the steel crossguard.
Elara’s frustration flared at her companion’s silence.
She took a step closer, her voice rising in her agitation.

"Vala! Listen to me! This isn’t just another routine hunting raid against regular monsers... This is an official Lord War broadcast live across the entire globe! There are a lot of experienced Hero combatants down there! We have high-ground advantage up here on the wall... why are we just standing here like statues watching them fight alone..."
Vala slowly turned her head. Her blue eyes were completely calm, radiating an unshakeable rock-solid composure that instantly silenced the younger archer’s rising panic.
"Focus, Elara," Vala commanded smoothly. "And stop doubting the battle plan. Do you really believe for a single second that any of those five down there would fail a direct command from our Lord?"
Elara blinked with her throat tightening. "I... no, but..."
Vala gestured with her chin toward the towering Watchtower behind them, where Fenna had been firing her homing salvos earlier.

"Isn’t your personal mentor, Fenna, down on that field right now?" Vala continued, her voice softening slightly with genuine warmth. "You’ve trained under her bow every single morning since we were summoned. You know better than anyone what kind of monster she is when she holds a string. Have a bit of confidence in your seniors. Our job isn’t to second-guess Phase One... our job is to be absolute perfection when Phase Two triggers."
Elara stared at Vala for three long seconds.
She swallowed hard, taking a slow shaky breath as she clutched her composite longbow tightly against her chest.
"You’re right..." Elara admitted softly with an embarrassed flush touching her cheeks. "I’m... I’m overreacting. I should believe... I need to believe that they can make it through—"
Before Elara could even finish her sentence—
BAM!
A violent earth-shattering explosion erupted directly beneath the central clearing three hundred yards away.

A blinding column of superheated white light, scorched soil, and shattered bedrock shot eighty feet straight into the sky, completely obliterating the patch of grass where the two strike forces had been converging.
The shockwave was so immense that even the heavy stone battlements beneath Vala and Elara’s boots subtly vibrated.
SWISH!
Out from the center of the blinding white explosion, a slender graceful silhouette shot backward through the smoke!
Tasmin executed a breathtaking flawless triple backflip in mid-air.
Her dark pigtails whipped wildly through the wind with her dark tunic fluttering against her frame, before her boots landed lightly on the damp grass fifty yards away.
The soles of her leather combat boots slid smoothly across the soil, coming to an effortless balanced halt without losing a single drop of momentum.
A sharp playful smirk spread across Tasmin’s face as she straightened her posture with her twin shortswords spinning idly around her fingers with speed.

"Well, well, well..." Tasmin called out into the lingering smoke, her voice dripping with smooth condescending amusement. "If your brilliant plan was to catch me off guard and kill me... you’re a bit too slow, darling."
DZZZZZT!𝓯𝙧𝓮𝓮𝒘𝓮𝙗𝙣𝒐𝒗𝒆𝓵.𝓬𝓸𝒎
Out from the settling dust and floating ash, tiny, shimmering motes of blinding white light began to coalesce in mid-air.
The white motes gathered together in a swirling, luminous vortex, solidifying rapidly into the physical form of a young woman.
She was clad in pristine, high-tier white priestess robes embroidered with intricate golden runes that pulsed with radiant energy.
Her pale skin radiated a soft divine luminescence, and her sharp eyes burned with intense righteous hatred as she stared at the [Shadow Commander].
However, Tasmin didn’t let her guard down for even a fraction of a millisecond.
Her ears twitched beneath her hair with her eyes scanning the surrounding terrain with razor-sharp precision.
She knew there were two of them... two identical Light-Magic Specialists dispatched by Lord Sky to eliminate her.
Yet, currently, only one of the white-cloaked Heroes stood before her.
Noticeably sensing Tasmin’s sharp eyes searching the shadows around the clearing, the white-robed woman offered a cold haughty smile, adjusting her silk sleeve with arrogance.

"Looking for my twin sister, shadow-rat?" the woman taunted, her voice echoing with a high-pitched noble tone that carried across the open field. "Don’t bother looking. She won’t be interfering in this engagement. Unlike you uncivilized barbarians in the Blessed Land, we of The Unmovable Wall believe in what is known as a clean, honorable, and faithful 1-v-1 duel."
Hearing the words "faithful 1-v-1 duel" in the middle of an official Lord War, Tasmin almost burst out laughing right then and there.
A clean 1-v-1? In the middle of an active battlefield where hundreds of supercharged soldiers were screaming, heavy artillery was exploding, and blood was soaking the grass?!

Furthermore, Tasmin’s sensory skills could clearly feel a second suffocating thread of razor-sharp killing intent locked onto her spinal cord from the high rock formations two hundred yards to her left.
The twin was definitely hiding in ambush, waiting for the perfect second to thrust a blade through her ribs...
However, instead of calling out the blatant, pathetic lie, Tasmin chose to play along.
As a veteran people’s person, Tasmin knew that when an enemy took the time to talk, they were usually trying to gauge your demeanor, measure your reaction time, and analyze your physical posture.
And Tasmin was more than happy to let this arrogant priestess think she had the mental upper hand... it gave her the perfect opportunity to set a psychological trap.
Tasmin relaxed her stance, throwing her hands up in a dramatic, overly appreciative gesture as she let out a sweet musical laugh.

"Oh, my goodness!" Tasmin cheered, her crimson eyes sparkling with mock gratitude. "A faithful 1-v-1 duel?! That is just so incredibly heartfelt! I absolutely adore proper 1-v-1s... just the two of us with no annoying distractions!"
Tasmin took a small step forward, placing her right hand flat over her chest in a formal theatrical greeting.
"Allow me to introduce myself properly! I am Tasmin of the Blessed Land... Commander of the Soldiers under our magnificent Lord Vespera!"
The white-robed woman puffed out her chest, raising her chin with supreme arrogance as a blinding halo of mana erupted around her head, illuminating her white robes.

"Remember the name of the holy blade that purges your filthy existence from this realm!" the woman declared loudly, her voice projecting across the entire battlefield. "I am Celeste Sunsword! High Priestess of Light from The Unmovable Wall, ordained by the heavens to banish all dark shadows!"
Tasmin stood frozen on the grass for two full seconds.
Behind her calm smiling face, her internal thoughts completely stalled as a single deadpan thought echoed through her mind.
’Who the hell... has the actual surname Sword?! Is her father named Shield Sunsword?! Is her mother named Halberd Sunsword?! What kind of ridiculous, try-hard noble name is that?!’
Tasmin forced herself to maintain her polite cheerful smile, suppressing the intense urge to roll her eyes into the back of her head.
Celeste Sunsword drew a long slender rapier forged from glowing white light crystal from her belt, pointing the gleaming tip directly at Tasmin’s face.

"For the atrocities your people committed against our scouting units earlier this week..." Celeste spat coldly, "...you will draw your final breath on this field, Tasmin! You will die today by my hand!"
Tasmin’s smile widened, her eyes narrowing into sharp deadly slits.
She raised both of her gloved fists in front of her face, dropping her hips into a loose fluid martial arts combat stance.
"Is that so...?" Tasmin said playfully. "Sure thing, Celeste... let’s see who actually dies today."
BOOM!
In that exact second, the atmospheric pressure between them shattered.
A blinding holy white solar aura exploded from Celeste Sunsword’s body, illuminating the entire dust cloud in a divine glare.
Simultaneously, a thick suffocating pitch-black aura erupted from Tasmin’s core, wrapping around her limbs like writhing demonic tendrils!
Across the global network, on over FIVE HUNDRED MILLION screen displays, viewers held their collective breath...
In private viewing rooms, tavern halls, noble estates, and corporate war rooms across Earth and the Sovereign Realm, every single person watching the stream was completely glued to the display!
The live view count on the upper corner of the broadcast had hit an unprecedented mind-boggling peak... half a billion active viewers watching the clash between Light and Shadow!
If Lord Sky had been monitoring her stream metrics right at that moment, she would have screamed in ecstatic disbelief at the historic numbers her broadcast was generating.
CRACK!
Both women charged simultaneously.
The solid bedrock beneath their boots caved inward, sending clouds of shattered stone and dirt flying into the air as they accelerated toward each other at supersonic speeds.
"DIE, DARKNESS!" Celeste Sunsword shrieked at the top of her lungs!
She thrust her crystal rapier forward five times in a fraction of a second.
FWOOSH! FWOOSH! FWOOSH! FWOOSH! FWOOSH!
Five colossal beams of pure superheated white solar light erupted from her blade tip, tearing through the air like searing laser cannons directly toward Tasmin’s chest!
Tasmin’s neural reflexes processed the trajectory of the light beams instantly.
She could tell that if those attacks made direct contact with her physical body, her shadow pathways would suffer severe elemental damage...
Yet, as she sprinted straight toward the searing laser beams, a bright playful grin broke across Tasmin’s face.
She looked down at her right gauntlet.
Wrapped around her right wrist was a sleek dark-purple gauntlet.
It was a custom masterpiece forged personally by Thora, the Master Smith, and inscribed with high-tier defensive runes by Rowenna, the Grand Runemaster.

sentences.text: High atop the obsidian battlements of the Blessed Land’s Steel-Weave perimeter wall, the morning air was cold and saturated with a beautiful scent.
Row upon row of women stood in rigid, disciplined military formation.

Clad in lightweight tactical armor under dark hooded cloaks that fluttered against the rising wind, the archers held their heavy composite longbows at forty-five-degree angles, while the mages kept their staffs planted firmly against the smooth stone floor.
Behind them, the massive Watchtower cast a long intimidating shadow across the battlements, its automated turret arrays humming with latent power.
Down below, on the blood-soaked smoke-filled clearing between the two territories, the frontline Shieldmaidens were already drawn up in tight overlapping defensive formations.
They were preparing for Phase Two of the grand battle strategy laid out earlier that morning by their Sovereign...
However, Phase Two could only be officially initiated once Tasmin, Brida, Fenna, Gunnhild, and Hilda brought Phase One to a definitive, overwhelming conclusion.
And even though every single woman standing on the battlements knew just how terrifyingly strong the frontline strike team was, a quiet prickling anxiety hung over the wall like a heavy shroud...
Not everyone was entirely convinced that five women... no matter how ridiculously skilled or level-advanced could hold off an entire supercharged enemy army indefinitely.
Even from here, they could tell that Sky’s vanguard was currently buffed by a ten-fold stat multiplier, numbering in the thousands and backed by a very powerful spellcaster.
Near the central arch of the wall, Vala stood leaning her shoulder against the dark stone crenellations.
Her right hand rested firmly on the polished silver pommel of her sheath.
Ever since Silas had utilized his System to upgrade her class into that of a Magic Swordsman, Vala’s physical presence on the battlefield had transformed completely.

The air immediately surrounding her body was subtly distorted with a flickering aura of condensed elemental mana which was a delicate blend of wind and blade aura that made her dark hair sway continuously.
She took a slow deep breath through her nose with her sharp blue eyes staring down into the lingering cloud of dust and fire on the field below.
Beside her, Elara slowly lowered her composite longbow, her fingers trembling slightly against the worn leather grip.
"Vala..." Elara spoke softly, her voice barely audible over the whistling wind.
She turned her head, her hazel eyes wide with mounting tension as she looked at the magic swordsman.
"Are... are you truly sure we shouldn’t march down there and support them?
They’re down on that open field completely surrounded by a lot of buffed troops!
What if Brida’s barrier collapses?
What if they get flanked and overwhelmed by Sky’s Hero officers?"
Vala didn’t answer right away.
She kept her gaze fixed on the pommel of her sword, her thumb gently tracing the intricate runic engravings etched into the steel crossguard.
Elara’s frustration flared at her companion’s silence.
She took a step closer, her voice rising in her agitation.
"Vala!
Listen to me!
This isn’t just another routine hunting raid against regular monsers...
This is an official Lord War broadcast live across the entire globe!
There are a lot of experienced Hero combatants down there!
We have high-ground advantage up here on the wall... why are we just standing here like statues watching them fight alone..."
Vala slowly turned her head.
Her blue eyes were completely calm, radiating an unshakeable rock-solid composure that instantly silenced the younger archer’s rising panic.
"Focus, Elara," Vala commanded smoothly.
"And stop doubting the battle plan.
Do you really believe for a single second that any of those five down there would fail a direct command from our Lord?"
Elara blinked with her throat tightening.
"I... no, but..."
Vala gestured with her chin toward the towering Watchtower behind them, where Fenna had been firing her homing salvos earlier.
"Isn’t your personal mentor, Fenna, down on that field right now?" Vala continued, her voice softening slightly with genuine warmth.
"You’ve trained under her bow every single morning since we were summoned.
You know better than anyone what kind of monster she is when she holds a string.
Have a bit of confidence in your seniors.
Our job isn’t to second-guess Phase One... our job is to be absolute perfection when Phase Two triggers."
Elara stared at Vala for three long seconds.
She swallowed hard, taking a slow shaky breath as she clutched her composite longbow tightly against her chest.
"You’re right..." Elara admitted softly with an embarrassed flush touching her cheeks.
I’m overreacting.
I should believe...
I need to believe that they can make it through—"
Before Elara could even finish her sentence—
BAM!
A violent earth-shattering explosion erupted directly beneath the central clearing three hundred yards away.

A blinding column of superheated white light, scorched soil, and shattered bedrock shot eighty feet straight into the sky, completely obliterating the patch of grass where the two strike forces had been converging.
The shockwave was so immense that even the heavy stone battlements beneath Vala and Elara’s boots subtly vibrated.
SWISH!
Out from the center of the blinding white explosion, a slender graceful silhouette shot backward through the smoke!
Tasmin executed a breathtaking flawless triple backflip in mid-air.
Her dark pigtails whipped wildly through the wind with her dark tunic fluttering against her frame, before her boots landed lightly on the damp grass fifty yards away.
The soles of her leather combat boots slid smoothly across the soil, coming to an effortless balanced halt without losing a single drop of momentum.
A sharp playful smirk spread across Tasmin’s face as she straightened her posture with her twin shortswords spinning idly around her fingers with speed.
"Well, well, well..." Tasmin called out into the lingering smoke, her voice dripping with smooth condescending amusement.
"If your brilliant plan was to catch me off guard and kill me... you’re a bit too slow, darling."
DZZZZZT!𝓯𝙧𝓮𝓮𝒘𝓮𝙗𝙣𝒐𝒗𝒆𝓵.𝓬𝓸𝒎
Out from the settling dust and floating ash, tiny, shimmering motes of blinding white light began to coalesce in mid-air.
The white motes gathered together in a swirling, luminous vortex, solidifying rapidly into the physical form of a young woman.
She was clad in pristine, high-tier white priestess robes embroidered with intricate golden runes that pulsed with radiant energy.
Her pale skin radiated a soft divine luminescence, and her sharp eyes burned with intense righteous hatred as she stared at the [Shadow Commander].
However, Tasmin didn’t let her guard down for even a fraction of a millisecond.
Her ears twitched beneath her hair with her eyes scanning the surrounding terrain with razor-sharp precision.
She knew there were two of them... two identical Light-Magic Specialists dispatched by Lord Sky to eliminate her.
Yet, currently, only one of the white-cloaked Heroes stood before her.
Noticeably sensing Tasmin’s sharp eyes searching the shadows around the clearing, the white-robed woman offered a cold haughty smile, adjusting her silk sleeve with arrogance.
"Looking for my twin sister, shadow-rat?" the woman taunted, her voice echoing with a high-pitched noble tone that carried across the open field.
"Don’t bother looking.
She won’t be interfering in this engagement.
Unlike you uncivilized barbarians in the Blessed Land, we of The Unmovable Wall believe in what is known as a clean, honorable, and faithful 1-v-1 duel."
Hearing the words "faithful 1-v-1 duel" in the middle of an official Lord War, Tasmin almost burst out laughing right then and there.
A clean 1-v-1?
In the middle of an active battlefield where hundreds of supercharged soldiers were screaming, heavy artillery was exploding, and blood was soaking the grass?!

Furthermore, Tasmin’s sensory skills could clearly feel a second suffocating thread of razor-sharp killing intent locked onto her spinal cord from the high rock formations two hundred yards to her left.
The twin was definitely hiding in ambush, waiting for the perfect second to thrust a blade through her ribs...
However, instead of calling out the blatant, pathetic lie, Tasmin chose to play along.
As a veteran people’s person, Tasmin knew that when an enemy took the time to talk, they were usually trying to gauge your demeanor, measure your reaction time, and analyze your physical posture.
And Tasmin was more than happy to let this arrogant priestess think she had the mental upper hand... it gave her the perfect opportunity to set a psychological trap.
Tasmin relaxed her stance, throwing her hands up in a dramatic, overly appreciative gesture as she let out a sweet musical laugh.
"Oh, my goodness!" Tasmin cheered, her crimson eyes sparkling with mock gratitude.
"A faithful 1-v-1 duel?!
That is just so incredibly heartfelt!
I absolutely adore proper 1-v-1s... just the two of us with no annoying distractions!"
Tasmin took a small step forward, placing her right hand flat over her chest in a formal theatrical greeting.
"Allow me to introduce myself properly!
I am Tasmin of the Blessed Land...
Commander of the Soldiers under our magnificent Lord Vespera!"
The white-robed woman puffed out her chest, raising her chin with supreme arrogance as a blinding halo of mana erupted around her head, illuminating her white robes.
"Remember the name of the holy blade that purges your filthy existence from this realm!" the woman declared loudly, her voice projecting across the entire battlefield.
"I am Celeste Sunsword!
High Priestess of Light from The Unmovable Wall, ordained by the heavens to banish all dark shadows!"
Tasmin stood frozen on the grass for two full seconds.
Behind her calm smiling face, her internal thoughts completely stalled as a single deadpan thought echoed through her mind.
’Who the hell... has the actual surname Sword?!
Is her father named Shield Sunsword?!
Is her mother named Halberd Sunsword?!
What kind of ridiculous, try-hard noble name is that?!’
Tasmin forced herself to maintain her polite cheerful smile, suppressing the intense urge to roll her eyes into the back of her head.
Celeste Sunsword drew a long slender rapier forged from glowing white light crystal from her belt, pointing the gleaming tip directly at Tasmin’s face.
"For the atrocities your people committed against our scouting units earlier this week..." Celeste spat coldly, "...you will draw your final breath on this field, Tasmin!
You will die today by my hand!"
Tasmin’s smile widened, her eyes narrowing into sharp deadly slits.
She raised both of her gloved fists in front of her face, dropping her hips into a loose fluid martial arts combat stance.
"Is that so...?" Tasmin said playfully.
"Sure thing, Celeste... let’s see who actually dies today."
BOOM!
In that exact second, the atmospheric pressure between them shattered.
A blinding holy white solar aura exploded from Celeste Sunsword’s body, illuminating the entire dust cloud in a divine glare.
Simultaneously, a thick suffocating pitch-black aura erupted from Tasmin’s core, wrapping around her limbs like writhing demonic tendrils!
Across the global network, on over FIVE HUNDRED MILLION screen displays, viewers held their collective breath...
In private viewing rooms, tavern halls, noble estates, and corporate war rooms across Earth and the Sovereign Realm, every single person watching the stream was completely glued to the display!
The live view count on the upper corner of the broadcast had hit an unprecedented mind-boggling peak... half a billion active viewers watching the clash between Light and Shadow!
If Lord Sky had been monitoring her stream metrics right at that moment, she would have screamed in ecstatic disbelief at the historic numbers her broadcast was generating.

Both women charged simultaneously.
The solid bedrock beneath their boots caved inward, sending clouds of shattered stone and dirt flying into the air as they accelerated toward each other at supersonic speeds.

She thrust her crystal rapier forward five times in a fraction of a second.
FWOOSH!
FWOOSH!
FWOOSH!

Five colossal beams of pure superheated white solar light erupted from her blade tip, tearing through the air like searing laser cannons directly toward Tasmin’s chest!
