"My Lord is a Newbie Lord..." Brida continued casually, "...while your Lord Sky is a Classic Lord, which means your territory has been in the game far longer than ours."
Brida’s red eyes thinned slightly with her expression turning terrifyingly cold as she asked a blunt deadpan question.
"So tell me, Hog... why are your kicks so damn weak?"
Hog froze, his breath catching in his throat.
"Were you holding back just now?" Brida asked.
"Because you better not be holding back on me... or I’m going to cave your brains in right here."
Hog stood on the dirt, his leg still pressed against her unyielding cheek, as cold paralyzing terror seized his entire soul.
’Holding back...?’ Hog thought, his mind screaming in incomprehensible horror as sweat drenched his back. ’Holding what back?!’
He had kicked her with literally everything he possessed...
He had used his 10x stat buff, his full physical momentum, his maximum muscle output, and every drop of his rage...
It was a strike powerful enough to probably shatter a stone fortress wall.
...And she hadn’t even felt it?
Brida let out a deep boisterous laugh that echoed across the cratered battlefield like the ringing of a giant brass anvil.
She casually reached up with her broad gloved hand, wiping a smudge of dirt from her cheek right where Hog’s 10x-buffed steel-shod boot had struck her just a second prior.
She didn’t have a single scratch on her skin.
Her visor gleamed under the morning sun with her red eyes burning with a wild infectious thrill for battle.
"Gwahahaha!" Brida chuckled, rolling her broad shoulders as her iron boots shifted in the damp soil.
"Not bad, big guy!
Now... let’s have a true battle, Hog!"
Standing ten paces away, Hog felt the blood in his veins freeze into solid ice.
He stared at the six-foot-tall shieldmaiden with his single uninjured eye widened to the size of a saucer with his chest heaving as hot steam vented from his nostrils.
Cold terrifying sweat drenched his back beneath his iron chest plate.

’What in the hell...’ Hog thought, his mind spiraling in horror. ’What on earth did Lord Vespera feed this woman to the point where she can just casually ignore a full-power ten-fold stat-multiplied roundhouse kick directly to her face...’
It defied every single law of physical combat he had learned over a lifetime of fighting in the basin.
Even dragon-kin and armored raid bosses flinched when struck with that kind of concentrated force.
...However, Hog was an experienced squad leader.

He had survived dozens of brutal territory engagements under Lord Sky, and his pride as The Unmovable Wall’s strongest troop refused to let him accept the terrifying reality standing right before him.
’No...’ Hog reasoned frantically in his internal thoughts with his teeth grinding together so hard his jaw muscles throbbed. ’There is no way that hit was completely one-sided!
I felt it...
When my boot connected with her jaw, a sharp tingly vibration traveled all the way up my right fibula!
She definitely felt that pain!’
Hog took a slow deliberate breath, steadying his footing as he stared at Brida’s armored form.

’She’s acting,’ Hog convinced himself with his mind grasping at any logical explanation to keep his morale from completely shattering. ’She knows those floating streaming drones are tracking every single micro-movement... so she’s just putting on a tough unbothered front for the camera stream so she doesn’t embarrass her territory in front of a lot of viewers...
She’s holding back her grimace... she has to be!’
Brida didn’t care about the stream metrics, nor did she care about Hog’s desperate internal cope.
She raised her broad hands with her eyes locking onto his broad chest.
"Alright, Hog," Brida announced cheerfully.
"I’m moving."
Brida took a single deliberate stride forward.
She didn’t raise her battleaxe and she didn’t draw her shield or anything.
Brida didn’t even cock her fist back for a strike.
...Yet, the exact second her boot touched the dirt, a suffocating bloodthirsty wave of physical Murderous Intent erupted from her body like a physical wall of pressure.
FWOOSH!
The staggering weight of her aura distorted the atmospheric air pressure around Hog!
It felt as if a ten-ton iron slab had suddenly been dropped onto Hog’s shoulders.
His instincts... honed by years of life-or-death battles screamed in pure panic.
SWISH!
Before his brain could even process a logical thought, Hog’s body reacted purely on survival reflex.
He violently threw himself backward, executing a desperate high-speed dodge to the right with his boots scraping two deep trenches through the mud as he landed in a defensive crouch twenty feet away.
"Haah...
Haah...
Haah..."
He panted heavily with his hands raised and his eyes darting frantically to see where the incoming blow was coming from...
...Only to realize Brida hadn’t thrown a strike at all.
She was simply standing in the exact same spot with her arms hanging casually at her sides, looking at him with a wide disappointed grin.
"Pfft!
Hahaha!" Brida taunted, letting out a loud mocking scoff as she tilted her head.
"What’s the matter, big guy?
Are you scared already?
Is this really how men are in this world?
Jumping at shadows before a fist is even thrown?"
Behind her visor, Brida’s thoughts took a quiet deeply appreciative turn.

’Hah...’ Brida thought inwardly, an affectionate warmth touching her heart as a image of her Lord flashed through her mind. ’I am so bloody glad that the only man I ever have to belong to is my Lord Silas.
If I had to deal with skittish, weak-willed men like this every day, I’d have lost my mind weeks ago...’
Brida reached up to her chest plate, unbuckling the heavy leather straps securing her outer adamantine pauldrons.
CLANK!
She unceremoniously tossed the heavy iron pauldrons onto the grass.
She unfastened her armguards, her leg greaves, and finally reached up to the iron clasps at her neck, lifting her heavy helm completely off her head.
THUD!
She threw her helmet to the side, letting it crash into the dirt.
As the heavy steel helmet came off, a long cascading waterfall of luscious black hair tumbled down over her broad shoulders.
Her radiant sun-kissed skin, high cheekbones, and striking piercing eyes were revealed to the open air for the very first time on the global broadcast.
She was drop-dead breathtakingly gorgeous... a wild valkyrie-like beauty that radiated both terrifying physical power and undeniable feminine charm.

It was almost physically impossible to reconcile the fact that this stunning black-haired goddess was the exact same bloodthirsty monster who had spent the last twenty minutes boisterously laughing while pulverizing heavy armored guards into ragdolls.

chapters.title: Chapter 310: Phase One Is Over [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: There was a very specific reason why Hog... a standard territory troop without a Hero title had managed to rise from a basic guard to the supreme Troop Commander of The Unmovable Wall within less than two years of service under Lord Sky.
It was all because of his ancestral Family Secret Technique: Muscle Ignition...
By forcibly igniting and burning the high-density muscle tissue that made up their physical bodies, his bloodline could temporarily force their nervous systems into a state of ’Flow’!
Because the brain was forced to operate at maximum emergency thresholds to compensate for the rapid tissue burning, all mental limiters were completely shattered.
His neural reflexes, physical strength, and movement speed were boosted past human limits... boosting his core Strength and Speed stats by hundreds of points in game terms.
Standing in his wiry steam-emitting state, Hog’s mind entered a state of hyper-acute clarity.
He analyzed every single inch of Brida’s posture... her collarbone, her floating ribs, her liver, her solar plexus, and her temples.
STEP!

Hog took a sharp step back, venting another cloud of white steam, and launched a devastating lightning-fast combination of bare-knuckle strikes that completely threw caution, defense, and self-preservation to the wind.
BANG! BANG! BANG! BANG! BANG!
A rain of punches rained down upon Brida’s body.
Hog’s fists turned into continuous blinding blurs of blood-red mana.
He struck her jaw.
BANG!
Her ribs...
BANG!
Her solar plexus...
BANG!
Her throat and her temple in a fraction of a second.
BANG! BANG!
’BURN!’ Hog screamed frantically in his internal thoughts, burning more and more of his vital muscle tissue with every blow! ’BURN IT ALL! HIGHER OUTPUT! MORE SPEED! DESTROY HER!’
HISSSSSSS!
Thick clouds of burning steam and friction-heat erupted from his knuckles as he drove his entire body forward, coiling his right hip for the final devastating finisher.
"DIEEEE!" Hog bellowed at the top of his lungs!
BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
Hana’s final full-power straight punch slammed directly into the center of Brida’s stomach!
The resulting explosion was catastrophic as a fifty-foot shockwave of compressed air, shattered dirt, and red-hot energy erupted from the point of impact.
The wind pressure blasted outward across the clearing, violently throwing nearby wounded soldiers and debris flying through the air like dry leaves.
A thick opaque cloud of white steam and brown dust enveloped both combatants.
Hog staggered backward two paces with his chest heaving as he gasped for air.
"Hah... Hah... Hah..."
His wiry body was trembling violently, his arms completely drained of strength, and his skin covered in severe third-degree friction burns from his own technique.
His muscle mass had been burned down to thirty percent of its original volume.
He looked into the settling dust, a triumphant exhausted smirk spreading across his bleeding lips.

’There’s no way...’ Hog thought, his chest rising and falling as he wiped sweat from his eye. ’There is no physical way any human... any Hero... could survive that combination. Her internal organs have to be completely liquidized.’
Slowly... the thick steam and dust dispersed in the morning wind.
Hog’s triumphant smirk completely froze.
Standing in the exact same position she had been in when she took that single step backward... was Brida.
Her hair was completely untouched by the heat.
Her tunic was intact.
She stood with her arms hanging casually at her sides, looking down at her own stomach where Hog’s final fist had landed, then looked up at Hog with a thoughtful approving nod.
"Whew..." Brida remarked casually, her voice sounding completely relaxed and unbothered. "That was quite a very big combination!"
Brida reached down, gently patting the fabric over her stomach with her hand.
In her thoughts, Brida offered a quiet honest evaluation of the attack.

’Honestly...’ Brida thought inwardly, her eyes gleaming with genuine respect, ’...if I didn’t possess my passive [Unyielding Bedrock Body], those rapid strikes would have actually broken a couple of my ribs and bruised my liver. That technique of his is genuinely impressive for a guy like him.’
...But then again, she did possess [Unyielding Bedrock Body].
Her Vitality and adamantine bone density had absorbed ninety-nine percent of the force, rendering his burning muscle combination completely useless against her physical core.
So really, all Hog could blame was his own terrible luck for going up against a Grand Titan Bastion.
Brida looked at Hog’s wiry steam-emitting frame, deciding to offer him a polite genuine compliment for his effort.

"You know, Hog..." Brida spoke loudly, trying her best to sound encouraging and respectful, "...your martial skills are actually really impressive! Those punches felt pretty nice, even though I didn’t really feel much of them at all! And honestly, I think that new, skinny wiry figure of yours looks way better than that oversized ugly muscle-mass you were carrying around earlier!"
Hog stood on the grass with his eye staring at her in total silence.
Brida genuinely wasn’t trying to be disrespectful.
In her mind, she was offering him sincere praise for his technique and complimenting his streamlined body...

...But because she said it with such casual unbothered honesty after tanking his ultimate combination without a scratch, her words sounded like the most brutal soul-crushing and condescending insult in the entire history of the Sovereign Realm.
CRACK!
Hog’s teeth gritted together so hard that blood trickled from his gums.
A wave of pure suicidal rage consumed his mind as his single eye ignited with a blinding white glare and he threw away every last drop of his self-preservation.
"I’LL KILL YOUUUUUU!" Hog roared out, his voice sounding completely insane.
BOOM!
Hog burned the very last ten percent of his remaining muscle tissue, accelerating across the dirt at maximum speed for one final desperate execution strike.
...However, Brida was completely prepared this time.
She didn’t stand there casually to tank the blow.
Her red eyes narrowed into sharp deadly slits as she dropped her hips into a low stable stance.
HUMMMMMMM!
A dense suffocating aura of pitch-black mana erupted from Brida’s core, wrapping tightly around her right fist like a heavy iron gauntlet.
She drew her right hand back to her hip, her muscles coiling with terrifying concentrated power.
Hog, charging forward at high speed, saw her black-fisted stance and instantly understood the nature of this final clash.
This was no longer a prolonged brawl.
This was a speed race...
This was a raw contest of execution speed... whoever landed their fist first would claim the opponent’s life!
Hana drove his right fist forward with his knuckles aiming straight for Brida’s throat...
...However, right as Hog’s fist reached within three inches of her skin—
SWISH!
Brida’s body blurred.
Out of nowhere, Brida moved at a speed that was easily several times faster than her usual movement.
Her physical form vanished from Hog’s field of vision, leaving behind a dark shadow residual in the air.
STEP!
Before Hog could even process where she had gone, Brida materialized directly behind his back.
’I haven’t used Full Counter yet...’ Brida thought. ’This is the perfect opportunity!’

All of the immense kinetic force, muscle ignition energy, and shockwave pressure that Hog had driven into her body during his entire five-punch combination had been absorbed and stored deep within Brida’s adamantine bones.
And now... she was releasing fifty percent of that accumulated energy outward in a single point-blank strike.
Brida drove her black-mana-coated right fist straight into the center of Hog’s spine.
BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
A deafening concussive explosion erupted across the battlefield.
The incomprehensible force detonating from her fist didn’t just break bone... it completely pulverized physical matter.
Hog’s entire torso was instantly atomized into a blinding spray of red mist and shattered armor, the shockwave tearing a fifty-yard trench straight through the dirt behind him.
SWISH!
The red mist dispersed in the wind, leaving behind an empty cratered clearing.
Brida stood in the center of the crater, wiping her brow, and instead of feeling a single drop of remorse or sorrow for slaying the brave troop commander...
She threw her hands into the air and began hopping up and down on the grass like an excited child, shouting out with unbridled joy.
"FUCK YEAH! THAT felt amazing!"
Far across the field, on the high command deck of The Unmovable Wall...
Lord Sky stood frozen behind his disguise helmet with his throat thinning, his breath catching in his lungs as he watched Hog get atomized on his HUD interface.
"Dammit..." Sky cursed under his breath, his hands clenching into tight fists. "Hog... you fool..."
Sky reached for his comm-link, preparing to order the entire secondary legion of heavy knights to advance and lock down the frontline—
FWOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOSH!
Suddenly, a colossal hurricane-force gust of wind struck the front of The Unmovable Wall!
The sudden atmospheric shockwave was so violent that it blew away the surrounding smoke, dust, and fire, blinding Sky’s gun crews and forcing his guards to shield their eyes.
By the time the dust cleared and Sky reopened his visor...
It was already too late.
Hovering fifty feet directly in the air above the upper gun decks... was Fenna.
The master sniper was suspended mid-air against the blue sky, her traveler’s cloak fluttering wildly in the wind.
Held in her hands was her massive, dark star-iron composite longbow, drawn all the way back to her ear, notched with dozens of sleek black homing arrows!
Behind her, a glowing blue [Multi-Shot Volley] spell was active!
’I’m within the boundary...’ Fenna thought, her eyes completely calm and focused behind her hood.
Lord Silas had given her an explicit instruction before the battle had started... she wasn’t allowed to simply shoot down the heavy cannons from the safety of the Blessed Land’s walls.

She had to advance across the field, cross the minimum distance boundary of three hundred yards from the enemy hull, and execute the strike in close quarters to maximize engagement metrics for the stream.
And she had reached the boundary.
THWIP-THWIP-THWIP-THWIP!
Fenna released the string!

Dozens of sleek black homing arrows shot forward through the air in a synchronized fan-shaped salvo, screaming straight toward the thirty heavy mana cannons mounted along the mobile fortress’s lower hull.
Seeing the incoming dark salvo...
"DIVINE AEGIS DOME!" Sky’s elite Hero shield-user screamed out, stepping to the front railing and slamming her tower shield down.
A massive, semi-transparent pink energy barrier expanded over the lower gun decks, seeking to intercept the arrows.
...However, Fenna’s arrows weren’t standard projectiles.
Inscribed onto the steel tips of every single arrow were [Armor-Piercing Runes] forged personally by Grand Runemaster Rowenna!
CRACK! CRACK! CRACK!
The black arrows struck the pink barrier... and passed straight through the energy shield as if it were made of thin wet paper.
The armor-piercing runes completely bypassed fifty percent of the barrier’s energy density.
STAB! STAB! STAB!
All thirty black arrows embedded themselves directly into the breech chambers and mana-crystal loading arrays of the thirty heavy cannons!
An instant later...
BOOOOOOOOOOM! KABOOM! BOOOOOOOOM! BOOOOOOOOM!
A continuous chain explosion erupted across the entire lower hull of The Unmovable Wall!
All thirty heavy mana cannons exploded simultaneously.
Fireballs, melting steel, and detonating mana crystals tore through the lower gun ports, completely obliterating the mobile fortress’s primary siege artillery array in a single, magnificent inferno.
SWISH!
Fenna executed a breathtaking, flawless backward flip in mid-air, floating down from the sky like a leaf!
Gunnhild stepped forward below, catching Fenna smoothly in her arms.
Fenna adjusted her hood, looking over at Brida, and called out crisp orders.
"Mission accomplished! All cannons are destroyed! Let’s draw back!"
Brida, still grinning from her fistfight, nodded enthusiastically.
"Yeah! Let’s get out of here!"

Without wasting a single second, the forward strike team... Brida, Fenna, Gunnhild, Hilda, and Tasmin as well as Hilda turned on their heels, retreating across the field toward the open gates of the Blessed Land at high speed.
Brida’s armor as well as weapons floated through the air attaching themselves to her body making her smile.
Sky stood on his burning command deck, his face twisting in rage beneath his helmet.
"AFTER THEM!" Sky bellowed furiously into his comms. "DON’T LET THEM ESCAPE! ALL UNITS, PURSUE AND KILL—"
Before Sky’s surviving forces could even take three strides—
HUMMMMMMMMM!
High above the field, the divine mist covering the Blessed Land thinned down even further, pulling back to reveal the entire upper perimeter of the Steel-Weave walls.
Standing atop the obsidian battlements, line after line of archers, mages, and Magic Swordsmen led by Vala lowered their weapons, staring straight down at Sky’s army with cold intent.
Phase One was officially over.
The girls who had been waiting on the walls were finally making their move.
[Author’s Note]
I think that’s all the Bonus Chapters I’m owing you with one extra, Haah...

’BURN!’ Hog screamed frantically in his internal thoughts, burning more and more of his vital muscle tissue with every blow! ’BURN IT ALL!
HIGHER OUTPUT!
MORE SPEED!
DESTROY HER!’
HISSSSSSS!
Thick clouds of burning steam and friction-heat erupted from his knuckles as he drove his entire body forward, coiling his right hip for the final devastating finisher.
"DIEEEE!" Hog bellowed at the top of his lungs!
BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
Hana’s final full-power straight punch slammed directly into the center of Brida’s stomach!
The resulting explosion was catastrophic as a fifty-foot shockwave of compressed air, shattered dirt, and red-hot energy erupted from the point of impact.
The wind pressure blasted outward across the clearing, violently throwing nearby wounded soldiers and debris flying through the air like dry leaves.
A thick opaque cloud of white steam and brown dust enveloped both combatants.
Hog staggered backward two paces with his chest heaving as he gasped for air.
"Hah...
Hah...
Hah..."
His wiry body was trembling violently, his arms completely drained of strength, and his skin covered in severe third-degree friction burns from his own technique.
His muscle mass had been burned down to thirty percent of its original volume.
He looked into the settling dust, a triumphant exhausted smirk spreading across his bleeding lips.
’There’s no way...’ Hog thought, his chest rising and falling as he wiped sweat from his eye. ’There is no physical way any human... any Hero... could survive that combination.
Her internal organs have to be completely liquidized.’
Slowly... the thick steam and dust dispersed in the morning wind.
Hog’s triumphant smirk completely froze.
Standing in the exact same position she had been in when she took that single step backward... was Brida.
Her hair was completely untouched by the heat.
Her tunic was intact.
She stood with her arms hanging casually at her sides, looking down at her own stomach where Hog’s final fist had landed, then looked up at Hog with a thoughtful approving nod.
"Whew..." Brida remarked casually, her voice sounding completely relaxed and unbothered.
"That was quite a very big combination!"
Brida reached down, gently patting the fabric over her stomach with her hand.
In her thoughts, Brida offered a quiet honest evaluation of the attack.

’Honestly...’ Brida thought inwardly, her eyes gleaming with genuine respect, ’...if I didn’t possess my passive [Unyielding Bedrock Body], those rapid strikes would have actually broken a couple of my ribs and bruised my liver.
That technique of his is genuinely impressive for a guy like him.’
...But then again, she did possess [Unyielding Bedrock Body].
Her Vitality and adamantine bone density had absorbed ninety-nine percent of the force, rendering his burning muscle combination completely useless against her physical core.
So really, all Hog could blame was his own terrible luck for going up against a Grand Titan Bastion.
Brida looked at Hog’s wiry steam-emitting frame, deciding to offer him a polite genuine compliment for his effort.
"You know, Hog..." Brida spoke loudly, trying her best to sound encouraging and respectful, "...your martial skills are actually really impressive!
Those punches felt pretty nice, even though I didn’t really feel much of them at all!
And honestly, I think that new, skinny wiry figure of yours looks way better than that oversized ugly muscle-mass you were carrying around earlier!"
Hog stood on the grass with his eye staring at her in total silence.
Brida genuinely wasn’t trying to be disrespectful.
In her mind, she was offering him sincere praise for his technique and complimenting his streamlined body...

...But because she said it with such casual unbothered honesty after tanking his ultimate combination without a scratch, her words sounded like the most brutal soul-crushing and condescending insult in the entire history of the Sovereign Realm.
CRACK!
Hog’s teeth gritted together so hard that blood trickled from his gums.
A wave of pure suicidal rage consumed his mind as his single eye ignited with a blinding white glare and he threw away every last drop of his self-preservation.
"I’LL KILL YOUUUUUU!" Hog roared out, his voice sounding completely insane.
BOOM!
Hog burned the very last ten percent of his remaining muscle tissue, accelerating across the dirt at maximum speed for one final desperate execution strike.
...However, Brida was completely prepared this time.
She didn’t stand there casually to tank the blow.
Her red eyes narrowed into sharp deadly slits as she dropped her hips into a low stable stance.
HUMMMMMMM!
A dense suffocating aura of pitch-black mana erupted from Brida’s core, wrapping tightly around her right fist like a heavy iron gauntlet.
She drew her right hand back to her hip, her muscles coiling with terrifying concentrated power.
Hog, charging forward at high speed, saw her black-fisted stance and instantly understood the nature of this final clash.
This was no longer a prolonged brawl.
This was a speed race...
This was a raw contest of execution speed... whoever landed their fist first would claim the opponent’s life!
Hana drove his right fist forward with his knuckles aiming straight for Brida’s throat...
...However, right as Hog’s fist reached within three inches of her skin—
SWISH!
Brida’s body blurred.
Out of nowhere, Brida moved at a speed that was easily several times faster than her usual movement.
Her physical form vanished from Hog’s field of vision, leaving behind a dark shadow residual in the air.
STEP!
Before Hog could even process where she had gone, Brida materialized directly behind his back.
’I haven’t used Full Counter yet...’ Brida thought. ’This is the perfect opportunity!’

All of the immense kinetic force, muscle ignition energy, and shockwave pressure that Hog had driven into her body during his entire five-punch combination had been absorbed and stored deep within Brida’s adamantine bones.
And now... she was releasing fifty percent of that accumulated energy outward in a single point-blank strike.
Brida drove her black-mana-coated right fist straight into the center of Hog’s spine.
BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
A deafening concussive explosion erupted across the battlefield.
The incomprehensible force detonating from her fist didn’t just break bone... it completely pulverized physical matter.
Hog’s entire torso was instantly atomized into a blinding spray of red mist and shattered armor, the shockwave tearing a fifty-yard trench straight through the dirt behind him.
SWISH!
The red mist dispersed in the wind, leaving behind an empty cratered clearing.
Brida stood in the center of the crater, wiping her brow, and instead of feeling a single drop of remorse or sorrow for slaying the brave troop commander...
She threw her hands into the air and began hopping up and down on the grass like an excited child, shouting out with unbridled joy.
"FUCK YEAH!
THAT felt amazing!"
Far across the field, on the high command deck of The Unmovable Wall...
Lord Sky stood frozen behind his disguise helmet with his throat thinning, his breath catching in his lungs as he watched Hog get atomized on his HUD interface.
"Dammit..." Sky cursed under his breath, his hands clenching into tight fists.
"Hog... you fool..."
Sky reached for his comm-link, preparing to order the entire secondary legion of heavy knights to advance and lock down the frontline—
FWOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOSH!
Suddenly, a colossal hurricane-force gust of wind struck the front of The Unmovable Wall!
The sudden atmospheric shockwave was so violent that it blew away the surrounding smoke, dust, and fire, blinding Sky’s gun crews and forcing his guards to shield their eyes.
By the time the dust cleared and Sky reopened his visor...
It was already too late.
Hovering fifty feet directly in the air above the upper gun decks... was Fenna.
The master sniper was suspended mid-air against the blue sky, her traveler’s cloak fluttering wildly in the wind.
Held in her hands was her massive, dark star-iron composite longbow, drawn all the way back to her ear, notched with dozens of sleek black homing arrows!
Behind her, a glowing blue [Multi-Shot Volley] spell was active!
’I’m within the boundary...’ Fenna thought, her eyes completely calm and focused behind her hood.
Lord Silas had given her an explicit instruction before the battle had started... she wasn’t allowed to simply shoot down the heavy cannons from the safety of the Blessed Land’s walls.

She had to advance across the field, cross the minimum distance boundary of three hundred yards from the enemy hull, and execute the strike in close quarters to maximize engagement metrics for the stream.
And she had reached the boundary.
THWIP-THWIP-THWIP-THWIP!
Fenna released the string!

Dozens of sleek black homing arrows shot forward through the air in a synchronized fan-shaped salvo, screaming straight toward the thirty heavy mana cannons mounted along the mobile fortress’s lower hull.
Seeing the incoming dark salvo...
"DIVINE AEGIS DOME!" Sky’s elite Hero shield-user screamed out, stepping to the front railing and slamming her tower shield down.
A massive, semi-transparent pink energy barrier expanded over the lower gun decks, seeking to intercept the arrows.
...However, Fenna’s arrows weren’t standard projectiles.
Inscribed onto the steel tips of every single arrow were [Armor-Piercing Runes] forged personally by Grand Runemaster Rowenna!
CRACK!
CRACK!
CRACK!
The black arrows struck the pink barrier... and passed straight through the energy shield as if it were made of thin wet paper.
The armor-piercing runes completely bypassed fifty percent of the barrier’s energy density.
STAB!
STAB!
STAB!
All thirty black arrows embedded themselves directly into the breech chambers and mana-crystal loading arrays of the thirty heavy cannons!
An instant later...
BOOOOOOOOOOM!
KABOOM!
BOOOOOOOOM!
BOOOOOOOOM!
A continuous chain explosion erupted across the entire lower hull of The Unmovable Wall!
All thirty heavy mana cannons exploded simultaneously.
Fireballs, melting steel, and detonating mana crystals tore through the lower gun ports, completely obliterating the mobile fortress’s primary siege artillery array in a single, magnificent inferno.
SWISH!
Fenna executed a breathtaking, flawless backward flip in mid-air, floating down from the sky like a leaf!
Gunnhild stepped forward below, catching Fenna smoothly in her arms.
Fenna adjusted her hood, looking over at Brida, and called out crisp orders.
"Mission accomplished!
All cannons are destroyed!
Let’s draw back!"
Brida, still grinning from her fistfight, nodded enthusiastically.
"Yeah!
Let’s get out of here!"
Without wasting a single second, the forward strike team...
Brida, Fenna, Gunnhild, Hilda, and Tasmin as well as Hilda turned on their heels, retreating across the field toward the open gates of the Blessed Land at high speed.
Brida’s armor as well as weapons floated through the air attaching themselves to her body making her smile.
Sky stood on his burning command deck, his face twisting in rage beneath his helmet.
"AFTER THEM!" Sky bellowed furiously into his comms.
"DON’T LET THEM ESCAPE!
ALL UNITS, PURSUE AND KILL—"
Before Sky’s surviving forces could even take three strides—
HUMMMMMMMMM!
High above the field, the divine mist covering the Blessed Land thinned down even further, pulling back to reveal the entire upper perimeter of the Steel-Weave walls.
Standing atop the obsidian battlements, line after line of archers, mages, and Magic Swordsmen led by Vala lowered their weapons, staring straight down at Sky’s army with cold intent.
Phase One was officially over.
The girls who had been waiting on the walls were finally making their move.
[Author’s Note]
I think that’s all the Bonus Chapters I’m owing you with one extra, Haah...

chapters.title: Chapter 311: Phase Two Starts Now!
paragraphs: The deafening chain-reaction detonations of thirty heavy mana cannons tore through the lower hull of The Unmovable Wall, sending jagged shards of scorched steel, melting brass plating, and blinding plumes of black smoke boiling up into the morning sky.
The heat radiating off the burning gun ports rippled across the open battlefield in suffocating waves, turning the damp soil of the basin into a smoking, glass-strewn wasteland.
High atop the stone battlements of the Blessed Land’s perimeter wall, line after line of archers and mages watched the fiery spectacle with wide gleaming eyes.
Below on the clearing, through the thick haze of floating ash, they could see Brida, Fenna, Gunnhild, Hilda, and Tasmin executing a synchronized high-speed tactical retreat.

The five forward operatives were sprinting back across the scorched earth with effortless grace, completely unharmed, leaving behind a trail of atomized troops, broken spell arrays, and ruined siege artillery.
In that exact second, every single woman stationed on the battlements, inside the courtyard, and along the front gates realized the exact same thing.
Phase One was officially complete.
Which meant it was time for Phase Two.
From a strategic standpoint, Silas’s overall blueprint for this entire territory war was hilariously straightforward.
There were no overly complex forty-step maneuvers, no convoluted naval signals, and no tedious multi-day sieges.
Silas had reduced the entire conflict down to two simple sweeping phases.

Phase One was the blunt force disruption... sending some of the Vanguard’s heaviest hitters out to crush Sky’s forward momentum, destroy his primary artillery, and test the limits of his territory’s defenses.
Phase Two was the real objective.

Across the entire battlefield... whether they were standing on the high obsidian walls, running across the muddy grass, or riding atop giant spirit beasts... every single girl in the Blessed Land thought the exact same thought at the exact same time.
’It’s time to aura farm as much as humanly possible.’
That was the core of Phase Two. That was their next big thing to do.

This wasn’t just a battle for territory line boundary markers or structural integrity points... this was a global broadcast being transmitted live to hundreds of millions of viewers across the Sovereign Realm and Earth.

Silas had explicitly ordered them to maximize every second of camera time, look unfathomably cool, radiate terrifying dominance, and farm endless engagement metrics for their territory’s official brand.
HEAVE... CREAK!
The colossal iron-reinforced front gates of the Blessed Land swung wide open with a deep echoing groan of iron hinges.
Instantly, row upon row of heavily armored Shieldmaidens, frontline sword-sworn warriors, and guards stepped through the threshold onto the field.
Their boots struck the earth in unison with their heavy iron greaves creating a rhythm that sounded like a approaching thunderstorm.
High above the gates, perched at the very peak of the Tier 2 Reinforced Watchtower, Kaelia stood flanked by elite longbow archers.
While the archers beside her maintained rigid, deadly military posture with their composite bows notched and ready, Kaelia was practically vibrating with unbridled, giddy excitement.
Her bright eyes sparkled as she looked down at the massive army deploying below, her long ears twitching at every explosion.
However, unlike the archers who carried sleek star-iron longbows or magical staves, Kaelia was holding... a heavy, soot-stained cast-iron frying pan.
She had gripped the handle with both hands, holding the heavy kitchen utensil firmly against her chest like a divine artifact of war.

’If anything tries to fly up here and attack my Watchtower...’ Kaelia thought to herself, her mind racing with dead-serious calculations, ’...if an enemy spell projectile or a rogue flying beast comes close, I’ll just use my pan to bat it straight back down! I’ll smack it right out of the sky!’
She paused, looking down at the flat, heavy bottom of the cast-iron pan, then blinked her eyes in quiet hopeful contemplation.

’I mean... it would work, right?’ Kaelia reassured herself inwardly, nodding firmly. ’Thora forged this pan out of heavy alloy. It’s practically an unbreakable shield! If a dragon shoots fire, I’ll just swat the fireball back like a tennis ball!’
The archers standing beside her on the Watchtower shot her quick, side-eye glances of utter confusion, they could tell what she was thinking about but nobody dared question her logic.
She looked far too confident...
Down below, the girls who had been stationed along the high obsidian perimeter wall made their grand entry.
They didn’t waste time taking the stone staircases down to the courtyard.
Instead, the women stepped up onto the stone crenellations and threw themselves directly off the fifty-foot wall into open air.
FWOOSH! FWOOSH! FWOOSH!
In mid-fall, the women spread their arms wide.
The special cloaks and enchanted robes forged by Rowenna and Thora flared outward instantly, expanding like sleek aerodynamic wings.

The runic fabric caught the rising thermal currents generated by the burning cannons below, allowing the entire deployment of female warriors to glide down from the sky with breathtaking weightless elegance.
They descended upon the battlefield like a flock of deadly, beautiful Valkyries with their dark cloaks fluttering against the morning sky!
They touched down onto the trampled grass in perfect synchronized alignment.
They didn’t stumble neither did they slide at all.
They landed naturally on their boots, instantly fanning out into a textbook three-tiered battle array.
The heavy Shieldmaidens locked their iron tower shields flat up front, forming an impenetrable metallic wall.
Directly behind them stood the mages, their staves glowing with elemental energy.
And forming the rear anchor was the longbow archers, their composite bows drawn back in perfect formation.
Commanding the center of this newly deployed army was Morwenna.
The Dread Queen was riding atop Titan... the hulking Alpha Blessed Wolf of the Umbral Basin.
Morwenna sat tall in the saddle with her dark pirate coat swaying over her pristine uniform, her hand resting gracefully on the hilt of her curved Corsair.
As Titan took slow intimidating strides forward, Morwenna’s mind drifted to the interior Keep behind them.

’Unbelievable...’ Morwenna thought inwardly, her thoughts filled with sharp affectionate irritation. ’That overgrown green weed is still sitting inside the Keep, lounging on a velvet couch and sipping mana-tea while the rest of us are out here doing physical labor on camera.’
Morwenna shook her head in her thoughts, mildly disgusted by Eluned’s total lack of urgency.

’How can a Nature Goddess be so unfathomably lazy?’ Morwenna scoffed internally. ’She has lived for thousands of years, yet her primary goal in life seems to be finding new creative ways to lay her head on Lord Silas’s lap and nap for twelve hours straight. What an Insufferable creature...’
Putting the lazy goddess out of her mind, Morwenna re-focused her attention on the burning clearing ahead.
She nudged Titan’s flanks, riding the wolf to the front of the Vanguard line, stopping fifty yards ahead of the Shieldmaidens.
Far across the smoke-choked field, Lord Sky stood on the elevated command deck of The Unmovable Wall, staring at the deployed Blessed Land army through his disguise helmet’s optical zoom lenses.
Behind his silver-and-black streaming mask, Sky’s black eyes narrowed into sharp calculating slits.

At first glance, the army standing before him was remarkably small. Compared to the hundreds of heavy infantry, mercenary guilds, and secondary shock-troopers The Unmovable Wall possessed, Blessed Land’s deployment numbered only 70 or so women.
...However, as a veteran Classic Lord who had fought through dozens of territory wars, Sky knew better than anyone that raw troop numbers didn’t mean shit in the Sovereign Realm.
Every single woman standing in that formation radiated a cold, disciplined, and utterly terrifying pressure.
They weren’t panicking.
They weren’t sweating.

They stood amidst the burning wreckage of his artillery with the composure of seasoned conquerors and the pirate woman riding the golden wolf up front felt like a walking natural disaster waiting to detonate.
Morwenna raised her chin, her piercing gaze locking directly onto Sky’s masked face across the distance.
She drew her Corsair halfway from its scabbard, letting the steel blade click sharply against the iron guard.
Her voice, amplified by her internal mana pathways, boomed across the entire basin like a clear, melodic war horn.

"Hear me, Lord of the Moving Wall! Everything that your pathetic territory has faced up until this very second... our forward skirmishers, our archers, and our frontline shields was nothing more than a mere prelude!"
Morwenna paused, letting her words sink into the minds of the five hundred million viewers watching the stream.
"Now..." Morwenna declared with chilling conviction, "...you shall face the true, unbridled power of the Blessed Land! Prepare to be utterly overwhelmed!"
...However, despite her fierce, legendary declaration, a light pink blush touched Morwenna’s cheeks.
Behind her, the entire Vanguard army remained dead silent.
Not a single woman cheered... Not a single shield was banged as the silence was almost deafening.
Under normal circumstances, the women loved nothing more than letting out boisterous bloodthirsty battle cries before a charge.
But today... they were exercising extreme verbal restraint.
Morwenna understood completely, which was why her cheeks were slightly pink.
They were waiting.
Every single girl in the army was rigidly sticking to the script that Silas had made them memorize this morning.
The dramatic silence was a engineered pause... a theatrical cliffhanger designed to force Lord Sky into asking the exact question they needed him to ask.
As long as Sky asked the question... Phase Two could officially progress to its grand climax.
Sky stood on his command deck, looking at the silent army, then looking up at the high stone Watchtower.
The silence was creeping under his skin. He raised his broad sword, pointing it toward Morwenna, his audio transmitter projecting his loud commanding voice across the field.

"A dramatic speech, Pirate Queen!" Sky called out, trying to reclaim control of the broadcast narrative. "But where is your master?! Where is Lord Vespera?! Since this is supposed to be an official high-stakes Lord War with both sides giving their absolute all, your Lord ought to be standing out here on the field leading her people... unless, of course... she’s afraid to show her face—"
ROOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOAR!
Before Sky could even finish the word ’afraid’—
An earth-shattering apocalyptic sound erupted from deep within the misty perimeter of the Blessed Land.
It was a roar unlike anything anyone on that battlefield had ever heard in their lives.
It was deafening and immense, yet carried a smooth frequency that commanded unquestionable authority over all living creation.
The soundwave was so massive that the lingering smoke clouds over the basin were instantly blown apart, and the solid ground beneath thousands of soldiers violently vibrated.
Sky’s breath caught in his throat behind his helmet.
His battle instincts flared in pure terror, yet his mind couldn’t pinpoint what kind of creature could possibly produce a roar of that magnitude.
Hearing the roar, Morwenna’s light pink blush faded, replaced by a sharp triumphant grin.
She raised her naval saber, pointing the gleaming blade straight up into the sky, executing the exact final line of her script.
"My Lord?" Morwenna called out. "She has already arr—"
Morwenna intentionally paused right there, leaving her sentence incomplete.
It was totally fine that she didn’t finish her words, because that dramatic pause was also a calculated part of the script she had memorized.
BOOM!
Out from the divine, translucent mist of the Blessed Land, a colossal shadow broke through the cloud line.
A massive, majestic Crimson Dragon took to the sky.
FWOOSH!
Its gigantic, thirty-foot wingspan swept through the air, generating a massive downforce of wind that flattened the grass for hundreds of yards below.

Its scales were a deep, iridescent ruby-crimson that glinted like polished gemstones under the morning sun, and its long, serpentine body radiated an ancient, terrifying heat that evaporated the damp mist in seconds.
Across the global network, over FIVE HUNDRED MILLION viewers watching the stream simultaneously gasped in mind-boggling shock.
In tavern halls, corporate boardrooms, guild sanctuaries, and imperial palaces across the Sovereign Realm and Earth, every single person watching the stream stood up from their chairs.
Even the executives of the biggest mega-corporations in the world who monitored Lord War broadcasts to evaluate territory investments were completely frozen in disbelief.

In the Sovereign Realm, obtaining a loyal dragon unit of any color or rank was considered an almost impossible mythical feat that required decades of luck, fortunes in high-tier taming catalysts, and legendary Hero contracts.
...But not only did Lord Vespera possess a fully grown, perfectly loyal Dragon...
Anyone with high-tier beast-identification skills could see it instantly... this was no standard fire dragon or elemental wyrm!
This was a thought-to-be-extinct Primordial Crimson Dragon...
An ancient apex predator whose bloodline predated the very founding of the Sovereign Realm.
SWISH!
At that exact moment, Tasmin, Brida, Fenna, Gunnhild, and Hilda arrived back at the formation, taking their places alongside Morwenna.
High above, Talira began her descent.
[Author’s Note]
Sorry for no updates yesterday, once I finished those Chapters, I got really sick and had to go to the hospital but I’m good now.

Every single woman standing in that formation radiated a cold, disciplined, and utterly terrifying pressure.
They weren’t panicking.
They weren’t sweating.

They stood amidst the burning wreckage of his artillery with the composure of seasoned conquerors and the pirate woman riding the golden wolf up front felt like a walking natural disaster waiting to detonate.
Morwenna raised her chin, her piercing gaze locking directly onto Sky’s masked face across the distance.
She drew her Corsair halfway from its scabbard, letting the steel blade click sharply against the iron guard.
Her voice, amplified by her internal mana pathways, boomed across the entire basin like a clear, melodic war horn.
"Hear me, Lord of the Moving Wall!
Everything that your pathetic territory has faced up until this very second... our forward skirmishers, our archers, and our frontline shields was nothing more than a mere prelude!"
Morwenna paused, letting her words sink into the minds of the five hundred million viewers watching the stream.
"Now..." Morwenna declared with chilling conviction, "...you shall face the true, unbridled power of the Blessed Land!
Prepare to be utterly overwhelmed!"
...However, despite her fierce, legendary declaration, a light pink blush touched Morwenna’s cheeks.
Behind her, the entire Vanguard army remained dead silent.
Not a single woman cheered...
Not a single shield was banged as the silence was almost deafening.
Under normal circumstances, the women loved nothing more than letting out boisterous bloodthirsty battle cries before a charge.
But today... they were exercising extreme verbal restraint.
Morwenna understood completely, which was why her cheeks were slightly pink.
They were waiting.
Every single girl in the army was rigidly sticking to the script that Silas had made them memorize this morning.
The dramatic silence was a engineered pause... a theatrical cliffhanger designed to force Lord Sky into asking the exact question they needed him to ask.
As long as Sky asked the question...
Phase Two could officially progress to its grand climax.
Sky stood on his command deck, looking at the silent army, then looking up at the high stone Watchtower.
The silence was creeping under his skin.
He raised his broad sword, pointing it toward Morwenna, his audio transmitter projecting his loud commanding voice across the field.
"A dramatic speech, Pirate Queen!" Sky called out, trying to reclaim control of the broadcast narrative.
"But where is your master?!
Where is Lord Vespera?!

Since this is supposed to be an official high-stakes Lord War with both sides giving their absolute all, your Lord ought to be standing out here on the field leading her people... unless, of course... she’s afraid to show her face—"
ROOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOAR!
Before Sky could even finish the word ’afraid’—
An earth-shattering apocalyptic sound erupted from deep within the misty perimeter of the Blessed Land.
It was a roar unlike anything anyone on that battlefield had ever heard in their lives.
It was deafening and immense, yet carried a smooth frequency that commanded unquestionable authority over all living creation.
The soundwave was so massive that the lingering smoke clouds over the basin were instantly blown apart, and the solid ground beneath thousands of soldiers violently vibrated.
Sky’s breath caught in his throat behind his helmet.
His battle instincts flared in pure terror, yet his mind couldn’t pinpoint what kind of creature could possibly produce a roar of that magnitude.
Hearing the roar, Morwenna’s light pink blush faded, replaced by a sharp triumphant grin.
She raised her naval saber, pointing the gleaming blade straight up into the sky, executing the exact final line of her script.
"My Lord?" Morwenna called out.
"She has already arr—"
Morwenna intentionally paused right there, leaving her sentence incomplete.
It was totally fine that she didn’t finish her words, because that dramatic pause was also a calculated part of the script she had memorized.
BOOM!
Out from the divine, translucent mist of the Blessed Land, a colossal shadow broke through the cloud line.
A massive, majestic Crimson Dragon took to the sky.
FWOOSH!
Its gigantic, thirty-foot wingspan swept through the air, generating a massive downforce of wind that flattened the grass for hundreds of yards below.

Its scales were a deep, iridescent ruby-crimson that glinted like polished gemstones under the morning sun, and its long, serpentine body radiated an ancient, terrifying heat that evaporated the damp mist in seconds.
Across the global network, over FIVE HUNDRED MILLION viewers watching the stream simultaneously gasped in mind-boggling shock.
In tavern halls, corporate boardrooms, guild sanctuaries, and imperial palaces across the Sovereign Realm and Earth, every single person watching the stream stood up from their chairs.
Even the executives of the biggest mega-corporations in the world who monitored Lord War broadcasts to evaluate territory investments were completely frozen in disbelief.

In the Sovereign Realm, obtaining a loyal dragon unit of any color or rank was considered an almost impossible mythical feat that required decades of luck, fortunes in high-tier taming catalysts, and legendary Hero contracts.
...But not only did Lord Vespera possess a fully grown, perfectly loyal Dragon...
Anyone with high-tier beast-identification skills could see it instantly... this was no standard fire dragon or elemental wyrm!
This was a thought-to-be-extinct Primordial Crimson Dragon...
An ancient apex predator whose bloodline predated the very founding of the Sovereign Realm.
SWISH!
At that exact moment, Tasmin, Brida, Fenna, Gunnhild, and Hilda arrived back at the formation, taking their places alongside Morwenna.
High above, Talira began her descent.

chapters.title: Chapter 312: A Change Of Priorities
paragraphs: The colossal Crimson Dragon angled her wings, gliding down toward the front of the Vanguard line.
TAP!
Talira touched down onto the earth directly beside Morwenna.

Even though a creature of her massive physical weight should have created an earth-shattering impact crater, Talira skillfully concealed her landing kinetic force, sending only tiny, gentle tremors through the soil beneath her talons.
Standing proudly atop the dragon’s flat, broad head was Lord Vespera...
Vespera casually stepped off Talira’s snout, landing lightly on the grass.
She raised her gloved hand, gently patting the thick ruby-red scales on the side of Talira’s massive snout.
"Good girl, Talira," Silas praised softly with her voice calm and relaxed.
PURRRRR...

The moment Silas uttered those three words, the colossal, terrifying Primordial Dragon... an apex predator capable of leveling a lot of things let out a deep vibrating purr that sounded like a heavy engine.

Lord Sky, watching through his helmet’s optical lenses three hundred yards away, could have sworn on his life that he saw the giant dragon’s fierce, golden eyes light up with a bright undeniably happy glow, its red scales subtly flushing a lighter shade of crimson from the praise.
Vespera turned her head, stepping forward onto the grass to face Lord Sky.
She patted Talira’s massive flank once more.
"Well, Lord Sky..." Vespera greeted smoothly, her voice projecting clearly across the field. "It’s quite surprising that I pulled out a dragon right in front of your entire army, isn’t it?"
Sky stood on his command deck with his throat dry behind his mask.
He swallowed hard, forcing himself to maintain his composure for his stream audience, though his voice sounded strained.
"It is... extraordinarily surprising, Lord Vespera. I didn’t expect a brand-new territory to command a Primordial beast."
Vespera offered a subtle smirk beneath her hood, adjusting her cuffs.
"Well..." Vespera reminded him casually, "...we are currently at war, aren’t we? You shouldn’t expect your opponents to lay out all their cards beforehand."
Sky’s jaw clenched tightly beneath his full-face helmet.
Inside his mind, Sky felt a cold, paralyzing sense of dread settling into his chest.
He had not only been outdone in terms of frontline Hero strength... he had been outplayed, out-maneuvered, and completely out-staged on a global broadcast level!
His engagement metrics were plummeting while Blessed Land’s brand value was skyrocketing to unprecedented heights.
...But Sky was a veteran Classic Lord. He had built The Unmovable Wall from nothing through pure resilience.
He was NOT going to give up.
Sky raised his sword high into the air, his audio transmitter bellowing with fierce authority.
"ALL SURVIVING UNITS! FORM UP! CLERICS, ADVANCE TO THE FRONTLINE AND DISTRIBUTE HIGH-TIER REGENERATION SPELLS IMMEDIATELY! WE FIGHT TO THE VERY END!"
SHRRRRR!
Dozens of Sky’s high-tier Cleric combatants rushed forward from the secondary decks of the mobile fortress, casting wide-area healing circles over the wounded infantry and Hero officers on the field!

Sky turned his head toward the side railing, locking his eyes onto a short, stout female dwarven blacksmith clad in heavy, soot-stained leather aprons... Brenna, his territory’s smithy and beast keeper.
All of Sky’s hidden secondary Hero combatants were already assembling along the lower ramps, preparing to march onto the field for the final ground collision.
Sky looked at Brenna, his voice dropping into a hard, urgent command:
"It’s time, Brenna. Release the Wyverns!"
Brenna offered a firm, heavy nod.
"Understood, Lord Sky!"
Brenna reached into her belt, pulling out a heavy runic brass horn, and blew a sharp echoing signal into the air!
HOOOOORN!
GRAAHHH! RAHH! GRAAH!
From the massive, cavernous flight decks built into the upper rear hull of The Unmovable Wall, iron cage doors slammed open.
A flock of over thirty massive, dark-green Iron-Scale Wyverns erupted into the sky.
Their leather wings beat furiously against the wind as they took flight, their yellow eyes burning with mind-controlled aggression as they formed an aerial assault formation above Sky’s army.
Sky offered a sharp smirk behind his mask.
He didn’t expect thirty Wyverns to defeat a Primordial Crimson Dragon.

But at the very least, thirty aggressive, aerial beasts would serve as a massive airborne distraction... forcing the Crimson Dragon into a chaotic dogfight while his ground troops closed the gap to engage Silas’s small army.

Down on the grass, Silas stood beside Talira’s massive leg. He felt the shift in atmospheric pressure, looking up at the flock of thirty dark-green Wyverns screaming through the sky toward their position.𝓯𝓻𝓮𝙚𝙬𝓮𝙗𝒏𝙤𝒗𝙚𝙡.𝒄𝒐𝓶
Silas reached out, gently patting Talira’s warm scale-covered flank.

He noticed that Talira’s golden eyes were locked onto the flying Wyverns, her long tail swaying slightly against the grass with her nostrils venting tiny sparks of irritation at the lesser reptilian creatures daring to screech in her presence.
Silas offered a soft, amused chuckle.
"Go ahead, Talira. You have permission to deal with them."
HUMMMMMMM!
The exact second Silas gave the command—
Talira’s massive ruby wings spread wide!
FWOOSH!
She shot straight up into the heavens like a crimson rocket.
The launch velocity generated a kinetic shockwave that blasted the grass flat for fifty yards around her takeoff point!
Hovering high above the clouds, the flock of thirty Iron-Scale Wyverns saw the single Crimson Dragon ascending toward them.
Mind-controlled by Brenna’s runic horn, the Wyverns let out bloodthirsty screeches, diving straight toward Talira from all directions with open jaws and venomous talons.
Talira looked at the thirty diving Wyverns, her golden dragon eyes narrowing into razor-sharp contemptuous slits.
"Try it, lesser worms," Talira’s dragon voice echoed through the atmosphere.
Talira didn’t even bother opening her massive jaws to unleash a traditional dragon fire-breath.
She simply raised her long, elegant head toward the sky, channeling a tiny fraction of her ancient magic into her horn crest.
HUMMMMMMMMMMMMMMM!
A blinding, incandescent sphere of pure, high-density White Lightning ignited atop Talira’s central horn!
BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
A single, colossal bolt of blinding white lightning... over thirty feet wide erupted from her horn, splitting the sky in two.
The divine white lightning didn’t just strike one target...
It branched out across the upper atmosphere in a terrifying, web-like electrical cascade, striking all thirty Iron-Scale Wyverns simultaneously in a fraction of a second.
HISSSSSSS... FLASH!
There were no bloody corpses falling from the sky and there were no severed wings.
The moment the white lightning touched the thirty Wyverns, their physical bodies, iron scales, bones, and blood were instantly vaporized into nothingness.
All thirty Wyverns ceased to exist in a single silent flash of blinding white light, leaving behind only a drifting cloud of harmless ozone ash in the upper atmosphere.
The entire sky was left completely, pristine clean.
Talira hovered gracefully against the blue clouds with her ruby wings beating slowly, her golden eyes looking around the empty ash-filled air.
She let out a quiet, bored dragon huff through her nostrils, her internal voice ringing with pure disappointment.
’This is light work...’ Talira thought to herself, floating weightlessly in the empty sky. ’...Is this pathetic trash really what I did all of that grueling training for?’
Inside an ultra-exclusive, top-floor suite located in the most prestigious residential district of the capital, Elora sat gracefully at a wide, polished obsidian dining table.

The private room was a masterpiece of imperial luxury... high vaulted ceilings adorned with glowing mana-crystal chandeliers, plush velvet drapery trailing down floor-to-ceiling panoramic windows, and rare elemental orchids blooming softly in silver vases along the walls.
Floating directly above the center of her table was a crystal-clear, high-definition holographic projection of the global LordTube stream.

The golden broadcast display flickered, showing the grand, breathtaking scene taking place thousands of leagues away in the Umbral Basin... the massive, ruby-red scales of the Primordial Crimson Dragon glistening under the morning sun, its thirty-foot wingspan fanning the air as it stood proudly beside a dark-hooded figure.
For the first time in as long as she could remember, Elora’s usually emotionless, porcelain-like face fractured into a visible expression of genuine shock.
Her cool distant gaze widened slightly, her delicate fingers pausing mid-air where she had been holding a crystal glass of chilled fruit nectar.
"A Dragon... huh?" Elora murmured softly to herself, her melodic voice echoing through the silent room.
Elora leaned back slightly in her plush leather chair, her sharp analytical mind immediately spinning through her extensive mental archives.
She remembered seeing a dragon before... or rather, she remembered seeing the terrifying, colossal remains of one.
Back during the high-stakes expedition into the ancient Secret Realm, it had erupted from the ground.
But that had been nothing more than ancient calcified bone... a relic of an era long forgotten, not to mention that it had been rotting and turned to dust almost immediately.
There was absolutely no guarantee that the creature standing live on her holographic screen was of the same species or bloodline.
After all, when that ancient skeleton had erupted from the earth at that time, there hadn’t been a single living dragon anywhere near the site.

Elora shifted her posture, resting her chin lightly on her knuckles as she narrowed her eyes, focusing her attention away from the Primordial Crimson Dragon and locking onto the slender figure standing calmly beside its massive snout.
The mysterious Lord of the Blessed Land... Lord Vespera.
Elora zoomed in on the holographic projection, scrutinizing every single pixel of Vespera’s posture, dark robes, and aura.
A quiet calculating thought surfaced in her mind.
’It couldn’t possibly be Silas anymore...’ Elora thought, analyzing the physical height, the relaxed feeling, and the overwhelming authority radiating off Vespera’s frame.
Of course, a rational part of her brain reminded her that high-tier spatial disguise artifacts were capable of completely masking a person’s voice, height, gender, and mana signature.
Vespera could very easily be wearing an elaborate top-tier spatial disguise... so she couldn’t definitively rule out the possibility with one hundred percent certainty.

However, looking at the breathtaking historical display on the stream... a Lord who commanded a Primordial Crimson Dragon and an army of elite, invincible female warriors... Elora felt a sudden, profound shift in her personal priorities.
’What a waste of time...’
Until today, Elora had been subtly entertaining the idea of pursuing a romantic relationship with Silas Graves since she assumed that he was the Lord of Blessed Land.
But looking at the floating golden screen now, a cool decisive smile touched her lips.
Silas was interesting, sure... but Lord Vespera was a titan who was currently rewriting the geopolitical landscape of the Sovereign Realm on a global broadcast.

’Forget Silas,’ Elora concluded in her mind, her eyes glinting with sharp ambitious conviction. ’My intentions are changing. The main purpose was that I thought he was the Lord Of Blessed Land, now I have no reason to think of this anymore...’
A soft, quiet sigh escaped her lips as she recalled her recent actions.
She remembered spending a staggering eight million spirit credits just to purchase a custom vehicle for Silas as a casual gesture of goodwill.
She shook her head gently with her expression relaxing into complete indifference.
’Ah, well... eight million credits,’ Elora thought, dismissing the thought entirely. ’It doesn’t matter. That was barely a microscopic dent in my personal savings account anyway.’
Elora raised two slender fingers, snapping them lightly in the quiet air of her suite.
SNAP!
A side door swung open instantly, and a young maid dressed in a crisp, black-and-white uniform rushed into the dining room.
The maid bowed deeply, her forehead nearly touching the polished marble floor.
"You called for me, Lady Elora?" the maid asked respectfully, her voice trembling slightly under her mistress’s intense presence.
Elora didn’t even turn her head, her eyes remaining fixed on the glowing holographic projection of Vespera and the dragon.

"Compile every single piece of information available across the global networks, imperial registries, and private intelligence guilds regarding Lord Vespera," Elora commanded smoothly, her tone leaving zero room for argument. "I want a complete, comprehensive dossier by tonight. Cross-reference her public movements and compile a detailed list of every single possible identity she might be hiding behind."
The maid raised her head slightly with her lips parting as she tried to speak.
"Lady Elora, the magistrate’s council has already placed a strict informational blackout on the Umbral Basin due to the live broadcast, so gathering private—"
Before the maid could finish her sentence, Elora raised her hand, interrupting her mid-word with a single cold glance.
"I did not ask for an explanation of the difficulties," Elora spoke quietly, her voice dropping into a chilling authoritative tone. "I gave you a command. Go."
The maid’s face turned ghostly white.
She bowed frantically, stepping backward three paces before turning on her heel and sprinting out of the suite at top speed to execute the order.

The maid’s face turned ghostly white.
She bowed frantically, stepping backward three paces before turning on her heel and sprinting out of the suite at top speed to execute the order.

chapters.title: Chapter 313: Thor’s Realization
paragraphs: Left alone in the quiet luxury of her private dining suite, Elora raised her crystal glass, taking a slow elegant sip of her chilled fruit nectar while staring at Vespera’s hooded silhouette on the screen.
A smooth scheming smile spread across her flawless face.
’So now...’ Elora thought, her mind already drafting long-term political maneuvers, ’...how exactly do I arrange our very first private meeting?’
Meanwhile, miles away in the ultra-luxurious, six-star private dining pavilion suspended above the neon-lit skyline of Rhyx City...
CHOMP! CRUNCH! GLUB! GLUB! GLUB!
The boisterous, thunderous sounds of slaughter echoed off the gold-leaf walls of the dining suite.
Thor was currently sitting slumped in her massive gilded mahogany chair, single-handedly devouring her fourth entire mountain serving of legendary culinary dishes.
Her broad muscled arms were covered in savory glazes, her wild blonde hair falling over her shoulders as she tore through a four-foot roasted manticore leg with her bare teeth.

She swallowed a three-pound chunk of roasted meat whole, grabbed a giant silver pitcher of dwarf-mead, and chugged the entire gallon down her throat in five seconds flat, letting golden foam spill over her singlet and dark trousers.

"GWAHAHAHA!" Thor laughed boisterously, slamming the empty silver pitcher flat onto the marble tabletop with enough force to make the crystal chandeliers above rattle violently! "Good! GOOD! Bring more!"

Seated beside her in an opulent velvet chair, the royal-blue-haired Princess of the Lord World covered her smiling lips with her delicate silk-embroidered fan, her azure eyes watching the broadcast on the maximized golden holographic wall screen.

"I must admit, Lady Thor..." the Princess remarked smoothly, her voice carrying elegance. "...looking at the battlefield layout now, the Blessed Land truly does not possess many warriors at all. Aside from their Lord and that dragon, their ground deployment barely numbers seventy or eighty women, while Lord Sky commands over two hundred troops."
Thor wiped her greasy mouth with the back of her broad forearm, letting out a loud dismissive scoff as she looked at the floating screen.

"Bah! You speak like a pampered imperial politician who has never held an axe in her life, Princess!" Thor declared bluntly, slamming her calloused fist flat against her thigh. "In a real war, the number of useless bodies standing on a field does not matter for a damn thing! Look at those women! Look at how they move!"
Thor leaned forward in her chair, her storm-blue eyes narrowing into those of an ancient battle-hardened Norse God of Thunder.

"They have quality!" Thor boomed out, pointing a thick, meat-stained finger toward the screen where Brida, Tasmin, and Morwenna stood in formation. "They have incredible, top-tier, god-like quality... Every single one of those lasses moves like a seasoned Valhalla warrior who has bled through a thousand battles! Seeing an army like that... it makes me respect this Vespera even more!"
Thor turned her broad head toward the line of bowing, sweating imperial butlers waiting by the double oak doors, shouting at the top of her lungs.
"HEY! BUTLERS! BRING ME A FIFTH SERVING! I NEED TEN MORE ROASTED BOARS AND ANOTHER BARREL OF MEAD RIGHT NOW!"
The butlers bowed in terror, running off to the imperial kitchens at top speed to fulfill her absurd order.

Thor turned her attention back to the massive holographic display, her storm-blue eyes locking onto the colossal Primordial Crimson Dragon... Talira hovering gracefully above the Blessed Land’s vanguard.
Thor squinted her eyes, a rare look of deep nostalgia touching her broad features.
"Hmph..." Thor grumbled softly in her throat. "It has been quite a long time since I last saw a real Dragon with my own eyes... especially a pure-blooded Crimson one."
The Princess raised her blue eyebrows, leaning slightly closer to Thor. "Are Crimson Dragons truly that rare in the higher realms?"
"Rare?" Thor laughed heartlessly. "There are only a tiny handful of true Crimson Dragons left alive throughout the entire cosmos! In the whole Sovereign Realm, you could count them on one hand!"
Thor reached up, scratching her thick blonde hair as she recalled ancient realm history.

"I personally knew one of the legendary Crimson Dragon Kings back during the Great Realm Wars..." Thor reminisced. "An absolute monster of a dragon. But she was eventually hunted down and slain by that insufferable bastard, Ititius, centuries ago. I don’t know if that old dragon had a daughter or an heir before she died... but seeing this one floating on that screen brings back old memories."
Thor grinned widely, her storm-blue eyes flashing with intense battle-hungry curiosity.

"By Odin’s beard..." Thor declared loudly, "I would love to personally visit this Blessed Land territory after this war is over! I want to challenge that dragon to a strength contest and drink mead with their Lord!"
Thor turned her head, looking straight at the royal-blue-haired Princess. "Where is this territory located on the map anyway? What is the regional name?"
The Princess opened her silk fan, consulting a glowing blue imperial map floating beside her armrest.
"According to the official LordTube registry data..." the Princess answered smoothly, "...the Blessed Land is situated in a neutral, unregistered border territory known as the Umbral Basin."
The second the words ’Umbral Basin’ left the Princess’s lips, Thor froze completely solid.
Her storm-blue eyes blinked once then twice.
"Umbral Basin...?" Thor repeated, her voice dropping its boisterous tone.
Hadn’t she heard that name somewhere before?
BOOM!
Without warning, Thor slammed her broad, heavy palm flat onto the marble dining table!
The staggering force of her physical impact caused the entire six-star pavilion to shake violently.

The crystal glasses shattered, the silver platters bounced three feet into the air, and the returning imperial butlers carrying her fifth serving flinched in horrified panic, nearly dropping their trays.
"MY GOODNESS!" the Princess gasped out, her delicate silk fan fluttering frantically as she shielded her face from the shaking table. "Lady Thor! What has gotten into you?!"
Thor didn’t even apologize.
Her mind was racing as she recalled the secret dimensional charts kept inside the Royal Archive of Valhalla back in Asgard.

She remembered where she had heard that name... The Umbral Basin wasn’t just a random backwater wilderness in the Sovereign Realm... it was one of the primary, ancient spatial nexus points where a forgotten Gate of Asgard hung suspended in the upper atmosphere above the basin.
Thor kept her mouth shut, suppressing the urge to blurt out divine realm secrets in front of imperial royalty.
She quickly smoothed her expression back into a boisterous grin, waving her hand dismissively at the sweating butlers.
"Gwahahaha! My apologies, Princess!" Thor laughed loudly, grabbing a fresh roast leg off the new tray. "Just remembered an old errand! I’ll have to do some private research on that basin later!"
The royal-blue-haired Princess narrowed her azure eyes, offering Thor a sharp, playful smile. She leaned forward, resting her chin on her fan:

"If your private research proves fruitful... and if you truly intend to travel to this Umbral Basin after the war... could you perhaps carry me along with you, Lady Thor? I am thoroughly fascinated by this Lord Vespera as well."
Thor immediately shook her head, taking a massive bite of roast meat:
"Bah! No chance, Princess! I am a God of Thunder, not an imperial taxi driver! I travel fast and hard... a delicate royal girl like you would get blown away by my flight currents!"
The Princess didn’t get offended. Instead, a serene amused smile spread across her porcelain face. She raised her ringed hand, snapping her fingers lightly toward the head butler.
"Bring out the Imperial Chef’s special." the Princess commanded smoothly.
CLICK!
The double doors opened once more, and four master butlers marched in, carrying a colossal gold-plated serving platter covered by a massive, jewel-encrusted silver dome!
When the dome was lifted, an aroma so intoxicatingly divine erupted into the pavilion air that Thor’s jaw literally dropped open!

Piled high on the golden platter were prime cuts of roasted Astral Kraken heart, glazed in thousand-year-old divine honey, garnished with glowing mana-truffles, and accompanied by a crystal decanter of legendary Imperial Ambrosia... a legendary, stat-boosting feast worth over fifty million spirit credits.
Thor’s mouth instantly watered like a cascading waterfall... Her storm-blue eyes widened to the size of saucers as she stared at the glowing food.
She slowly turned her head, looking at the smiling, royal-blue-haired Princess with a narrow suspicious glare.
"Hey... Princess... is this... is this a blatant bribe?"
The Princess covered her mouth with her fan, her azure eyes sparkling with refined playfulness.
"It is a shameless bribe, Lady Thor."
Thor stared at the golden platter of Astral Kraken heart for two full seconds... then let out a roaring, thunderous laugh that shook the room.
"GWAHAHAHA!" Thor bellowed in delight, snatching the entire golden platter with both hands! "WELL SAID! I ACCEPT YOUR BRIBE, PRINCESS! YOU’VE GOT A RIDE TO THE UMBRAL BASIN!"
Thor crammed a massive piece of golden-glazed kraken heart into her mouth, chewing violently, her storm-blue eyes locking onto the holographic screen as the battlefield below ignited.
"ALRIGHT!" Thor cheered, wiping golden honey from her chin. "SHOW ME MORE!"
Back on the smoke-choked clearing of the Umbral Basin...

Lord Sky stood on the elevated command deck of The Unmovable Wall, staring across the three-hundred-yard gap at the majestic Primordial Crimson Dragon... Talira and the dark-hooded figure of Warlord Vespera standing on the grass below.
Sky let out a deep, heavy, and exhausted sigh behind his silver-and-black streaming helmet.
Cold sweat poured down his neck beneath his clothes.

The sight of a thought-to-be-extinct Primordial Crimson Dragon effortlessly vaporizing thirty Iron-Scale Wyverns with a single bolt of divine white lightning was enough to make any Lord’s heart throb in pure, unadulterated terror.
...However, Sky was a veteran Classic Lord.
He took a slow, steadying breath, analyzing his internal HUD interface.

Even though Brida’s supersonic charge had dismantled his frontline heavy knights, and even though Tasmin had defeated his twin Light Specialists, The Unmovable Wall was still a massive, well-established mobile territory.
He had a lot more than two hundred total troops remaining in his territory ranks... he still possessed over two hundred and twenty elite, battle-ready troops, mages, and heroes ready for deployment.
’A Dragon...?’ Sky thought, his heart hammering against his ribs like a trapped bird. ’Seriously...? How does a brand-new, unregistered Lord even acquire a Primordial Dragon?!’
TAP!
Suddenly, a heavy, reassuring hand rested firmly onto Sky’s shoulder.
Sky turned his masked head. Standing beside him was Hiro... his most trusted, highest-ranking Hero.
Hiro wore a clean white martial tunic, his long dark hair swaying in the wind, and a thick, dark-purple silk blindfold bound tightly over his eyes.
Despite being completely blindfolded, Hiro’s physical posture radiated an unshakeable aura of calm and sword mastery.

"Do not lose your focus, Lord Sky," Hiro spoke smoothly. "A dragon is a formidable beast, but it is still a creature of blood and bone... We have bled together in worse zones than this. We will win this war."
Beside Hiro, another elite Hero stepped forward to the railing... the tall woman clad in pink-tinted tower armor who held the massive Divine Aegis Shield.
She offered Sky a warm determined smile through her open visor, resting her hand flat against her chest plate.
"I will put in every single drop of my physical effort, Lord Sky! My barriers will shield our army from the dragon’s lightning until our blades reach their Lord’s neck!"
THUMP... THUMP...
Deep within the subterranean foundation of The Unmovable Wall, Elm’s [Four-Leaf Resonance] magic throbbed softly through the iron hull.
The gentle, silver-and-white clover aura washed over Sky’s body once more, providing a warm spiritual wave of quiet reassurance from his bedridden Hero down in the green nutrient tank.
Sky looked at his Hero officers, his heart swelling with immense overwhelming gratitude behind the disguise.

’Thanks, guys...’ Sky resolved in her internal thoughts, her black eyes sharpening into razor-sharp slits beneath the helmet. ’I want to win... and to win this war, I have to go all out with everything our home possesses!’
Sky took three slow deliberate steps forward to the very front edge of his command deck, looking down at Vespera standing in the distance.
"Lord Vespera!" Sky bellowed, his voice amplified by his helmet’s audio transmitter, projecting across the entire basin. "I thank you for personally stepping onto this field! But this war ends NOW!"
Sky raised his right hand high into the sky, pointing his gloved palm toward the morning sun.
Every drop of his mana ignited within his core.
"ILLUMINATE!" Sky roared at the top of his lungs.
BLAWFFFFFFFFFFFFF!
A blinding nuclear flare of pure intense white light erupted from Sky’s hand, shooting straight up into the atmosphere.
