chapters.title: Chapter 314: Blow...
paragraphs: The light didn’t just illuminate the sky... it expanded instantaneously, turning the vision of every single person, dragon, and streaming drone on the battlefield into a solid sheet of pure white.
Down on the grass, Vespera raised her gloved hand to her hood with her vision completely blinded by the white flare.
"Haah~"
Vespera let out a soft exasperated sigh beneath her breath.
’What’s this guy trying to do now?’ Vespera thought, mildly annoyed by the endless succession of flashy spell activations.
Three seconds passed.
HISSSSSSS...
The blinding white light slowly died down, fading back into the natural morning wind...
...Revealing a terrifying radical transformation of the entire battlefield terrain.

Carved deep into the earth across the entire three-thousand-yard width of the clearing... stretching from the base of The Unmovable Wall all the way to the outer perimeter of the Blessed Land’s walls were thousands of glowing dark-purple runic arrays.
’Oh Rowenna did say this was going to happen, I was wonderi—’
HUMMMMMMMMMMMMMMM!
The second the white light cleared, the thousands of purple runes ignited simultaneously.
BOOM!
The ambient temperature inside the runic field skyrocketed instantly to over two hundred degrees Fahrenheit.
Simultaneously, a crushing suffocating Gravity Domain Field activated across the entire clearing.
The atmospheric gravity multiplied by fifty times its natural one.
The air became so heavy that the very grass was flattened flat against the soil, and small pebbles were crushed into fine powder under the sheer, downward gravitational pressure.
’I still wonder, is this fucker trying to kill us?’
The entire battlefield including The Unmovable Wall itself was completely trapped inside this superheated, fifty-times gravity field.
Twenty times was one way but fifty times? What was he, a Saiyan?
...However, noticeably, the remaining two hundred plus soldiers, Hero combatants, and heavy knights of The Unmovable Wall were completely 100% unharmed by the intense gravity.
Inscribed onto the leather vambraces and armor plates of every single soldier in Sky’s army were pre-crafted [Counter-Gravity Alignment Runes] forged by Brenna.
The counter-runes completely neutralized the downward gravitational pull for Sky’s forces, allowing them to move with total, unhindered freedom.
Sky drew his broad steel sword, pointing the gleaming blade straight toward Vespera and the Blessed Land’s Vanguard.
"ALL UNITS!" Sky bellowed furiously! "REGULAR WARRIORS! HEROES! EVERYONE! CHARGE AND ASSASSINATE THEIR LORD!"
"ROAAAAAAAR!"

With an earth-shattering, bloodthirsty battle cry, all two hundred plus supercharged, 10x-buffed soldiers, heavy knights, and Heroes of The Unmovable Wall erupted forward into a full-scale all-out charge,
They sprinted across the runic field at high speeds with their blades raised, seeking to crush the enemy while they were pinned down by fifty-times gravity.
Sky offered a confident, triumphant smirk behind his mask.
By pinning the Blessed Land’s small, seventy-person army beneath a massive gravity field, their speed-type heroes like Tasmin and heavy shieldmaidens like Brida would be completely immobilized.
...However, down on the grass...
Vespera stood beside Talira’s massive crimson leg, looking at the two hundred plus charging soldiers rushing toward them.
A calm amused smile touched Vespera’s lips beneath her dark hood.
She turned her head slightly, looking back at Morwenna, Brida, Tasmin, Fenna, and the other women standing in formation behind her.
"Go crazy," Vespera commanded softly.
SWISH! SWISH! SWISH! SWISH!
The exact second the command left his lips—
All the women of the Blessed Land exploded forward into a full-speed counter-charge.
They sprinted straight past Vespera and Talira with their boots tearing through the soil, moving with speed that created shockwaves.
Far across the field, Lord Sky, Hiro, and the entire charging army of The Unmovable Wall completely froze in horror.
’Wh–what the hell is going on here? Isn’t the gravity working?’
Their forward momentum faltered with their eyes widening in utter disbelief behind their visors.
How on earth were they moving at full speed inside a fifty-times gravity field?!
What Sky didn’t know... was that Vespera was a master of battlefield intelligence.
Days before this official Lord War had ever started, Silas had utilized Rowenna’s invisible [Listening Runes] to monitor Sky’s private command deck.
Silas had overheard Sky’s entire discussion regarding the deployment of the purple Gravity Runic Field.
In response, Silas had instructed Runemaster Rowenna to forge custom [Anti-Gravity Wristbands] for every single one of the seventy-plus women.

The dark-purple runic wristbands wrapped around their forearms completely inverted the downward fifty-times gravitational force, converting the environmental pressure into a massive speed boost that doubled their movement velocity.
’Though we’ll have to take out the gravity in a bit...’
BOOOOOOOOOOM!
The two armies converged on the central clearing like two colliding tectonic plates.
They would soon be colliding, Vespera was sure of it however the plan for the gravity would have to be executed before anything.
Standing amidst the roaring battlefield, Vespera took a calm deliberate step forward, gently placing her gloved right hand flat against Talira’s massive crimson flank.
"Talira..." Vespera spoke softly.
Talira... hovering slightly above the grass in her colossal dragon form slowly lowered her massive head.
Her golden dragon eyes widened, staring down at her Lord with deep reverence.
Hearing her gentle voice, a sudden breath-catching thought echoed inside Talira’s head.
’Does... does My Lord want me...’ Talira thought, her golden eyes sparkling with overwhelming ecstatic joy, ’...to join the battle as well?’
Vespera looked up at the towering beast and gave her a single firm nod of approval.
’Of course I do want you to participate...’

Talira could of course go in her dragon form but Vespera had mainly asked her to pull up in it so they could farm aura, there was nothing too serious about it... they had been training these past few days and she deserved to have a break.
’Besides, she was very giddy to face strong people.’ Vespera thought, while she wasn’t sure if there was anyone that strong here, it wouldn’t hurt to try.
HUMMMMMMM!
The exact second the permission was granted, Talira’s massive, ruby-red dragon form erupted in a blinding incandescent pillar of pure white lightning and crimson elemental mana.
The atmospheric pressure blew away the surrounding ash and dirt for forty yards, sending violent shockwaves rippling across the clearing.
SWRRRRH!
Inside the towering pillar of divine lightning, Talira’s massive dragon vessel rapidly density-condensed.
Her wings folded inward, her massive tail shrank, and her reptilian mass morphed smoothly back into her Human Form.
When the blinding light faded, Talira stood on the grass as a fierce, drop-dead gorgeous dragon-girl.

She possessed long, cascading ruby-red hair that reached down to her waist, two polished, iridescent black dragon horns curving proudly from her temples, glowing eyes with vertical reptilian slits, and a long scale-armored crimson tail that swished rhythmically behind her boots.

She was clad in custom high-tier Blessed Land armor... lightweight adamantine shoulder plates, runic arm vambraces, protective gauntlets, and a sleek scale-armored tail guard forged personally by Thora.
BOOM!
Without saying a single word, Talira planted her boots into the earth and shot forward into the battlefield like a missile.

The launch velocity of her departure generated an explosive gust of atmospheric wind that swept across the grass, violently kicking up the hem of Vespera’s dark cloak and blowing her spatial hood straight back off her head.
SWISH.
Vespera reached up with a gloved hand, catching the edge of her hood and smoothly pulling it back down over her violet eyes.
Standing directly beside her, Morwenna did not charge forward alongside the other women or Talira.
She stood tall atop her massive Alpha Blessed Wolf, Titan with her dark pirate coat fluttering against the northern breeze.
Morwenna rested her left hand gracefully on the polished silver hilt of her curved naval saber, pulling up directly beside her Lord’s side.
Morwenna looked out across the chaotic clearing with a small smile on her face, she was still wondering for a way to have sex with her Lord and it would only be a matter of time.
"Now... we wait."
Vespera offered a calm silent nod of agreement.
SCHWING!
With a smooth, practiced motion of her right wrist, Vespera drew her primary steel sword from its leather scabbard, letting the gleaming blade rest flat at her side.
Her luminous purple eyes locked onto the distant ranks of Sky’s advancing forces.
’Now...’ Vespera thought to herself, her internal voice ringing with sharp focus, ’...I just need someone competent to come directly for me.’
She had spent the last several mornings refining her foundational stances, and this massive Lord War was the best place to put her practice into action.
She needed a real high-stakes combat environment to test her Tide Blade Arts against experienced opponents.
Meanwhile, on the rear lines of the Blessed Land’s deployed battle array...
Fenna stood surrounded by her archer squad, her hazel eyes tracking the movements of Sky’s advancing heavy infantry through her bow’s optical sightlines.
"Ranged salvo! Fire on my mark!" Fenna commanded.
THWIP-THWIP-THWIP-THWIP!
At her signal, every longbow archer standing on the rear line released their strings in unison.
Dozens of sleek, black composite arrows shot into the sky, arcing high over the central clearing before plunging downward straight toward Sky’s charging vanguard.
Far across the field, Lord Sky stood on his elevated command deck alongside his Heroes.
Seeing the dark rain of arrows descending from the clouds, Sky’s eyes narrowed behind his disguise helmet as memories of earlier artillery strikes flashed through his mind.
’Those arrows!’ Sky recalled frantically. ’They’re the explosive variants that destroyed the lower gun decks!’
Not only the decks but they exploded the first time he had seen them too, if not for the four leaf clover spell that Elm was using, it was hard to know if his people would have survived that easily.
Behind him, Kassandra... the Hero clad in pink-tinted tower armor who commanded the Divine Aegis Shield stepped forward to the railing.
"AEGIS REFRACTION DOME!" Kassandra barked, thrusting her gloved palm forward.
HUMMMMM!
A shimmering wide-area pink energy barrier expanded over the heads of Sky’s advancing soldiers, designed to intercept and detonate the incoming arrows mid-air before they could touch the infantry.
...However, just like before...
SWISH! SWISH! SWISH!
Fenna’s black arrows didn’t collide with the pink barrier at all.

The moment the arrows reached the energy dome, the [Armor-Piercing Runes] inscribed onto their steel tips activated, allowing the arrows to simply float straight past Kassandra’s barrier as if it didn’t even exist.
The black arrows descended into the front ranks of Sky’s infantry, embedding themselves deep into the damp mud among the charging troops.
Sky’s soldiers, seeing the arrows land right between their boots, instantly braced themselves for an apocalyptic explosion.
"GET DOWN! COVER YOUR HEADS!" a sergeant screamed out.
The infantrymen threw their arms over their helmets, diving flat into the mud, waiting for the blast...
...1 second...
...2 seconds...
...3 seconds passed.
The sudden expected explosion never came.
A thick eerie silence hung over the front rank.
"Huh...?" several heavy soldiers grunted out, slowly raising their heads from the dirt.
One brave heavy knight pushed himself up, leaning down to grab the shaft of a black arrow embedded in the mud right beside his boot.
He pulled it free, inspecting the steel tip carefully under the morning sun.
"What is this...?" the knight muttered, squinting his eyes. "There aren’t any explosive runes engraved on these arrowheads at all! They’re just standard steel—"
Before the knight could finish his sentence—
DZZZZZZZT!
Every single black arrow embedded across the three-thousand-yard field suddenly lit up with an intense, pulsing blue light!
BOOM! BOOM! BOOM! BOOM! BOOM!
Simultaneously, all thirty arrows detonated... not into fire or shrapnel, but into high-frequency shockwaves.
KABAGHHH!
The explosive shockwaves ripped through the ground, instantly scrambling, disrupting, and dispelling the thousands of purple 50x gravity runes carved across the clearing.
The atmospheric gravity field collapsed in a single microsecond, freeing the terrain from its superheated pressure.
Far across the field, Lord Sky let out a deep, long, and intensely frustrated sigh behind his disguise mask.

’Unbelievable...’ Sky thought, his teeth gritting in defeat. ’It’s almost as if every single tactic, spell array, and strategic play I set up was completely seen through before the battle even started!’
BOOM!
The shockwaves sent dozens of Sky’s heavy infantrymen flying thirty feet into the air, tumbling head-over-heels across the dirt.
Before the front line of The Unmovable Wall could even recover their balance or clear the mud from their visors—
SWISH!
The very first attacker from the Blessed Land’s Vanguard burst straight through the rising dust cloud!
Vala... the Magic Swordsman closed the distance at high speed.
’Finally...’
Her silver-and-blue longsword was completely engulfed in a roaring, superheated aura of crimson fire magic with her sharp eyes locking onto the disoriented troops ahead.
’I will make my Lord proud.’
"Blow," Vala commanded softly.
BOOOOOOOOOOM!
Vala swung her fiery blade in a horizontal arc.
A fifty-foot crescent wave of compressed elemental fire exploded from her sword tip, blasting through the frontline shields and incinerating their defensive formations in a single strike.

chapters.title: Chapter 315: Lupina’s Trauma
paragraphs: Immediately behind Vala, the rest of the Blessed Land’s Vanguard arrived.

The heavy Shieldmaidens, led by Brida and Gunnhild, slammed their iron tower shields into the enemy line, while Rowenna and the mages unleashed elemental volleys from behind as the two armies collided in a full-blown chaotic melee battle.
CRUNCH! KABAM!
"Haaaaah!"
Gunnhild... the muscular Shieldmaiden sprinted straight into a clump of three heavy armored guards
She reached out with her bare leather-gloved right hand, grabbing one six-foot male soldier by his ankle.
"Hehe~ Hold on tight!"

With a roar of pure physical power, Gunnhild effortlessly lifted the entire 250-pound armored man up into the air with one hand, swinging his body like a heavy iron club and slamming him directly into his two comrades.
"AGH!"
BAM!
All three men crashed hard into the mud with their armor denting violently as they groaned in agony.
SWISH!
From Gunnhild’s right side, an enemy infantryman swung a heavy halberd toward her ribs.
’I’m grateful to my Lord for upgrading me... or else I wouldn’t be able to have such fun.’
Gunnhild didn’t even draw her weapon... she simply executed a nimble backward leap, dodging the blade by an inch.
As her boots touched down, she spun her body around, landing a devastating, lightning-fast reverse side-kick directly into the back of a female guard’s head.𝚏𝗿𝗲𝐞𝐰𝚎𝕓𝐧𝚘𝘃𝗲𝐥.𝐜𝚘𝕞
THWACK!
The female guard’s helmet flew off with her body tumbling across the grass before coming to a halt.
Gunnhild rolled her neck, calling out over the roaring sounds of clashing steel to the surrounding Vanguard women.
"Remember the order, girls! We don’t need to kill the women! They’re going to be our sisters in the future once our Lord takes this land!"
SWISH!
At that exact second, another female guard from The Unmovable Wall charged straight at Gunnhild, screaming a battle cry with her shortsword raised.
Gunnhild didn’t draw a blade. She simply planted her back boot and delivered a powerful, forward push-kick into open air.
BOOM!
A concentrated projectile of compressed wind magic shot out from the sole of Gunnhild’s boot, striking the charging female guard squarely in her chest plate.
The wind pressure rattled the guard’s armor, blasting her fifteen feet backward into the mud, dazing her completely without crushing her ribs.
Gunnhild smirked, her red eyes gleaming as she added loudly.
"...Though, of course, that doesn’t mean we can’t beat them up a little!"
Gunnhild ducked under a flying spear, looking up toward the higher command decks of The Unmovable Wall.
’We need to deal with their Heroes...’ Gunnhild thought internally, evaluating the flow of the battle. ’...But I’ll leave those high-tier duels to the girls at the top.’
Far across the clearing, Lord Sky stood on his command deck, watching the Vanguard’s bizarre combat behavior through his helmet’s zoom lenses.
His black eyes narrowed in real-time tactical analysis.

’They’re holding back their lethal strikes against my female soldiers...’ Sky realized, his stomach twisting. ’They’re deliberately using non-lethal shoves, wind-pushes, and blunts... because they intend to recruit them into their territory after this war is over!’
The arrogant confidence of the Blessed Land was astounding. But Sky wasn’t going to let them treat his troops like future captives.
Sky turned around, looking down at his remaining female combatants with his audio transmitter projecting a stern urgent order.
"ALL FEMALE UNITS! DO NOT HOLD BACK! GO AS HARD AS YOU POSSIBLY CAN! THEY ARE NOT SPARING YOU OUT OF MERCY... THEY ARE TESTING YOUR RESOLVE! SHOW THEM THE MIGHT OF THE UNMOVABLE WALL!"
"YES, MY LORD!" the female guards roared back with their morale reigniting as they charged into the fray with renewed fury.

Sky turned his head toward the back of his command deck, locking his eyes onto the two female Heroes standing in reserve... Lupina, the silver-haired wolf-girl, and Morrighan, the tall horned demonic caster.
Sky’s voice softened slightly, carrying genuine respect as he addressed them.

"Lupina. Morrighan. As per our terms, both of you are slated to be transferred to the Blessed Land once this war concludes if they win but while you still stand under my banner today... take this opportunity to step onto that field and take down a few of Blessed Land’s women!"
Lupina and Morrighan looked at each other for a brief second.
Lupina’s wolf ears twitched against her silver hair, while Morrighan’s long spade tail swished slowly behind her mythril armor, her molten gold eyes glowing with quiet resolve.
Both women turned toward Sky, bowing their heads in unison.
"We will, Lord Sky," They replied.
BOOM!
Lupina didn’t wait a single second.
"I’m going first!" Lupina barked out, her wild wolf instincts taking total control.

She dropped down onto all fours, her hands and boots striking the iron ramp as she sprinted across the battlefield like a feral beast with her long silver hair trailing wildly in the wind behind her and her throat venting a low aggressive wolf growl.
GRRRRRRRR!
Lupina closed the distance to the frontline in a flash of grey speed.

As she charged, memories of her previous humiliation flashed through her mind... she could still vividly feel the phantom ache in her jaw from the brutal reverse heel-kick Tasmin had delivered to her face not too ago.
’I’m not weak!’ Lupina growled in her thoughts, her three-inch steel claw gauntlets extending with sharp clicks. ’I am a Hero of The Unmovable Wall! I’ll prove my worth on this field!’
Lupina locked her eyes onto the very first Blessed Land Shieldmaiden in her path... a tall heavily armored Vanguard woman holding an adamantine broadsword.
"You will do nicely..."
Lupina launched herself off all fours, tackling the Vanguard woman mid-stride!
The Vanguard Shieldmaiden reacted with terrifyingly fast instincts.
She twisted her body sideways, letting Lupina’s tackle graze past her shoulder, and immediately counter-attacked with a swift, powerful front kick aimed straight for Lupina’s stomach.
"Not so fast."
CLANG!
Lupina whipped her right arm down, using her steel claw gauntlet to parry the boot away.
Lupina’s wolf ears flattened against her skull as sheer disbelief shocked her mind.
’What the hell are these people made of?!’ Lupina thought frantically. ’She reacted to my mid-air tackle without even blinking!’
It was almost as if she was used to this kind of thing and wait, wasn’t she just a regular Troop? Who was the person that said a Troop and a Hero wasn’t the same thing?
Refusing to back down, Lupina spun her body mid-air, driving a heavy full-force kick straight into the Vanguard woman’s face.
THWACK!
Lupina’s boot connected flush against the shieldmaiden’s cheek.
"Ghk-!"
...However, the Vanguard woman didn’t fall.
She literally ate the kick with her neck flexing as she absorbed the impact, and immediately swung her broad left fist flat into Lupina’s ribs.
BAM!
"UGHHH!" Lupina gasped with the physical blow knocking the wind clean out of her lungs!
At that exact second, a male guard from The Unmovable Wall rushed in from the side, swinging his broadsword to attack the woman.
"Heh... what amazing timing."
The shieldmaiden didn’t flinch.
She reached out with her bare hands, grabbing the male guard by his hair with her right hand and grabbing Lupina by the back of her neck with her left hand.
’N–no, don’t you da—’
KABAM!
The Vanguard woman forcefully smashed their heads together with terrifying physical power.
CRACK!
"EEEE!" Lupina let out a sharp painful wolf cry as her forehead slammed violently against the male guard’s iron helmet.
The male guard dropped instantly into the mud, completely knocked cold with blood streaming from his nose.
Lupina staggered backward, her vision spinning with bright stars, clutching her bruised forehead as her wolf ears twitched in agony.
The Shieldmaiden looked down at the unconscious male guard, then turned her eyes to Lupina, offering a calm reassuring smile.
"Don’t worry, little wolf... you’ll soon be our sister once the war is over—"
"SHUT UP!" Lupina shrieked in a frenzy.
Driven by panicked survival instinct, Lupina crossed her arms and raked her three-inch steel claws straight across the Vanguard woman’s chest plate at blinding speed.
CRUNCH!
The lethal steel claws caved in the adamantine armor, tearing through the fabric beneath and slicing deep lacerations across the woman’s stomach.
"Ugh!"
A thick spray of crimson blood splashed across the grass as the Vanguard woman gasped, staggering backward and falling over onto her knees.
’I shouldn’t have left my guard down at all...’
Lupina panicked with her wolf ears flat, as she executed three rapid backward leaps to create distance while panting heavily.
"Hah... Hah... I didn’t mean that..."
Running up from behind, Morrighan stopped beside the fallen woman.
’I see so she’s part of Blessed Land, isn’t she?’
This was a human, it was a shame that Blessed Land didn’t have any demon which she could check out.
Morrighan’s molten gold eyes looked down at the spreading puddle of crimson blood around the woman’s stomach.
Morrighan felt a sudden pang of guilt... this was one of Lord Vespera’s people.
...However, before Morrighan could cast a dark stabilization spell...
A bright emerald-green light suddenly erupted from the woman’s chest armor.
The deep bloody lacerations across the woman’s stomach sealed up in a fraction of a second.
The severed muscle fibers reattached, the torn skin closed, and the bleeding stopped entirely.
The woman pushed herself up from the mud, wiping blood from her lips, as she muttered with a dry irritated scoff.
"Damn wolves... that claw hurt. It won’t be my first time though."
Morrighan stood frozen on the grass, her molten gold eyes wide in shock as she stared at the woman’s completely unblemished stomach.
’Is... is she truly blessed...?’ Morrighan thought, her heart trembling as Vespera’s iconic words echoed in her soul.
Meanwhile, Lupina continued her wild sprint across the chaotic battlefield.
She didn’t want to waste any more time dealing with frontline Shieldmaidens.
She wanted to prove her strength and to show that she wasn’t just a weakling who got knocked out in one kick.
SWISH!
Another female soldier sprinted toward her with a shortsword.
"Hey you!"
Lupina dropped low, driving an explosive front kick squarely into the soldier’s abdomen.
BOOM!
"Ugh!"
The shockwave generated by Lupina’s beast-kin mana was immense, blasting the soldier thirty feet straight into the air.
Before the soldier could land, another woman lunged from the left.
"Hmph! Why are all of you trying to grab me, perverts?!"
Lupina flipped mid-air, landing lightly on the woman’s shoulders, and executed a swift leg-sweep that crashed the woman face-first into the dirt.
’That’s the second, hopefully there aren’t mor—’
A third guard thrust a broadsword toward Lupina’s throat.
Lupina skipped backward, her claws ringing against the steel blade.
CLANG!
Sparks came to life but Lupina managed to gain the upper hand by pushing the sword aside, and delivering a swift side-kick that sent the guard tumbling away.
"Ugh! Fuck you!"
Lupina landed on all fours, panting heavily with her wolf ears twitching as she raised her head to scan the clearing...
...And her entire body went completely rigid.
Fifty yards away, standing amidst a swirling vortex of pitch-black void smoke... was Tasmin.

Tasmin was casually walking through a group of five heavy guards, her crimson eyes glowing with cold dominance as thick shadowy tendrils erupted from her back, impaling and tossing enemy soldiers like ragdolls.
THUMP-THUMP.
Lupina’s heart hammered violently against her ribs. Cold paralyzing terror seized her soul.
Her wolf tail tucked tightly between her legs, her jaw throbbing with phantom pain as memories of Tasmin’s brutal reverse heel-kick flooded her mind.
The aura radiating off the S-Rank Shadow Commander was suffocating. It felt like she was going to die...

’No...’ Lupina thought, her teeth clenching as tears of frustration welled in the corners of her eyes. ’I can’t keep running! I can’t keep hiding like a scared puppy! Lord Vespera is watching this stream... I have to face my fears!’
Lupina swallowed her panic, her wolf ears pinning back as she forced her trembling legs forward, accelerating into a full sprint straight toward Tasmin.
SWISH!
Suddenly, out of nowhere—
A dark figure skidded smoothly into the grass directly blocking Lupina’s path.
Fenna lowered her composite longbow, her hazel eyes locking onto Lupina’s face behind her traveler’s hood.
"I cannot allow you to go any further," Fenna spoke calmly with her voice steady.
Lupina skidded to a halt with her wolf claws extended and her eyes darting suspiciously to the master sniper.
’A ploy...?’ Lupina thought frantically. ’Is she trying to protect her Commander?!’
...However, looking into Fenna’s eyes, Lupina realized Fenna was serious.
Fenna glanced over her shoulder for a brief microsecond, watching Tasmin mercilessly impale guards with shadow tendrils.
Fenna knew the internal territory roster... Lupina was one of the two Heroes pledged to join the Blessed Land after the war.
If Lupina recklessly charged into Tasmin’s dark kill-zone right now in her current state, Tasmin’s automated shadow tendrils might accidentally slay her before anyone could stop it.
And if Lupina died here, what was the point of moving forward with Lord Sky’s transfer agreement in her case? They had to ask for another person?
Fenna turned her gaze back to Lupina, letting out a soft, quiet sigh beneath her hood.
’Again...?’ Fenna thought inwardly with her mind feeling mildly exhausted by the endless series of unnecessary duels. ’I really didn’t want to engage in a full battle when it isn’t strictly needed.’
"GET OUT OF MY WAY!" Lupina roared, throwing away all caution.
BOOM!

sentences.text: Immediately behind Vala, the rest of the Blessed Land’s Vanguard arrived.

CRUNCH!
KABAM!
"Haaaaah!"
Gunnhild... the muscular Shieldmaiden sprinted straight into a clump of three heavy armored guards
She reached out with her bare leather-gloved right hand, grabbing one six-foot male soldier by his ankle.
"Hehe~ Hold on tight!"

BAM!

THWACK!
The female guard’s helmet flew off with her body tumbling across the grass before coming to a halt.
Gunnhild rolled her neck, calling out over the roaring sounds of clashing steel to the surrounding Vanguard women.
"Remember the order, girls!
We don’t need to kill the women!
They’re going to be our sisters in the future once our Lord takes this land!"
SWISH!
At that exact second, another female guard from The Unmovable Wall charged straight at Gunnhild, screaming a battle cry with her shortsword raised.
Gunnhild didn’t draw a blade.
She simply planted her back boot and delivered a powerful, forward push-kick into open air.
BOOM!
A concentrated projectile of compressed wind magic shot out from the sole of Gunnhild’s boot, striking the charging female guard squarely in her chest plate.
The wind pressure rattled the guard’s armor, blasting her fifteen feet backward into the mud, dazing her completely without crushing her ribs.
Gunnhild smirked, her red eyes gleaming as she added loudly.
"...Though, of course, that doesn’t mean we can’t beat them up a little!"
Gunnhild ducked under a flying spear, looking up toward the higher command decks of The Unmovable Wall.
’We need to deal with their Heroes...’ Gunnhild thought internally, evaluating the flow of the battle. ’...But I’ll leave those high-tier duels to the girls at the top.’
Far across the clearing, Lord Sky stood on his command deck, watching the Vanguard’s bizarre combat behavior through his helmet’s zoom lenses.
His black eyes narrowed in real-time tactical analysis.

’They’re holding back their lethal strikes against my female soldiers...’ Sky realized, his stomach twisting. ’They’re deliberately using non-lethal shoves, wind-pushes, and blunts... because they intend to recruit them into their territory after this war is over!’
The arrogant confidence of the Blessed Land was astounding.
But Sky wasn’t going to let them treat his troops like future captives.
Sky turned around, looking down at his remaining female combatants with his audio transmitter projecting a stern urgent order.
"ALL FEMALE UNITS!
DO NOT HOLD BACK!
GO AS HARD AS YOU POSSIBLY CAN!
THEY ARE NOT SPARING YOU OUT OF MERCY...
THEY ARE TESTING YOUR RESOLVE!
SHOW THEM THE MIGHT OF THE UNMOVABLE WALL!"
"YES, MY LORD!" the female guards roared back with their morale reigniting as they charged into the fray with renewed fury.
Sky turned his head toward the back of his command deck, locking his eyes onto the two female Heroes standing in reserve...
Lupina, the silver-haired wolf-girl, and Morrighan, the tall horned demonic caster.
Sky’s voice softened slightly, carrying genuine respect as he addressed them.
"Lupina.
Morrighan.

As per our terms, both of you are slated to be transferred to the Blessed Land once this war concludes if they win but while you still stand under my banner today... take this opportunity to step onto that field and take down a few of Blessed Land’s women!"
Lupina and Morrighan looked at each other for a brief second.
Lupina’s wolf ears twitched against her silver hair, while Morrighan’s long spade tail swished slowly behind her mythril armor, her molten gold eyes glowing with quiet resolve.
Both women turned toward Sky, bowing their heads in unison.
"We will, Lord Sky," They replied.
BOOM!
Lupina didn’t wait a single second.
"I’m going first!" Lupina barked out, her wild wolf instincts taking total control.

She dropped down onto all fours, her hands and boots striking the iron ramp as she sprinted across the battlefield like a feral beast with her long silver hair trailing wildly in the wind behind her and her throat venting a low aggressive wolf growl.
GRRRRRRRR!
Lupina closed the distance to the frontline in a flash of grey speed.

As she charged, memories of her previous humiliation flashed through her mind... she could still vividly feel the phantom ache in her jaw from the brutal reverse heel-kick Tasmin had delivered to her face not too ago.
’I’m not weak!’ Lupina growled in her thoughts, her three-inch steel claw gauntlets extending with sharp clicks. ’I am a Hero of The Unmovable Wall!
I’ll prove my worth on this field!’
Lupina locked her eyes onto the very first Blessed Land Shieldmaiden in her path... a tall heavily armored Vanguard woman holding an adamantine broadsword.
"You will do nicely..."
Lupina launched herself off all fours, tackling the Vanguard woman mid-stride!
The Vanguard Shieldmaiden reacted with terrifyingly fast instincts.
She twisted her body sideways, letting Lupina’s tackle graze past her shoulder, and immediately counter-attacked with a swift, powerful front kick aimed straight for Lupina’s stomach.
"Not so fast."
CLANG!
Lupina whipped her right arm down, using her steel claw gauntlet to parry the boot away.
Lupina’s wolf ears flattened against her skull as sheer disbelief shocked her mind.
’What the hell are these people made of?!’ Lupina thought frantically. ’She reacted to my mid-air tackle without even blinking!’
It was almost as if she was used to this kind of thing and wait, wasn’t she just a regular Troop?
Who was the person that said a Troop and a Hero wasn’t the same thing?
Refusing to back down, Lupina spun her body mid-air, driving a heavy full-force kick straight into the Vanguard woman’s face.
THWACK!
Lupina’s boot connected flush against the shieldmaiden’s cheek.
"Ghk-!"
...However, the Vanguard woman didn’t fall.
She literally ate the kick with her neck flexing as she absorbed the impact, and immediately swung her broad left fist flat into Lupina’s ribs.
BAM!
"UGHHH!" Lupina gasped with the physical blow knocking the wind clean out of her lungs!
At that exact second, a male guard from The Unmovable Wall rushed in from the side, swinging his broadsword to attack the woman.
"Heh... what amazing timing."
The shieldmaiden didn’t flinch.
She reached out with her bare hands, grabbing the male guard by his hair with her right hand and grabbing Lupina by the back of her neck with her left hand.
’N–no, don’t you da—’
KABAM!
The Vanguard woman forcefully smashed their heads together with terrifying physical power.
CRACK!
"EEEE!" Lupina let out a sharp painful wolf cry as her forehead slammed violently against the male guard’s iron helmet.
The male guard dropped instantly into the mud, completely knocked cold with blood streaming from his nose.
Lupina staggered backward, her vision spinning with bright stars, clutching her bruised forehead as her wolf ears twitched in agony.
The Shieldmaiden looked down at the unconscious male guard, then turned her eyes to Lupina, offering a calm reassuring smile.
"Don’t worry, little wolf... you’ll soon be our sister once the war is over—"
"SHUT UP!" Lupina shrieked in a frenzy.
Driven by panicked survival instinct, Lupina crossed her arms and raked her three-inch steel claws straight across the Vanguard woman’s chest plate at blinding speed.
CRUNCH!
The lethal steel claws caved in the adamantine armor, tearing through the fabric beneath and slicing deep lacerations across the woman’s stomach.
"Ugh!"
A thick spray of crimson blood splashed across the grass as the Vanguard woman gasped, staggering backward and falling over onto her knees.
’I shouldn’t have left my guard down at all...’
Lupina panicked with her wolf ears flat, as she executed three rapid backward leaps to create distance while panting heavily.
"Hah...
Hah...
I didn’t mean that..."
Running up from behind, Morrighan stopped beside the fallen woman.
’I see so she’s part of Blessed Land, isn’t she?’
This was a human, it was a shame that Blessed Land didn’t have any demon which she could check out.
Morrighan’s molten gold eyes looked down at the spreading puddle of crimson blood around the woman’s stomach.
Morrighan felt a sudden pang of guilt... this was one of Lord Vespera’s people.
...However, before Morrighan could cast a dark stabilization spell...
A bright emerald-green light suddenly erupted from the woman’s chest armor.
The deep bloody lacerations across the woman’s stomach sealed up in a fraction of a second.
The severed muscle fibers reattached, the torn skin closed, and the bleeding stopped entirely.
The woman pushed herself up from the mud, wiping blood from her lips, as she muttered with a dry irritated scoff.
"Damn wolves... that claw hurt.
It won’t be my first time though."
Morrighan stood frozen on the grass, her molten gold eyes wide in shock as she stared at the woman’s completely unblemished stomach.

chapters.title: Chapter 316: Can I... Be Blessed Too?
paragraphs: Lupina launched herself forward with her steel claws blurring into a lethal three-strike claw combination aimed directly at Fenna’s throat and chest.
SWISH! SWISH! SWISH!
Fenna didn’t even draw a blade.
She simply leaned her upper body backward, her incredible archer reflexes allowing her to dodge all three claw thrusts by millimeters.
"STOP MOVING AROUND SO MUCH...!" Lupina rushed forward with her claw extended however just before she could slash Fenna’s throat open...𝙧𝙚𝙚𝔀𝒆𝓫𝓷𝙤𝓿𝒆𝙡.𝒄𝙤𝓶
[ACTIVE SKILL ACTIVATED: WIND-WALK GLIDE]
THWIP!
Fenna executed a weightless backflip with her boots landing lightly on the branch of a nearby scorched tree ten feet above the ground.
"WOLF’S FURY!" Lupina shrieked, unleashing her core Hero mana skill.
HUMMMMMMM!
A fiery silver-and-white wolf aura exploded from Lupina’s body.
Her movement speed doubled instantly, her eyes glowing with wild feral light as she kicked off the tree trunk, shattering the wood into splinters.
BOOM!
Lupina plummeted down toward Fenna like a silver meteor with her steel claws tearing through the air.
"AAAAGH!"
A thirty-foot crescent wave of compressed, razor-sharp wind magic shot out from Lupina’s claws, slicing through the ground and demolishing three massive stone boulders in its path.
The impact blasted a twenty-foot crater into the earth, sending shattered bedrock flying into the sky.
’She’s actually quite stronger than I originally gave her credit for...’
BOOM!
Dust and rock filled the air as Lupina landed in the center of the crater, her claws dripping with silver mana and her wolf ears twitching as she looked around for Fenna’s corpse.
’She couldn’t have survived all of tha—’
"Over here," a cool voice called out from behind her.
Lupina snapped her head around.
Fenna was standing on a floating chunk of rock five feet behind her with her composite longbow fully drawn and a single arrow notched against the string.
Fenna didn’t notch a lethal arrow. Inscribed onto the tip was a [Knockout Rune].
THWIP!
Fenna released the string.
The arrow shot forward at point-blank range, moving faster than Lupina’s eyes could track.
CLANG!
Lupina frantically brought her steel claw gauntlets together in a desperation cross-block.
BOOOOOOM!
The knockout rune detonated upon contact with Lupina’s claws as a massive pressurized wave of blunt force and sleeping gas exploded flat against Lupina’s face.
’We made it to calm Brida down but who thought we would need it so soon...?’
The physical force shattered Lupina’s steel claws into pieces, shutting down her nervous system instantly.
"GAHHH...!"
Lupina’s eyes rolled back into her head.
Her silver wolf ears flattened with her body flying backward through the smoke before crashing softly onto the grass, completely out cold.
Fenna lowered her composite bow, landing lightly beside the unconscious wolf-girl, and let out a long, quiet breath as the dust settled over the clearing.
"Haah~ I really don’t want to fight useless battles."
Tasmin stood amidst the lingering wisps of pitch-black void smoke with her dark coat fluttering against the cold mountain air of the Umbral Basin.
Her sharp eyes swept across the immediate radius of the clearing, watching thick, shadowy tendrils retract smoothly back into her spine.

Around her boots lay half a dozen disarmed heavy guards from The Unmovable Wall, all groaning in disoriented exhaustion with their defensive shields dented and fractured from the impact of her shadow strikes.
’I’m still in the middle of experimentation though...’
With a silent, fluid motion, Tasmin turned her gaze to the left.
Fenna was stepping out from the settling dust cloud of the crater, carrying the unconscious body of Lupina over her shoulder.
The silver-haired wolf-girl’s steel gauntlets were completely shattered with her wolf ears twitching flat against her silver hair as she slept off the effects of Fenna’s knockout rune.
Tasmin looked at the limp form of the beast-kin Hero, her dark eyes narrowing into a cold, evaluating stare.

’That one...’ Tasmin thought internally, her shadow tendrils coiling lazily around her waist. ’The moment this war concludes and she officially steps foot inside our border... I am going to have to personally break her down in the training yards. Running blindly into a kill-zone without reading the battlefield.. At her strength? She’s going to end up as nothing more than a punching bag if she doesn’t learn how to use her ears.’
Tasmin could understand if it was Brida after all, Brida was as dumb as rocks but then again, the average Demi Human was smarter than her.
Before Tasmin could take a step toward Fenna, a sudden spike of elemental mana flared violently from the eastern flank of the clearing.
WHOOOOOOSH!
The air temperature shot from sub-zero frost to scorching inferno in a single microsecond.
Tasmin snapped her head to the right.

Two massive waves of roaring elemental energy... one of superheated crimson fire and the other of crystalline sub-zero ice were sweeping across the dirt, instantly incinerating grass on one side while flash-freezing the mud into jagged blue glaciers on the other.
Tasmin didn’t flinch.
She planted her boots into the cracked bedrock and shot off the ground, ascending twenty feet into the air via a condensed foothold of shadow mana.
WHOOSH!
Hovering mid-air, her crimson eyes locked onto the two Hero figures advancing side-by-side through the dual-elemental storm.
It was Ignis... the Flame Hero of Lord Sky and Frost... the Glacial Hero of Lord Sky.
They were the dual elemental Wardens Sky had held in reserve, and the raw pressure radiating from their combined mana cores was forcing back whole clusters of women and men alike.
A dark sharp grin touched Tasmin’s lips as her twin shortswords slipped seamlessly into her palms.

"Finally..." Tasmin whispered, her voice laced with anticipation. "I’ve been waiting for you two to step off that deck. I sensed your core signatures the moment the barriers dropped... but as of right now..."
"I’ll handle this!" Tasmin called out mid-air, preparing to dive straight into the dual storm—
THWACK!
KABAAAAAM!

Before Tasmin could plunge downward, a colossal five-foot-tall tower shield forged of solid adamantine soared through the air, embedding itself with massive force directly into the bedrock right in front of Tasmin’s descending path.
’No matter... I’ll just spread my domain and—’
However...
The broad face of a shield absorbed the incoming torrent of roaring flames and jagged ice spears, sending a massive shockwave of steam and shattered frost boiling up into the sky.
SWISH!
Brida landed with a heavy earth-shaking thud directly beside the embedded tower shield.
Her muscular frame was clad in massive silver plate armor, her hair caught the harsh light of the burning clearings as her hand clamped onto the grip of her shield.
Brida glanced up at Tasmin, her broad face breaking into a wide confident smirk.

"Hold your horses, Tas..." Brida boomed out, her voice reverberating over the roaring sounds of clashing steel. "You aren’t the only heavy hitter on this battle line. You’ve had your fun tearing through their infantry lines... leave the wall duty to the wall."
Tasmin landed lightly on the top rim of Brida’s shield with her dark coat settling around her boots.
She looked down at the muscular Shieldmaiden, her cold expression softening into a reluctant sigh as she sheathed her weapons.
"Fine," Tasmin murmured with her crimson eyes tracking Ignis and Frost below. "Don’t let them burn the outer tree line."
Far across the central clearing, separated from the roaring frontline clashes, a suffocating silence hung around the solitary figure of Morrighan.
The tall horned demoness stood frozen in the damp mud, her fingers trembling slightly within her heavy spiked mythril demonic gauntlets.

Her molten-gold eyes were fixed entirely on the distant figure of Lord Vespera, who stood calmly with her single steel longsword resting flat at her side with her hood casting a deep shadow over her glowing purple eyes.
Morrighan bit her dark lower lip so hard a tiny drop of dark crimson blood almost surfaced.
Inside her mind, a single sentence was echoing over and over again like a divine melody echoing through a dark abyss.

’It doesn’t matter where you were born, what mana flows through your veins, or what horns sit upon your head. The very rules of my domain dictate one absolute truth: as long as you step foot inside the Blessed Land... you are blessed.’
Morrighan couldn’t remember the last time anyone had ever promised her such a thing.
In fact, no one ever had.
She was a demonic being... a creature born of abyssal brimstone and dark mana.
Her very physical existence was marked by the two polished, obsidian-black horns curving majestically from her temples, and the long, spade-tipped tail that currently hung still behind her boots.
Her origin was a tragedy of bloody prejudice.
She was the product of a forbidden union between a high ranking demon and a human nun who had belonged to the Holy Church.
The moment her birth was discovered, the Church had executed both her parents without trial.

Morrighan herself was supposed to have been put to the sword as an infant monster, but she had managed to survive in the dark monster-infested ruins of the world until she was summoned into the Sovereign Realm by her original Lord before meeting Lord Sky.
Yet, even under Sky’s banner, the human infantrymen had feared her.
They whispered behind her back... They refused to share barracks with her and they treated her like a ticking curse waiting to detonate.
Morrighan looked down at the mud beneath her boots, her heart hammering violently against her ribs.

’Look at her...’ Morrighan thought, her eyes misting with an overwhelming mix of shyness, hope, and reverence as she stared at Vespera. ’This is the very first time... the first time since I stepped into this ruthless world... that I have ever wanted to belong to a Lord so badly.’
Taking a slow, trembling breath, Morrighan began walking across the clearing toward Vespera.
She didn’t run and she didn’t draw a blade.
She simply walked with her mythril boots making quiet thudding sounds against the damp grass.
Vespera turned her head as the tall demoness approached.
Beneath her hood, Vespera’s luminous purple eyes softened, and a warm genuine smile curved her lips.
Morrighan stopped ten feet away.
Her lips trembled, her spade tail swishing nervously behind her skirt as she looked at the single-armed Lord.
She wanted a place.
A real home... A home where these obsidian horns curving from her skull meant nothing... Where her dark blood wasn’t treated as an abomination.

Lupina didn’t care about her horns, but that was simply because the silver-haired beast-kin girl was far too airheaded and dense to understand complex social prejudice... to Lupina, anyone who could run fast was fine.
But Morrighan understood.
She knew how cold the world was to demons.
"Lord Vespera..." Morrighan spoke.
"Yes, Morrighan?" Vespera replied warmly, her posture completely relaxed.
Morrighan swallowed hard, her molten-gold eyes searching Vespera’s face for even a single shred of deceit or hesitation.

"Is it... is it truly real?" Morrighan asked, her voice dropping to a whisper. "What you promised me back at the trade clearing... will I truly be accepted here? Despite... despite these horns? Despite the abyssal brimstone that flows in my veins?"
Vespera’s purple eyes shone with unshakeable conviction. She didn’t hesitate for even a fraction of a second.
She offered Morrighan an assuring, gentle smile that seemed to wash away years of built-up trauma in a single pulse of light.

"Every single word of it is true, Morrighan," Vespera promised softly. She tilted her head slightly toward the right, gesturing toward the formidable figure standing beside her. "You don’t even have to take my word for it alone. You can ask Morwenna right here."
Morwenna stood atop her Alpha Wolf, Titan, resting her hand lazily on the hilt of her curved naval saber.
Hearing her name, Morwenna cast a cool, dismissive glance down at the horned demoness.
Her grey eyes were completely devoid of disgust or fear.

"Tch," Morwenna scoffed, her tone as dry as sea salt. "Don’t ask foolish questions, demon girl. In this territory, nobody gives a damn whether you were born from a demon, an abyssal void, or a fish in the sea. As long as you respect our Lord and carry your weight alongside the rest of us, you are welcome here."
Morwenna paused, a slight, amused smirk touching her lips as she added under her breath:
"...Besides, the weed over at the central manor would probably like you anyway. She’s obsessed with anything that grows out of the dark."
Morrighan’s breath hitched in her throat. Her pale cheeks flushed a dark burning violet as tears gathered in the corners of her gold eyes.
She bit her lip, her heart overflowing with an overwhelming sense of gratitude and relief.
But she was a Hero of The Unmovable Wall, and she knew that true acceptance in the Sovereign Realm had to be earned with strength.
"Thank you..." Morrighan whispered.
HUMMMMMMM!
The second those words left her mouth, an intense suffocating aura of pure abyssal mana erupted from Morrighan’s body.
Dozens of complex, pitch-black Demonic Cursed Magic Circles materialized in the air around her, spinning rapidly across a fifty-yard radius.
The grass beneath her boots turned to black ash as dark brimstone smoke billowed into the sky.

"I cannot simply walk into your territory as a charity case, Lord Vespera!" Morrighan declared, her echoing voice ringing across the clearing with fierce resolve. "I must prove my worth to you! I am coming at you with my full power!"

sentences.text: Lupina launched herself forward with her steel claws blurring into a lethal three-strike claw combination aimed directly at Fenna’s throat and chest.
SWISH!
SWISH!
SWISH!
Fenna didn’t even draw a blade.
She simply leaned her upper body backward, her incredible archer reflexes allowing her to dodge all three claw thrusts by millimeters.
"STOP MOVING AROUND SO MUCH...!" Lupina rushed forward with her claw extended however just before she could slash Fenna’s throat open...𝙧𝙚𝙚𝔀𝒆𝓫𝓷𝙤𝓿𝒆𝙡.𝒄𝙤𝓶
[ACTIVE SKILL ACTIVATED: WIND-WALK GLIDE]
THWIP!
Fenna executed a weightless backflip with her boots landing lightly on the branch of a nearby scorched tree ten feet above the ground.
"WOLF’S FURY!" Lupina shrieked, unleashing her core Hero mana skill.
HUMMMMMMM!
A fiery silver-and-white wolf aura exploded from Lupina’s body.
Her movement speed doubled instantly, her eyes glowing with wild feral light as she kicked off the tree trunk, shattering the wood into splinters.
BOOM!
Lupina plummeted down toward Fenna like a silver meteor with her steel claws tearing through the air.
"AAAAGH!"
A thirty-foot crescent wave of compressed, razor-sharp wind magic shot out from Lupina’s claws, slicing through the ground and demolishing three massive stone boulders in its path.
The impact blasted a twenty-foot crater into the earth, sending shattered bedrock flying into the sky.
’She’s actually quite stronger than I originally gave her credit for...’
BOOM!
Dust and rock filled the air as Lupina landed in the center of the crater, her claws dripping with silver mana and her wolf ears twitching as she looked around for Fenna’s corpse.
’She couldn’t have survived all of tha—’
"Over here," a cool voice called out from behind her.
Lupina snapped her head around.
Fenna was standing on a floating chunk of rock five feet behind her with her composite longbow fully drawn and a single arrow notched against the string.
Fenna didn’t notch a lethal arrow.
Inscribed onto the tip was a [Knockout Rune].
THWIP!
Fenna released the string.
The arrow shot forward at point-blank range, moving faster than Lupina’s eyes could track.
CLANG!
Lupina frantically brought her steel claw gauntlets together in a desperation cross-block.
BOOOOOOM!
The knockout rune detonated upon contact with Lupina’s claws as a massive pressurized wave of blunt force and sleeping gas exploded flat against Lupina’s face.
’We made it to calm Brida down but who thought we would need it so soon...?’
The physical force shattered Lupina’s steel claws into pieces, shutting down her nervous system instantly.
"GAHHH...!"
Lupina’s eyes rolled back into her head.
Her silver wolf ears flattened with her body flying backward through the smoke before crashing softly onto the grass, completely out cold.
Fenna lowered her composite bow, landing lightly beside the unconscious wolf-girl, and let out a long, quiet breath as the dust settled over the clearing.
"Haah~ I really don’t want to fight useless battles."
Tasmin stood amidst the lingering wisps of pitch-black void smoke with her dark coat fluttering against the cold mountain air of the Umbral Basin.
Her sharp eyes swept across the immediate radius of the clearing, watching thick, shadowy tendrils retract smoothly back into her spine.

Around her boots lay half a dozen disarmed heavy guards from The Unmovable Wall, all groaning in disoriented exhaustion with their defensive shields dented and fractured from the impact of her shadow strikes.
’I’m still in the middle of experimentation though...’
With a silent, fluid motion, Tasmin turned her gaze to the left.
Fenna was stepping out from the settling dust cloud of the crater, carrying the unconscious body of Lupina over her shoulder.
The silver-haired wolf-girl’s steel gauntlets were completely shattered with her wolf ears twitching flat against her silver hair as she slept off the effects of Fenna’s knockout rune.
Tasmin looked at the limp form of the beast-kin Hero, her dark eyes narrowing into a cold, evaluating stare.
’That one...’ Tasmin thought internally, her shadow tendrils coiling lazily around her waist. ’The moment this war concludes and she officially steps foot inside our border...
I am going to have to personally break her down in the training yards.
Running blindly into a kill-zone without reading the battlefield..
At her strength?
She’s going to end up as nothing more than a punching bag if she doesn’t learn how to use her ears.’
Tasmin could understand if it was Brida after all, Brida was as dumb as rocks but then again, the average Demi Human was smarter than her.
Before Tasmin could take a step toward Fenna, a sudden spike of elemental mana flared violently from the eastern flank of the clearing.
WHOOOOOOSH!
The air temperature shot from sub-zero frost to scorching inferno in a single microsecond.
Tasmin snapped her head to the right.

Two massive waves of roaring elemental energy... one of superheated crimson fire and the other of crystalline sub-zero ice were sweeping across the dirt, instantly incinerating grass on one side while flash-freezing the mud into jagged blue glaciers on the other.
Tasmin didn’t flinch.
She planted her boots into the cracked bedrock and shot off the ground, ascending twenty feet into the air via a condensed foothold of shadow mana.
WHOOSH!
Hovering mid-air, her crimson eyes locked onto the two Hero figures advancing side-by-side through the dual-elemental storm.
It was Ignis... the Flame Hero of Lord Sky and Frost... the Glacial Hero of Lord Sky.
They were the dual elemental Wardens Sky had held in reserve, and the raw pressure radiating from their combined mana cores was forcing back whole clusters of women and men alike.
A dark sharp grin touched Tasmin’s lips as her twin shortswords slipped seamlessly into her palms.
"Finally..." Tasmin whispered, her voice laced with anticipation.
"I’ve been waiting for you two to step off that deck.
I sensed your core signatures the moment the barriers dropped... but as of right now..."
"I’ll handle this!" Tasmin called out mid-air, preparing to dive straight into the dual storm—
THWACK!
KABAAAAAM!

Before Tasmin could plunge downward, a colossal five-foot-tall tower shield forged of solid adamantine soared through the air, embedding itself with massive force directly into the bedrock right in front of Tasmin’s descending path.
’No matter...
I’ll just spread my domain and—’
However...
The broad face of a shield absorbed the incoming torrent of roaring flames and jagged ice spears, sending a massive shockwave of steam and shattered frost boiling up into the sky.
SWISH!
Brida landed with a heavy earth-shaking thud directly beside the embedded tower shield.
Her muscular frame was clad in massive silver plate armor, her hair caught the harsh light of the burning clearings as her hand clamped onto the grip of her shield.
Brida glanced up at Tasmin, her broad face breaking into a wide confident smirk.
"Hold your horses, Tas..." Brida boomed out, her voice reverberating over the roaring sounds of clashing steel.
"You aren’t the only heavy hitter on this battle line.
You’ve had your fun tearing through their infantry lines... leave the wall duty to the wall."
Tasmin landed lightly on the top rim of Brida’s shield with her dark coat settling around her boots.
She looked down at the muscular Shieldmaiden, her cold expression softening into a reluctant sigh as she sheathed her weapons.
"Fine," Tasmin murmured with her crimson eyes tracking Ignis and Frost below.
"Don’t let them burn the outer tree line."
Far across the central clearing, separated from the roaring frontline clashes, a suffocating silence hung around the solitary figure of Morrighan.
The tall horned demoness stood frozen in the damp mud, her fingers trembling slightly within her heavy spiked mythril demonic gauntlets.

Her molten-gold eyes were fixed entirely on the distant figure of Lord Vespera, who stood calmly with her single steel longsword resting flat at her side with her hood casting a deep shadow over her glowing purple eyes.
Morrighan bit her dark lower lip so hard a tiny drop of dark crimson blood almost surfaced.
Inside her mind, a single sentence was echoing over and over again like a divine melody echoing through a dark abyss.
’It doesn’t matter where you were born, what mana flows through your veins, or what horns sit upon your head.
The very rules of my domain dictate one absolute truth: as long as you step foot inside the Blessed Land... you are blessed.’
Morrighan couldn’t remember the last time anyone had ever promised her such a thing.
In fact, no one ever had.
She was a demonic being... a creature born of abyssal brimstone and dark mana.
Her very physical existence was marked by the two polished, obsidian-black horns curving majestically from her temples, and the long, spade-tipped tail that currently hung still behind her boots.
Her origin was a tragedy of bloody prejudice.
She was the product of a forbidden union between a high ranking demon and a human nun who had belonged to the Holy Church.
The moment her birth was discovered, the Church had executed both her parents without trial.

Morrighan herself was supposed to have been put to the sword as an infant monster, but she had managed to survive in the dark monster-infested ruins of the world until she was summoned into the Sovereign Realm by her original Lord before meeting Lord Sky.
Yet, even under Sky’s banner, the human infantrymen had feared her.
They whispered behind her back...
They refused to share barracks with her and they treated her like a ticking curse waiting to detonate.
Morrighan looked down at the mud beneath her boots, her heart hammering violently against her ribs.

’Look at her...’ Morrighan thought, her eyes misting with an overwhelming mix of shyness, hope, and reverence as she stared at Vespera. ’This is the very first time... the first time since I stepped into this ruthless world... that I have ever wanted to belong to a Lord so badly.’
Taking a slow, trembling breath, Morrighan began walking across the clearing toward Vespera.
She didn’t run and she didn’t draw a blade.
She simply walked with her mythril boots making quiet thudding sounds against the damp grass.
Vespera turned her head as the tall demoness approached.
Beneath her hood, Vespera’s luminous purple eyes softened, and a warm genuine smile curved her lips.
Morrighan stopped ten feet away.
Her lips trembled, her spade tail swishing nervously behind her skirt as she looked at the single-armed Lord.
She wanted a place.
A real home...
A home where these obsidian horns curving from her skull meant nothing...
Where her dark blood wasn’t treated as an abomination.

Lupina didn’t care about her horns, but that was simply because the silver-haired beast-kin girl was far too airheaded and dense to understand complex social prejudice... to Lupina, anyone who could run fast was fine.
But Morrighan understood.
She knew how cold the world was to demons.
"Lord Vespera..." Morrighan spoke.
"Yes, Morrighan?" Vespera replied warmly, her posture completely relaxed.
Morrighan swallowed hard, her molten-gold eyes searching Vespera’s face for even a single shred of deceit or hesitation.
"Is it... is it truly real?" Morrighan asked, her voice dropping to a whisper.
"What you promised me back at the trade clearing... will I truly be accepted here?
Despite... despite these horns?
Despite the abyssal brimstone that flows in my veins?"
Vespera’s purple eyes shone with unshakeable conviction.
She didn’t hesitate for even a fraction of a second.
She offered Morrighan an assuring, gentle smile that seemed to wash away years of built-up trauma in a single pulse of light.
"Every single word of it is true, Morrighan," Vespera promised softly.
She tilted her head slightly toward the right, gesturing toward the formidable figure standing beside her.
"You don’t even have to take my word for it alone.
You can ask Morwenna right here."
Morwenna stood atop her Alpha Wolf, Titan, resting her hand lazily on the hilt of her curved naval saber.
Hearing her name, Morwenna cast a cool, dismissive glance down at the horned demoness.
Her grey eyes were completely devoid of disgust or fear.
"Tch," Morwenna scoffed, her tone as dry as sea salt.
"Don’t ask foolish questions, demon girl.
In this territory, nobody gives a damn whether you were born from a demon, an abyssal void, or a fish in the sea.
As long as you respect our Lord and carry your weight alongside the rest of us, you are welcome here."
Morwenna paused, a slight, amused smirk touching her lips as she added under her breath:
"...Besides, the weed over at the central manor would probably like you anyway.
She’s obsessed with anything that grows out of the dark."
Morrighan’s breath hitched in her throat.
Her pale cheeks flushed a dark burning violet as tears gathered in the corners of her gold eyes.
She bit her lip, her heart overflowing with an overwhelming sense of gratitude and relief.
But she was a Hero of The Unmovable Wall, and she knew that true acceptance in the Sovereign Realm had to be earned with strength.
"Thank you..." Morrighan whispered.
HUMMMMMMM!
The second those words left her mouth, an intense suffocating aura of pure abyssal mana erupted from Morrighan’s body.
Dozens of complex, pitch-black Demonic Cursed Magic Circles materialized in the air around her, spinning rapidly across a fifty-yard radius.
The grass beneath her boots turned to black ash as dark brimstone smoke billowed into the sky.
"I cannot simply walk into your territory as a charity case, Lord Vespera!" Morrighan declared, her echoing voice ringing across the clearing with fierce resolve.
"I must prove my worth to you!
I am coming at you with my full power!"

chapters.title: Chapter 317: Blessed
paragraphs: Vespera looked at the surrounding dark cursed arrays with her glowing purple eyes widening slightly in appreciation.
She smoothly adjusted her grip on her single steel longsword, letting her Gold Core mana cycle fluidly through her internal circuits then she offered a confident radiant smile.

"Why not?" Vespera replied smoothly, her voice sounding cool and steady. "Come at me with everything you have, Morrighan! Though... I won’t be coming at you with my full power, considering I have zero intention of accidentally killing my future Hero."
Morwenna’s grey eyes narrowed from atop her wolf as she watched Morrighan’s first move.
WHOOSH!
A pulsating, dark-crimson sigil materialized over Morrighan’s palm as she thrust her hand toward Vespera!
’Mark Of The Abyss...!’
Morrighan attempted to brand Vespera’s core with her signature debuff curse... a spell designed to increase all incoming damage by 25% and suppress mana regeneration by half!
SWISH!
The dark crimson sigil shot through the air, aiming straight for Vespera’s chest plate...
...However, the moment the cursed sigil reached a three-foot boundary around Vespera’s body, it simply dissolved into empty red sparks.
Vespera’s underlying Sovereign Authority and Gold Core power completely rejected the low-tier status effect before it could even attach.
Morwenna scoffed loudly from the sidelines, leaning on her saber hilt.
"Tch! Opening a duel with a debuff curse before even testing your blade? That’s a coward’s move, demon girl!"
Morrighan flinched slightly with her pale cheeks flushing a darker violet at Morwenna’s sharp critique.
She took a deep steadying breath, letting the shame wash away as she centered her focus.
She dropped low, pulling her heavy mythril gauntlets up into a broad defensive caster-martial stance.
"Then let us test raw strength, My Lord!" Morrighan roared!
BOOM!
’Demon’s Resolve!’
A violent aura of crimson-and-black energy erupted around Morrighan’s frame.
Her obsidian horns emitted a terrifying abyssal light, her golden eyes burning with intense demonic power as her physical strength, speed, and durability doubled in a single instant.
BOOM!
Morrighan planted her mythril boot into the dirt, shattering the bedrock as she launched herself forward like a dark cannonball.
Vespera stood her ground with her luminous purple eyes sharpening beneath her hood.
The second Morrighan closed the distance, Vespera activated the Tidal-Blade Second Style: Rip-Current Perception.
HUMMMMMM!
A subtle invisible pulse of high-pressure water mana erupted into the ambient air around Morrighan’s advancing body.
Vespera focused her mental awareness, attempting to trigger the perception phase.

In theory, the atmospheric water moisture was supposed to read Morrighan’s micro-telegraphs... muscle tension, breath control, weight distribution and highlight glowing blue current lines pointing straight to Morrighan’s open gaps.
...However, just as Morwenna had warned during their earlier training sessions, the Second Style was insanely difficult to master.
Vespera’s vision didn’t flood with clear, glowing blue lines.
The atmospheric moisture read the dark brimstone heat radiating off Morrighan’s demonic aura, creating distorted, flickering blue wisps that faded in and out of sight.
Vespera couldn’t get a clear, stable read on the opening.
’Fucking hell...’ Vespera thought with a sigh. ’The heat from her demonic mana is warping the moisture pressure... I can’t rely on full perception.’
BOOM!
Morrighan arrived directly in front of her!
"BRIMSTONE PUNCH!" Morrighan yelled out, driving her heavy spiked mythril gauntlet straight for Vespera’s chest.
The fist was wrapped in a roaring vortex of dark brimstone flames.
Vespera couldn’t read the complete flaw, but her raw combat instincts and gold-core reaction speed kicked in.
CLANG!
Vespera raised her single steel longsword horizontally, catching Morrighan’s massive spiked gauntlet right against the flat of her blade.
KABAGHHH!
The physical impact of Morrighan’s boosted demonic strength was immense.
The shockwave blasted the grass beneath their boots forty feet into the air, forcing Vespera’s boots to skid backward five feet across the torn mud.
"HAAAAAH!"
Morrighan didn’t stop.
Driven by her fierce desire to prove her worth, she spun her body mid-air, her heavy scale-armored crimson tail whipping around like a steel mace straight toward Vespera’s exposed left flank.
SWISH!
Vespera executed rapid footwork, stepping inside the arc of the tail strike... She swung her longsword upward, using a basic deflection arc—
CLANG!
The blade struck the scale armor of Morrighan’s tail, sending bright orange sparks showering into the dust.
’Chains... I need my chains...’
While her tail was still engaged, Morrighan thrust her left palm straight down into the dirt!
CRACK! CRACK! CRACK!
Four massive, shadow-forged abyssal chains erupted out of the mud directly beneath Vespera’s boots, coiling around her ankles and pulling tight.
Vespera felt the chilling stamina-draining cold of the abyssal chains locking her legs in place.
’Impulsive... but creative!’ Vespera evaluated internally, her eyes gleaming with genuine admiration. ’She chained a physical distraction straight into a crowd-control spell!’
"BRIMSTONE BOLT!" Morrighan screamed, thrusting both hands forward at point-blank range.
A massive smoky fireball of dark demonic fire shot straight for Vespera’s face.
Vespera didn’t panic.
She didn’t draw on her Tier 3 destructive spells like Fulgur Annihilation or Incineration Ray since she was explicitly keeping this fight strictly focused on her swordsmanship and controlled output.
HUMMMMM!
Vespera channeled her Gold Core wind mana through her single blade, executing a high-speed vertical slash.
VWOOSH!
A crescent of compressed wind pressure exploded from her steel tip, slicing the incoming brimstone fireball cleanly in half.
The two halves of dark fire detonated harmlessly behind Vespera, scorching the distant mud.
CRUNCH!
With a flex of her mana, Vespera shattered the abyssal chains around her ankles, stepping free from the dark links.
Morrighan was panting heavily now as she landed.
"Hah... Hah..."
The heavy toll of `Demon’s Resolve` was already starting to drain her stamina reserves, but her golden eyes burned with ferocious unyielding spirit.
"AGAIN!" Morrighan bellowed, drawing deep on her lingering reserves.
She rushed forward, throwing a barrage of heavy, gauntleted punches, tail sweeps, and brimstone blasts.
CLANG! BAM! CLANG! VWOOSH!
Vespera retreated step-by-step across the clearing, parrying every strike with her longsword blurring into a silver circle of steel.
Throughout the intense exchange, Vespera continuously maintained the Second Style: Rip-Current Perception.
She cycled ambient moisture through her internal circuits, pushing her mind to filter out the chaotic brimstone heat and read Morrighan’s underlying movement telegraphs.
’I need this to work...’
Ten seconds... twenty seconds... thirty seconds of high-speed clashing passed.
Morrighan’s movements were gradually slowing down.
Her shoulder was dipping half an inch low on every third punch and her breath control was becoming ragged.
And then... for a single, fleeting microsecond...
In Vespera’s heightened perception, the ambient moisture pressure suddenly clicked into place.

A single razor-thin wisp of glowing blue light current materialized in the air... pointing directly to a microscopic opening under Morrighan’s left armpit as she raised her gauntlet for a heavy overhead strike.
’THERE!’ Vespera’s mind screamed.
It wasn’t a full perfect vision of the Second Style... it was barely a slim, brief opening that lasted for a fraction of a second but it was enough.
SWISH!
Vespera executed an instantaneous forward step, slipping cleanly under Morrighan’s raised mythril gauntlet.
She didn’t use the cutting edge of her sword.

Instead, Vespera reversed her grip, driving the flat pommel of her longsword precisely into the open gap under Morrighan’s left rib cage, followed by a swift, gentle tap of her gloved hand against the side of Morrighan’s neck.
THWACK!
The precise impact shut down the nerve cluster along Morrighan’s spine.
The dark cursed magic circles spinning around the clearing instantly shattered into harmless black particles as the crimson aura around Morrighan’s body faded away.
"Ah..." Morrighan let out a soft, airy breath.
Her molten-gold eyes lost their focus with her long crimson hair trailing in the wind as her knees buckled.
As her body tipped forward, falling toward the damp grass, a single cute and flustered thought flashed through Morrighan’s fading consciousness.
’Ah... her hand was so warm... I am finally... home...’
"My Lord..." Morrighan whispered softly.
THUD.
Morrighan’s tall horned frame landed gently on the mud, completely unconscious, a peaceful contented smile resting on her dark lips.
Vespera lowered her sword, letting out a long, quiet breath as steam rose from her blade.
She looked down at the sleeping demoness, reaching up to adjust her spatial hood as a slight, sheepish look touched her face.
"Ah..." Vespera muttered softly to herself, looking at Morwenna. "Did I... did I go a little too hard on her?"
Morwenna chuckled dryly from atop her wolf, shaking her head.
"She’s fine, Captain. Her ribs are intact. She just needs an hour of sleep."
Vespera looked at her single steel longsword with her thoughts turning back to the slim, flickering wisp of the Second Style she had managed to trigger at the very end.

’I barely caught that opening...’ Vespera thought. ’The Second Style really is a nightmare to master in real-time combat. I couldn’t push my perception speed as fast as I wanted... I just need to train a lot more but damn...’
Nobody else was coming to her.
’Are they afraid?’
Meanwhile, far across the central battlefield...
The chaotic clash between the main forces was reaching a terrifying elemental climax.
Ignis... the Flame Hero and Frost... the Glacial Hero were completely terrorizing both sides of the clearing.
Because they were operating as a paired elemental Hero team, their combined mana output was creating immense collateral destruction.

Ignis was hurling fifty-foot fireballs that incinerated defensive barriers, while Frost was casting wide-area blizzards that froze the weapons of both Sky’s infantrymen and Blessed Land’s Vanguard women alike.
They did not care about casualties at all.
"GET BACK!" a Shieldmaiden screamed out, retreating as a wall of blue ice spiked out of the ground.

"HAHAHAHA!" Ignis laughed hysterically, his hands engulfed in white-hot flames as he floated ten feet above the scorched dirt. "Is this all the famous Blessed Land has to offer?! You can’t even close the distance through our dual domain!"
Beside him, Frost hovered with cold arrogant detachment with his icy blue eyes scanning the disoriented troops below.
"It’s useless," Frost declared coldly. "Our anti-gravity rune arrays protect us from ground lockdown, and our combined elemental density cannot be pierced by simple infantry charges!"
Sky’s disoriented troops and Blessed Land’s Vanguard were both being pushed back by the unbridled environmental pressure of fire and ice.
...Suddenly...
HUMMMMMMM!
Directly beneath the floating boots of Ignis and Frost, the damp scorched earth began to glow with a brilliant deep-sapphire light.
A massive intricate Runic magic circle stretching thirty yards wide materialized on the ground, its complex runic geometric lines spinning with terrifying power.
SWISH!
A sleek elegant figure stepped out from behind a frozen rock pillar.
Rowenna calmly walked into the open clearing.
She reached up with her gloved hand, smoothly pulling back her dark hood to reveal her striking features as her long hair fluttered in the wind.
She wasn’t holding any staff as her hands were completely empty, resting casually at her sides.
Ignis and Frost stopped their attacks mid-air, snapping their heads down to glare at the lone Rune Weaver.

"Look who finally stepped out!" Ignis taunted arrogantly with a wide sneer on his face. "A runic arcanist! Don’t bother trying to pull us down with spatial tricks, woman! We carry special High-Tier Anti-Gravity Runes carved directly into our chest armor! Your basic spells won’t even nudge us—"
Rowenna paused in her tracks.
She looked up at the two hovering Heroes with her sharp eyes completely unbothered as her voice cut cleanly through their taunts with icy authority.
"Yes..." Rowenna interrupted smoothly, a sharp, dangerous grin curving her lips. "...I know you have anti-gravity runes."
Ignis and Frost froze, their eyes widening in sudden instinctual horror.
KRA-THOOOOOOOOOM!
Before either Hero could react, Rowenna snapped her right fingers.
KABAAAAAM!
The deep-sapphire runic array on the ground violently exploded with twenty times the force of standard atmospheric gravity.
The space above the circle visually distorted, bending light and air inward like a collapsing black hole.
CRASH! KABAGHHH!
The anti-gravity runes carved into Ignis and Frost’s armor instantly shattered under the astronomical weight of the 20x gravity well.
Both Heroes didn’t just fall... they were forcefully, violently slammed straight down from mid-air into the bedrock like two dropped iron anvils!
BOOOOOOM!
The velocity of their collision smashed a forty-foot crater into the dirt.𝐟𝕣𝗲𝕖𝕨𝗲𝐛𝗻𝗼𝐯𝗲𝚕.𝗰𝚘𝐦

Bedrock shattered into fine powder as Ignis and Frost were pinned flat on their bellies in the dirt, the overwhelming 20x gravity pressing down on their spines so hard they couldn’t even lift a single finger or vent a breath of fire.
Rowenna stood at the edge of the crater, looking down at the two trapped Heroes with a calm predatory smirk on her face.
She dusted off her sleeves, her voice echoing coldly across the silent battlefield.
"I’ve been listening..." Rowenna finished smoothly. "...from the very beginning."
