chapters.title: Chapter 322: Legacy Of A Dragon Slayer
paragraphs: Brida stepped heavily forward, towering over the completely immobilized Hero.
The Titan Bastion raised her colossal Astral-Forged Void Cleaver high over her head.
Her red eyes burned with final executionary intent.
She was preparing to bring the massive axe down to cleave Kassandra completely in half.
Tasmin pulled back hard on her chains, tightening the metal links around Kassandra’s throat, preparing to sever the Hero’s head from her shoulders in a brutal, synchronized decapitation.
"Gah! Fuu!"
Kassandra squeezed her eyes shut, waiting for the inevitable end but the strike never landed.
A sudden incomprehensible shift in the atmospheric pressure washed over the center of the battlefield.
It wasn’t the heavy, crushing weight of gravity. It wasn’t the roaring heat of fire or the chilling bite of frost either.
It was a cold and terrifying silence.
Before Brida could swing her axe downward, and before Tasmin could pull her chains taut...
An invisible and geometrically perfect slash cut straight through the air directly between them.
The strike did not carry any roaring sound effects.
It did not create a massive shockwave of displaced air. It was simply a localized deletion of space.
The invisible slash cleanly severed Tasmin’s super-heated Eclipse-Thread chains exactly down the middle.
The incredibly dense mythril links snapped effortlessly and fell into the mud.

The exact same invisible strike continued forward, cleanly cutting a microscopic perfectly horizontal line straight through the thick, adamantine face of Brida’s tower shield, leaving a razor-thin glowing gap entirely across the metal surface without actually applying any force to Brida herself.
"Huh?!" Both Brida and Tasmin let out.
Finally, the invisible strike reached the fading dissolving walls of the Shield World domain.
The remaining pink fabric of the domain was sliced completely in half, collapsing instantly into a harmless shower of pink dust that rained down over the crushed bedrock.
Brida froze completely.
Her massive axe remained held high in the air.
Her red eyes widened in genuine instinctual shock as she looked down at the clean, perfect cut running across her previously unbreakable shield.
Tasmin instantly dropped her severed chain handles.
She used a quick Phantom Leap to blink twenty feet backward, landing in a low, hyper-defensive crouch.
Her twin shortswords were raised and ready with her eyes scanning the clearing with a bit of a panic.
Kassandra, suddenly freed from the agonizing burning chains, dropped heavily onto one knee in the mud.
She was panting heavily, clutching her bruised throat, but as she looked up through the settling pink dust, a deeply relieved smirk touched her lips.
Footsteps approached through the quiet clearing.
Tap!
Tap!
Slow unbothered footsteps walking calmly across the shattered bedrock.
The tall, lean figure of a man stepped out from the dissipating dust cloud.
He was dressed in the high-quality combat uniform of Sky’s elite vanguard.𝘧𝘳𝘦ℯ𝓌𝘦𝒷𝘯𝑜𝑣𝘦𝓁.𝒸𝘰𝓂
His posture was perfectly relaxed with his hands resting casually at his sides, completely lacking any aggressive combat stance.
A thick dark cloth blindfold was wrapped securely around his eyes, obscuring the upper half of his face entirely.
It was Hiro.
Kassandra let out a long ragged breath, looking up at the blindfolded Hero from her position in the mud.
"It is... about time..." Kassandra coughed with her voice hoarse from the void flames. "I was beginning to think... you were just going to stand back and let these two monsters execute me."
Hiro stopped walking. He stood perfectly still exactly ten feet away from the tense, highly defensive forms of Brida and Tasmin.
He didn’t draw a weapon.
Hiro simply tilted his head toward the two S-Rank women with an eerie, serene smile curving his lips.
"You must forgive my tardiness, Kassandra," Hiro spoke.
’Is this really the way he speaks? Aeli said he was quite different initially...’
His voice was incredibly smooth and lacking any sort of fear or adrenaline.

"I was simply observing," Hiro continued calmly. "I must commend the strength of the Blessed Land’s Vanguard. It is exceedingly rare to see someone breach the physical hardness of the Shield World with such effortless, brutal synergy. You two are truly magnificent warriors."
Brida slowly lowered her Void Cleaver.
Her boisterous, laughing demeanor completely vanished, replaced by the grim focus of a veteran.
Her heavy boots shifted cautiously in the mud and her eyes locked onto the blindfolded man with deep instinctual caution.
"Who the hell is this guy?" Brida muttered, her voice dropping into a low, dangerous growl. "I didn’t even feel him swing... There was no kinetic buildup and no muscle telegraph at all."
Tasmin’s crimson eyes were narrowed into sharp lethal slits.
Her shadow mana curled tightly around her boots, entirely ready to execute a supreme evasion maneuver at a moment’s notice.
"Do not let your guard down, Brida," Tasmin warned softly, her voice tight with immense tension. "His core signature... it is completely suppressed. I cannot read his depth."
Hiro let out a soft, highly amused chuckle. He raised his right hand slowly toward his face.

"You are on the offensive," Hiro noted calmly with his fingers gently grasping the edge of his dark cloth blindfold. "That is good. Caution is the hallmark of true veterans. However... mere physical caution will not save you from what comes next."
The atmosphere in the clearing plummeted into absolute, freezing dread.
Slowly and deliberately, Hiro pulled the blindfold away from his face, letting the dark cloth slip from his fingers and fall silently into the mud.
Brida and Tasmin both tensed, expecting to see glowing magical eyes capable of casting devastating illusions or targeted spells.
Instead, they saw nothing?
Hiro’s eyes were completely gone.
His eye sockets were deep, hollow, and heavily scarred, bearing the gruesome marks of a brutal violent gashing that had occurred a very long time ago.
The flesh had healed perfectly around the empty voids, leaving a chilling macabre visage of permanent physical blindness.
Yet, he wasn’t looking at them with empty sockets.
As Hiro stood there with his ruined face exposed to the open air, a terrifying unnatural phenomenon began to spread across the battlefield.
From the empty voids of his scarred eye sockets, a brilliant piercing blue light began to violently leak outward.
The light didn’t just illuminate his face. It bled directly into the surrounding environment, altering the very fabric of reality around him.
Deep, jagged lines of glowing blue energy began to spread out from the crushed dirt beneath his boots.

The lines crawled rapidly across the shattered bedrock, climbed up the broken stone pillars, and etched themselves directly into the ambient air itself, forming a massive three-dimensional geometric web.
The blue lines mapped absolutely everything.
They mapped every single pebble, every blade of grass, the exact angle of Brida’s heavy axe, and the microscopic shadow seams surrounding Tasmin’s boots.
It was spatial awareness at its finest.

"It has been a very long time since I lost my physical sight," Hiro whispered, his serene smile remaining perfectly intact even as the terrifying blue light flooded the battlefield. "The physical wounds healed... but the darkness remained. However... true sight does not require eyes."
The glowing blue jagged lines suddenly shifted entirely.
They changed from a bright sapphire into a deep and infinitely suffocating shade of dark purple.

The entire world surrounding the girls was instantly drowned in the suffocating purple light, suppressing the ambient mana, locking the coordinates entirely in place, and subjecting both Brida and Tasmin to a terrifying inescapable domain of perception.
Hiro stood perfectly still in the absolute center of the purple hellscape, his voice echoing perfectly into their minds.
"Mind’s Eye."
The eastern ridge of the Umbral Basin offered a panoramic view of the chaotic blood-soaked battlefield below.
Gideon stood perfectly still near the absolute edge of the jagged stone cliff.
He did not flinch as a stray volley of heavy magical artillery fire from the distant Blessed Land Vanguard slammed into the bedrock thirty yards to his left.
The resulting explosion sent a violent shower of dirt, ash, and stone shrapnel washing over his heavy mythril plate armor, but he didn’t even raise a hand to shield his face.
The Last Dragon-Slayer merely watched the carnage unfold.
His pale gray eyes, marked by an unnatural golden ring around the pupil, scanned the war zone with the cold look of an apex predator.
A large gruesome scar ran vertically entirely across his left eye.
It was a permanent, horrific reminder of a hunt that had gone terribly wrong in his youth.
The flesh had healed over the decades, but the memory of the beast that had taken his eye had not faded for even a single second.
From his elevated vantage point, he observed the heavy infantry lines of Sky’s army... The Unmovable Wall colliding violently with the women of the Blessed Land’s army.
It was a massacre.
Down in the western quadrant, he saw the blinding pink flashes of Kassandra’s defensive dome being deployed, only to violently dissolve into useless dust moments later.

In the central clearing, he watched the catastrophic explosions generated by Ignis and Frost, only to see both elemental Wardens forcefully and brutally crushed into the dirt by a massive deep-purple spatial singularity.
Sky’s elite commanders were falling one by one, completely overwhelmed by the perfection of the enemy forces.
Gideon’s jaw tightened.
He let out a low, disgusted scoff.
"Weak," Gideon muttered.
His voice was a deep rasp that carried easily over the howling winds of the battlefield.

"You rely entirely on your shiny little elemental toys and static spatial domains," Gideon criticized the unconscious Wardens below. "The moment an enemy bypasses your predictable formulas, you fall apart like unbaked clay. You call yourselves Heroes, but you do not even know how to properly bleed. Pathetic..."
Gideon rested his heavy leather-clad gauntlets on the thick pommel of his massive weapon.
The Dragon-Bone Greatsword was planted tip-first into the solid stone directly in front of his boots.
It was an absolute monstrosity of a weapon, a Tier 4 relic forged entirely from the spinal column of an ancient primordial dragon that his great-grandfather had slain centuries ago.
The blade was impossibly sharp, its edge carrying the lingering hateful power of its original owner.
Gideon was not here to play infantry commander.
He didn’t care about Lord Sky’s territorial expansion.
He didn’t care about Blessed Land’s incredible synergy or the shifting borders of the Sovereign Realm.
He had joined Sky’s mobile fortress for one specific reason.
Sky’s territory constantly moved into the most dangerous untamed sectors of the Unknown Zones, crossing paths with some of the rarest monsters in existence.
Gideon was here for a hunt.

His pale gray eyes shifted away from the main melee line, scanning through the thick clouds of black smoke until they locked onto a single, isolated figure tearing through a cluster of Sky’s heavy shield-bearers near the northern ruins.
Talira.
She was currently fighting in her humanoid form.
Her long cascading ruby-red hair whipped wildly in the wind as she moved with terrifying lethality.
Two polished dragon horns curved proudly from her temples.
Her long scale-armored crimson tail swished violently behind her boots with the heavy mythril-tipped spike at the end shattering enemy shields and ribcages with every single sweeping arc.
The Hunter’s Talisman hanging around Gideon’s neck grew instantly, searingly hot against his scarred chest.
HUMMMMMM!
The Dragon-Bone Greatsword began to vibrate violently in his grip, humming with an eager bloodlust as the weapon recognized the presence of its mortal enemy.
Gideon’s pulse began to race.
A deep throb echoed in his ears. It was a familiar, intoxicating, adrenaline-fueled rhythm that he hadn’t felt in such a long time.
It had been so incredibly long since he had actually seen a living breathing dragon.
"There you are..." Gideon whispered softly.
A terrifying obsessive grin slowly stretched across his heavily scarred face.
His mind was instantly assaulted by a violent inescapable flashback.
He saw the massive, scaly claws tearing through the dark sky of his youth...
He felt the searing unbearable heat of white-hot dragon fire instantly melting his father’s armor into liquid slag.

He remembered the agonizing pain of the jagged claw slicing across his left eye, permanently taking half his vision and leaving him bleeding out in the freezing mud while the beast flew away into the clouds.
His clan’s legacy was a fading ember.
His ancestors had been one of the most feared warriors in the entire Sovereign Realm.
They had hunted beasts that could level entire mountain ranges yet, Gideon had spent his entire life obsessively training for a hunt that had never actually come.
Until this exact moment.
Gideon wanted to hunt a Dragon.

Her red eyes burned with final executionary intent.
She was preparing to bring the massive axe down to cleave Kassandra completely in half.
Tasmin pulled back hard on her chains, tightening the metal links around Kassandra’s throat, preparing to sever the Hero’s head from her shoulders in a brutal, synchronized decapitation.
"Gah!
Fuu!"
Kassandra squeezed her eyes shut, waiting for the inevitable end but the strike never landed.
A sudden incomprehensible shift in the atmospheric pressure washed over the center of the battlefield.
It wasn’t the heavy, crushing weight of gravity.
It wasn’t the roaring heat of fire or the chilling bite of frost either.
It was a cold and terrifying silence.
Before Brida could swing her axe downward, and before Tasmin could pull her chains taut...
An invisible and geometrically perfect slash cut straight through the air directly between them.
The strike did not carry any roaring sound effects.
It did not create a massive shockwave of displaced air.
It was simply a localized deletion of space.
The invisible slash cleanly severed Tasmin’s super-heated Eclipse-Thread chains exactly down the middle.
The incredibly dense mythril links snapped effortlessly and fell into the mud.

The exact same invisible strike continued forward, cleanly cutting a microscopic perfectly horizontal line straight through the thick, adamantine face of Brida’s tower shield, leaving a razor-thin glowing gap entirely across the metal surface without actually applying any force to Brida herself.
"Huh?!" Both Brida and Tasmin let out.
Finally, the invisible strike reached the fading dissolving walls of the Shield World domain.
The remaining pink fabric of the domain was sliced completely in half, collapsing instantly into a harmless shower of pink dust that rained down over the crushed bedrock.
Brida froze completely.
Her massive axe remained held high in the air.
Her red eyes widened in genuine instinctual shock as she looked down at the clean, perfect cut running across her previously unbreakable shield.
Tasmin instantly dropped her severed chain handles.
She used a quick Phantom Leap to blink twenty feet backward, landing in a low, hyper-defensive crouch.
Her twin shortswords were raised and ready with her eyes scanning the clearing with a bit of a panic.
Kassandra, suddenly freed from the agonizing burning chains, dropped heavily onto one knee in the mud.
She was panting heavily, clutching her bruised throat, but as she looked up through the settling pink dust, a deeply relieved smirk touched her lips.
Footsteps approached through the quiet clearing.
Tap!
Tap!
Slow unbothered footsteps walking calmly across the shattered bedrock.
The tall, lean figure of a man stepped out from the dissipating dust cloud.
He was dressed in the high-quality combat uniform of Sky’s elite vanguard.𝘧𝘳𝘦ℯ𝓌𝘦𝒷𝘯𝑜𝑣𝘦𝓁.𝒸𝘰𝓂
His posture was perfectly relaxed with his hands resting casually at his sides, completely lacking any aggressive combat stance.
A thick dark cloth blindfold was wrapped securely around his eyes, obscuring the upper half of his face entirely.
It was Hiro.
Kassandra let out a long ragged breath, looking up at the blindfolded Hero from her position in the mud.
"It is... about time..." Kassandra coughed with her voice hoarse from the void flames.
"I was beginning to think... you were just going to stand back and let these two monsters execute me."
Hiro stopped walking.
He stood perfectly still exactly ten feet away from the tense, highly defensive forms of Brida and Tasmin.
He didn’t draw a weapon.
Hiro simply tilted his head toward the two S-Rank women with an eerie, serene smile curving his lips.
"You must forgive my tardiness, Kassandra," Hiro spoke.
’Is this really the way he speaks?
Aeli said he was quite different initially...’
His voice was incredibly smooth and lacking any sort of fear or adrenaline.
"I was simply observing," Hiro continued calmly.
"I must commend the strength of the Blessed Land’s Vanguard.
It is exceedingly rare to see someone breach the physical hardness of the Shield World with such effortless, brutal synergy.
You two are truly magnificent warriors."
Brida slowly lowered her Void Cleaver.
Her boisterous, laughing demeanor completely vanished, replaced by the grim focus of a veteran.
Her heavy boots shifted cautiously in the mud and her eyes locked onto the blindfolded man with deep instinctual caution.
"Who the hell is this guy?" Brida muttered, her voice dropping into a low, dangerous growl.
"I didn’t even feel him swing...
There was no kinetic buildup and no muscle telegraph at all."
Tasmin’s crimson eyes were narrowed into sharp lethal slits.
Her shadow mana curled tightly around her boots, entirely ready to execute a supreme evasion maneuver at a moment’s notice.
"Do not let your guard down, Brida," Tasmin warned softly, her voice tight with immense tension.
"His core signature... it is completely suppressed.
I cannot read his depth."
Hiro let out a soft, highly amused chuckle.
He raised his right hand slowly toward his face.
"You are on the offensive," Hiro noted calmly with his fingers gently grasping the edge of his dark cloth blindfold.
"That is good.
Caution is the hallmark of true veterans.
However... mere physical caution will not save you from what comes next."
The atmosphere in the clearing plummeted into absolute, freezing dread.
Slowly and deliberately, Hiro pulled the blindfold away from his face, letting the dark cloth slip from his fingers and fall silently into the mud.
Brida and Tasmin both tensed, expecting to see glowing magical eyes capable of casting devastating illusions or targeted spells.
Instead, they saw nothing?
Hiro’s eyes were completely gone.
His eye sockets were deep, hollow, and heavily scarred, bearing the gruesome marks of a brutal violent gashing that had occurred a very long time ago.
The flesh had healed perfectly around the empty voids, leaving a chilling macabre visage of permanent physical blindness.
Yet, he wasn’t looking at them with empty sockets.
As Hiro stood there with his ruined face exposed to the open air, a terrifying unnatural phenomenon began to spread across the battlefield.
From the empty voids of his scarred eye sockets, a brilliant piercing blue light began to violently leak outward.
The light didn’t just illuminate his face.
It bled directly into the surrounding environment, altering the very fabric of reality around him.
Deep, jagged lines of glowing blue energy began to spread out from the crushed dirt beneath his boots.

The lines crawled rapidly across the shattered bedrock, climbed up the broken stone pillars, and etched themselves directly into the ambient air itself, forming a massive three-dimensional geometric web.
The blue lines mapped absolutely everything.
They mapped every single pebble, every blade of grass, the exact angle of Brida’s heavy axe, and the microscopic shadow seams surrounding Tasmin’s boots.
It was spatial awareness at its finest.
"It has been a very long time since I lost my physical sight," Hiro whispered, his serene smile remaining perfectly intact even as the terrifying blue light flooded the battlefield.
"The physical wounds healed... but the darkness remained.
However... true sight does not require eyes."
The glowing blue jagged lines suddenly shifted entirely.
They changed from a bright sapphire into a deep and infinitely suffocating shade of dark purple.

The entire world surrounding the girls was instantly drowned in the suffocating purple light, suppressing the ambient mana, locking the coordinates entirely in place, and subjecting both Brida and Tasmin to a terrifying inescapable domain of perception.
Hiro stood perfectly still in the absolute center of the purple hellscape, his voice echoing perfectly into their minds.
"Mind’s Eye."
The eastern ridge of the Umbral Basin offered a panoramic view of the chaotic blood-soaked battlefield below.
Gideon stood perfectly still near the absolute edge of the jagged stone cliff.
He did not flinch as a stray volley of heavy magical artillery fire from the distant Blessed Land Vanguard slammed into the bedrock thirty yards to his left.
The resulting explosion sent a violent shower of dirt, ash, and stone shrapnel washing over his heavy mythril plate armor, but he didn’t even raise a hand to shield his face.
The Last Dragon-Slayer merely watched the carnage unfold.
His pale gray eyes, marked by an unnatural golden ring around the pupil, scanned the war zone with the cold look of an apex predator.
A large gruesome scar ran vertically entirely across his left eye.
It was a permanent, horrific reminder of a hunt that had gone terribly wrong in his youth.
The flesh had healed over the decades, but the memory of the beast that had taken his eye had not faded for even a single second.
From his elevated vantage point, he observed the heavy infantry lines of Sky’s army...
The Unmovable Wall colliding violently with the women of the Blessed Land’s army.
It was a massacre.
Down in the western quadrant, he saw the blinding pink flashes of Kassandra’s defensive dome being deployed, only to violently dissolve into useless dust moments later.

In the central clearing, he watched the catastrophic explosions generated by Ignis and Frost, only to see both elemental Wardens forcefully and brutally crushed into the dirt by a massive deep-purple spatial singularity.
Sky’s elite commanders were falling one by one, completely overwhelmed by the perfection of the enemy forces.
Gideon’s jaw tightened.
He let out a low, disgusted scoff.
"Weak," Gideon muttered.
His voice was a deep rasp that carried easily over the howling winds of the battlefield.
"You rely entirely on your shiny little elemental toys and static spatial domains," Gideon criticized the unconscious Wardens below.
"The moment an enemy bypasses your predictable formulas, you fall apart like unbaked clay.
You call yourselves Heroes, but you do not even know how to properly bleed.
Pathetic..."
Gideon rested his heavy leather-clad gauntlets on the thick pommel of his massive weapon.
The Dragon-Bone Greatsword was planted tip-first into the solid stone directly in front of his boots.
It was an absolute monstrosity of a weapon, a Tier 4 relic forged entirely from the spinal column of an ancient primordial dragon that his great-grandfather had slain centuries ago.
The blade was impossibly sharp, its edge carrying the lingering hateful power of its original owner.
Gideon was not here to play infantry commander.
He didn’t care about Lord Sky’s territorial expansion.
He didn’t care about Blessed Land’s incredible synergy or the shifting borders of the Sovereign Realm.
He had joined Sky’s mobile fortress for one specific reason.
Sky’s territory constantly moved into the most dangerous untamed sectors of the Unknown Zones, crossing paths with some of the rarest monsters in existence.
Gideon was here for a hunt.

His pale gray eyes shifted away from the main melee line, scanning through the thick clouds of black smoke until they locked onto a single, isolated figure tearing through a cluster of Sky’s heavy shield-bearers near the northern ruins.
Talira.
She was currently fighting in her humanoid form.
Her long cascading ruby-red hair whipped wildly in the wind as she moved with terrifying lethality.
Two polished dragon horns curved proudly from her temples.
Her long scale-armored crimson tail swished violently behind her boots with the heavy mythril-tipped spike at the end shattering enemy shields and ribcages with every single sweeping arc.
The Hunter’s Talisman hanging around Gideon’s neck grew instantly, searingly hot against his scarred chest.
HUMMMMMM!
The Dragon-Bone Greatsword began to vibrate violently in his grip, humming with an eager bloodlust as the weapon recognized the presence of its mortal enemy.
Gideon’s pulse began to race.
A deep throb echoed in his ears.
It was a familiar, intoxicating, adrenaline-fueled rhythm that he hadn’t felt in such a long time.
It had been so incredibly long since he had actually seen a living breathing dragon.
"There you are..." Gideon whispered softly.
A terrifying obsessive grin slowly stretched across his heavily scarred face.
His mind was instantly assaulted by a violent inescapable flashback.
He saw the massive, scaly claws tearing through the dark sky of his youth...
He felt the searing unbearable heat of white-hot dragon fire instantly melting his father’s armor into liquid slag.

He remembered the agonizing pain of the jagged claw slicing across his left eye, permanently taking half his vision and leaving him bleeding out in the freezing mud while the beast flew away into the clouds.
His clan’s legacy was a fading ember.
His ancestors had been one of the most feared warriors in the entire Sovereign Realm.
They had hunted beasts that could level entire mountain ranges yet, Gideon had spent his entire life obsessively training for a hunt that had never actually come.
Until this exact moment.
Gideon wanted to hunt a Dragon.

chapters.title: Chapter 323: Legacy Of A Dragon Slayer [II]
paragraphs: "I can smell you, dragon," Gideon hissed, gripping the thick hilt of his greatsword so hard the bones in his knuckles popped. "Your fire... Your fear... Your arrogance... You think you are the apex predator on this entire battlefield but you have never faced a true Dragon-Slayer."
Gideon smoothly pulled the massive Dragon-Bone Greatsword out of the bedrock.
He didn’t announce his presence and he didn’t issue a grand, honorable challenge to the Vanguard.
’It’s not like I care about the rules anyway.’ He thought.
Gideon simply stepped off the edge of the stone ridge with his heavy mythril armor carrying him into a rapid forty-foot freefall directly toward the northern ruins.
KRA-THOOOOOM!
Gideon landed directly in the center of the muddy clearing, precisely thirty yards away from Talira’s current position.
The physical density of his landing shattered the bedrock upon impact, sending a massive shockwave of displaced dirt, mud, and stone shrapnel flying violently outward in a perfect circle.
"Huh?"
Talira had just finished driving her armor-plated fist straight through the dense chest plate of a heavy guard.
She casually dropped the unconscious, bleeding soldier into the mud.
Her glowing golden eyes, marked by their vertical reptilian slits, snapped instantly toward the sudden impact point.
She saw the towering scarred man standing in the fresh crater, holding a sword made entirely of ancient yellowed bone.
Instantly, Talira’s draconic instincts flared with a primal warning.
The air around the man smelled intensely of her slaughtered kin and deep generational hatred.
"Who are you?" Talira demanded.
Her voice was a deep growl that carried a vibration, making the loose pebbles on the ground shake.
"You do not smell like the other fragile humans of this army," Talira noted with her scale-armored tail swishing aggressively behind her. "You reek of death."
Gideon slowly rolled his neck, the thick joints popping audibly in the quiet clearing.
He raised the massive Dragon-Bone Greatsword, pointing the jagged pale tip directly at the center of Talira’s chest.
"I am the man who is going to peel the scales from your corpse and forge them into a new set of armor for my clan," Gideon replied coldly.
A sudden sharp pulse of aggressive golden lightning mana erupted from Gideon’s left hand.
VZZZZZZT!
He cast his Hunter’s Mark.

The special draconic debuff shot across the thirty-yard gap instantly as it completely bypassed Talira’s natural, radiating aura and etched a faint glowing golden sigil directly onto her left collarbone!
Talira frowned deeply, feeling a sudden unnatural vulnerability wash over her incredibly dense scales exactly where the mark sat.
Before she could process the debuff, Gideon exploded forward.
He didn’t use a high-tier spatial blink as he relied entirely on raw explosive physical acceleration!
BOOM! BOOM! BOOM!
His boots tore massive trenches into the mud as he crossed the thirty-yard distance in a fraction of seconds.
He raised the heavy bone sword high over his head, fully committing to the execution.
"Scale-Breaker Strike!" Gideon roared.
He swung the massive blade downward with terrifying velocity.
The jagged edge of the sword hummed with concentrated, armor-piercing lightning mana that was specifically calibrated over centuries of research to cleanly bypass draconic scale defenses.
Talira’s golden eyes widened.
Her primordial combat instincts screamed that she could not simply tank this hit with her raw durability.
She crossed her arms aggressively above her head, engaging the dense resistant scales of her custom runic arm vambraces, bracing her entire frame for the massive impact.
CLANGGGGGGG!
The collision of the Dragon-Bone Greatsword against her heavy armor created a deafening metallic roar that shook the very air.
Bright orange sparks and jagged, wild arcs of golden lightning showered violently across the mud.
Talira gritted her teeth with her boots sinking three full inches deep into the solid bedrock from the downward pressure.
The strike was incredibly heavy, far heavier than any normal human should have been able to generate!
But Talira was not a normal human... She was a Primordial Crimson Dragon.
"You hit hard for a fragile little human," Talira growled with her lips pulling back to reveal sharp elongated fangs. "But not hard enough!"
Talira aggressively shoved her arms upward, violently parrying the heavy greatsword away from her body.
Simultaneously, she pivoted heavily on her left heel, utilizing the massive unnatural momentum of her scale-armored crimson tail.
VWOOOOOOSH!
The heavy tail whipped through the air like a lethal steel mace.
The mythril-tipped spike, forged explicitly for her by Thora in the Blessed Land, aimed directly for Gideon’s exposed ribs.
Gideon didn’t retreat.
His pale gray eyes tracked the microscopic muscle twitch in Talira’s hips before the tail even moved.
He dropped his center of gravity instantly, bringing the flat, broad side of his bone greatsword down to perfectly block the incoming tail sweep!
WHAM!
The mythril spike slammed into the dragon-bone blade with multi-ton force.
The impact sent a massive shockwave of displaced air tearing through the clearing, forcing Gideon to slide five feet backward through the thick mud.
However, thanks to his Slayer’s Resilience passive trait, the immense bone-crushing blunt force of the dragon’s physical attack was completely reduced by forty percent.
Gideon didn’t lose his balance, he refused to stagger.
He simply used the backward slide to instantly re-chamber his heavy weapon.
"Is that all the physical strength a primordial beast can muster when trapped inside a pathetic human shell?!" Gideon mocked violently, his voice laced with venomous pride.
Gideon surged forward again.
He swung the heavy greatsword in a rapid brutal flurry of horizontal slashes, heavy vertical chops, and blindingly fast thrusts.
Talira met him blow for blow. She didn’t draw a weapon as her physical body was the ultimate weapon!
She used her heavy, armor-plated gauntlets, her dense crimson scales, and the hardened bone of her forearms to repeatedly parry, deflect, and violently redirect the massive bone sword!
CLACK! CLANG! WHAM!
The two heavy-melee specialists engaged in a terrifying high-speed clash of raw physical power.
Every single time their attacks collided, the shockwaves blew away the surrounding mud, creating a rapidly expanding crater of destroyed bedrock beneath their shifting boots.
Despite her stats, Gideon was completely dominating the flow of the fight.
His entire martial art style had been meticulously engineered over centuries by his ancestors to specifically hunt humanoid dragon-kin and fully transformed dragons.

He knew exactly how Talira’s joints moved... He knew the precise reach of her tail, the exact wind-up time required for her to breathe fire, and the exact blind spots created by her peripheral vision.
He repeatedly slipped cleanly inside her guard, delivering brutal, grazing cuts across her ribs, her thighs, and her forearms.
SHRRRR-IP!
The Dragon-Bane Edge passive of his weapon ensured that every single minor cut inflicted a deep burning pain that actively bypassed her rapid regeneration.
"GHK!" Talira grunted, stumbling backward as the greatsword opened a shallow bleeding gash across her right bicep.
However, even while taking accumulating damage, Talira was still a monster.
Her combat adaptability was terrifying.
She quickly recognized that fighting him in a purely technical martial exchange was a losing battle.
He had too much specialized technique. He had trained his entire life for this exact specific scenario.
So, she changed the rules.
As Gideon stepped forward to deliver a heavy thrust toward her stomach, Talira didn’t try to block it with her arms.
Instead, she simply opened her mouth.
FWOOOOOOSH.
A massive point-blank torrent of white-hot volcanic fire erupted directly from her throat.
The fifty-foot wide river of pure annihilation engulfed Gideon completely before he could even finish his swing.
The flames were so incredibly hot that the surrounding bedrock instantly melted into a glowing bubbling river of liquid lava!
Gideon disappeared entirely inside the roaring column of absolute fire!
Talira ceased her breath, panting heavily with thick white smoke rising from her elongated fangs.
She expected to see a pile of melted mythril and charred bone resting in the lava.
Instead, as the smoke cleared, Gideon was still standing.
His heavy dragon-scale pauldrons were glowing red-hot, and the leather straps of his armor were smoking heavily, but his flesh was entirely intact.
The Slayer’s Resilience passive trait had neutralized the fatal intensity of the draconic fire, allowing him to endure the blast through pure grit.
"Nice try," Gideon snarled, his scarred face twisting into a demonic obsessive smile.
He raised his heavy right boot.
KRA-THOOOOOM!
Gideon slammed his boot violently into the liquid bedrock, executing his Thunderous Stomp.
A massive concentrated shockwave of golden lightning-charged earth exploded outward from his boot.
The seismic blast tore through the ground, slamming directly into Talira’s legs with terrifying voltage.
"AH!" Talira cried out.
The lightning mana violently disrupted her central nervous system...
The shock staggered her backward, completely seizing her leg muscles and forcing her to drop heavily onto one knee, entirely rooting her to the spot.
Gideon didn’t hesitate for a microsecond.
He raised the massive greatsword high above his head, stepping forward and aiming directly for her exposed ruby-red neck.
"Die, beast!" Gideon roared but Talira’s golden eyes did not show fear.
They did not show submission... They showed primordial rage instead.
’Y-you...’
She had spent over an entire century trapped inside the suffocating darkness of the Warden’s Eye artifact.
She had watched her mother rot.
She had been freed by the kindness of Lord Silas, and though she was arrogant at first... she had sworn to fight for the Blessed Land.
She refused to be killed by a pathetic, obsessive human wielding a rusty bone sword in the mud.
As the greatsword descended rapidly toward her neck, Talira’s draconic mana core violently erupted.
"I AM NOT PREY!" Talira screamed at the absolute top of her lungs!
Her massive aura exploded outward in a colossal shockwave of pure, unfiltered fire and wind mana.
The shockwave slammed heavily into Gideon.
It threw him completely off balance, forcing him to abort his execution swing and desperately slide ten feet backward through the mud just to stay on his feet.
"Fuck!"
Before his eyes, the humanoid woman vanished entirely into a blinding pillar of towering crimson light.
"RAHHHHHHH!"
A terrifying earth-shattering draconic roar echoed across the entire Umbral Basin.
The volume of the sound silenced the surrounding battlefield, causing the sky itself to tremble.
When the crimson light finally faded, Talira was no longer a humanoid woman.
She had unleashed her True Dragon Form.
A colossal Primordial Crimson Dragon towered over the battlefield.
Her wingspan stretched out to an immense terrifying fifty feet, casting a massive, suffocating shadow entirely over Gideon’s tiny form.
Her scales had hardened into a dark volcanic black-crimson hue that was virtually impenetrable.
Massive, jagged spikes ran down the entire length of her long, serpentine spine. Four massive, swept-back horns crowned her terrifying reptilian skull.
Her massive jaws opened wide, dripping with liquid fire. Her glowing golden eyes locked directly onto the Dragon-Slayer far below.
Gideon looked up at the towering, seventy-foot monster.
He didn’t show an ounce of fear.
His pale gray eyes widened with euphoric ecstasy as the adrenaline flooded his system like an intoxicating drug.
"Yes," Gideon whispered, his voice trembling with obsessive joy. "YES! Show me your true skin! Let me finally earn my bloodline!"𝕗𝐫𝚎𝗲𝘄𝐞𝕓𝐧𝕠𝘃𝕖𝐥.𝐜𝚘𝚖
Talira didn’t bother speaking.
She lunged forward, her massive, multi-ton jaws snapping down toward Gideon with terrifying supersonic speed.
Gideon engaged his high-speed footwork, diving aggressively to the left.
CRUNCH!
Talira’s massive jaws completely shattered the bedrock exactly where Gideon had been standing just a second prior, leaving a crater the size of a small house!
As Gideon rolled back onto his feet, he immediately swung his greatsword in a wide arc.
The heavy blade bit deeply into the dense scales of Talira’s massive, descending forearm.
SHRRRRR-IP!
Sparks flew wildly into the air.
The anti-dragon mana forced the blade cleanly through the outer layer of her thick scales, drawing a deep long gash of burning, glowing dragon blood that splashed against the mud.
"GRAHHH!"
Talira roared in genuine pain, but she did not retreat.
Her Combat Growth passive was already rapidly activating under the intense stress of the engagement.
’I see...’
She realized that staying on the ground allowed the tiny technical human to easily dodge her massive strikes and counter-attack her vulnerable joints.
So, Talira violently flapped her colossal fifty-foot wings.
FWOOOOOOSH!
The atmospheric downforce generated by the massive wing-beat created a hurricane.
The extreme wind pressure slammed into Gideon, forcing him to plant his greatsword deep into the dirt just to avoid being blown entirely across the clearing.
Talira launched herself into the sky as she ascended rapidly into the dark, smoke-filled storm clouds high above the battlefield.
"You cannot run from me!" Gideon screamed into the sky.
His obsession completely overrode his sense as he refused to let the hunt escape!
He yanked his greatsword out of the dirt.
Utilizing the lingering wind currents generated by her massive wings, he violently launched himself upward.

He repeatedly slipped cleanly inside her guard, delivering brutal, grazing cuts across her ribs, her thighs, and her forearms.
SHRRRR-IP!
The Dragon-Bane Edge passive of his weapon ensured that every single minor cut inflicted a deep burning pain that actively bypassed her rapid regeneration.
"GHK!" Talira grunted, stumbling backward as the greatsword opened a shallow bleeding gash across her right bicep.
However, even while taking accumulating damage, Talira was still a monster.
Her combat adaptability was terrifying.
She quickly recognized that fighting him in a purely technical martial exchange was a losing battle.
He had too much specialized technique.
He had trained his entire life for this exact specific scenario.
So, she changed the rules.
As Gideon stepped forward to deliver a heavy thrust toward her stomach, Talira didn’t try to block it with her arms.
Instead, she simply opened her mouth.
FWOOOOOOSH.
A massive point-blank torrent of white-hot volcanic fire erupted directly from her throat.
The fifty-foot wide river of pure annihilation engulfed Gideon completely before he could even finish his swing.
The flames were so incredibly hot that the surrounding bedrock instantly melted into a glowing bubbling river of liquid lava!
Gideon disappeared entirely inside the roaring column of absolute fire!
Talira ceased her breath, panting heavily with thick white smoke rising from her elongated fangs.
She expected to see a pile of melted mythril and charred bone resting in the lava.
Instead, as the smoke cleared, Gideon was still standing.
His heavy dragon-scale pauldrons were glowing red-hot, and the leather straps of his armor were smoking heavily, but his flesh was entirely intact.
The Slayer’s Resilience passive trait had neutralized the fatal intensity of the draconic fire, allowing him to endure the blast through pure grit.
"Nice try," Gideon snarled, his scarred face twisting into a demonic obsessive smile.
He raised his heavy right boot.
KRA-THOOOOOM!
Gideon slammed his boot violently into the liquid bedrock, executing his Thunderous Stomp.
A massive concentrated shockwave of golden lightning-charged earth exploded outward from his boot.
The seismic blast tore through the ground, slamming directly into Talira’s legs with terrifying voltage.
"AH!" Talira cried out.
The lightning mana violently disrupted her central nervous system...
The shock staggered her backward, completely seizing her leg muscles and forcing her to drop heavily onto one knee, entirely rooting her to the spot.
Gideon didn’t hesitate for a microsecond.
He raised the massive greatsword high above his head, stepping forward and aiming directly for her exposed ruby-red neck.
"Die, beast!" Gideon roared but Talira’s golden eyes did not show fear.
They did not show submission...
They showed primordial rage instead.
’Y-you...’
She had spent over an entire century trapped inside the suffocating darkness of the Warden’s Eye artifact.
She had watched her mother rot.
She had been freed by the kindness of Lord Silas, and though she was arrogant at first... she had sworn to fight for the Blessed Land.
She refused to be killed by a pathetic, obsessive human wielding a rusty bone sword in the mud.
As the greatsword descended rapidly toward her neck, Talira’s draconic mana core violently erupted.
"I AM NOT PREY!" Talira screamed at the absolute top of her lungs!
Her massive aura exploded outward in a colossal shockwave of pure, unfiltered fire and wind mana.
The shockwave slammed heavily into Gideon.
It threw him completely off balance, forcing him to abort his execution swing and desperately slide ten feet backward through the mud just to stay on his feet.
"Fuck!"
Before his eyes, the humanoid woman vanished entirely into a blinding pillar of towering crimson light.
"RAHHHHHHH!"
A terrifying earth-shattering draconic roar echoed across the entire Umbral Basin.
The volume of the sound silenced the surrounding battlefield, causing the sky itself to tremble.
When the crimson light finally faded, Talira was no longer a humanoid woman.
She had unleashed her True Dragon Form.
A colossal Primordial Crimson Dragon towered over the battlefield.
Her wingspan stretched out to an immense terrifying fifty feet, casting a massive, suffocating shadow entirely over Gideon’s tiny form.
Her scales had hardened into a dark volcanic black-crimson hue that was virtually impenetrable.
Massive, jagged spikes ran down the entire length of her long, serpentine spine.
Four massive, swept-back horns crowned her terrifying reptilian skull.
Her massive jaws opened wide, dripping with liquid fire.
Her glowing golden eyes locked directly onto the Dragon-Slayer far below.
Gideon looked up at the towering, seventy-foot monster.
He didn’t show an ounce of fear.
His pale gray eyes widened with euphoric ecstasy as the adrenaline flooded his system like an intoxicating drug.
"Yes," Gideon whispered, his voice trembling with obsessive joy.
"YES!
Show me your true skin!
Let me finally earn my bloodline!"𝕗𝐫𝚎𝗲𝘄𝐞𝕓𝐧𝕠𝘃𝕖𝐥.𝐜𝚘𝚖
Talira didn’t bother speaking.
She lunged forward, her massive, multi-ton jaws snapping down toward Gideon with terrifying supersonic speed.
Gideon engaged his high-speed footwork, diving aggressively to the left.
CRUNCH!
Talira’s massive jaws completely shattered the bedrock exactly where Gideon had been standing just a second prior, leaving a crater the size of a small house!
As Gideon rolled back onto his feet, he immediately swung his greatsword in a wide arc.
The heavy blade bit deeply into the dense scales of Talira’s massive, descending forearm.
SHRRRRR-IP!
Sparks flew wildly into the air.
The anti-dragon mana forced the blade cleanly through the outer layer of her thick scales, drawing a deep long gash of burning, glowing dragon blood that splashed against the mud.
"GRAHHH!"
Talira roared in genuine pain, but she did not retreat.
Her Combat Growth passive was already rapidly activating under the intense stress of the engagement.
’I see...’
She realized that staying on the ground allowed the tiny technical human to easily dodge her massive strikes and counter-attack her vulnerable joints.
So, Talira violently flapped her colossal fifty-foot wings.
FWOOOOOOSH!
The atmospheric downforce generated by the massive wing-beat created a hurricane.
The extreme wind pressure slammed into Gideon, forcing him to plant his greatsword deep into the dirt just to avoid being blown entirely across the clearing.
Talira launched herself into the sky as she ascended rapidly into the dark, smoke-filled storm clouds high above the battlefield.
"You cannot run from me!" Gideon screamed into the sky.
His obsession completely overrode his sense as he refused to let the hunt escape!
He yanked his greatsword out of the dirt.
Utilizing the lingering wind currents generated by her massive wings, he violently launched himself upward.

chapters.title: Chapter 324: Dragon Slayer’s End
paragraphs: He leaped thirty feet into the air with his heavy boots slamming violently onto the jagged moving scales of Talira’s massive, ascending tail.
Gideon had successfully mounted the dragon mid-flight.
He grabbed onto one of her massive tail spikes with his left hand to secure his grip, while holding the heavy greatsword tightly in his right.
He began rapidly scaling her massive body as she climbed higher and higher into the sky.
Talira felt the human crawling up her spine like a persistent agonizing parasite.
"RAHHHHHHHH!"
She roared in profound annoyance as she executed a violent, high-speed aerial barrel roll, attempting to throw him completely off her back.
’Why the hell is this human still on my back?!’
The extreme G-forces and dizzying centrifugal motion threatened to snap Gideon’s grip entirely.
But he held on with terrifying obsessive willpower.
His muscles screamed in agony and his scarred face twisted with effort, but he slowly continued to climb up her massive spine.
Talira realized rolling simply wasn’t working.
Her Combat Growth kicked into overdrive as she didn’t just rely on her fire anymore.
’I have to ue wind...’
Talira channeled massive amounts of compressed, emerald-green wind mana directly into her own scales.
Suddenly, the ambient air surrounding her entire massive body began to violently shred and slice in every conceivable direction.
Razor-sharp, high-velocity wind-blades erupted directly from her scales, forming a chaotic tornado of pure cutting force entirely around her spine.
"GHK!" Gideon grunted in sudden, agonizing pain.
The razor-sharp wind blades tore brutally through the weak points of his heavy mythril armor.
Deep bloody gashes opened rapidly across his exposed arms, his thighs, and his scarred cheeks.
His blood sprayed wildly into the rushing wind as Talira continued her vertical ascent, dragging him higher and higher into the freezing, oxygen-deprived upper atmosphere.
The volume of damage was rapidly overwhelming his durability as he was bleeding heavily.
His stamina was rapidly draining from the extreme altitude and the continuous shredding wind blades.
But his obsession kept him going. He absolutely refused to let go.
Through sheer willpower, he finally managed to drag his battered, bleeding body all the way up to the base of Talira’s massive neck.
Gideon planted his heavy boots securely between two of her massive spinal spikes.

He raised the heavy Dragon-Bone Greatsword high above his head with both hands, aiming the glowing lightning-charged tip directly at the vulnerable, softer scales located right at the base of her reptilian skull.
If he drove the blade deep enough, he could sever her spinal column and instantly kill the beast, securing his legacy forever.
"This is for my father!" Gideon screamed into the roaring wind. His pale gray eyes were wide with bloodthirsty triumph.
"THIS IS FOR MY CLAN!"
He began his final, executionary downward thrust but before the heavy bone blade could even touch her scales...
HUMMMMMMM.
A blinding celestial light suddenly illuminated the dark, storm-filled sky directly above them.
Gideon froze mid-swing with his eyes snapping instinctively upward.
High above the massive dragon, hovering completely effortlessly in the freezing, thin air of the upper atmosphere, was a single glowing figure.
It was Aeliana.
The evolved Astrea Archon of the Stars floated gracefully in the sky.
Her pristine white robes fluttered lightly in the fierce wind as her long starlight-blonde hair flowed perfectly around her shoulders.
Her voluminous chest heaved gently with her calm breathing, giving her a stunning, shapely hourglass figure that radiated an effortless grace.
Her luminous cosmic green eyes looked down at Gideon with an expression of terrifying coldness.
Her newly acquired Spatial Constellation Drift passive allowed her to bypass gravity entirely.
She was effectively floating on the edge of the spatial wind currents, turning her into an untouchable orbital cannon.
Aeliana simply raised her slender right index finger, pointing it directly down at Gideon’s chest.
PCHOOOOOM!
A compressed microscopic beam of pure, destructive starlight mana fired instantly from her fingertip.
The Arcane Piercer traveled at the literal speed of light.
The starlight beam slammed directly into the center of Gideon’s heavy, dragon-scale chest plate.
The anti-dragon armor was completely useless against high-tier celestial magic as the compressed beam easily punched a clean smoking hole straight through the thick mythril.
It bypassed his physical durability entirely, striking his sternum with the force of a falling meteor!
"GAAAAAH!" Gideon screamed in agonizing shock.
The massive impact instantly shattered several of his ribs and blew him violently off of Talira’s neck.
He lost his grip on his greatsword.
The heavy weapon remained embedded harmlessly in the outer layer of Talira’s scales as Gideon’s battered, bleeding body was launched completely backward into the open empty sky.
Talira felt the agonizing parasite finally removed from her neck.
She instantly ceased her violent aerial maneuvers as the chaotic shredding wind blades stopped instantly.
She looked up, her massive glowing golden eyes locking onto the small, beautifully floating form of Aeliana.
The dragon let out a soft, low, highly appreciative rumble from deep within her massive chest.
Aeliana offered a gentle elegant smile. She floated smoothly downward to land perfectly on the flat broad top of Talira’s massive reptilian skull with her boots touching the dark scales.
"You fought very well, Talira," Aeliana spoke.
Her soft voice easily reached the dragon’s ears through a spatial transmission, completely ignoring the roaring wind.
"But I think it is time we finally put this annoying little bug in his place," Aeliana declared.
Talira let out a terrifying roar of agreement.
The massive dragon folded her wings tight against her body and entered a steep dive.
Gideon was currently in a chaotic, completely uncontrolled freefall. He was plummeting rapidly back toward the battlefield below.
He was bleeding heavily from the wind blades with his chest completely crushed and smoking from the starlight impact.
He desperately tried to align his body, reaching out frantically with his hands, but he had no magic to save him as he was completely helpless in the air.
Talira easily caught up to his falling body.
She didn’t use her fire breath.
’That would be too easy...’
She simply utilized the multi-ton mass of her rapidly descending body.
WHAM!
Talira aggressively swatted Gideon’s falling body entirely out of the sky with the broad flat side of her massive crimson wing.
The impact sent Gideon spinning violently out of control, crashing down toward the Umbral Basin like a broken, discarded ragdoll.
KRA-THOOOOOOOM!
Gideon slammed brutally into the shattered bedrock of the central clearing.
The catastrophic impact created a massive fifty-foot crater, sending a massive cloud of dirt and stone shrapnel soaring high into the air.
A few seconds later, Talira landed heavily at the edge of the crater.
The sheer weight of her body shook the entire battlefield, completely silencing the surrounding infantry skirmishes.
With a brilliant flash of bright crimson light, the massive dragon rapidly condensed, transforming smoothly back into her humanoid form.
Talira stepped forward with her scale-armored tail swishing angrily behind her boots.
Aeliana floated gently down from the sky, her boots lightly touching the bedrock exactly beside Talira.
The Astrea Archon of the Stars folded her hands gracefully in front of her waist, looking down into the deep crater.
Gideon lay perfectly still in the center of the crushed stone.
He was on the verge of death.
His heavy mythril armor was completely shattered. His chest was crushed inward, and he was bleeding profusely from dozens of deep lacerations.
He couldn’t move his arms and he couldn’t lift his head.
His pale gray eyes stared blankly up at the sky with his breathing incredibly ragged and wet.
His greatsword, the legacy of his entire clan, was nowhere to be found...
He had failed.
Talira walked slowly down into the crater, stopping right at the edge of his broken body.
She looked down at the Dragon-Slayer who had obsessed over killing her and the man who had caused her so much immense pain during the aerial battle.
Aeliana stepped up quietly beside her, her cosmic green eyes calm and entirely unbothered by the sight of blood.
"He is at your mercy, Talira," Aeliana stated softly, her voice echoing perfectly in the quiet crater. "He hunted you specifically. It is your right. Do you wish to execute him?"
Talira stared down at Gideon’s bleeding, ruined face.
She thought about the Warden’s Eye.
She thought about her mother’s rotting corpse. She thought about the endless cycle of hatred and violence that had consumed her entire life until Aeliana had freed her.
Talira let out a slow breath with her glowing golden eyes narrowing.
"No," Talira stated firmly.
Her voice carried a deep surprising sense of maturity. She looked away from Gideon in pure disgust.

"My Lord and everyone showed me kindness when I deserved none," Talira spoke proudly, standing incredibly tall. "I will not let this pathetic little human drag me down into his miserable cycle of revenge. He is already broken. Let him crawl back to his army and live the rest of his pathetic life knowing that a dragon chose to spare him out of pity. I will be the bigger person."
It was a beautiful and incredibly dramatic speech of personal growth and absolute forgiveness.
Aeliana listened to the entire speech with a gentle supportive smile on her beautiful face.
"That is wonderfully spoken, Talira," Aeliana praised her softly. "You have grown so much since we first met."
Then, Aeliana casually raised her right index finger, pointing it directly at Gideon’s head.
PCHOOOOOM!
A high-velocity beam of destructive starlight mana fired instantly from her finger.
It blew a massive smoking hole straight through the center of Gideon’s skull.
The Dragon-Slayer’s body jerked exactly once, then went completely, permanently limp in the mud. He was instantly dead.
Talira froze entirely.
Her golden eyes widened in utter shock.
She slowly turned her head, looking at Aeliana with an expression of pure bewilderment.
"Wha... what?!" Talira stammered, pointing a violently shaking gauntlet at the headless corpse. "I... I just gave a whole speech about sparing him! I said I was going to be the bigger person!"
Aeliana lowered her hand gracefully, delicately tucking a stray strand of starlight-blonde hair behind her long elven ear.
Her cosmic green eyes blinked with innocence.

"I know," Aeliana replied. "And it was a very lovely speech. But if we let him live, he would just go back, train harder, unlock some new tragic power-up, and come back stronger to try and kill you again in a few months."
Aeliana offered a small chilling smile.
"And I most certainly would not like that," Aeliana concluded simply. "It is far more efficient to simply execute him now while he cannot defend himself."
Talira stood there, completely dumbfounded by the terrifying ruthlessness hiding behind the High Elf’s gentle beautiful smile.
Aeliana stepped forward. She reached out with her delicate hand to gently tap the tip of Talira’s nose.
"You are very cute when you try to be noble, though," Aeliana giggled softly.
Talira’s pale cheeks flushed a deep burning crimson.
She opened her mouth to aggressively argue, but found herself completely at a loss for words against the woman’s logic.
However, before either of them could say another word, the atmosphere in the entire central clearing underwent a terrifying shift.
The light of the morning sun vanished completely.
The sky above them didn’t just turn dark.
It was forcefully overwritten by a deep and infinitely vast shade of dark purple light.
Aeliana and Talira both snapped their heads instantly toward the western quadrant of the battlefield.
The ambient mana in the air was completely suppressed.
The people in the Umbral Basin felt as though they had been forcibly locked into place by an overwhelming pressure.
A single and terrifyingly serene voice echoed directly into the minds of every single combatant on the field.
"Mind’s Eye."
The central battleground of the Umbral Basin had been completely reduced to a chaotic unrecognizable wasteland of torn bedrock, shattered ice, and burning craters.
The heavy scent of boiling blood, and scorched earth hung in the freezing air.

The sky above was a swirling unnatural vortex of gray ash and updrafts, painted in violent, flashing hues of crimson, sapphire, and pink from the continuous apocalyptic clashes of powerhouses occurring in every single quadrant.
The ground trembled continuously.
KRA-THOOOOOM!
Another massive shockwave ripped through the western tree line, blowing away the lingering fog and sending a dozen heavy infantrymen tumbling helplessly across the mud.
Yet, directly in the exact center of this hellscape, a strange surreal bubble of quiet anticipation had formed.

chapters.title: Chapter 325: Sky Vs Vespera
paragraphs: The clashing armies of the Blessed Land and The Unmovable Wall seemed to unconsciously pull back from this specific stretch of shattered ground with their primal instincts warning them to give the predators room to breathe.
Through the drifting smoke and falling ash, two figures walked slowly and deliberately toward one another.
On the southern side, walking with the terrifying elegance of an apex predator, was Lord Vespera.
Her dark hood completely obscured the upper half of her face, leaving only her glowing luminous purple eyes visible beneath the fabric.
Her single steel longsword hung casually at her side with her silver armor gleaming faintly under the chaotic light of the war zone.
Her empty left sleeve fluttered lightly in the wind, a testament to the heavy battle-scarred persona she projected to the millions watching on the Sovereign Network stream.
On the northern side, approaching with unyielding confidence, was Lord Sky.
The master of The Unmovable Wall was clad in a magnificent advanced suit of deep blue and gold mythril battle armor.
A sleek, high-tech combat helmet completely covered his head, its visor glowing with a sharp blue light.
A long, pristine white cape flowed majestically from his broad shoulders, completely unstained by the surrounding mud and blood.
They did not run as they simply walked, their boots crushing the broken stone beneath their feet with small sounds.
The distance between them closed from fifty yards... To thirty yards... To fifteen yards...
Finally, they both stopped.
The noise of the battlefield seemed to fade entirely into the background, leaving only the sound of the freezing wind whipping between the two Lords.
Sky looked past Vespera’s shoulder, his glowing blue visor scanning the distant catastrophes happening across the basin.
He saw Ignis and Frost falling.
He saw his heavy shield lines completely failing against the terrifying coordinated strikes of Vespera’s Vanguard.
Sky slowly turned his head back, locking his gaze directly onto Vespera’s spatial hood.
"I have fought dozens of Lords across the Known and Unknown Zones," Sky spoke.
His voice was filtered through the mechanical vocal processor of his helmet, giving it a deep sound.

"I have broken siege lines... I have shattered alliances... I have commanded the Unmovable Wall against dungeon breaks that would have wiped towns off the map," Sky continued, his voice laced with genuine respect. "But I have never, in all my years of conquest, seen an army quite like yours, Vespera."
Sky reached up with his right hand with his heavy gold-trimmed gauntlet resting casually on the hilt of his weapon.

"Your Vanguard," Sky praised, nodding slowly. "They do not fight like standard summoned units... They do not fight like mercenaries hired for a paycheck. They fight with a loyalty that borders on fanaticism. Every single one of them is a monstrous anomaly and I can see that you have built a truly terrifying foundation."
Beneath the dark spatial hood, Vespera let out a soft amused hum.
"I appreciate the compliment, Lord Sky," Vespera replied.
Her voice was cool and laced with a feminine elegance that completely belied the violence she was capable of unleashing.

"But you are too modest," Vespera continued smoothly, her glowing purple eyes curving into a smile. "Your Unmovable Wall is exactly as advertised... Your infantry lines possess extreme, unbreakable discipline. Your elemental Wardens pushed my girls to their absolute limits. You did not build this army by accident. You are a classic, high-tier conqueror, Sky. You command respect, and your troops die for you without hesitation."
Vespera slowly raised her right hand.
She gripped the leather-wrapped hilt of her single steel longsword, angling the blade slightly toward the dirt.

"It is a genuine shame that your territory won’t be here forever," Vespera said quietly with wind mana beginning to swirl visibly around the edge of her steel blade. "Under different circumstances, we might have been highly lucrative trading partners."
Sky let out a deep chuckle that vibrated through his vocal processor.
"Perhaps in another life, Vespera," Sky agreed warmly. "But in this realm, there can be only one territory in the sector. Only one of us walks out of this basin with our territory intact."
SHRRRRING!
With a smooth, flawless motion, Sky completely drew his weapon from its scabbard.
It was a magnificent slender rapier forged of pure, translucent blue crystal.
The blade seemed to be made entirely of frozen compressed water, radiating a brilliant, blinding aura of pure white light.
"Let us show the Sovereign Network exactly why we sit upon the thrones of our respective empires," Sky declared, dropping his center of gravity into a flawless dueling stance.
Vespera did not say another word.
She simply smiled.
BOOM.
The bedrock beneath Vespera’s boots violently exploded into fine powder.
She engaged her raw Gold-core physical acceleration, tearing across the fifteen-yard gap in a single heartbeat.
Vespera brought her single steel longsword around in a blindingly fast, horizontal execution arc, aiming directly for the side of Sky’s helmet!
Sky did not flinch as his combat reflexes were elite, honed through years of frontline leadership.
He smoothly brought the crystal rapier up, angling the flat of the blade perfectly to intercept the heavy steel strike.
CLANGGGGGGG!
The collision of steel against magical crystal sent a deafening high-frequency shockwave ripping through the clearing.
A massive ring of displaced air blew the falling ash away from their bodies, exposing the intensity of the clash.
Vespera immediately felt the immense power of Sky’s mana core through the crossguard.
He wasn’t just a backline commander who let his Heroes do all the heavy lifting.
He was a genuine brawler.
"A bit too direct, Vespera!" Sky shouted over the ringing steel. "But I don’t mind it!"
Sky instantly channeled his unique dual-elemental magic directly into his rapier.
’Hydro-Luminescence!’
The crystal blade in his hand violently flared with blinding white light.
The light did not just shine... it actively refracted through the hyper-compressed water mana surrounding the blade, acting like a prism that multiplied the intensity a thousand times over.
Vespera’s glowing purple eyes widened slightly behind her hood.
’He’s never used this before... or has he? I’m not a hardcore fan.’
The light was utterly blinding, burning into her eyes like a miniature sun erupting at point-blank range.
It was a flawless combination... using water to bend light directly into the opponent’s line of sight, completely blinding them in the middle of a high-speed sword exchange.
Deprived of her vision temporarily, Vespera immediately relied on her spatial awareness and wind mana.
She rapidly twisted her wrist, disengaging the blade lock, and threw her body entirely backward just as Sky executed a lethal high-speed thrust.
SWISH!
’I have to make this interesting so I won’t solo him yet.’
The glowing crystal rapier missed her throat by a mere fraction of an inch with the heat of the light magic lightly singeing the fabric of her dark coat.
"You cannot fight what you cannot see!" Sky pressed the absolute advantage!
He lunged forward with his footwork becoming elegant and completely fluid.
He didn’t swing his sword like a brute.
He wielded the rapier with the precision of a master surgeon, delivering a terrifying relentless flurry of high-speed thrusts and blindingly fast parries.
CLACK! CLACK! CLANG!
Vespera was forced onto the defensive!
She retreated rapidly across the crushed bedrock with her single arm blurring as she desperately used her steel longsword to deflect the incoming strikes!
Every single time Sky thrust his weapon, the water mana surrounding the blade would suddenly expand, shooting microscopic razor-sharp jets of high-pressure water directly toward Vespera’s joints.
She was fighting a man who commanded the fluidity of the ocean and the blinding speed of pure light.
"You are fast, Sky!" Vespera called out with her voice slightly strained as she parried another heavy thrust that sent bright sparks raining into the mud! "But light only travels in straight lines!"
Vespera planted her boot firmly into the dirt, stopping her retreat.
Instead of backing away, she aggressively stepped directly into his guard.
Vespera surged her Gold-core wind mana directly into her legs, executing a terrifyingly complex series of pivoting footwork that completely broke his line of sight.
She spun to the outside of his right shoulder, moving faster than the human eye could effectively track.
’Tidal-Blade First Style!’ Vespera declared in her thoughts as she swung her longsword upward in a massive crescent arc, condensing atmospheric wind pressure along the cutting edge.
’Severing Horizon.’
A razor-thin blade of water pressure exploded from the tip of her steel sword, tearing through the air directly toward Sky’s exposed ribs.
Vespera was keeping it small since this wasn’t really the time to use the full thing.
Sky’s mechanical visor flashed violently with danger warnings.
"Aegis Ripple!" Sky commanded!
He didn’t try to physically block the wind blade. Instead, he snapped his left fingers together.
A massive swirling wall of pressurized glowing water erupted directly from the dirt beside his boots, forming a dense rotating whirlpool shield exactly between himself and the incoming wind attack.
KRA-THOOOOOM!
The compressed blade slammed into the rotating water shield with catastrophic force.
The water sheared violently through the outer layers of the water, but the rotational power of the whirlpool actively absorbed and dispersed the cutting power.
The attack safely detonated into a massive, harmless shower of pouring rain that washed over both Lord Commanders.
Sky smiled behind his mechanical helmet.

"Your magic is incredibly sharp, Vespera," Sky praised, casually flicking his crystal rapier to the side. "But water is fluid... It has no shape. It has no rigid structure for you to cleanly sever so my defense is absolute."
The pouring rain fell heavily around them, soaking the crushed bedrock and turning the battlefield into a slippery dangerous arena.
Vespera stood perfectly still in the rain with her dark coat completely saturated with water.
Her glowing purple eyes remained entirely fixed on Sky’s confident posture.
Internally, however, a massive grin was stretching across Silas’s hidden face.
’You idiot,’ Silas thought. ’You just handed me the exact environmental condition I desperately needed.’
Silas had been struggling to master the second technique of Morwenna’s incredibly complex swordsmanship.

The Second Style of the Tide-Blade Arts required the user to read the microscopic shifts in ambient atmospheric moisture to predict the opponent’s exact muscle movements, telegraphs, and structural weak points.

During the earlier spar with the demoness Morrighan, Silas had failed to utilize the technique properly because Morrighan’s demonic brimstone heat had constantly warped and evaporated the moisture in the air, ruining his perception.
But Sky didn’t use fire.
Sky used water.
And right now, Sky had just generously saturated the entire thirty-yard radius of their battlefield with a thick layer of pouring rain and lingering mist.
The environment was perfectly optimized for the Dread Queen’s signature perception technique.
Vespera slowly lowered her steel longsword, angling the tip completely toward the ground.
She relaxed her posture entirely, completely dropping her defensive guard as she closed her glowing purple eyes beneath her spatial hood.
Sky frowned deeply with his mechanical visor zooming in on her bizarre behavior.

"What are you doing?" Sky asked, his voice laced with genuine suspicion. "Are you surrendering the duel? The Sovereign Network is watching, Vespera. Do not give up just because your wind cannot break my water."
Vespera did not answer.
She simply breathed in the cold wet air.
’Tidal-Blade Second Style.’
HUMMMMMMM!
Vespera violently surged her Gold Core, pushing her internal mana circuits to their maximum limit.
She didn’t channel the mana into her blade as she channeled it entirely into her sensory perception.
’Rip-Current Perception.’
Vespera snapped her purple eyes open.
The entire world completely changed.
She no longer saw the mud, the falling ash, or the distant explosions and she no longer saw Sky’s shiny blue armor or his glowing white crystal rapier.
’So is this how Morwenna saw me on that day...? And she said that this was hard?’
Her vision was entirely overwritten by a hyper-detailed three-dimensional geometric map formed exclusively of glowing blue water particles.
Every single drop of rain falling from the sky.
Every single ounce of moisture clinging to Sky’s armor. The microscopic humidity in the air that was currently being displaced by Sky’s breathing and his subtle muscle twitches.
It all instantly locked into focus.
Suddenly, clear, glowing blue lines began to materialize across Sky’s body.
The lines wrapped around his joints, highlighting the exact distribution of his physical weight.
They tracked the flow of mana from his core into his rapier.
And, most importantly, the glowing blue lines converged violently onto three distinct, glaring red spots on his posture.
One on his left ankle, where he favored his weight slightly too heavily.
One on his right wrist, where his grip on the rapier was entirely too rigid for a fluid thrust.
And one perfectly in the center of his chest plate, where his water shield spell left a microscopic delay in mana coverage immediately after casting.
Vespera saw the truth of his defenses.
’I see you,’ Vespera thought coldly.
"If you will not attack," Sky declared, raising his rapier and flooding it with blinding light. "then I will simply end this!"
