chapters.title: Chapter 326: Mind’s Eye
paragraphs: Sky shot forward, moving with speed as he thrust his rapier directly toward Vespera’s heart, the blade surrounded by a massive spiraling drill of high-pressure water designed to crush her ribcage upon impact.
To the naked eye, the attack was completely flawless.
But to Vespera’s Rip-Current Perception, it was moving in agonizing slow motion, and the glaring red weak point on his right wrist was practically screaming at her.
Vespera didn’t retreat as she simply took a single precise half-step to the left.
SWISH!
The massive spiraling drill of water and light missed her hood by a fraction of a millimeter.
The force of the attack blew past her ear, shattering a stone pillar forty yards behind her.
Sky’s eyes widened in shock behind his visor.
He had completely overextended his thrust, relying on the blinding light to guarantee the hit.
Vespera smoothly brought the flat pommel of her steel longsword up.

She didn’t use the cutting edge as she didn’t want to kill him so she simply drove the heavy steel pommel directly into the glowing red weak point located perfectly on the inside of Sky’s right wrist.
CRACK!
"GAHH!" Sky cried out in sudden agonizing pain.
The precise impact struck the exact nerve cluster controlling his grip.
His fingers instantly went completely numb as the glowing crystal rapier slipped helplessly from his hand, falling uselessly into the mud.
Before Sky could even process the disarmament, Vespera was already moving.
She used the momentum of her own strike to spin her body completely around, sweeping her right leg out in a low brutal arc.
Her heavy boot slammed directly into the glowing red weak point on Sky’s left ankle.
CRUNCH!
The impact violently shattered Sky’s physical balance as his entire center of gravity completely collapsed!
Sky’s armored frame tipped helplessly backward.
THUD!
The Lord of the Unmovable Wall crashed heavily onto his back in the freezing mud, completely disarmed and defeated in the span of three seconds.
Vespera smoothly reversed the grip on her steel longsword.

She stepped forward, planting her boot firmly on Sky’s chest plate, pinning him to the dirt then she brought the razor-sharp tip of her steel blade down, stopping it exactly one inch from the glowing blue visor of his mechanical helmet.
The rain continued to fall heavily around them as the duel was absolutely over.
Sky lay in the mud, staring up at the razor-sharp tip of the steel blade.
He felt the heavy, crushing weight of Vespera’s boot on his chest.
For a long, tense moment, neither of them moved then, the mechanical vocal processor of Sky’s helmet emitted a deep static-filled sigh.
A loud lighthearted laugh suddenly burst from Sky’s hidden lips, completely lacking any anger or pride.
"Hahaha! Well damn!" Sky laughed, raising his empty armored hands into the air in a gesture of surrender. "You got me, Vespera! I didn’t even see that footwork coming! Your perception is monstrous!"
Vespera kept the blade steady with her purple eyes glowing in the dark.

"You fought incredibly well, Lord Sky," Vespera replied smoothly, honoring the classic Lord. "But your grip was too tight, and your weight distribution favored your left side... Water is fluid, but your fundamentals are too rigid."
Sky laughed again, shaking his head against the mud.
"Fair enough, fair enough," Sky conceded gracefully. "You are the better duelist, and your Vanguard has completely dismantled my frontlines. I know when I am beaten."
Sky slowly reached his hands up toward the latches of his heavy mechanical helmet.

"I officially surrender the Lord War, Vespera," Sky announced loudly, ensuring the network drones could pick up the audio. "The Unmovable Wall yields to the Blessed Land. You have earned your victory today... Let us end this stream and discuss the rest."
Vespera slowly lowered her blade, stepping her boot off of his chest plate.
"A wise decision," Vespera agreed, preparing to sheath her sword.
But before Sky could do anything, and before Vespera could slide her blade away...
The atmosphere in the Umbral Basin underwent a terrifying unnatural shift.
The freezing rain suddenly stopped falling mid-air as the droplets hung suspended in the atmosphere like frozen glass.
The light of the morning sun was violently completely severed.
The entire sky above them didn’t just turn dark.
It was forcefully overwritten by a deep and infinitely vast shade of dark purple light that instantly flooded the entire basin.
Vespera and Sky both froze.
The mana in the air was completely suppressed and it felt as though they had been forcibly locked into an inescapable cage of something.
A single terrifyingly serene voice echoed directly into the minds of every single combatant on the entire battlefield, completely bypassing their physical ears.
"Mind’s Eye."
Sky grunted, immediately struggling to sit up in the mud as the suffocating purple light washed over his heavy blue armor.
"What the hell is this?!" Sky complained loudly, tapping the side of his mechanical helmet in immense frustration. "My HUD is completely offline! The arrays are scrambled!"
Sky looked around wildly at the dark purple void that had swallowed the battlefield.
"Dammit!" Sky cursed. "The stream connection just severed completely! The network drones have been entirely knocked out of the sky by whatever this purple domain is! The broadcast is dead!"
But as Sky was complaining... something was terribly wrong.
Vespera stood perfectly still, her longsword gripped tightly in her hand, staring entirely in shock at the figure sitting in the mud.
Because the voice complaining about the stream connection... was no longer a deep male voice.
It was the high-pitched sweet voice of a woman.
Sky froze mid-complaint.
The Lord of the Unmovable Wall slowly lowered her heavy, armored gauntlets as she looked down at her own chest.
The massive, imposing suit of deep blue and gold mythril battle armor had completely vanished into thin air.
The perception of the Mind’s Eye domain had forcefully stripped away the high-tier illusion magic sustaining the disguise.
Sky was no longer a towering male Lord.
Sitting in the freezing mud was a young woman.
She was swimming inside an oversized extremely comfortable-looking gray hoodie that fell past her knees.
She wore basic dark leggings and heavy mud-stained combat boots.
Her heavy mechanical helmet was sitting uselessly on her head, completely offline and completely dead.
Sky gulped loudly.
Her hands trembled as she reached up, grabbing the sides of the dead helmet.
With a soft click, she pulled the heavy metal off of her head, tossing it uselessly into the mud.
Long beautiful black hair tumbled down perfectly around her shoulders.
Her eyes were wide with panic.
Her soft pale cheeks flushed a deep, embarrassed crimson as she realized she was sitting exposed in her oversized sleepwear.
The disguise... the male persona... it had failed completely.
"Oh... oh fuck..." Sky whispered softly, her voice trembling with horror.
She slowly looked up, terrified to see the reaction of the imposing, ruthless Lord Vespera.
She expected the Lord of the Blessed Land to strike her down for the deception but as Sky looked up... her blue eyes widened even further.
Because Vespera was not standing there.
The sleek silver armor, the intimidating dark spatial hood, the single-armed aesthetic... it had all entirely vanished into thin air, forcefully stripped away by the exact same perception domain.
Standing exactly where Vespera had been was a tall and undeniably handsome young man.
He wore a tight black undershirt that perfectly highlighted his sculpted, athletic physique, and flexible dark canvas combat trousers.
Both of his arms were perfectly intact, gripping the steel longsword with trained precision.
His striking face was set in a hard scowl with his messy dark hair fluttered in the freezing wind.
And his eyes... his eyes were the most beautiful thing she had ever seen.
They were marked by a dense suffocating golden ring around the pupil that radiated the aura of a sovereign.
Silas stared down at the black-haired woman sitting in the mud in an oversized hoodie.
Sky stared up at the handsome, golden-eyed man gripping the steel sword.
The suffocating silence of the purple domain stretched between them for five agonizing seconds of pure mutual shock.
"Who the fuck are you?" Silas demanded bluntly, his actual deep voice breaking the silence. "You aren’t Sky."
Sky scrambled backward in the mud, hugging her knees to her chest inside her massive hoodie with her face burning incredibly bright red.
"Who the fuck are YOU?!" Sky shrieked back defensively, pointing a shaking finger directly at Silas! "You aren’t Vespera! Where is the Lord of Blessed Land?!"

"I am the Warlord, you idiot!" Silas shot back, immensely irritated that his flawless and carefully cultivated female persona had just been ripped apart on an open battlefield. "You’re telling me the Lord of the Unmovable Wall is actually a woman wearing pajamas in a war zone?!"
Silas had no problem with Sky being a woman but still... he couldn’t say anything about it, Thora had said so after all.
"They are incredibly comfortable!" Sky argued fiercely, crossing her arms over her chest defensively. "And at least I wasn’t pretending to be a woman with one arm just to look edgy on a live stream!"
Silas opened his mouth to deliver a scathing retort about her gaming chair posture but before they could continue their embarrassing argument...
The suffocating purple light of the domain suddenly pulsed violently around them.
Silas snapped his mouth shut.
His golden-ringed eyes narrowed sharply with his combat instincts instantly overriding his irritation.
He felt the terrifying pressure radiating through the domain.
’What happened?’
Sky stopped pouting, her eyes widening in sudden serious alarm as she felt her mana core completely suppressed by the purple light.
Both of the disguised Lords slowly turned their heads, looking far across the crushed bedrock toward the edge of the battlefield, exactly where the center of the terrifying domain had originated.
"What is that?" Sky whispered, her voice dropping all pretense of arrogance.
Silas gripped his sword tighter, stepping protectively in front of the unarmored girl.
"I don’t know," Silas replied coldly. "But whatever it is... it just locked down my entire Vanguard."
Far across the basin, entirely enveloped in the exact same suffocating purple light.
The massive, sixty-foot crater created by the destruction of the Shield World was dead silent.
Tasmin remained in a low defensive crouch.
Her twin shortswords were held tight in her hands, her eyes locked entirely on the blindfolded man standing ten feet away.
Brida, the Grand Titan Bastion, stood tall beside her.
The razor-thin cut running entirely across the adamantine face of her tower shield glowed in the dark.
Kassandra knelt in the mud slightly behind them, clutching her bruised throat, completely exhausted from the void flames.
And in the center of the standoff stood Hiro.
The blind vanguard of Sky’s army had dropped his dark cloth blindfold into the mud.
His empty scarred eye sockets leaked a brilliant, piercing blue light that actively etched a massive three-dimensional geometric web into the very air itself.
The purple domain surrounding them was the manifestation of that web.
It was a terrifying domain that stripped away all falsehoods, all illusions, and all evasions.
Hiro stood perfectly relaxed with his hands still resting casually at his sides.
"Do not be afraid of the light," Hiro spoke. "My domain, the Mind’s Eye, is not a weapon of malice. It is simply a weapon of truth."
Hiro slowly raised his right hand with his fingers tracing the invisible lines of blue light floating in the air before him.

"When the beast took my eyes so many years ago," Hiro explained calmly, stepping slowly forward, "I thought my life as a warrior was entirely finished. I spent years in the dark but slowly, the darkness taught me something profound. Physical eyes are incredibly flawed. They are easily deceived by light, by shadow, by simple illusions."
Tasmin’s shadow mana flared violently around her boots, desperately trying to find a spatial seam to sink into.
But it was entirely useless.
The purple light of the domain completely suppressed her Shadow-Submersion Drift as the shadows themselves were locked in place.
She could not hide.

"The Mind’s Eye does not see light," Hiro continued, his empty sockets bleeding blue energy. "It sees reality itself. It sees the exact coordinates of every single atom in this basin. It sees the microscopic tension in your muscles, the flow of mana in your cores, and the exact trajectory of your thoughts before you even execute them."

sentences.text: Sky shot forward, moving with speed as he thrust his rapier directly toward Vespera’s heart, the blade surrounded by a massive spiraling drill of high-pressure water designed to crush her ribcage upon impact.
To the naked eye, the attack was completely flawless.
But to Vespera’s Rip-Current Perception, it was moving in agonizing slow motion, and the glaring red weak point on his right wrist was practically screaming at her.
Vespera didn’t retreat as she simply took a single precise half-step to the left.
SWISH!
The massive spiraling drill of water and light missed her hood by a fraction of a millimeter.
The force of the attack blew past her ear, shattering a stone pillar forty yards behind her.
Sky’s eyes widened in shock behind his visor.
He had completely overextended his thrust, relying on the blinding light to guarantee the hit.
Vespera smoothly brought the flat pommel of her steel longsword up.

She didn’t use the cutting edge as she didn’t want to kill him so she simply drove the heavy steel pommel directly into the glowing red weak point located perfectly on the inside of Sky’s right wrist.
CRACK!
"GAHH!" Sky cried out in sudden agonizing pain.
The precise impact struck the exact nerve cluster controlling his grip.
His fingers instantly went completely numb as the glowing crystal rapier slipped helplessly from his hand, falling uselessly into the mud.
Before Sky could even process the disarmament, Vespera was already moving.
She used the momentum of her own strike to spin her body completely around, sweeping her right leg out in a low brutal arc.
Her heavy boot slammed directly into the glowing red weak point on Sky’s left ankle.
CRUNCH!
The impact violently shattered Sky’s physical balance as his entire center of gravity completely collapsed!
Sky’s armored frame tipped helplessly backward.
THUD!
The Lord of the Unmovable Wall crashed heavily onto his back in the freezing mud, completely disarmed and defeated in the span of three seconds.
Vespera smoothly reversed the grip on her steel longsword.

She stepped forward, planting her boot firmly on Sky’s chest plate, pinning him to the dirt then she brought the razor-sharp tip of her steel blade down, stopping it exactly one inch from the glowing blue visor of his mechanical helmet.
The rain continued to fall heavily around them as the duel was absolutely over.
Sky lay in the mud, staring up at the razor-sharp tip of the steel blade.
He felt the heavy, crushing weight of Vespera’s boot on his chest.
For a long, tense moment, neither of them moved then, the mechanical vocal processor of Sky’s helmet emitted a deep static-filled sigh.
A loud lighthearted laugh suddenly burst from Sky’s hidden lips, completely lacking any anger or pride.
"Hahaha!
Well damn!" Sky laughed, raising his empty armored hands into the air in a gesture of surrender.
"You got me, Vespera!
I didn’t even see that footwork coming!
Your perception is monstrous!"
Vespera kept the blade steady with her purple eyes glowing in the dark.
"You fought incredibly well, Lord Sky," Vespera replied smoothly, honoring the classic Lord.
"But your grip was too tight, and your weight distribution favored your left side...
Water is fluid, but your fundamentals are too rigid."
Sky laughed again, shaking his head against the mud.
"Fair enough, fair enough," Sky conceded gracefully.
"You are the better duelist, and your Vanguard has completely dismantled my frontlines.
I know when I am beaten."
Sky slowly reached his hands up toward the latches of his heavy mechanical helmet.
"I officially surrender the Lord War, Vespera," Sky announced loudly, ensuring the network drones could pick up the audio.
"The Unmovable Wall yields to the Blessed Land.
You have earned your victory today...
Let us end this stream and discuss the rest."
Vespera slowly lowered her blade, stepping her boot off of his chest plate.
"A wise decision," Vespera agreed, preparing to sheath her sword.
But before Sky could do anything, and before Vespera could slide her blade away...
The atmosphere in the Umbral Basin underwent a terrifying unnatural shift.
The freezing rain suddenly stopped falling mid-air as the droplets hung suspended in the atmosphere like frozen glass.
The light of the morning sun was violently completely severed.
The entire sky above them didn’t just turn dark.
It was forcefully overwritten by a deep and infinitely vast shade of dark purple light that instantly flooded the entire basin.
Vespera and Sky both froze.
The mana in the air was completely suppressed and it felt as though they had been forcibly locked into an inescapable cage of something.
A single terrifyingly serene voice echoed directly into the minds of every single combatant on the entire battlefield, completely bypassing their physical ears.
"Mind’s Eye."
Sky grunted, immediately struggling to sit up in the mud as the suffocating purple light washed over his heavy blue armor.
"What the hell is this?!" Sky complained loudly, tapping the side of his mechanical helmet in immense frustration.
"My HUD is completely offline!
The arrays are scrambled!"
Sky looked around wildly at the dark purple void that had swallowed the battlefield.
"Dammit!" Sky cursed.
"The stream connection just severed completely!
The network drones have been entirely knocked out of the sky by whatever this purple domain is!
The broadcast is dead!"
But as Sky was complaining... something was terribly wrong.
Vespera stood perfectly still, her longsword gripped tightly in her hand, staring entirely in shock at the figure sitting in the mud.
Because the voice complaining about the stream connection... was no longer a deep male voice.
It was the high-pitched sweet voice of a woman.
Sky froze mid-complaint.
The Lord of the Unmovable Wall slowly lowered her heavy, armored gauntlets as she looked down at her own chest.
The massive, imposing suit of deep blue and gold mythril battle armor had completely vanished into thin air.
The perception of the Mind’s Eye domain had forcefully stripped away the high-tier illusion magic sustaining the disguise.
Sky was no longer a towering male Lord.
Sitting in the freezing mud was a young woman.
She was swimming inside an oversized extremely comfortable-looking gray hoodie that fell past her knees.
She wore basic dark leggings and heavy mud-stained combat boots.
Her heavy mechanical helmet was sitting uselessly on her head, completely offline and completely dead.
Sky gulped loudly.
Her hands trembled as she reached up, grabbing the sides of the dead helmet.
With a soft click, she pulled the heavy metal off of her head, tossing it uselessly into the mud.
Long beautiful black hair tumbled down perfectly around her shoulders.
Her eyes were wide with panic.
Her soft pale cheeks flushed a deep, embarrassed crimson as she realized she was sitting exposed in her oversized sleepwear.
The disguise... the male persona... it had failed completely.
"Oh... oh fuck..." Sky whispered softly, her voice trembling with horror.
She slowly looked up, terrified to see the reaction of the imposing, ruthless Lord Vespera.
She expected the Lord of the Blessed Land to strike her down for the deception but as Sky looked up... her blue eyes widened even further.

chapters.title: Chapter 327: All Roads Lead To Eluned [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: Brida gritted her teeth, stepping heavily in front of Tasmin to shield the assassin.
"Stop talking like a damn philosopher!" Brida roared, dropping her caution immediately.
She flooded her boots with earth mana, completely ignoring the suppressing pressure of the domain.
"Earth-Shattering Cleave!" Brida bellowed!
She ripped the Void Cleaver through the air, bringing the massive battleaxe crashing straight down toward Hiro’s skull.
It was a flawless strike possessing thousands of pounds of raw force but Hiro didn’t dodge and he didn’t raise a heavy shield either.
He simply tilted his head slightly to the left.
SWISH!
The massive mythril blade missed his ear by exactly one millimeter.
The wind pressure of the passing axe blew his dark hair wildly, but the blade itself hit absolutely nothing but empty air.
’I need to push my... self...’
Hiro casually raised his left hand, placing his index finger gently against the flat side of the descending battleaxe.
He didn’t use brute strength as he used spatial magic instead.
With a tiny, microscopic flick of his wrist, Hiro applied the exact precise amount of opposing kinetic force required to completely unbalance the multi-ton swing.
CRACK!
"GAHH!" Brida grunted in shock.
The massive Void Cleaver was violently deflected to the side with the momentum of her own strike forcefully tearing the heavy weapon entirely out of her leather grip.
The battleaxe sailed through the air, crashing harmlessly into the distant mud.
Before Brida could recover her posture, Hiro smoothly stepped entirely inside her heavy guard.
Hiro simply pressed his open palm flat against the absolute center of Brida’s impenetrable silver breastplate.
"Spatial Repulsion," Hiro whispered softly.
KRA-THOOOOOOOM!
’Isn’t he supposed to be a swordsman...?’
An invisible concentrated blast of raw spatial pressure detonated perfectly against Brida’s armor.
The attack didn’t test her physical vitality nor did it test her muscle density. It instead rewrote the spatial coordinates of her body in a way.
Brida’s Unyielding Bedrock Body passive trait completely failed to anchor her.
The S-Rank Grand Titan Bastion was violently blasted entirely off her feet with her frame launched through the air like a cannonball.
"BRIDA!" Tasmin screamed and she immediately reacted.
With her shadows locked, she relied entirely on her raw speed.
She lunged forward, swinging her twin shortswords in a blindingly fast X-shaped execution arc aimed directly for Hiro’s throat.
"Too slow," Hiro murmured softly.
Without even turning his head to look at her, Hiro smoothly brought his right arm up.
He executed a flawless invisible slash with the edge of his bare hand.
CLANG! CLANG!
The invisible strike perfectly intercepted both of Tasmin’s dark mythril blades simultaneously.
The perfection of the parry completely shattered Tasmin’s grip as both of her shortswords were violently knocked into the air!
Hiro followed up instantly. He extended two fingers and lightly, almost gently, tapped the exact center of Tasmin’s chest.
BZZZZZT!
Another highly concentrated pulse of spatial pressure detonated.
Tasmin coughed up a violent spray of blood with the impact crushing the breath entirely out of her lungs as she was blasted backward through the air.
CRASH! CRASH!
Brida and Tasmin crashed heavily into the mud twenty yards away, both completely disarmed, bruised, and violently pushed back by a man who hadn’t even drawn a weapon.
Hiro stood perfectly still in the center of the crater, his empty scarred sockets leaking bright blue light into the terrifying purple domain.
Kassandra, kneeling in the mud just a few feet behind Hiro, saw the entire exchange.
Her pink eyes widened with fanatic awe.
’Is this really Hiro...?’
The blind vanguard had just effortlessly dismantled two monsters who had nearly killed her.
Seeing the two Vanguard women struggling to stand up in the distance, Kassandra realized this was the exact perfect moment to secure her victory and reclaim her honor.
"I will finish them!" Kassandra yelled fiercely.

She forced her bruised, battered body up from the mud as she surged every single drop of remaining mana into her pink runic armor, preparing to launch a devastating kinetic blast at the vulnerable Vanguard women.
Kassandra shot forward with her fist glowing with bright pink energy, fully intending to blow Tasmin’s head off while she was unarmed.
But as Kassandra took her third step...
ZIP!
A nearly invisible silent streak of light shot down from the high stone ridge located far above the battlefield.
It was a masterfully crafted projectile perfectly calculated to bypass standard wind resistance and spatial anomalies.
THWACK!
The projectile slammed directly into the exact microscopic gap between Kassandra’s heavy pink helmet and her neck armor.
It was a specialized non-lethal knockout arrow.
"Guh—" Kassandra choked with her pink eyes rolling completely into the back of her head.
The concentrated sleep toxin instantly flooded her exhausted nervous system as her glowing pink fist sputtered and died.
THUD!
Kassandra collapsed face-first into the mud, completely knocked out cold before she could even launch her attack.
Hiro stopped.
He didn’t turn his head as his empty sockets simply focused entirely on the high stone ridge overlooking the crater.
Up on the edge of the jagged cliff, standing perfectly still against the howling chaotic winds of the purple domain.
Fenna.
The Vanguard’s elite sniper remained in a half-crouch with her heavy composite bow still raised and the bowstring perfectly vibrating from the release of the arrow.
Fenna’s sharp hazel eyes were locked directly onto Hiro’s scarred face.
She had perfectly calculated the exact trajectory to bypass the spatial lock and neutralize the immediate threat to her sisters.
Down in the mud, Brida groaned heavily, forcing herself up onto one knee.
Tasmin wiped a thick streak of blood from her dark lips with her eyes glaring at the blind man.
Both Vanguard women looked up toward the ridge.
Fenna lowered her bow slightly.
She looked down at Brida and Tasmin with her expression completely calm and purely professional.
Fenna slowly raised her left hand, offering them a single confident thumbs up.
Brida let out a ragged bloody laugh while Tasmin smirked, reaching down to pull a spare dagger from her boot.
’Does this bitch need to laugh over everythin—’
But Fenna’s thumbs up only lasted for exactly one second.
Her eagle-sharp eyes suddenly widened in horror as she saw the geometric blue lines of the Mind’s Eye domain violently shifting entirely around Hiro’s hands.
Fenna dropped her hand, raising her bow aggressively as she screamed at the top of her lungs with her voice tearing through the quiet purple void!
"Look out!"
The sky above the Blessed Land territory did not just change color. It felt as though the very fabric of the atmosphere had been forcefully suffocated.

Far away from the chaotic frontlines of the Umbral Basin, inside the fortified pristine walls of the main Keep, the bright morning light was suddenly and violently overwritten by a deep unnatural shade of dark purple.
The ambient mana in the air grew instantly heavy, pressing down on the stone courtyards and the lush garden terraces like an invisible, crushing weight.
Inside the main lounge of the Keep, Morwenna stepped in through the front door

The SSS-Rank Dread Queen was clad in her signature dark pirate cloak with her hair falling in wild untamed waves across her shoulders, and her stormy gray eyes immediately darted toward the massive glass windows overlooking the distant valley.
She could physically feel her own mana resisting the heavy purple light radiating from the distant horizon.
"What in the depths of the abyss is that?" Morwenna muttered.
Her hand reflexively dropped to the sword resting at her hip.
"It is a high-tier spatial domain," a calm melodic voice answered from the center of the room.
Morwenna turned her head.
Eluned, the SSS-Rank Goddess of Nature and the undisputed First Wife of the Blessed Land, was lounging gracefully on the plush velvet sofa.
She was wearing a simple elegant green sundress that perfectly complemented her stunning emerald eyes and flowing silver-green hair.
A silver plate of freshly harvested glowing red mana-apples rested on the low wooden table directly in front of her.
Eluned picked up a slice of apple, popping it casually into her mouth. She didn’t look bothered by the terrifying purple sky outside the window at all.

"It seems Lord Sky’s vanguard possesses a rather unique trick," Eluned noted smoothly, chewing the sweet fruit. "It is completely suppressing the ambient mana across the entire western quadrant. A forced perception field, if I had to guess."
Morwenna frowned deeply. She stepped away from the window with her heavy boots clicking against the polished floorboards.
"Are you not worried?" Morwenna asked, her tone becoming very serious. "That domain is massive. It requires a monstrous amount of energy to sustain a spatial lock of that magnitude."
Eluned simply smiled, picking up another apple slice.

"Worried? About what exactly?" Eluned asked, her tone entirely light and breezy. "Lord Silas is out there. Aeliana is hovering in the upper atmosphere with enough artillery to completely vaporize a mountain I think. Talira is currently flying around as a primordial dragon. Brida, Tasmin, and Rowenna are on the ground."
Eluned swallowed the fruit, delicately dusting off her slender fingers.

"Whoever cast that domain has essentially locked themselves inside a cage with six calamities as well as the other girls," Eluned declared with unwavering faith. "They will handle it. Our Lord does not lose."
Morwenna stared at the Nature Goddess for a long quiet moment and she slowly released her tight grip on the hilt of her sword.
Eluned was right.
’I won’t tell her though...’
The overwhelming firepower currently deployed on the western front was absurd.
If anything, Morwenna was slightly annoyed she had been assigned to rear defense while the rest of the girls got to completely let loose and destroy things.
It was a tactical decision... someone had to protect the Keep in case people slipped through but that didn’t make it any less frustrating.
However, looking at Eluned sitting comfortably on the sofa, a different and far more pressing thought completely overtook the Dread Queen’s mind.
Morwenna slowly approached the center of the lounge.
Her stormy gray eyes shifted nervously.
She completely dropped her usual boisterous aggressive pirate captain persona as she suddenly looked incredibly hesitant, fidgeting tightly with the dark leather cuffs of her gloves.
"Eluned..." Morwenna started.
Her voice dropped to a surprisingly quiet respectful tone.
Eluned raised a delicate eyebrow, leaning back against the plush velvet cushions.
"Yes, Morwenna?" Eluned asked smoothly. "Do you need something?"
Morwenna swallowed hard.
Her pride was a massive tangible thing but her overwhelming desire for her Lord was eclipsing her pride.
She had tried everything to get Silas into her bed.
’Not everything but considering Eluned did it, there has to be a method that I’m not aware about right?’

She had sparred with him in the freezing rain and she had thrown herself at him though he was busy but she constantly found herself completely outmaneuvered, outclassed, and thoroughly flustered by his attitude.
Meanwhile, Eluned commanded his attention with effortless grace.
’Even though I don’t like it, I’ve decided...’
Morwenna took a deep breath as she stepped forward.
THUD!
Morwenna went entirely on her knees on the thick luxurious carpet, kneeling directly in front of the sofa.
She bowed her head with her hair spilling entirely over her dark shoulders.
"Teach me," Morwenna pleaded.
Her voice was tight with genuine desperation.
Eluned blinked, taken aback by the sudden display of utter submission from the highly aggressive pirate.
"Teach you what?" Eluned asked, leaning forward slightly.
Morwenna looked up, her stormy gray eyes burning with raw determination.

"Teach me how to properly seduce him," Morwenna begged. "Teach me how to handle him. I want him so badly it physically hurts my core. But every single time I try to push him, he completely reverses the dynamic and leaves me a blushing stuttering mess. You... you have him wrapped around your finger. You know exactly what he wants."
Morwenna leaned forward with her hands resting on the edge of the low table.
"Please," Morwenna whispered. "I am begging you. Give me lessons so that I can finally share his bed."
Eluned stared down at the kneeling pirate captain.
For a few long seconds, the Nature Goddess remained perfectly still, her emerald eyes completely unreadable.
Then, very slowly, a brilliant wicked and incredibly bratty grin began to stretch entirely across Eluned’s beautiful face.
Oh, this was absolutely perfect.
Eluned casually crossed her long slender legs, leaning back into the velvet cushions with the supreme undeniable authority of the First Wife.
"Lessons?" Eluned repeated, her voice dripping with sweet sadistic amusement. "You want me to teach you the delicate refined art of pleasing our Lord?"

The perfection of the parry completely shattered Tasmin’s grip as both of her shortswords were violently knocked into the air!
Hiro followed up instantly.
He extended two fingers and lightly, almost gently, tapped the exact center of Tasmin’s chest.
BZZZZZT!
Another highly concentrated pulse of spatial pressure detonated.
Tasmin coughed up a violent spray of blood with the impact crushing the breath entirely out of her lungs as she was blasted backward through the air.
CRASH!
CRASH!
Brida and Tasmin crashed heavily into the mud twenty yards away, both completely disarmed, bruised, and violently pushed back by a man who hadn’t even drawn a weapon.
Hiro stood perfectly still in the center of the crater, his empty scarred sockets leaking bright blue light into the terrifying purple domain.
Kassandra, kneeling in the mud just a few feet behind Hiro, saw the entire exchange.
Her pink eyes widened with fanatic awe.
’Is this really Hiro...?’
The blind vanguard had just effortlessly dismantled two monsters who had nearly killed her.
Seeing the two Vanguard women struggling to stand up in the distance, Kassandra realized this was the exact perfect moment to secure her victory and reclaim her honor.
"I will finish them!" Kassandra yelled fiercely.

She forced her bruised, battered body up from the mud as she surged every single drop of remaining mana into her pink runic armor, preparing to launch a devastating kinetic blast at the vulnerable Vanguard women.
Kassandra shot forward with her fist glowing with bright pink energy, fully intending to blow Tasmin’s head off while she was unarmed.
But as Kassandra took her third step...
ZIP!
A nearly invisible silent streak of light shot down from the high stone ridge located far above the battlefield.
It was a masterfully crafted projectile perfectly calculated to bypass standard wind resistance and spatial anomalies.
THWACK!
The projectile slammed directly into the exact microscopic gap between Kassandra’s heavy pink helmet and her neck armor.
It was a specialized non-lethal knockout arrow.
"Guh—" Kassandra choked with her pink eyes rolling completely into the back of her head.
The concentrated sleep toxin instantly flooded her exhausted nervous system as her glowing pink fist sputtered and died.
THUD!
Kassandra collapsed face-first into the mud, completely knocked out cold before she could even launch her attack.
Hiro stopped.
He didn’t turn his head as his empty sockets simply focused entirely on the high stone ridge overlooking the crater.
Up on the edge of the jagged cliff, standing perfectly still against the howling chaotic winds of the purple domain.
Fenna.
The Vanguard’s elite sniper remained in a half-crouch with her heavy composite bow still raised and the bowstring perfectly vibrating from the release of the arrow.
Fenna’s sharp hazel eyes were locked directly onto Hiro’s scarred face.
She had perfectly calculated the exact trajectory to bypass the spatial lock and neutralize the immediate threat to her sisters.
Down in the mud, Brida groaned heavily, forcing herself up onto one knee.
Tasmin wiped a thick streak of blood from her dark lips with her eyes glaring at the blind man.
Both Vanguard women looked up toward the ridge.
Fenna lowered her bow slightly.
She looked down at Brida and Tasmin with her expression completely calm and purely professional.
Fenna slowly raised her left hand, offering them a single confident thumbs up.
Brida let out a ragged bloody laugh while Tasmin smirked, reaching down to pull a spare dagger from her boot.
’Does this bitch need to laugh over everythin—’
But Fenna’s thumbs up only lasted for exactly one second.
Her eagle-sharp eyes suddenly widened in horror as she saw the geometric blue lines of the Mind’s Eye domain violently shifting entirely around Hiro’s hands.
Fenna dropped her hand, raising her bow aggressively as she screamed at the top of her lungs with her voice tearing through the quiet purple void!
"Look out!"
The sky above the Blessed Land territory did not just change color.
It felt as though the very fabric of the atmosphere had been forcefully suffocated.

Far away from the chaotic frontlines of the Umbral Basin, inside the fortified pristine walls of the main Keep, the bright morning light was suddenly and violently overwritten by a deep unnatural shade of dark purple.
The ambient mana in the air grew instantly heavy, pressing down on the stone courtyards and the lush garden terraces like an invisible, crushing weight.
Inside the main lounge of the Keep, Morwenna stepped in through the front door

The SSS-Rank Dread Queen was clad in her signature dark pirate cloak with her hair falling in wild untamed waves across her shoulders, and her stormy gray eyes immediately darted toward the massive glass windows overlooking the distant valley.
She could physically feel her own mana resisting the heavy purple light radiating from the distant horizon.
"What in the depths of the abyss is that?" Morwenna muttered.
Her hand reflexively dropped to the sword resting at her hip.
"It is a high-tier spatial domain," a calm melodic voice answered from the center of the room.
Morwenna turned her head.
Eluned, the SSS-Rank Goddess of Nature and the undisputed First Wife of the Blessed Land, was lounging gracefully on the plush velvet sofa.
She was wearing a simple elegant green sundress that perfectly complemented her stunning emerald eyes and flowing silver-green hair.
A silver plate of freshly harvested glowing red mana-apples rested on the low wooden table directly in front of her.
Eluned picked up a slice of apple, popping it casually into her mouth.
She didn’t look bothered by the terrifying purple sky outside the window at all.
"It seems Lord Sky’s vanguard possesses a rather unique trick," Eluned noted smoothly, chewing the sweet fruit.
"It is completely suppressing the ambient mana across the entire western quadrant.
A forced perception field, if I had to guess."
Morwenna frowned deeply.
She stepped away from the window with her heavy boots clicking against the polished floorboards.
"Are you not worried?" Morwenna asked, her tone becoming very serious.
"That domain is massive.
It requires a monstrous amount of energy to sustain a spatial lock of that magnitude."
Eluned simply smiled, picking up another apple slice.
"Worried?
About what exactly?" Eluned asked, her tone entirely light and breezy.
"Lord Silas is out there.
Aeliana is hovering in the upper atmosphere with enough artillery to completely vaporize a mountain I think.
Talira is currently flying around as a primordial dragon.
Brida, Tasmin, and Rowenna are on the ground."
Eluned swallowed the fruit, delicately dusting off her slender fingers.
"Whoever cast that domain has essentially locked themselves inside a cage with six calamities as well as the other girls," Eluned declared with unwavering faith.
"They will handle it.
Our Lord does not lose."
Morwenna stared at the Nature Goddess for a long quiet moment and she slowly released her tight grip on the hilt of her sword.
Eluned was right.
’I won’t tell her though...’
The overwhelming firepower currently deployed on the western front was absurd.
If anything, Morwenna was slightly annoyed she had been assigned to rear defense while the rest of the girls got to completely let loose and destroy things.
It was a tactical decision... someone had to protect the Keep in case people slipped through but that didn’t make it any less frustrating.
However, looking at Eluned sitting comfortably on the sofa, a different and far more pressing thought completely overtook the Dread Queen’s mind.
Morwenna slowly approached the center of the lounge.
Her stormy gray eyes shifted nervously.
She completely dropped her usual boisterous aggressive pirate captain persona as she suddenly looked incredibly hesitant, fidgeting tightly with the dark leather cuffs of her gloves.
"Eluned..." Morwenna started.
Her voice dropped to a surprisingly quiet respectful tone.
Eluned raised a delicate eyebrow, leaning back against the plush velvet cushions.
"Yes, Morwenna?" Eluned asked smoothly.
"Do you need something?"
Morwenna swallowed hard.
Her pride was a massive tangible thing but her overwhelming desire for her Lord was eclipsing her pride.
She had tried everything to get Silas into her bed.
’Not everything but considering Eluned did it, there has to be a method that I’m not aware about right?’

She had sparred with him in the freezing rain and she had thrown herself at him though he was busy but she constantly found herself completely outmaneuvered, outclassed, and thoroughly flustered by his attitude.
Meanwhile, Eluned commanded his attention with effortless grace.
’Even though I don’t like it, I’ve decided...’
Morwenna took a deep breath as she stepped forward.
THUD!
Morwenna went entirely on her knees on the thick luxurious carpet, kneeling directly in front of the sofa.
She bowed her head with her hair spilling entirely over her dark shoulders.
"Teach me," Morwenna pleaded.
Her voice was tight with genuine desperation.
Eluned blinked, taken aback by the sudden display of utter submission from the highly aggressive pirate.
"Teach you what?" Eluned asked, leaning forward slightly.
Morwenna looked up, her stormy gray eyes burning with raw determination.
"Teach me how to properly seduce him," Morwenna begged.
"Teach me how to handle him.
I want him so badly it physically hurts my core.
But every single time I try to push him, he completely reverses the dynamic and leaves me a blushing stuttering mess.
You... you have him wrapped around your finger.
You know exactly what he wants."
Morwenna leaned forward with her hands resting on the edge of the low table.
"Please," Morwenna whispered.
"I am begging you.
Give me lessons so that I can finally share his bed."
Eluned stared down at the kneeling pirate captain.
For a few long seconds, the Nature Goddess remained perfectly still, her emerald eyes completely unreadable.
Then, very slowly, a brilliant wicked and incredibly bratty grin began to stretch entirely across Eluned’s beautiful face.
Oh, this was absolutely perfect.
Eluned casually crossed her long slender legs, leaning back into the velvet cushions with the supreme undeniable authority of the First Wife.
"Lessons?" Eluned repeated, her voice dripping with sweet sadistic amusement.
"You want me to teach you the delicate refined art of pleasing our Lord?"

chapters.title: Chapter 328: Evelyn [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: "Yes!" Morwenna nodded vigorously, completely missing the dangerous glint in Eluned’s eyes. "I will do anything!"
"Anything?" Eluned echoed softly.
"Anything," Morwenna confirmed, sealing her own fate in Eluned’s hands.
Eluned’s grin widened into a beaming smile.
She raised her delicate right hand, lazily pointing her index finger toward the hallway leading to the Keep’s kitchen.
"Go make me some tea..." Eluned commanded smoothly.
Morwenna froze as she blinked in utter confusion.
’What does this Bitch want me to do...?’
"Tea?" Morwenna asked.

"Yes, tea," Eluned instructed with her voice becoming specific and unapologetically bossy. "I want tea... Not the dried leaves from the pantry. I want you to go out to the garden, pluck the fresh flowers, and steep them properly. Add a touch of wild honey from Kaelia’s pantry and bring it to me."
Morwenna’s jaw dropped entirely open.

"You... you want me to brew you tea?" Morwenna stammered, her pirate pride instantly flaring up like a struck match. "I am asking you for very important seduction lessons and you are treating me like a damn scullery maid?!"
Eluned let out a soft mocking sigh, looking casually at her manicured nails.

"Well, if you don’t want to learn patience, obedience, and how to properly serve..." Eluned trailed off, giving a dramatic dismissive shrug. "I suppose you can just go back to trying to tackle him in the mud like a feral beast. Let me know how that works out for you. Vir... gin..."
Morwenna gritted her teeth so hard a faint grinding sound echoed loudly in the quiet lounge.
Her stormy gray eyes flared with immense burning irritation.
She absolutely hated being ordered around... She was a captain and she was the one that gave the orders.
But... she desperately wanted Silas.
"Fine," Morwenna grumbled heavily.
She forced herself up from the carpet. With a heavy dramatic sigh of total defeat, she reached directly into her storage ring. It was a prototype that Thora had gotten to make.
With a flash of light, her heavy leather pirate coat vanished.
In its place, she pulled out a frilly ridiculous white kitchen apron, tying it aggressively around her waist over her dark undershirt.
"Three drops of honey with proper steeping," Morwenna muttered angrily to herself.
She turned on her heel and stomped heavily toward the kitchen hallway.
"I swear to the abyss, if this doesn’t actually help me get into his bed, I am going to poison the next cup, weed." Morwenna threatened the empty air.
Eluned watched the terrifying SSS-Rank Dread Queen angrily march into the kitchen wearing a frilly white apron.
The Nature Goddess let out a soft delighted giggle, resting her chin comfortably on her hand.
’Now I can tell her to do whatever I want~’ Eluned thought gleefully, her emerald eyes sparkling with unrestrained mischief.
Far out on the crushed, ruined bedrock of the western front, completely ignorant of the domestic hierarchy currently being established in his Keep, Silas stood in the mud.
The Lord of the Blessed Land was entirely focused on the completely surreal situation unfolding directly in front of him.
The terrifying deep purple light of the Mind’s Eye domain washed heavily over the landscape.
His sleek silver armor and imposing dark hood had completely vanished, forcefully stripped away by the perception field.
Standing exactly ten feet away from him, sitting helplessly in the freezing mud, was the Lord of The Unmovable Wall.
She was not a broad-shouldered man with a metallic voice.
She was a petite, undeniably beautiful young woman with long, silky black hair and sharp exhausted dark eyes.
She was swimming entirely inside a massively oversized dark-gray Earth traveler’s hoodie and heavy trousers.
"So," Silas spoke slowly.
His deep voice cut through the quiet suffocating tension of the purple domain.
"If your name isn’t actually Sky... what is it?" Silas asked.
The black-haired girl scowled deeply.
She scrambled up from the mud, furiously dusting off her oversized hoodie.
She didn’t look like a Lord right now.
She looked like an incredibly stressed college student who had just been forcefully dragged out of her dorm room in the middle of a marathon study session.
’I’d know because I used to be one of them...’
Without answering him, she reached deep into the pocket of her hoodie.
She pulled out a slim, expensive-looking silver case and a sleek plasma lighter.
With trembling fingers, she popped the case open. She pulled out a thin white cigarette and placed it securely between her soft lips.
CLICK! FWOOSH!
A tiny blue flame ignited the tip. She took a long deep drag, holding the smoke in her chest for three entire seconds before slowly exhaling a thick plume of gray smoke into the freezing purple air.
"Haah~"
Silas frowned deeply, his golden-ringed eyes watching her with a mix of genuine curiosity and apprehensiveness.

"You do realize those are terrible for your health, right?" Silas pointed out bluntly. "We are in the Sovereign Realm facing monsters and horrors, and you’re actively choosing to poison your own lungs."
She let out a harsh scoff, taking another heavy drag.

"I have a Lord core, Vespera... or whoever the hell you are," she shot back irritably with the smoke curling rapidly around her dark hair. "Cancer isn’t exactly on my radar. This is the only thing that actually forces my brain to slow down for five damn seconds. Governing a mobile fortress full of meatheads is incredibly stressful."
She flicked a bit of ash onto the shattered bedrock with her sharp dark eyes locking directly onto his.
"And for the record," she continued, her voice losing the arrogant Lord persona and settling into a natural exhausted tone. "It’s Evelyn... My real name is Evelyn."
Silas nodded slowly, fully absorbing the information.
"Evelyn," Silas repeated, testing the name. "It suits you a lot better than Sky. I’m Silas."
Evelyn snorted, rolling her dark eyes.
"Of course it is," Evelyn muttered. "Silas and Evelyn... What nice names, we’re both just a couple of people faking our entire public personas to avoid political bullshit."
"Pretty much," Silas agreed with a small smirk. "Though, I must admit, the oversized hoodie is a bold choice for frontline combat."
"Bite me," Evelyn grumbled, crossing her arms tightly over her chest.
Before they could continue their bizarre unprecedented bonding moment, the heavy purple light of the domain pulsed violently around them again.
The ambient pressure was suffocating.
Evelyn’s sharp dark eyes instantly shifted away from Silas. She tracked the glowing blue lines that were actively etched into the very air itself.
Her brilliant, strategic mind immediately began calculating the raw mana density required to sustain the spatial lock.

"This... this is impossible," Evelyn whispered, her cigarette hanging loosely from her lips. "Hiro is incredibly strong. He’s one of my best vanguards but he doesn’t have the internal mana reserves to cast a domain of this magnitude. This should be physically burning out his mana circuits."
Evelyn wasn’t even aware he had a domain at all, but she wouldn’t admit it.
Silas narrowed his golden eyes, stepping up firmly beside her.
He looked out across the ruined battlefield toward the distant massive crater where the center of the purple light originated.
"Unless he isn’t the one providing the fuel," Silas noted coldly.
Evelyn snapped her fingers, her dark eyes widening in sudden horrific realization.

"Elm!" Evelyn gasped. "He’s tethered to Elm! She’s my backline support... She possesses an incredibly massive ocean-like mana pool, but she has absolutely zero offensive capabilities as of right now and she was acting as a pure living battery for the entire fortress."
That was also the reason why it felt like Elm’s energy had cut off, Evelyn had been thinking maybe she deactivated it but it seemed that was not the case.
’Fuck!’
Evelyn took off in a rapid desperate sprint across the crushed bedrock as she headed straight toward the center of the domain.
"Hiro!" Evelyn screamed at the top of her lungs, completely abandoning her tactical restraint."Hiro, stand down! The duel is over! I surrendered! Cut the connection!"
She ran forward, waving her unarmored arms frantically to get her vanguard’s attention but as she crossed the thirty-yard mark...
HUMMMMM.
A sudden terrifying shift in the spatial pressure directly in front of her occurred.
An invisible concentrated slash of raw mana tore straight through the air, aimed exactly at her center of mass!
Evelyn’s eyes widened in utter horror.
"Fuc—"
She was completely unarmored.
The disguise artifact that provided her passive defenses was entirely offline and the invisible slash was going to cut her completely in half!
SWISH!
A blur of dark movement stepped effortlessly in front of her.
CLANGGGGGGG!
A deafening shockwave of displaced air exploded violently outward.
Silas had drawn his steel longsword with blinding speed.
He stood firmly planted in the mud directly in front of Evelyn, the flat of his heavy steel blade completely intercepting the invisible spatial slash.
The force of the parry pushed Silas back half an inch, his boots leaving thick trenches in the dirt, but his Gold Core frame held the line effortlessly.
"What the hell?!" Evelyn shrieked, stumbling backward and falling onto her hands in the freezing mud. "He... he just attacked me! I’m his Lord!"
Silas smoothly lowered his steel longsword with his golden-ringed eyes locking onto the distant figure of Hiro standing far away in the crater.
"He can’t see you, Evelyn," Silas explained coldly.
He instantly mapped the entire combat scenario, according to what they had heard from Hiro talking with other Heroes on the Listening Runes.
’I didn’t think his domain was going to be this massive though...’

"His physical eyes are gone, and this domain is a spatial lock," Silas continued, not taking his eyes off the threat. "He isn’t looking at faces or reading signatures. He is reading pure spatial awareness and hostile intent and right now from what I can guess, his brain is processing the entire battlefield as a massive threat."
Silas flicked his blade, sending the lingering spatial friction harmlessly into the dirt.

"Because he is relying on a fragile external battery to sustain this massive spell like you said," Silas deduced sharply, "I guess his automatic targeting parameters are likely set to indiscriminately repel any approaching spell or fast-moving entity to protect his absolute focus. To him, you aren’t Evelyn. You are just another hostile mass of atoms rushing his position."
Evelyn stared at Silas in awe.
In less than five seconds, the Lord of the Blessed Land had perfectly analyzed the exact weakness and targeting mechanism of her own vanguard’s ultimate ability.

"Then... what do we do?" Evelyn asked, hurriedly pushing herself up from the mud. "If he keeps this domain active, it’s going to fry his internal circuits... He can’t handle Elm’s raw output for more than a few minutes without causing permanent brain damage. We have to cut the power on Elm."
Evelyn looked at Silas, her dark eyes filled with urgent desperate stress.

"And you, why aren’t you running over there to save your girls?" Evelyn asked, genuinely confused by his calm demeanor. "They are trapped in an domain against an enemy who can manipulate space itself. Doesn’t that worry you?"
Silas let out a soft amused scoff.
He didn’t look worried, he looked incredibly calm as she said.
Silas slowly lifted his chin, his glowing golden eyes looking high up into the dark purple sky.
Hovering effortlessly in the air, glowing with brilliant celestial radiance, was the Astrea Archon of the Stars.
And currently descending rapidly from the dark clouds was the massive, seventy-foot-long Primordial Crimson Dragon.
"Worry about them?" Silas repeated, shaking his head. "Evelyn, my girls are much harder to deal with than this. On the other hand..."
Silas looked down at Evelyn with a completely straight face.

"I’m hoping they don’t accidentally turn your guy into a red smear on the bedrock before we figure out how to safely shut this down," Silas admitted bluntly. "Let’s go find this Elm battery of yours before he completely fries his own brain."
Evelyn stared at him for a second, then quickly nodded. She tossed her half-smoked cigarette entirely into the mud.
"Follow me," Evelyn ordered.
She took off in a rapid sprint toward the eastern ridge where her command lines and support units were securely situated.
Silas kept his longsword drawn, effortlessly keeping pace with the stressed hoodie-wearing Lord as they navigated rapidly through the dark purple hellscape.
’I want to learn about how she differs her identities...’
Meanwhile, exactly in the center of the massive sixty-foot crater.
Hiro stood perfectly still.
To the outside world, he looked like an untouchable serene god of space.
His hands rested calmly at his sides.
The brilliant, piercing blue light leaked flawlessly from his empty eye sockets, mapping the spatial layout of the entire Umbral Basin.𝕗𝐫𝐞𝕖𝕨𝐞𝗯𝚗𝕠𝘃𝐞𝚕.𝐜𝗼𝚖
But internally, Hiro was in agonizing hell.
’Forgive me, My Lord,’ Hiro thought desperately.
His mind was burning with white-hot pain.
The raw unfiltered power of Elm’s massive mana pool was forcefully surging through his relatively fragile internal circuits.
His brain was attempting to consciously process the exact spatial coordinates, the atomic structure, and the kinetic trajectories of billions of variables simultaneously.
It was as one would say, a sensory overload.

He stood firmly planted in the mud directly in front of Evelyn, the flat of his heavy steel blade completely intercepting the invisible spatial slash.
The force of the parry pushed Silas back half an inch, his boots leaving thick trenches in the dirt, but his Gold Core frame held the line effortlessly.
"What the hell?!" Evelyn shrieked, stumbling backward and falling onto her hands in the freezing mud.
"He... he just attacked me!
I’m his Lord!"
Silas smoothly lowered his steel longsword with his golden-ringed eyes locking onto the distant figure of Hiro standing far away in the crater.
"He can’t see you, Evelyn," Silas explained coldly.
He instantly mapped the entire combat scenario, according to what they had heard from Hiro talking with other Heroes on the Listening Runes.
’I didn’t think his domain was going to be this massive though...’
"His physical eyes are gone, and this domain is a spatial lock," Silas continued, not taking his eyes off the threat.
"He isn’t looking at faces or reading signatures.
He is reading pure spatial awareness and hostile intent and right now from what I can guess, his brain is processing the entire battlefield as a massive threat."
Silas flicked his blade, sending the lingering spatial friction harmlessly into the dirt.

"Because he is relying on a fragile external battery to sustain this massive spell like you said," Silas deduced sharply, "I guess his automatic targeting parameters are likely set to indiscriminately repel any approaching spell or fast-moving entity to protect his absolute focus.
To him, you aren’t Evelyn.
You are just another hostile mass of atoms rushing his position."
Evelyn stared at Silas in awe.
In less than five seconds, the Lord of the Blessed Land had perfectly analyzed the exact weakness and targeting mechanism of her own vanguard’s ultimate ability.
"Then... what do we do?" Evelyn asked, hurriedly pushing herself up from the mud.
"If he keeps this domain active, it’s going to fry his internal circuits...
He can’t handle Elm’s raw output for more than a few minutes without causing permanent brain damage.
We have to cut the power on Elm."
Evelyn looked at Silas, her dark eyes filled with urgent desperate stress.
"And you, why aren’t you running over there to save your girls?" Evelyn asked, genuinely confused by his calm demeanor.
"They are trapped in an domain against an enemy who can manipulate space itself.
Doesn’t that worry you?"
Silas let out a soft amused scoff.
He didn’t look worried, he looked incredibly calm as she said.
Silas slowly lifted his chin, his glowing golden eyes looking high up into the dark purple sky.
Hovering effortlessly in the air, glowing with brilliant celestial radiance, was the Astrea Archon of the Stars.
And currently descending rapidly from the dark clouds was the massive, seventy-foot-long Primordial Crimson Dragon.
"Worry about them?" Silas repeated, shaking his head.
"Evelyn, my girls are much harder to deal with than this.
On the other hand..."
Silas looked down at Evelyn with a completely straight face.
"I’m hoping they don’t accidentally turn your guy into a red smear on the bedrock before we figure out how to safely shut this down," Silas admitted bluntly.
"Let’s go find this Elm battery of yours before he completely fries his own brain."
Evelyn stared at him for a second, then quickly nodded.
She tossed her half-smoked cigarette entirely into the mud.
"Follow me," Evelyn ordered.
She took off in a rapid sprint toward the eastern ridge where her command lines and support units were securely situated.
Silas kept his longsword drawn, effortlessly keeping pace with the stressed hoodie-wearing Lord as they navigated rapidly through the dark purple hellscape.
’I want to learn about how she differs her identities...’
Meanwhile, exactly in the center of the massive sixty-foot crater.
Hiro stood perfectly still.
To the outside world, he looked like an untouchable serene god of space.
His hands rested calmly at his sides.
The brilliant, piercing blue light leaked flawlessly from his empty eye sockets, mapping the spatial layout of the entire Umbral Basin.𝕗𝐫𝐞𝕖𝕨𝐞𝗯𝚗𝕠𝘃𝐞𝚕.𝐜𝗼𝚖
But internally, Hiro was in agonizing hell.
’Forgive me, My Lord,’ Hiro thought desperately.
His mind was burning with white-hot pain.
The raw unfiltered power of Elm’s massive mana pool was forcefully surging through his relatively fragile internal circuits.
His brain was attempting to consciously process the exact spatial coordinates, the atomic structure, and the kinetic trajectories of billions of variables simultaneously.
It was as one would say, a sensory overload.

chapters.title: Chapter 329: The Weakness Of Mind’s Eye [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: Every single falling drop of freezing rain, every shifting pebble, and the terrifying dense mana signatures of the women surrounding him were all flooding his mind with infinite data points.
"Ugh... We need to win..."
If he maintained the Mind’s Eye for even three more minutes, his brain would literally hemorrhage so he had to end this instantly.
Twenty yards away, Tasmin pushed herself up from the mud.
The Shadow Commander wiped a thick streak of blood from her dark lips.
Her crimson eyes locked entirely onto Hiro’s serene, blindfolded face.
She had just watched him effortlessly swat away Brida’s multi-ton axe and perfectly parry her own strike.
He was untouchable in a clean straightforward exchange butTasmin was a Huntress and she didn’t fight clean.
"Let’s see just how perfectly you can process things, blind man," Tasmin hissed.
Tasmin didn’t use a Phantom Leap as she stayed on the ground, engaging her raw physical speed once more.
SWISH!
She shot forward, picking up two jagged chunks of shattered bedrock from the mud as she ran.
Instead of swinging her shortswords, Tasmin violently hurled the massive stones directly toward Hiro’s chest.
At the exact same second, she whipped her dark Eclipse-Thread chains outward.
She explicitly layered her attacks, channeling a massive burst of blinding chaotic crimson flames through the metal links.
The attack was a mess... It was completely uncoordinated, lacking any pure martial form.
It was just a massive, overlapping wave of rocks, screaming chains, and explosive fire.
Hiro didn’t flinch.
He raised his right hand with his mind desperately tracking the incoming sensory data.
’Spatial Deflection.’
CRACK! BOOM!
The invisible spatial pressure effortlessly deflected the two heavy stones, sending them crashing into the distance.
The exact same wave parted the crimson flames flawlessly down the middle, perfectly protecting his unarmored body but Tasmin didn’t care about the deflection at all.
Her sharp crimson eyes were locked on his right hand.
She watched his fingers so she watched the microscopic twitch of his muscles.
...And then Tasmin saw it.
The deflection was perfect, but his response lagged... barely a heartbeat, but enough.
When forced to process the mass of the rocks alongside the chaotic unstable crimson flames, his brain had physically stalled.
The number of spells and physical variables was too complex to process instantly.
Tasmin’s dark lips curled into a sharp lethal smirk.
She immediately aborted her charge, using a rapid back-step to slide fifteen yards away, completely retreating from his immediate effective range.
"I see," Tasmin whispered quietly to herself.
As Tasmin backed off, the rest of the Vanguard finally arrived at the edge of the crater.
KRA-THOOOOOM.
The massive Primordial Crimson Dragon landed heavily on the upper lip of the destroyed bedrock.
Talira’s weight shook the entire ground, her massive golden eyes glaring down at the blind man.
With a brilliant flash of light, she transformed smoothly back into her humanoid form, her crimson tail swishing aggressively as she drew a deep breath of fire.
VWOOOOOOM!
Aeliana slowly floated down from the dark purple clouds.
The Astrea Archon of the Stars hovered exactly twenty feet above the crater floor.
Her luminous cosmic green eyes tracked the blue lines of the domain with Starlight mana actively sparked and hissed around her delicate fingers.
Footsteps echoed from the northern side.
Rowenna, the Grand Runemaster, walked casually to the edge of the crater.
She elegantly adjusted the sleeves of her pristine white robes, her deep blue eyes entirely unbothered by the domain.
Finally, Brida marched heavily forward to stand exactly beside Tasmin.
The Titan Bastion reached down, pulling her massive Void Cleaver entirely out of the mud, cracking her thick neck with a loud pop.
Hiro was now completely surrounded by five S-Rank walking calamities in a way.

"Tasmin," Rowenna called out softly, her voice carrying clearly across the crater. "His domain is highly suppressive... He is utilizing forced spatial awareness to redirect force. Have you mapped a viable counter-strategy?"
Tasmin didn’t look away from Hiro. Her eyes glowed with certainty.
"I have," Tasmin declared loudly, ensuring Hiro heard every single word.
Tasmin raised one of her dark shortswords, pointing the sharp mythril tip directly at Hiro’s chest.

"He is relying on his spatial awareness to read our spells," Tasmin explained. "If you throw a single sword swing, a single arrow, or a single massive boulder at him, his mind perfectly processes the exact requirement to effortlessly deflect it. He can redirect raw force flawlessly."
Tasmin smiled dangerously.

"But he is still just a human," Tasmin continued confidently. "His brain has a hard processing limit. He is relying on an external mana source to sustain this domain, which means his own mind is the physical bottleneck."
Tasmin tightened her grip on her twin blades.

"When I threw chaotic unstable crimson flames at him alongside physical debris, his deflection lagged a bit," Tasmin revealed clearly. "He struggled to process the number of things going on simultaneously so we can guess his brain physically stalled from sensory overload."
In the center of the crater, Hiro’s serene stoic expression completely cracked.
His jaw tightened visibly. The glowing blue light leaking from his empty sockets flickered violently for a fraction of a second.
Tasmin had perfectly deduced his weakness in a single, probing exchange.
"So," Tasmin concluded, raising her voice to address the entire Vanguard. "The strategy is incredibly simple. We do not engage him in a clean duel. We do not throw single, isolated attacks..."
Tasmin’s S-Rank shadow mana violently erupted around her boots in a massive, swirling vortex.
"We throw too many spells for his brain to handle!" Tasmin commanded! "We overload his senses!"
Instantly, the entire Vanguard synchronized with terrifying precision.
"Understood!" Rowenna declared cleanly.
The Grand Runemaster slammed the heavy mythril butt of her Sapphire-Core World Weaver into the dirt.
’Omni-Elemental Runic Array!’

Four massive, multi-colored, incredibly intricate magic circles materialized instantly in the air around Rowenna and she didn’t summon a single spell... she summoned a chaotic overlapping mixture of deep purple gravity wells, volatile crimson fire, and jagged sub-zero ice, perfectly designed to scramble Hiro’s control.
"I will incinerate his perception!" Talira roared.
The primordial dragon-girl opened her mouth wide as white-hot, volcanic fire violently condensed in her throat, mixing completely erratically with razor-sharp emerald-green wind blades.
It created an unstable swirling tornado of chaos.
Up in the air, Aeliana elegantly raised both of her slender hands toward the purple sky.
’Starfall Barrage!’
Hundreds of volatile glowing orbs of celestial starlight mana materialized entirely in the air above the crater.
The power of the cosmic magic completely distorted the spatial coordinates of the entire quadrant!
Hiro stood entirely still in the center of the crater, completely surrounded by a literal apocalypse of conflicting data.
His mind was screaming in white-hot agony.
The blue lines of his Mind’s Eye domain began to violently glitch and shatter around the edges of the crater...
He couldn’t process the exact trajectories of the hundreds of starlight orbs while simultaneously tracking the expansion of Talira’s fire and the gravitational pull of Rowenna’s magic circles.
The sensory input was simply too immense as his mind was violently overloading.
Brida stepped heavily forward to the front of the line.
She rested the massive flat of the Astral-Forged Void Cleaver casually against her thick, armored shoulder.
She looked at the terrified overwhelmed blind man standing in the center of the crumbling domain as a brutal grin stretched entirely across her scarred face.
"Well then, girls," Brida quipped loudly.
Her booming voice completely shattered the last remnants of Hiro’s serene silence.
"Why don’t we test out this little theory of yours... and see if we can kill him in one go?"

The shattered ruined expanse of the Umbral Basin blurred violently past Silas and Evelyn as they sprinted at maximum velocity through the suffocating, dark purple light of the forced perception domain.
Silas easily kept pace with the exhausted, unarmored girl running beside him.
His frame allowed him to cross the violently crushed bedrock effortlessly with his boots barely making a sound despite the heavy cratered terrain.
His glowing golden-ringed eyes were locked entirely onto the colossal, towering silhouette of The Unmovable Wall looming ominously on the eastern ridge of the battlefield.
It was certainly not Silas’s first time stepping inside an enemy’s command structure.
’Well it’s mostly me entering caves of monsters and I’ve been here several times.’
But he could never grow old of this one.
The Unmovable Wall wasn’t a standard static castle built of stone and mortar.
It was a terrifying massive mobile fortress that actively defied the natural laws of the Sovereign Realm.
As they closed the distance, the sheer scale of the engineering marvel became terrifyingly apparent.
Evelyn didn’t even hesitate as they reached the massive lowered steel boarding ramp at the base of the fortress.
She rushed straight into the dark, metallic underbelly of her own territory with her oversized gray hoodie flapping wildly behind her.
Silas rushed in directly after her, the heavy echoing thud of his combat boots entirely out of place in the high-tech dwarven-engineered corridors of a rival Lord.
"I have to admit, Evelyn, your engineering and architectural team is top-tier," Silas noted calmly.
He effortlessly kept up as she frantically scrambled down a narrow, spiraling metal staircase that led deep into the bowels of the fortress.

"The structural integrity required to move a mass this large without fracturing the internal support beams is staggering," Silas continued, casually observing the thick glowing mana-conduits running along the iron ceiling. "But I still have a dozen questions about your operation. How exactly do you handle the precise voice modulation during a live stream? The deep pitch of the male Sky was flawless. Are you using an artifact hidden in the helmet, or is the audio hardwired and filtered directly through your broadcast drones?"
Silas was just trying to make small talk which would lead to identities being discussed.
Evelyn shot him a completely incredulous wild-eyed glare over her shoulder as she took the metal stairs two at a time.
"Are you seriously asking me about my streaming setup and audio filters right now?!" Evelyn snapped.
Her breathing was incredibly ragged with her lungs burning as she threw her entire physical weight against a heavy rotating iron bulkhead door to push it open.

"My blind vanguard is actively frying his own brain out there on the dirt, and my oldest friend is literally burning her soul to ashes in a tank to power him!" Evelyn yelled, her voice echoing frantically through the dark corridor. "Can we please hold off the casual podcast interview until later?!"
Silas offered a small smirk, seamlessly slipping through the heavy bulkhead door right behind her before it could swing shut.
"Just gathering essential intelligence on a friend," Silas replied smoothly, his golden eyes scanning the dim flickering emergency lights of the subterranean level. "Lead the way, Evelyn."
They descended deeper and deeper into the heavily fortified foundations of the mobile fortress.
The air down here grew incredibly dense, it was filled with the sharp sterile tang of distilled mana-salts and other kinds of things that Silas could not even come close to naming at all.

As they rounded the final sharp corner into the deepest, most secure medical sector of the territory, the ambient temperature in the corridor suddenly and violently spiked to an absolutely unbearable degree.
"Brenna!" Evelyn shouted, her voice echoing off the metal walls.
Standing frantically in front of a massive reinforced iron blast door was Thora’s sister, Brenna.
The stout dwarf was aggressively slamming her heavy mythril-forged wrench against the digital access panel, her face completely slick with panicked terrified sweat.
"My Lord!" Brenna cried out, completely dropping her wrench as she stepped back from the door, ignoring Silas’s sudden presence out of desperation.

"The manual override is jammed!" Brenna reported frantically, pointing a thick trembling finger at the glowing metal. "The ambient mana pressure building up inside the medical chamber is actively warping the internal locking mechanisms! The run-off is fusing the door shut from the inside! I can’t get it open and Elm is in there!"
