chapters.title: Chapter 330: Elm’s Regrets
paragraphs: Silas stepped slowly forward with his glowing golden eyes narrowing sharply.
’This place is really hot...’
He could physically feel the terrifying unstable power of the raw mana leaking through the microscopic seams of the iron door.
The thick metal plating was actively glowing an angry cherry-red, radiating enough pure thermal heat to instantly blister human skin upon contact.
The amount of life force being forcibly converted into spell-fuel inside that room was astronomical.
Evelyn didn’t hesitate for a single agonizing microsecond.
"Stand back, Brenna!" Evelyn commanded.
Her voice lost all traces of the stressed hoodie-wearing adult and suddenly echoed with the absolute authority of a Lord.
Evelyn threw both of her bare hands forward, pointing her palms directly at the superheated center of the blast door.

She didn’t have her heavy mythril disguise armor, and she didn’t have her translucent blue crystal rapier, but she was still a high-tier Lord who had carved her territory out of the brutal Unknown Zones.
"Radiant... Annihilation."
A devastating beam of pure unfiltered light magic erupted directly from Evelyn’s outstretched palms.
KRA-THOOOOOOM!
The destructive light magic slammed perfectly into the center of the superheated iron blast door with catastrophic force.
The heavy melted metal was instantly and violently blown entirely off its reinforced hinges.
The massive slab of iron was sent flying violently inward into the medical chamber, crashing into the far wall in a blinding shower of molten orange sparks and shattered twisted steel.
Evelyn rushed recklessly through the smoking burning doorway, entirely ignoring the searing heat washing over her face, with Silas right on her heels.
The interior of the subterranean medical chamber was a terrifying nightmare.
The air inside the room was actively boiling. Thick, scalding white steam hissed violently from ruptured twisted coolant pipes running along the iron ceiling.
The heavy metal walls were vibrating and shuddering uncontrollably, groaning audibly under the unnatural stress of the massive, territory-wide spell currently anchoring the room to the battlefield.
’I didn’t think it was this bad...’ Evelyn thought.
In the center of the ruined chamber, submerged entirely inside a massive, ceiling-high glass containment cylinder, was Elm.
Silas’s golden-ringed eyes widened slightly at the sight.
Directly beneath the massive glass cylinder, a colossal glowing white Four-Leaf Clover magical circle was violently etched into the solid bedrock foundation of the fortress.
It was flaring with blinding, absolute brilliance, serving as the massive, singular conduit that routed Elm’s raw life force directly out to Hiro on the battlefield.
But the physical cost of sustaining that spell was horror.
The thick, glowing green nutrient fluid inside the glass tank was violently boiling, churning with millions of chaotic pressurized silver bubbles.
And Elm... Elm was actively dying.

Her beautiful, long silky white hair, which had once floated gracefully around her shoulders like a perfect halo of winter frost, was actively shedding and tearing away in large sickening clumps into the boiling fluid.
Her pale skin was stretched terrifyingly tight over her bones.

Her slender frame looked horribly thin and emaciated, as if her actual physical mass and bone density were being literally converted into raw burning mana to feed the glowing clover array beneath her.
Her pristine crystalline silver eyes were wide open, locked entirely and unblinkingly onto the iron ceiling as she forcefully pushed every single remaining drop of her life force down into the spell.
"Elm!" Evelyn screamed, running recklessly up to the boiling, superheated glass.

"Elm, stop!" Evelyn sobbed, slamming her bare hands against the scalding surface, completely ignoring the burns instantly forming on her palms. "Turn it off! The duel is over! I surrendered! Cut the magic right now!"
Inside the boiling, churning tank, Elm’s wide silver eyes slowly shifted downward.
She looked through the thick, vibrating glass, finding her Lord standing there in her oversized, soot-stained gray hoodie, her pale face completely streaked with desperate tears.
Despite the unimaginable soul-tearing agony ripping through her ruptured core and melting her body, Elm offered a soft and heartbreakingly loyal smile from beneath her flexible breathing apparatus.
Her voice echoed weakly through the chamber’s external comm-speaker, sounding completely fragile and broken.

"No, My Lord..." Elm whispered, her voice cracking with pain. "You... you cannot surrender. We... we have to win this broadcast. You built this territory from the dirt. You sacrificed everything for us. I will not let them take it from you."
Evelyn slammed her blistered, burning fists violently against the scalding hot glass.

"We already lost!" Evelyn cried out, tears of panic welling heavily in her dark eyes. "You are dying, Elm! The spell is literally eating your physical body alive! Turn it off before your core shatters completely into dust!"

"I am your sword, Evelyn..." Elm replied, her silver eyes rapidly filling with tears that instantly dissolved into the boiling green fluid surrounding her face. "I have sat alone in this dark room for so long... watching you fight the world... watching Hiro bleed for our people... I am finally useful to you again. I am helping you win."
Evelyn let out a heart-wrenching sob.
She didn’t care about the Lord War anymore.
She didn’t care about the mobile territory, the precious Spirit credits, the massive global stream, or the hundreds of millions of demanding viewers watching from around the world.
She refused to lose her very first Hero.
Evelyn forcefully surged every single drop of her remaining concentrated light and water mana entirely into her right fist.
CRASH! SHAAAAATTER!
Evelyn drove her glowing mana-infused fist directly into the absolute center of the weakened containment cylinder.
The heavy pressurized medical glass violently shattered into a million jagged flying pieces.
A massive, roaring tidal wave of boiling green nutrient fluid and sharp shattered glass washed entirely over the iron floor, splashing heavily against Silas’s dark combat boots.
Elm’s frail, incredibly thin, and ruined body spilled limply out of the broken tank, completely and violently disconnected from her thick life-support cables and breathing tubes.
Evelyn dropped instantly to her knees in the boiling spreading fluid.
She desperately caught Elm’s fragile, broken body securely in her arms before the Hero could hit the hard, unforgiving iron floor.
Evelyn ripped the hissing breathing apparatus completely off of Elm’s face, pulling the dying emaciated woman tightly against her chest, rocking her back and forth in the ruins of the chamber.
"There there... you’re with me now..."
Elm was trembling violently, her entire body seizing with failure.
Her skin was freezing, terrifyingly cold to the touch, despite the boiling hot green fluid thoroughly soaking their clothes.
Her breathing was terribly shallow, coming in weak rattling gasps.
Thick, sickly silver-tinted blood leaked slowly from the corner of her pale, cracking lips, running down her chin and dripping onto Evelyn’s gray hoodie.
Her vital life force was almost gone.
"Evelyn..." Elm coughed weakly.
Her crystalline silver eyes struggled immensely to focus on the sobbing, black-haired girl holding her so tightly.
"Did... did we push them back?" Elm forced the words out, her voice a fragile dying whisper. "Did... did my magic help Hiro? Did we win the war?"
Evelyn pulled Elm even tighter against her chest with her hot tears falling freely and heavily onto the dying Hero’s pale freezing cheeks.
"No, Elm," Evelyn choked out, her voice breaking entirely under the crushing weight of her failure. "We lost. The Blessed Land is too strong. We lost the war."
Elm let out a soft and agonizingly sad sigh.
She rested her head heavily and limply against Evelyn’s trembling shoulder, her beautiful silver eyes staring blankly at the smoking ruined iron wall of the medical chamber.

"I am so sorry, My Lord," Elm whispered, her voice barely audible over the hissing steam of the broken pipes. "I tried... I gave Hiro absolutely everything I had left. I just wanted... to stand beside you on the battlefield one last time. I just wanted to be your Hero again."

"Don’t apologize!" Evelyn sobbed loudly, burying her tear-stained face deeply into Elm’s wet thinning white hair. "You idiot, I’m the one who failed you! I should have found a proper cure so long ago! I should have never, ever let you cast that sacrificial spell! I’m so sorry, Elm. I’m so incredibly sorry!"
Elm coughed again, a violent rattling spasm that caused a fresh wave of silver blood to spill from her lips.
Her frail body grew incredibly limp in Evelyn’s desperate arms.

"It’s okay..." Elm murmured, an incredibly tragic, and completely accepting smile touching her pale bleeding lips. "I just... I really wished we could have done the things we talked about back in the beginning. I wanted to see the actual ocean again... I wanted to walk in a real living forest once more... not just these cold vibrating metal corridors."
Evelyn gripped her frantically, her brilliant and normally highly analytical mind completely shattered by the overwhelming grief of the moment.

"We will!" Evelyn promised frantically, her voice rising in panic as she felt Elm’s pulse fading. "If you just hold on, Elm, I swear to you! I’ll take you to the best medical facility in the entire Central City! I’ll sell the entire mobile fortress and all the treads if I have to! I’ll buy you a real forest! Just please... please don’t die on me!"
Elm slowly, weakly closed her beautiful, crystalline silver eyes.
"I wish... I could..." Elm breathed out softly.
Her chest completely stopped its fragile rise and fall as her body went still in Evelyn’s arms.
Silas stood exactly three feet away, watching the entire heartbreaking exchange in silence.
’Oh... I was wrong.’
The Lord of the Blessed Land looked down at the weeping, desperate girl in the oversized hoodie, entirely and completely broken over the devastating loss of her very first Hero.
He looked at the fragile dying woman in her arms who had willingly, stubbornly sacrificed her own soul just to give her Lord a tiny, fleeting chance at victory.
Silas felt a deep resonance in the center of his chest.
He looked at Evelyn, and he saw a terrifying reflection of himself.
If Eluned, Vespera, Tasmin, Brida, or Morwenna were ever lying dead or dying in his arms like this, he wouldn’t just weep.
He would burn the entire Sovereign Realm down to the bedrock and slaughter every single living entity in his path to save them... If he could...
Evelyn wasn’t a soulless corporate suit.
She wasn’t an arrogant, disconnected noble from the inner cities who treated her summoned units like disposable replaceable tools...
She was a true Lord who deeply loved her people. Much like Silas, well not exactly.
’Still I was wrong... and I’ll make it up to her.’
Silas let out a long weary sigh.
"Move," Silas commanded softly.
Silas walked deliberately forward with his heavy dark combat boots splashing loudly through the boiling green fluid.
He knelt down smoothly in the wet, ruined mud directly beside the sobbing Evelyn.
Evelyn looked up at him, her dark eyes completely red and devastated by her loss.

"What... what are you doing?" Evelyn choked out defensively, tightening her protective, desperate grip on Elm’s lifeless body, fully expecting the enemy Lord to execute them both to finalize the victory.
"Definitely not what you think I want to do..."
Who did she take him for? Someone that would kill another in their darkest moment, well it depended on who the person was.
’I’m going to bring her back...’
Tasmin had died before, and as Eluned had told him, as long as the time between death hadn’t been too long. He could bring someone back to life.
He simply reached out his large calloused right hand, gently and firmly placing his warm palm directly against Elm’s pale lifeless forehead.
Silas closed his glowing, golden-ringed eyes.
’Please Elu... Let me...’
The rune throbbed as it began glowing.
’Heal her!’
HUMMMMMMM!
A blinding pure and utterly majestic green light erupted directly from Silas’s palm.
The light did not carry destructive force... It did not carry offensive elemental magic and it did not burn or scorch.
It was the pure essence of healing.
The green light violently flooded directly into Elm’s frail broken body.
WHOOSH!
It completely bypassed her shattered ruined mana pathways and healed them as it went.
The supreme authority of Silas’s healing acted like a divine adhesive.
It flawlessly re-knitted her torn spiritual veins. It actively purged the dead tissue that had plagued her the time she had been sick.
And most importantly, it forcefully injected a massive wave of pure vitality into her failing biological system.
Elm’s crystalline silver eyes snapped violently wide open.
"HAH!"
Elm took a massive deep breath of actual fresh air only to cough a bit later.
The air in here was not fresh at all...

chapters.title: Chapter 331: End Of The War
paragraphs: The vibrant healthy color returned instantly to her pale sunken cheeks.
The terrifying skeletal thinness of her frame began to physically reverse as the Gold Core aggressively regenerated her lost cellular mass and muscle density in real-time.
Her beautiful silky white hair actively thickened, instantly regaining its lustrous healthy shine as the shedding completely stopped.
In a state of overwhelming shock from the sudden, massive influx of divine concentrated vitality, Elm’s subconscious stubborn grip on her sacrificial magic completely and entirely failed.
FSHHHHH!
She let go of the Four-Leaf Clover spell.
The massive glowing white array permanently etched into the stone floor beneath the shattered tank flickered violently for a fraction of a second, then permanently died.
The tether was officially broken.
Elm sat up slowly in Evelyn’s arms, her hands clutching her chest as she panted heavily, looking around the ruined room.
She was completely healed.
"What... what just happened?" Elm whispered with her voice clear and strong.
She looked down at her own healthy, completely restored hands in bewilderment, flexing her fingers without feeling a single ounce of the agonizing pain that had trapped her for such a long time.
Evelyn stared at Silas with her jaw dropped completely open and her dark eyes wide with an incomprehensible level of pure shock.
He hadn’t just stabilized her bleeding... He hadn’t just paused her death...
He had miraculously cured a shattered core that the medical facilities she had been able to use in Central City couldn’t even manage to touch.
Silas calmly pulled his hand back, resting his arm casually on his knee. He looked directly, intensely into Elm’s wide shocked silver eyes.

"You have a Lord who is completely willing to sell her entire empire and all of her pride just to save your life," Silas stated bluntly with his deep voice echoing in the chamber and leaving no room for any argument. "Do not ever throw that precious life away on a foolish suicide spell again. Value your life, Elm."
Silas stood up slowly from the boiling fluid, wiping his hand on his trousers as he looked over his shoulder toward the smoking ruined iron doorway.
"Now," Silas said calmly, his golden eyes narrowing slightly as he checked the surrounding area. "Well we won this, so I hope you’re ready to give me rewards..."
Far away, back in the devastated center of the ruined field.
The exact second Elm’s shock caused her to let go of the tether spell...
Hiro’s perception world completely collapsed.
The massive ocean-like flow of purple mana that had been actively fueling his internal circuits and sustaining the spatial lock instantly vanished.
PSSSSHHHH!
Hiro stood alone in the center of the crushed, sixty-foot crater, surrounded by an unstoppable apocalypse of incoming spells.
Hundreds of Aeliana’s celestial starlight orbs.
The roaring fifty-foot wide destructive tornado of Talira’s volcanic fire and razor-sharp emerald wind blades.
The chaotic crushing gravitational pulls of Rowenna’s massive multi-colored runic magic circles.
His brain had already been lagging heavily.
It had already been screaming in white-hot physical agony from the incomprehensible processing load of reading the exact spatial trajectories of every single attack.
And now, the external fuel was completely gone.
"No..." Hiro whispered softly, his voice completely, instantly lost in the roaring deafening noise of the Vanguard’s combined assault.
CRACK! SHATTER!
The terrifying, deep purple light of the Mind’s Eye domain violently, visibly glitched in the air!
The massive three-dimensional geometric web etched into the atmosphere completely shattered like incredibly brittle cheap glass.
The suffocating purple sky dissolved instantly, replaced by the brilliant and utterly blinding explosions of the Vanguard’s combined high-tier magic.
Hiro’s perception was broken as the overwhelming sensory overload had completely short-circuited his brain.
He was suddenly blind again in the middle of an active war zone.
And the Vanguard exploited his vulnerability with merciless perfection.
KRA-THOOOOOOM!
Aeliana’s Starfall Barrage slammed brutally into the crater floor.
Hundreds of volatile starlight orbs detonated in a massive deafening chain reaction of pure cosmic destruction.
The overlapping concussive force of the astral explosions completely obliterated Hiro’s footing, throwing him violently off balance.
FWOOOOOOSH!
Before he could even attempt to physically recover or execute a blind spatial blink, Talira’s volcanic fire tornado engulfed him entirely.
The white-hot liquid-dense flames aggressively scorched his high-tech uniform, completely incinerating the outer protective layers.

Simultaneously, the incredibly fast, razor-sharp emerald wind blades violently shredded the remaining fabric, leaving dozens of deep bleeding gashes entirely across his exposed arms, his chest, and his scarred face.

Hiro desperately swung his bare hands through the air, trying frantically to use whatever tiny microscopic fraction of spatial mana he had left in his core to deflect the burning flames away from his vital organs.
But the runic triggered after. It was clear that the girls weren’t trying to kill him or else how would he have survived all this?
HUMMMMM!
Rowenna’s gravity well triggered perfectly beneath his shifting boots.
A crushing agonizing twenty-times atmospheric downforce slammed violently into his shoulders.
"Ghk! Ahhhhhh!"
The raw gravitational weight forcefully and brutally dragged him entirely down onto one knee in the burning, completely scorched mud, pinning him helplessly in place.
"Brida!" Rowenna called out calmly with her voice carrying clearly and elegantly over the massive overlapping explosions.
"I GOT HIM!" Brida roared at the top of her lungs.
The Grand Titan Bastion surged violently through the roaring white-hot flames, completely ignoring the intense thermal heat thanks to her immense Vitality stat.
Brida didn’t draw her heavy axe as she didn’t want to accidentally cut him in half.
’I think it’s only fair to attack him for leaving a gash in my shield.’
She used her massive unbreakable adamantine tower shield.
’Let’s go!’
She executed a brutal fully committed shield bash, slamming the heavy, flat metal face perfectly and flawlessly into the exposed side of Hiro’s ribs!
CRUNCH!
"GAAAAAH!" Hiro screamed in genuine agony as the massive impact instantly shattered several of his ribs.
His entire body was violently launched incredibly high into the air, spinning completely out of control through the thick black smoke and burning fire like a broken toy.
’I want to die...’
He was completely overwhelmed.
His domain was broken, his mana core was empty, his brain was fried from sensory overload, and his physical body was completely ruined by the force of the assault.
As Hiro spun helplessly through the air, attempting desperately to orient his broken body for a landing...
A dark terrifying blur of absolute speed intercepted him entirely mid-air.
Tasmin.
The S-Rank Shadow Commander had used her Phantom Leap the exact second the purple domain shattered, instantly restoring her unrestricted access to the spatial seams and shadows.
Tasmin appeared directly above Hiro’s rapidly falling body.
"If you survive this then perhaps you deserve to live..."
WHAM!
Tasmin drove the heavy reinforced heel of her dark leather combat boot precisely into the center of Hiro’s chest.
The massive uncontested downward kick forcefully accelerated his fall, sending him crashing brutally and violently back down into the solid unyielding bedrock of the crater floor.
KRA-THOOOOOM!
Hiro slammed heavily into the stone.
A massive billowing cloud of dark dust, crushed rock, and splattered blood erupted violently from the impact point, completely shaking the surrounding terrain.
Hiro groaned incredibly weakly with his entire body undeniably broken.
He couldn’t lift his arms to defend himself.
He couldn’t move his shattered legs.

His heavily scarred empty eye sockets stared helplessly up at the sky as he tried to force himself up with his die-hard veteran instincts demanding he continue to fight to the death to secure victory for Lord Sky.
But his muscles simply refused to obey...
He couldn’t move a single inch.
Tasmin landed perfectly, smoothly on his chest, pinning his broken body entirely to the crushed bedrock with her physical weight.
SHRRRR-ING!
With a smooth practiced motion, Tasmin completely pressed the razor-sharp dark mythril edge of her shortsword directly against his exposed throat.
The freezing cold metal rested exactly over his pulsing jugular vein, ready to sever it with a single microscopic twitch of her wrist.
Tasmin leaned closely over him, her glowing eyes lacking any mercy, hesitation, or doubt.
"You’re done," Tasmin declared.
Her voice was a cold final whisper that completely sealed his ultimate fate on the battlefield.
Hiro completely froze.
He felt the cold unforgiving steel resting tightly against his neck and he felt the undeniable defeat settling deeply into his exhausted bones.
The blind vanguard let out a long shuddering breath, completely surrendering his remaining combat tension.
He let his bruised head fall back heavily against the crushed mud, accepting his loss.
The battle against the spatial perception domain was over.
High above the devastated Umbral Basin, the dark suffocating purple light completely dissolved, retreating and vanishing from the upper atmosphere.
The bright, golden, completely natural light of the morning sun violently broke through the lingering thick clouds of gray ash and dark smoke.
The sunlight illuminated the completely devastated and heavily scarred hellscape of the main battlefield.
High up in the clear sky, the hundreds of hovering high-tech network drones finally successfully rebooted their systems.
Their mechanical lenses flashed bright green, instantly reconnecting the live visual broadcast feed directly to the massive Sovereign Network.

Across the entire globe, from the towering skyscrapers of Valoria City to the deepest, most heavily fortified underground bunkers, over a billion viewers collectively held their breath as the visual feed finally cleared of static.
Nobody on the live stream had actually witnessed the terrifying strategic fight against Hiro.𝚏𝗿𝗲𝐞𝚠𝕖𝐛𝗻𝗼𝐯𝕖𝚕.𝚌𝗼𝗺
The forced perception of the purple domain had completely blacked out the cameras, leaving the audience in total suspense.
But as the thick smoke entirely settled over the central clearing... the aftermath of the clash was undeniable.
Ignis and Frost, the hyped dual elemental Wardens of the Unmovable Wall, lay completely unconscious and buried deep in the dirt, their expensive armors entirely shattered.
Gideon, the legendary Last Dragon-Slayer, lay completely dead in a massive crater with his corpse completely missing its head from a clean starlight execution.
Kassandra of the Divine Aegis, the immovable defensive juggernaut, was face down in the mud, knocked completely cold by a highly accurate sniper’s toxin arrow.

And Hiro, the ultimate, completely untouchable blind vanguard who manipulated space itself, was currently pinned helplessly to the bedrock by the Vanguard’s Shadow Commander with a dark blade resting against his throat.
The supercharged infantry army of The Unmovable Wall, who had previously been charging forward with a massive multiplier, had stopped their advance.
They stood frozen in the distance with their weapons lowered helplessly to the grass, staring in terrified awe at the six women standing victorious in the absolute center of the ruined battlefield.
Everyone watching on the global network, from the lowest tier rookie Lords to the highest most powerful members of the elite World Council, could agree on one single undeniable truth.
The Blessed Land had won the Lord War.
It was a complete victory over an established classic powerhouse.
Standing tall in the center of the crater, with her heavy boot firmly planted on Hiro’s chest, Tasmin slowly raised her free hand high into the air.
She looked over at Brida, who offered an exhausted but triumphant grin.
She looked at Rowenna, who smoothly and elegantly wiped a single speck of dust from her pristine white robes.
She looked at Talira, who puffed a small, satisfied ring of smoke from her lips.
She looked high up at Aeliana, who floated gently down from the sky with a beautiful smile.
And she looked out at the distant high stone ridge, where Fenna stood incredibly tall with her composite bow.
They had fought through crushing twenty-times gravity, roaring infernos, kinetic shields, and a domain of pure space.
And they had completely crushed them all.
Tasmin threw her head back, her eyes burning with fierce undeniable pride for the Lord who had summoned them.
"HAIL BLESSED LAND!" Tasmin screamed.
Her voice echoed incredibly powerfully, carrying completely across the entire devastated basin.
Instantly, without a single moment of hesitation, the rest of the Vanguard threw their weapons proudly into the air.
"HAIL BLESSED LAND!" Brida bellowed wildly.
"HAIL BLESSED LAND!" Talira roared into the sky.
"HAIL BLESSED LAND!" Rowenna, Aeliana, and Fenna cheered perfectly, flawlessly in unison.
Far away in the pristine Keep, standing in the middle of the kitchen wearing a frilly white apron, Morwenna heard the cheer echoing everywhere.
’Finally we can cheer...’
A massive thrilled smile completely overtook her face, and she slammed her leather-clad fist happily against the counter.
"HAIL BLESSED LAND!" Morwenna cheered loudly, her voice joining the chorus.
"You haven’t brought my tea yet, virgin! Chop chop before I get tired! I can only wait so long!"
’...Fuck you.’

sentences.text: The vibrant healthy color returned instantly to her pale sunken cheeks.
The terrifying skeletal thinness of her frame began to physically reverse as the Gold Core aggressively regenerated her lost cellular mass and muscle density in real-time.
Her beautiful silky white hair actively thickened, instantly regaining its lustrous healthy shine as the shedding completely stopped.
In a state of overwhelming shock from the sudden, massive influx of divine concentrated vitality, Elm’s subconscious stubborn grip on her sacrificial magic completely and entirely failed.
FSHHHHH!
She let go of the Four-Leaf Clover spell.
The massive glowing white array permanently etched into the stone floor beneath the shattered tank flickered violently for a fraction of a second, then permanently died.
The tether was officially broken.
Elm sat up slowly in Evelyn’s arms, her hands clutching her chest as she panted heavily, looking around the ruined room.
She was completely healed.
"What... what just happened?" Elm whispered with her voice clear and strong.
She looked down at her own healthy, completely restored hands in bewilderment, flexing her fingers without feeling a single ounce of the agonizing pain that had trapped her for such a long time.
Evelyn stared at Silas with her jaw dropped completely open and her dark eyes wide with an incomprehensible level of pure shock.
He hadn’t just stabilized her bleeding...
He hadn’t just paused her death...
He had miraculously cured a shattered core that the medical facilities she had been able to use in Central City couldn’t even manage to touch.
Silas calmly pulled his hand back, resting his arm casually on his knee.
He looked directly, intensely into Elm’s wide shocked silver eyes.

"You have a Lord who is completely willing to sell her entire empire and all of her pride just to save your life," Silas stated bluntly with his deep voice echoing in the chamber and leaving no room for any argument.
"Do not ever throw that precious life away on a foolish suicide spell again.
Value your life, Elm."
Silas stood up slowly from the boiling fluid, wiping his hand on his trousers as he looked over his shoulder toward the smoking ruined iron doorway.
"Now," Silas said calmly, his golden eyes narrowing slightly as he checked the surrounding area.
"Well we won this, so I hope you’re ready to give me rewards..."
Far away, back in the devastated center of the ruined field.
The exact second Elm’s shock caused her to let go of the tether spell...
Hiro’s perception world completely collapsed.
The massive ocean-like flow of purple mana that had been actively fueling his internal circuits and sustaining the spatial lock instantly vanished.
PSSSSHHHH!
Hiro stood alone in the center of the crushed, sixty-foot crater, surrounded by an unstoppable apocalypse of incoming spells.
Hundreds of Aeliana’s celestial starlight orbs.
The roaring fifty-foot wide destructive tornado of Talira’s volcanic fire and razor-sharp emerald wind blades.
The chaotic crushing gravitational pulls of Rowenna’s massive multi-colored runic magic circles.
His brain had already been lagging heavily.
It had already been screaming in white-hot physical agony from the incomprehensible processing load of reading the exact spatial trajectories of every single attack.
And now, the external fuel was completely gone.
"No..." Hiro whispered softly, his voice completely, instantly lost in the roaring deafening noise of the Vanguard’s combined assault.
CRACK!
SHATTER!
The terrifying, deep purple light of the Mind’s Eye domain violently, visibly glitched in the air!
The massive three-dimensional geometric web etched into the atmosphere completely shattered like incredibly brittle cheap glass.
The suffocating purple sky dissolved instantly, replaced by the brilliant and utterly blinding explosions of the Vanguard’s combined high-tier magic.
Hiro’s perception was broken as the overwhelming sensory overload had completely short-circuited his brain.
He was suddenly blind again in the middle of an active war zone.
And the Vanguard exploited his vulnerability with merciless perfection.
KRA-THOOOOOOM!
Aeliana’s Starfall Barrage slammed brutally into the crater floor.
Hundreds of volatile starlight orbs detonated in a massive deafening chain reaction of pure cosmic destruction.
The overlapping concussive force of the astral explosions completely obliterated Hiro’s footing, throwing him violently off balance.
FWOOOOOOSH!
Before he could even attempt to physically recover or execute a blind spatial blink, Talira’s volcanic fire tornado engulfed him entirely.
The white-hot liquid-dense flames aggressively scorched his high-tech uniform, completely incinerating the outer protective layers.

Simultaneously, the incredibly fast, razor-sharp emerald wind blades violently shredded the remaining fabric, leaving dozens of deep bleeding gashes entirely across his exposed arms, his chest, and his scarred face.

Hiro desperately swung his bare hands through the air, trying frantically to use whatever tiny microscopic fraction of spatial mana he had left in his core to deflect the burning flames away from his vital organs.
But the runic triggered after.
It was clear that the girls weren’t trying to kill him or else how would he have survived all this?
HUMMMMM!
Rowenna’s gravity well triggered perfectly beneath his shifting boots.
A crushing agonizing twenty-times atmospheric downforce slammed violently into his shoulders.
"Ghk!
Ahhhhhh!"
The raw gravitational weight forcefully and brutally dragged him entirely down onto one knee in the burning, completely scorched mud, pinning him helplessly in place.
"Brida!" Rowenna called out calmly with her voice carrying clearly and elegantly over the massive overlapping explosions.
"I GOT HIM!" Brida roared at the top of her lungs.
The Grand Titan Bastion surged violently through the roaring white-hot flames, completely ignoring the intense thermal heat thanks to her immense Vitality stat.
Brida didn’t draw her heavy axe as she didn’t want to accidentally cut him in half.
’I think it’s only fair to attack him for leaving a gash in my shield.’
She used her massive unbreakable adamantine tower shield.
’Let’s go!’
She executed a brutal fully committed shield bash, slamming the heavy, flat metal face perfectly and flawlessly into the exposed side of Hiro’s ribs!
CRUNCH!
"GAAAAAH!" Hiro screamed in genuine agony as the massive impact instantly shattered several of his ribs.
His entire body was violently launched incredibly high into the air, spinning completely out of control through the thick black smoke and burning fire like a broken toy.
’I want to die...’
He was completely overwhelmed.
His domain was broken, his mana core was empty, his brain was fried from sensory overload, and his physical body was completely ruined by the force of the assault.
As Hiro spun helplessly through the air, attempting desperately to orient his broken body for a landing...
A dark terrifying blur of absolute speed intercepted him entirely mid-air.
Tasmin.
The S-Rank Shadow Commander had used her Phantom Leap the exact second the purple domain shattered, instantly restoring her unrestricted access to the spatial seams and shadows.
Tasmin appeared directly above Hiro’s rapidly falling body.
"If you survive this then perhaps you deserve to live..."
WHAM!
Tasmin drove the heavy reinforced heel of her dark leather combat boot precisely into the center of Hiro’s chest.
The massive uncontested downward kick forcefully accelerated his fall, sending him crashing brutally and violently back down into the solid unyielding bedrock of the crater floor.
KRA-THOOOOOM!
Hiro slammed heavily into the stone.
A massive billowing cloud of dark dust, crushed rock, and splattered blood erupted violently from the impact point, completely shaking the surrounding terrain.
Hiro groaned incredibly weakly with his entire body undeniably broken.
He couldn’t lift his arms to defend himself.
He couldn’t move his shattered legs.

His heavily scarred empty eye sockets stared helplessly up at the sky as he tried to force himself up with his die-hard veteran instincts demanding he continue to fight to the death to secure victory for Lord Sky.
But his muscles simply refused to obey...
He couldn’t move a single inch.
Tasmin landed perfectly, smoothly on his chest, pinning his broken body entirely to the crushed bedrock with her physical weight.
SHRRRR-ING!
With a smooth practiced motion, Tasmin completely pressed the razor-sharp dark mythril edge of her shortsword directly against his exposed throat.
The freezing cold metal rested exactly over his pulsing jugular vein, ready to sever it with a single microscopic twitch of her wrist.
Tasmin leaned closely over him, her glowing eyes lacking any mercy, hesitation, or doubt.
"You’re done," Tasmin declared.
Her voice was a cold final whisper that completely sealed his ultimate fate on the battlefield.
Hiro completely froze.
He felt the cold unforgiving steel resting tightly against his neck and he felt the undeniable defeat settling deeply into his exhausted bones.
The blind vanguard let out a long shuddering breath, completely surrendering his remaining combat tension.
He let his bruised head fall back heavily against the crushed mud, accepting his loss.
The battle against the spatial perception domain was over.
High above the devastated Umbral Basin, the dark suffocating purple light completely dissolved, retreating and vanishing from the upper atmosphere.
The bright, golden, completely natural light of the morning sun violently broke through the lingering thick clouds of gray ash and dark smoke.
The sunlight illuminated the completely devastated and heavily scarred hellscape of the main battlefield.
High up in the clear sky, the hundreds of hovering high-tech network drones finally successfully rebooted their systems.
Their mechanical lenses flashed bright green, instantly reconnecting the live visual broadcast feed directly to the massive Sovereign Network.

Across the entire globe, from the towering skyscrapers of Valoria City to the deepest, most heavily fortified underground bunkers, over a billion viewers collectively held their breath as the visual feed finally cleared of static.
Nobody on the live stream had actually witnessed the terrifying strategic fight against Hiro.𝚏𝗿𝗲𝐞𝚠𝕖𝐛𝗻𝗼𝐯𝕖𝚕.𝚌𝗼𝗺

But as the thick smoke entirely settled over the central clearing... the aftermath of the clash was undeniable.
Ignis and Frost, the hyped dual elemental Wardens of the Unmovable Wall, lay completely unconscious and buried deep in the dirt, their expensive armors entirely shattered.

chapters.title: Chapter 332: Harper Valeriana Whitmore [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: "Hail Blessed Lan—"
BZZZT!
The massive holographic display flickered violently into darkness, cutting the live feed right in the middle of the Vanguard’s triumphant victory cheer.
Harper sank back into the plush imported leather of her executive chair, releasing a heavy drawn-out sigh that echoed in the deafening silence of the massive corner office.
Her manicured fingers combed idly through her vibrant purple hair, untangling the knots of stress that had been building at her temples for the past hour.
This office was absolutely massive, occupying the entire top floor of the Valoria City Lord Association Building.
Floor-to-ceiling windows offered a panoramic breathtaking view of the sprawling metropolis below.
She wasn’t wearing her usual casual dungeon-diving gear today...
An obsidian-black, sharply tailored corporate suit hugged her slender frame.
Reaching up to adjust her dark silk tie, she smoothed down the crisp starched collar of her white undershirt while her mind raced a mile a minute.

’The elf was calling down a literal shower of explosive star-like attacks...’ Harper thought, her purple eyes staring blankly at the dark projector screen. ’Blessed Land also has a woman transforming into a seventy-foot primordial dragon and breathing a river of lava... then there’s that Tasmin woman moving so fast she practically teleported through the shadows.’
The overwhelming strength of the Blessed Land was actively breaking her brain.
Harper was a Lord.
She was a highly respected Unique Lord with a powerful lightning core.
She had survived lethal dungeons and built a growing, stable territory in the Known Zones but sitting here and reviewing the combat data, the harsh truth was undeniable.
’Even just one of those women in the Vanguard could solo my entire territory without breaking a sweat.’
They weren’t just summoned units... They were walking natural disasters.
And then there was the commander who had actually led them into the field.
Lord Vespera.
The internet forums, guild chat rooms, and World Council analysts were currently going completely insane with wild conspiracy theories.

Millions of viewers were actively claiming that Vespera was actually a man under some disguise artifact but the issue with that statement was that, what kind of disguise could do that in front of billions of viewers?
’And my father’s original thought of Silas being the one to own Blessed Land...’
Harper scoffed out loud, rolling her eyes at the absurdity of the dead man.
"Well, Vespera can’t be Silas," Harper dismissed the idea, her voice cutting through the quiet office.

It was just basic logic to her. They were two fundamentally different people. She really couldn’t place the exact specific reason why, and the definitive proof was resting right on the tip of her tongue, but she refused to believe that the woman and the man she knew were the exact same person.
Which meant Silas was definitely not the active Lord of the Blessed Land. He couldn’t be...
First of all, Silas was a man.
Vespera was very clearly a woman with an incredibly shapely figure hidden under that sleek silver armor. Second, their personalities were entirely mismatched.
’I really can’t imagine Silas smiling warmly and acting elegant around a battlefield like Vespera did,’ Harper reasoned internally.
Silas was a rugged and brutally efficient survivor. He didn’t pose for cameras or act like an aristocratic noble dueling for honor.
He swung his sword, optimized his gains, and protected his people.
’But then again...’
Harper paused, staring down at the polished mahogany wood of her desk.
’Does any of that actually matter?’
Whether Silas was a frontline grunt, a hidden Lord, or a simple civilian manager, it didn’t change her current feelings in the slightest.
A warm rising heat spread slowly across her pale cheeks.
’I like Silas...’
It was a simple and terrifyingly honest thought.
She didn’t like him because of his rank, and she didn’t like him because she thought he secretly owned the highly famous Blessed Land.
She liked him because she genuinely wanted to be close to him.
During the Secret Realm raid, he had stepped in front of her. He treated the people he trusted with a fierce protective loyalty that made her chest ache with longing.
’I just want to feel more of how he treats the people he cares for,’ Harper thought with a soft smile touching her lips. ’Being around him would make me genuinely happy.’
Reaching across the heavy desk, she picked up her brand new smartphone.
It was a top-of-the-line World Council model she had bought just yesterday with her newly acquired unfathomable wealth.
As she unlocked the glass screen, her mind drifted back to the chaotic blood-soaked events of the past week.
She had murdered her own father.
That much was absolutely sure.
She could still perfectly remember the exact sensation of the mana leaving her core.
She was the one who had hit him with that highly concentrated blast of White Lightning.
CRACKLE!
She could still smell the sharp tang of ozone and burning flesh from the ruined carpet of his office.
But to her surprise, she didn’t end up locked in an Association prison cell.
Apparently, absolutely everybody in the city had hated the man.
His own corporate lawyer had immediately turned on him the second the body hit the floor.
The estate workers, the mansion staff, and the abused guild members had all actively testified against his character.
Because of their combined intervention and the volume of evidence against him, Harper had easily won the resulting legal case.
It was a total landslide victory in the World Council courts.
And then came the biggest surprise of all.
Her late Mother had secretly installed a highly specific iron-clad clause in her will years ago.
The clause stated that if her Dad died under any circumstances, Harper would immediately inherit absolutely everything.
There was no probate period and no asset freezing. It was just immediate and total transfer of ownership.
So as of three days ago, Harper was a billionaire.
She now legally owned all four of the massive Lord Association Buildings that her Father had been controlling.
She controlled the lucrative leasing rights... She controlled the guild taxation fees and she controlled the internal teleporter networks that connected the sectors.
Leaning back in her chair, she reminisced about the scale of the financial corruption the auditors had uncovered in his private vault.
’No wonder the people are so mad at him,’ Harper thought with a cynical smirk. ’The man was actively stealing tens of millions of Spirit Credits from the regional treasury.’
The Lord Council was practically glad that Harper had roasted him into ash.
’I have a lot of things to do,’ she reminded herself.
She had to restructure the corrupt boards... She had to fire his old cronies and she had to establish her own supply lines and clean up the syndicate mess he left behind.
But right now, none of that corporate empire-building mattered to her.
Looking down at her glowing phone screen, she opened her private Messages tab. She scrolled down to a specific, newly added contact name.
She had already sent nine text messages to Silas.
[Hey, it’s Harper.]
[Just checking in to see if you got back safely from the Secret Realm.]
[The Association courts cleared me. I’m officially a free woman.]
[I also inherited all of my dad’s stuff. It’s kind of crazy.]
[Are you busy right now?]
[I saw the news about the Unmovable Wall approaching your sector.]
[Please be careful out there.]
[The stream just started. Blessed Land’s Vanguard looks amazing.]
[You didn’t tell me if you were from a Known Zone In The Secret Realm Or An Unknown Zone, are you watching the stream? It’s incredible.]
There were no replies and not a single read receipt.
She had pulled his private network number directly from the restricted Association directory.
’Those are the perks of being at the top of the game,’ Harper thought, smiling softly as she tapped the glass screen.
Tapping the text box at the bottom of the screen, she decided to send him one more message.
Her thumbs flew quickly across the digital keyboard.
[When you get back, can we go on a date 🥺?]
She stared at the little yellow tear-eyed emoji for a few seconds.
’Is that too desperate?’
She didn’t care.
Hitting the send button, she watched the message bubble pop up on the screen, joining the long line of unanswered green texts.
SWOOSH!
She really truly wanted to go on a date with him.
She wanted to sit across from him at a nice restaurant in the upper districts and just talk without feral monsters trying to kill them.
Harper sighed heavily, dropping her phone onto the mahogany desk.
’He’s been gone for a while.’
She assumed he was currently busy dealing with being a Lord and dealing with being a Lord and trying to survive, but wasn’t this too much time? Was something wrong?
Crossing her arms tightly over her suit jacket, her mind wandered to an irritating rumor she had heard from the Valoria City broker networks earlier that morning.
She had heard that Elora had bought Silas a gift.
She had apparently gotten him a hyper-advanced Supercar...
Harper frowned deeply, her purple eyes narrowing with intense competitive jealousy.
’It was worth eight million credits, right?’
Harper scoffed at the price tag.
Eight million credits used to seem like an impossible mythical fortune to her when her father was restricting her allowance to keep her obedient.
Now, it was literal pocket change.
’I will just get him two or three of them now.’
She could buy him an entire fleet of customized luxury vehicles.
She could even forcefully buy out his residential lease and move his place from where he currently lived.
She could move him directly into the ultra-secure hyper-luxurious penthouse suite of her primary Association tower.
She would spoil him completely rotten.
’Because I—’
KNOCK! KNOCK!
The sharp sound of knuckles rapping against heavy mahogany broke her internal plotting.
"Come in," Harper called out, straightening her posture.
The heavy office doors slowly pushed open, and her newly appointed secretary nervously entered the room.
The young woman was holding a dark fabric draped carefully over her arm.
It was the dark trench coat that Harper had worn during the Secret Realm raid and when she had killed her Father... The coat had been burned, shredded, and ruined by the lightning attack.
Now, it was completely knit up.
The magical tailors in the lower sectors had flawlessly repaired the fabric, reinforcing the seams with defensive runic stitching that gleamed faintly in the office light.
Walking briskly across the carpet, the secretary respectfully handed the coat over the desk.
"Thank you," Harper said, taking the heavy garment.
The secretary bowed her head slightly, clutching her datapad to her chest.
"The people are gathered for the meeting, Ma’am," the woman informed her quietly.
Harper nodded and stood up from her leather executive chair.
She smoothly slid her arms into the sleeves of the heavy dark trench coat, wearing it directly over her tailored business suit.
It gave her an intimidating militaristic corporate aesthetic that perfectly matched her lightning core.
Leaving the office, she walked briskly down the plush carpeted hallway with her secretary trailing slightly behind her.
They reached the grand, imposing double doors of the primary boardroom however Harper didn’t knock nor did she announce her presence.
CREEEEEAK!
She pushed the doors open and walked confidently into the massive meeting room.
Twenty wealthy, arrogant, and deeply corrupt board members were sitting around a massive glass table.
They all stopped talking and stared at her.
Some looked at her with blatant corporate disdain and some looked at her with genuine, sweating fear, knowing exactly what she had done to the previous Chairman.
She ignored all of their expressions, walking directly to the Head of the table.
Pulling out the massive high-backed executive chair, she sat down heavily. She crossed her legs under the glass table, resting her hands flat on the smooth surface.
Letting her glowing purple eyes sweep across the terrified executives, she soaked in the heavy tension of the room.
"I am Harper Valeriana Whitmore," Harper introduced herself.
Her voice was cold, crisp, and lacking of the nervous hesitation she used to carry.
"I am the new Boss."
Offering them a terrifying sharp smile, she leaned forward.
"And I am also very glad to meet you."
Far away from the clean, air-conditioned skyscrapers of Valoria City.
Out in the devastated crushed ruins of the Umbral Basin, the cratered outside of the battlefield was currently a grim depressing scene of defeat.
The scent of ozone, dried blood, and burning flesh hung thickly in the freezing morning air.
The dead bodies of the Unmovable Wall soldiers that had died in the initial apocalyptic clashes were currently being gathered into large piles by the surviving infantry.
FWOOSH!
Heavy torches and fire magic were tossed onto the piles of the dead.
The bodies were being burned in massive roaring funeral pyres to prevent the rising scent of blood from attracting feral monsters from the Unknown Zone.

She could still perfectly remember the exact sensation of the mana leaving her core.
She was the one who had hit him with that highly concentrated blast of White Lightning.
CRACKLE!
She could still smell the sharp tang of ozone and burning flesh from the ruined carpet of his office.
But to her surprise, she didn’t end up locked in an Association prison cell.
Apparently, absolutely everybody in the city had hated the man.
His own corporate lawyer had immediately turned on him the second the body hit the floor.
The estate workers, the mansion staff, and the abused guild members had all actively testified against his character.
Because of their combined intervention and the volume of evidence against him, Harper had easily won the resulting legal case.
It was a total landslide victory in the World Council courts.
And then came the biggest surprise of all.
Her late Mother had secretly installed a highly specific iron-clad clause in her will years ago.
The clause stated that if her Dad died under any circumstances, Harper would immediately inherit absolutely everything.
There was no probate period and no asset freezing.
It was just immediate and total transfer of ownership.
So as of three days ago, Harper was a billionaire.
She now legally owned all four of the massive Lord Association Buildings that her Father had been controlling.
She controlled the lucrative leasing rights...
She controlled the guild taxation fees and she controlled the internal teleporter networks that connected the sectors.
Leaning back in her chair, she reminisced about the scale of the financial corruption the auditors had uncovered in his private vault.
’No wonder the people are so mad at him,’ Harper thought with a cynical smirk. ’The man was actively stealing tens of millions of Spirit Credits from the regional treasury.’
The Lord Council was practically glad that Harper had roasted him into ash.
’I have a lot of things to do,’ she reminded herself.
She had to restructure the corrupt boards...
She had to fire his old cronies and she had to establish her own supply lines and clean up the syndicate mess he left behind.
But right now, none of that corporate empire-building mattered to her.
Looking down at her glowing phone screen, she opened her private Messages tab.
She scrolled down to a specific, newly added contact name.
She had already sent nine text messages to Silas.
[Hey, it’s Harper.]
[Just checking in to see if you got back safely from the Secret Realm.]
[The Association courts cleared me.
I’m officially a free woman.]
[I also inherited all of my dad’s stuff.
It’s kind of crazy.]
[Are you busy right now?]
[I saw the news about the Unmovable Wall approaching your sector.]
[Please be careful out there.]
[The stream just started.
Blessed Land’s Vanguard looks amazing.]
[You didn’t tell me if you were from a Known Zone In The Secret Realm Or An Unknown Zone, are you watching the stream?
It’s incredible.]
There were no replies and not a single read receipt.
She had pulled his private network number directly from the restricted Association directory.
’Those are the perks of being at the top of the game,’ Harper thought, smiling softly as she tapped the glass screen.
Tapping the text box at the bottom of the screen, she decided to send him one more message.
Her thumbs flew quickly across the digital keyboard.
[When you get back, can we go on a date 🥺?]
She stared at the little yellow tear-eyed emoji for a few seconds.
’Is that too desperate?’
She didn’t care.
Hitting the send button, she watched the message bubble pop up on the screen, joining the long line of unanswered green texts.
SWOOSH!
She really truly wanted to go on a date with him.
She wanted to sit across from him at a nice restaurant in the upper districts and just talk without feral monsters trying to kill them.
Harper sighed heavily, dropping her phone onto the mahogany desk.
’He’s been gone for a while.’
She assumed he was currently busy dealing with being a Lord and dealing with being a Lord and trying to survive, but wasn’t this too much time?
Was something wrong?
Crossing her arms tightly over her suit jacket, her mind wandered to an irritating rumor she had heard from the Valoria City broker networks earlier that morning.
She had heard that Elora had bought Silas a gift.
She had apparently gotten him a hyper-advanced Supercar...
Harper frowned deeply, her purple eyes narrowing with intense competitive jealousy.
’It was worth eight million credits, right?’
Harper scoffed at the price tag.
Eight million credits used to seem like an impossible mythical fortune to her when her father was restricting her allowance to keep her obedient.
Now, it was literal pocket change.
’I will just get him two or three of them now.’
She could buy him an entire fleet of customized luxury vehicles.
She could even forcefully buy out his residential lease and move his place from where he currently lived.
She could move him directly into the ultra-secure hyper-luxurious penthouse suite of her primary Association tower.
She would spoil him completely rotten.
’Because I—’
KNOCK!
KNOCK!
The sharp sound of knuckles rapping against heavy mahogany broke her internal plotting.
"Come in," Harper called out, straightening her posture.
The heavy office doors slowly pushed open, and her newly appointed secretary nervously entered the room.
The young woman was holding a dark fabric draped carefully over her arm.
It was the dark trench coat that Harper had worn during the Secret Realm raid and when she had killed her Father...
The coat had been burned, shredded, and ruined by the lightning attack.
Now, it was completely knit up.
The magical tailors in the lower sectors had flawlessly repaired the fabric, reinforcing the seams with defensive runic stitching that gleamed faintly in the office light.
Walking briskly across the carpet, the secretary respectfully handed the coat over the desk.
"Thank you," Harper said, taking the heavy garment.
The secretary bowed her head slightly, clutching her datapad to her chest.
"The people are gathered for the meeting, Ma’am," the woman informed her quietly.
Harper nodded and stood up from her leather executive chair.
She smoothly slid her arms into the sleeves of the heavy dark trench coat, wearing it directly over her tailored business suit.
It gave her an intimidating militaristic corporate aesthetic that perfectly matched her lightning core.
Leaving the office, she walked briskly down the plush carpeted hallway with her secretary trailing slightly behind her.
They reached the grand, imposing double doors of the primary boardroom however Harper didn’t knock nor did she announce her presence.
CREEEEEAK!
She pushed the doors open and walked confidently into the massive meeting room.
Twenty wealthy, arrogant, and deeply corrupt board members were sitting around a massive glass table.
They all stopped talking and stared at her.
Some looked at her with blatant corporate disdain and some looked at her with genuine, sweating fear, knowing exactly what she had done to the previous Chairman.
She ignored all of their expressions, walking directly to the Head of the table.
Pulling out the massive high-backed executive chair, she sat down heavily.
She crossed her legs under the glass table, resting her hands flat on the smooth surface.
Letting her glowing purple eyes sweep across the terrified executives, she soaked in the heavy tension of the room.
"I am Harper Valeriana Whitmore," Harper introduced herself.
Her voice was cold, crisp, and lacking of the nervous hesitation she used to carry.
"I am the new Boss."
Offering them a terrifying sharp smile, she leaned forward.
"And I am also very glad to meet you."
Far away from the clean, air-conditioned skyscrapers of Valoria City.
Out in the devastated crushed ruins of the Umbral Basin, the cratered outside of the battlefield was currently a grim depressing scene of defeat.
The scent of ozone, dried blood, and burning flesh hung thickly in the freezing morning air.
The dead bodies of the Unmovable Wall soldiers that had died in the initial apocalyptic clashes were currently being gathered into large piles by the surviving infantry.
FWOOSH!
Heavy torches and fire magic were tossed onto the piles of the dead.
The bodies were being burned in massive roaring funeral pyres to prevent the rising scent of blood from attracting feral monsters from the Unknown Zone.

chapters.title: Chapter 333: Let’s Go... To Blessed Land
paragraphs: The soldiers that had survived the catastrophic Lord War which was actually quite a lot of people in that regard were completely disarmed.
They were all seated heavily on the ground in the ruined field.
Hundreds of heavy infantrymen, scouts, and broken shield-bearers sat in the mud with their heads bowed in shame.
Sitting alone near the edge of a massive blackened crater was Hiro.
The blind swordsman was entirely separated from the rest of his routed unit.
His dark high-tech uniform was shredded into ribbons and heavily stained with his own blood.
Hugging his knees tightly against his bruised chest, he was trying to cry while looking blindly toward the roaring heat of the funeral flames.
"I’m sorry..."
Tears leaked slowly from his scarred empty eye sockets, tracking through the soot on his cheeks as he was constantly apologizing to the empty air.
"I failed," Hiro whispered brokenly to himself. "I failed you, Lord Sky. I failed you, Elm. I wasn’t strong enough to hold the domain."
He felt completely and utterly useless.
He had been given the ultimate support battery and entrusted with the lives of the entire mobile fortress... and he still lost to Blessed Land.
Suddenly, a loud, heavy mechanical grinding sound echoed across the silent depressing field.
CLANG! CLANG! CLANG!
The massive reinforced steel-weave gates of the Blessed Land territory slowly began to open.
The surviving soldiers of the Unmovable Wall flinched collectively, looking up from the mud in sheer terror.
They fully expected a brutal merciless execution squad of Vanguard elites to march out and finish the job.
Instead, a completely different sight emerged from the fog.
Women riding on beasts stepped out from the open gates.
They were riding Blessed Wolves. The wolves were massive, standing tall at the shoulder with thick blond fur and glowing blue eyes.
About four of the women rode out onto the ruined battlefield.
They weren’t carrying drawn weapons, and they weren’t casting spells as they were carrying massive, heavy wooden trays stacked incredibly high with steaming food.
Riding through the ranks of defeated men, they began to actively distribute the trays of food to each and every single person currently left alive on the field.
The rich savory smell of roasted meat, fresh baked bread, and hot gravy completely overpowered the sickening smell of the burning pyres.
An alpha wolf trotted heavily toward the crater where Hiro was sitting.
Gunnhild was riding the beast.
Pulling back on the thick leather reins, the Vanguard’s Berserker stopped the massive wolf directly in front of the blind swordsman.
Gunnhild hopped down from the saddle.
Her heavy mythril boots splashed loudly in the mud as she marched straight toward him.
She held out a massive and incredibly hot tray of steaming food and shoved it firmly into his bruised chest.
"Here," Gunnhild grunted.
Hiro flinched violently with his blind face turning up toward her voice.
"What... what is this?" Hiro asked weakly.
"It’s food, idiot," Gunnhild told him bluntly. "Stop moping and eat."
Hiro slowly reached out his trembling hands and took the heavy tray.
The radiant heat of the fresh food warmed his freezing, blood-stained fingers.
He simply didn’t understand why the victors were feeding them instead of executing them.
"You did well... you weren’t going to beat us from the very beginning though but because of you, I can finally understand what war means so thank you."
A few dozen yards away in the mud, Kassandra slowly and painfully woke up.
The Unmovable Wall’s defensive tank groaned loudly as consciousness finally returned to her battered brain.
Her head was pounding with a vicious, throbbing ache. Fenna’s specialized knockout arrow had carried a remarkably potent sleep toxin that had completely paralyzed her nervous system.
Blinking her bright pink eyes open, she stared up at the gray sky.
Her heavy pink runic armor was completely deactivated and powered down.
A shadow suddenly fell over her face.
Kassandra flinched with her combat instincts flaring slightly as she tried to reach for a weapon that wasn’t there.
Looking up, she saw a young, incredibly beautiful woman wearing a pristine and perfectly clean black and white maid outfit standing directly over her.
It was Kaelia.
Smiling warmly, her bright eyes filled with genuine kindness, Kaelia knelt down softly in the mud, completely ignoring the dirt staining her white apron.
She offered her a large steaming plate of food.
"Here you go," Kaelia said sweetly.
"What... what is going on?" Kassandra asked with her voice raspy and dry.
"Our people won the battle," Kaelia told her gently. "Your people have lost the war."
Kassandra’s pink eyes widened in shock... They actually lost? The Unmovable Wall had fallen.
"But you should still eat," Kaelia continued, pushing the warm plate closer to her chest. "You must be very hungry after fighting so hard."
Slowly pushing herself up into a sitting position, Kassandra stared intensely at the smiling maid.
Inwardly, her heart thumped heavily against her ribs.
Her perception was screaming at her in absolute terror as she realized exactly how formidable this seemingly innocent woman actually was.
’Why is a maid so strong...?’
Kaelia’s aura was flawlessly suppressed beneath her maid uniform but the terrifying power of the mana hidden deep inside the maid’s core was suffocating.
’She is a complete monster.’
Kassandra realized that the Blessed Land was so insanely overpowered that even their domestic serving staff could probably level their forces and it made her a bit afraid but on the other hand...
’Ah, I feel so glad.’
It had actually taken a massive amount of convincing for Kaelia to convince Lord to finally let her leave the territory.
’Lord Silas worries over every little thing.’
She had begged Silas to allow her to join the girls in distributing the food to the wounded people.
Silas had eventually relented, and Kaelia was incredibly glad she got to help.
Not daring to refuse the offering, Kassandra took the food without much complaint.
She grabbed the wooden fork and took a large, hesitant bite of the meat and broth.
Her pink eyes instantly widened in pure shock as the rich, savory spices exploded across her tongue.
The meat practically melted in her mouth, completely saturated with refreshing stamina-restoring mana.
It was the best thing she had ever tasted in her entire life.
She began aggressively shoveling the food into her mouth, completely forgetting her pride and her defeat.
"This is incredible," Kassandra mumbled through a mouthful of rice.
Swallowing hard, she looked up at Kaelia. "Seriously, complimenting the chef. Whoever cooked this is a master."
Kaelia’s face instantly turned incredibly bright red. Gripping the edges of her white apron, she twisted the fabric nervously.
"I... uh... I’m the chef!" Kaelia stammered happily.
Kassandra blinked in surprise.
Leaning in slightly closer, Kaelia looked around nervously as if checking for spies.
"And don’t tell my Lord..." Kaelia whispered conspiratorially with a cute wink. "...but I gave you extra chicken."
Beaming proudly, Kaelia tilted her head. "How does it taste?"
Looking down at the massive roasted chicken thigh sitting in the center of her plate, Kassandra looked back up at the terrifyingly strong and incredibly sweet maid.
"It tastes like heaven," Kassandra admitted honestly.
Further down the line of defeated prisoners, Lupina slowly woke up from her forced slumber.
The wolf-girl Hero of the Unmovable Wall groaned loudly, aggressively rubbing her furry ears.
Sitting up in the mud, her tail drooped heavily behind her.
"Ugh..." Lupina whined loudly.
She looked around frantically at the massive craters and the burning pyres in the distance before spotting her partner.
"What happened?!" Lupina asked in a panic.
Morrighan was sitting quietly next to her on a shattered piece of bedrock.
The demoness Hero was calmly wrapping a clean white bandage tightly around her own bruised arm. She didn’t look panicked at all as she looked resigned to her fate.
"We lost the war, Lupina," Morrighan told her bluntly.
Lupina’s jaw dropped completely open.
"Lost?!" Lupina shrieked. "How did we lose?! Where is Lord Sky?!"
"Lord Sky surrendered," Morrighan explained calmly. "The battle is over."
Tying off the bandage with her sharp teeth, Morrighan let out a sigh.
"We are officially prisoners of war," Morrighan continued. "We will now be claimed by the Blesse—"
THUD!
They were abruptly interrupted by the heavy sound of massive paws hitting the mud.
Gunnhild rode directly up to them on her massive Blessed Wolf, staring down at the two defeated Heroes.
Reaching into her saddlebag, the Berserker pulled out two hot steaming wrapped packages of food and tossed them casually down into the mud directly in front of the girls.
Morrighan picked up the food package immediately.
"Thank you," Morrighan said respectfully.
The demoness looked up at the towering muscled blonde woman sitting atop the massive silver wolf.
Staring at her scarred face and her heavy armor, Morrighan felt a strange fluttering in her chest.
’She looks so incredibly cool,’ Morrighan thought to herself with her demonic heart skipping a tiny subtle beat at the intimidating presence of the warrior woman.
However, Lupina was not nearly as respectful.
Completely ignoring the food on the ground, Lupina began loudly complaining at the top of her lungs.

"This is completely unfair!" Lupina whined, pointing a furry finger at Gunnhild. "I didn’t even get to fight properly! I got knocked out by some stupid trick! I want a rematch! You guys totally cheated! I demand to speak to your Lord right now and—"
Gunnhild narrowed her eyes.
Reaching into her tray, she pulled out a massive and incredibly thick roll of freshly baked bread as she jumped down from the wolf with a heavy splash.
Before Lupina could finish her annoying high-pitched rant, Gunnhild shoved the entire roll of bread aggressively into Lupina’s open mouth.
"Mmph!"
Lupina’s eyes bulged completely out of her skull in shock.
"Eat," Gunnhild commanded bluntly. "You talk way too much."
Glaring furiously at the Berserker, Lupina slowly began chewing the massive mouthful of bread because she simply had no other choice.
Gunnhild snorted in amusement.
Turning around, she grabbed the heavy leather saddle of her Blessed Wolf and easily vaulted herself back up onto the massive beast.
Patting the thick soft gold fur right behind her saddle, she cleared a large space on the animal’s broad back.
Looking down at the two Unmovable Wall Heroes, a wide surprisingly warm and incredibly sisterly grin stretched across Gunnhild’s scarred face.
"Both of you are going to be my new sisters, right?" Gunnhild asked them loudly.
She patted the empty space on the wolf again.
"Come on," Gunnhild ordered cheerfully. "Let’s go."
Morrighan’s heart thumped heavily against her ribs.
Looking at the empty space on the wolf, and then looking at the towering open steel gates of the Blessed Land territory in the distance, she realized the truth.
They weren’t being dragged into a dark dungeon... They were being invited inside.
Grabbing the chewing, grumbling Lupina firmly by the collar of her armor, Morrighan forcefully dragged the wolf-girl to her feet.
Together, they climbed clumsily onto the back of the massive Blessed Wolf, sitting securely directly behind Gunnhild’s broad back.
Gunnhild snapped the leather reins.
"Hyah!"
The wolf howled into the morning sky.
Riding forward, they left the burning pyres of the ruined battlefield entirely behind them as they headed directly toward the open gates, ready to enter the Blessed Land.
’I can’t believe it but my dream... It’s going to come true right now...’
The heavy polished oak doors of the Keep’s primary dining hall remained firmly closed against the chaotic aftermath of the battlefield outside.
Inside, the atmosphere was completely different from the blood-soaked mud of the Umbral Basin.
A roaring fire crackled warmly in the massive stone hearth.
CRACKLE!𝓯𝓻𝓮𝙚𝙬𝓮𝙗𝒏𝙤𝒗𝙚𝙡.𝒄𝒐𝓶
The large mahogany dining table was set with pristine silver cutlery and crystal goblets.
Silas sat entirely relaxed at the head of the long table.
He was out of his heavy combat gear, currently wearing a simple comfortable black tunic that highlighted his muscular frame.
Sitting directly next to him, pressing her soft shoulder against his arm, was Eluned.
The Nature Goddess looked absolutely radiant in her elegant green sundress, her emerald eyes glowing with quiet satisfaction.
Sitting on the opposite side of the massive table were the defeated commanders of The Unmovable Wall.
Evelyn was slouched heavily in her wooden chair.
She was still wearing her oversized soot-stained dark gray Earth traveler’s hoodie.
Her long black hair was messy, and her dark eyes carried the heavy weight of total exhaustion.
’Fucking hell...’
Sitting directly beside Evelyn while ignoring the luxurious surroundings, was Elm.
The white-haired Hero was physically clinging to her Lord.
Elm had her arms wrapped tightly around Evelyn’s waist, resting her head against the hoodie.
She was fully healed, her pale cheeks flushed with vibrant healthy color thanks to Silas’s healing.
Her crystalline silver eyes kept darting around the room, still completely terrified that she was going to wake up back in that dark freezing medical tank.
She squeezed Evelyn tighter, incredibly grateful just to be breathing fresh air.
"You can let go, Elm," Evelyn whispered softly, patting the Hero’s white hair. "We’re safe."
