"Come on," Gunnhild ordered cheerfully.
"Let’s go."
Morrighan’s heart thumped heavily against her ribs.
Looking at the empty space on the wolf, and then looking at the towering open steel gates of the Blessed Land territory in the distance, she realized the truth.
They weren’t being dragged into a dark dungeon...
They were being invited inside.
Grabbing the chewing, grumbling Lupina firmly by the collar of her armor, Morrighan forcefully dragged the wolf-girl to her feet.
Together, they climbed clumsily onto the back of the massive Blessed Wolf, sitting securely directly behind Gunnhild’s broad back.
Gunnhild snapped the leather reins.
"Hyah!"
The wolf howled into the morning sky.
Riding forward, they left the burning pyres of the ruined battlefield entirely behind them as they headed directly toward the open gates, ready to enter the Blessed Land.
’I can’t believe it but my dream...
It’s going to come true right now...’
The heavy polished oak doors of the Keep’s primary dining hall remained firmly closed against the chaotic aftermath of the battlefield outside.
Inside, the atmosphere was completely different from the blood-soaked mud of the Umbral Basin.
A roaring fire crackled warmly in the massive stone hearth.
CRACKLE!𝓯𝓻𝓮𝙚𝙬𝓮𝙗𝒏𝙤𝒗𝙚𝙡.𝒄𝒐𝓶
The large mahogany dining table was set with pristine silver cutlery and crystal goblets.
Silas sat entirely relaxed at the head of the long table.
He was out of his heavy combat gear, currently wearing a simple comfortable black tunic that highlighted his muscular frame.
Sitting directly next to him, pressing her soft shoulder against his arm, was Eluned.
The Nature Goddess looked absolutely radiant in her elegant green sundress, her emerald eyes glowing with quiet satisfaction.
Sitting on the opposite side of the massive table were the defeated commanders of The Unmovable Wall.
Evelyn was slouched heavily in her wooden chair.
She was still wearing her oversized soot-stained dark gray Earth traveler’s hoodie.
Her long black hair was messy, and her dark eyes carried the heavy weight of total exhaustion.
’Fucking hell...’
Sitting directly beside Evelyn while ignoring the luxurious surroundings, was Elm.
The white-haired Hero was physically clinging to her Lord.
Elm had her arms wrapped tightly around Evelyn’s waist, resting her head against the hoodie.
She was fully healed, her pale cheeks flushed with vibrant healthy color thanks to Silas’s healing.
Her crystalline silver eyes kept darting around the room, still completely terrified that she was going to wake up back in that dark freezing medical tank.
She squeezed Evelyn tighter, incredibly grateful just to be breathing fresh air.
"You can let go, Elm," Evelyn whispered softly, patting the Hero’s white hair.
"We’re safe."

chapters.title: Chapter 334: Give Me My Money [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: "No," Elm mumbled stubbornly into the hoodie fabric. "I am staying right here."
Silas watched the interaction with a small smirk.
’She acts like a koala.’
Silas could not even blame her, Elm was quite cute though...
Before Silas could formally start the diplomatic negotiations, the door to the kitchen violently kicked open.
BAM!
Morwenna aggressively stomped into the dining room.
The woman was carrying a massive heavy silver serving tray balanced on one hand.
She was still wearing her dark pirate regalia underneath, but tied tightly around her waist was a ridiculously frilly bright white kitchen apron.
Her stormy gray eyes were glaring daggers at the floor.
’How did Elu get her to even do this first of all?’
CLATTER!
Morwenna practically dropped the massive silver tray onto the center of the mahogany table.
"Food is served," Morwenna grumbled loudly.
She aggressively crossed her arms over her chest, refusing to make eye contact with Silas.
’Don’t ask any questions... I’m doing this for you, you should be grateful to me.’
The tray was completely loaded with steaming plates.
There were massive cuts of roasted boar, thick bowls of rich brown gravy, heavily buttered root vegetables, and perfectly toasted loaves of bread.
The entire dining room instantly filled with a mouth-watering, incredibly savory aroma.
Evelyn blinked in genuine surprise, leaning forward to inspect the feast.
"Wait," Evelyn muttered, looking up at the scowling pirate captain. "You cooked this?"
"I heated it up and prepared the spices," Morwenna shot back defensively. "I did the actual roasting before the war started... I just finished the glazing. Don’t look at me like that, girl."
Silas raised a skeptical eyebrow.
He reached out and picked up a wooden fork.
He speared a thick steaming piece of the roasted boar, dipping it generously into the dark gravy before taking a bite.
Silas began to chew.
His golden-ringed eyes instantly widened.
The meat practically melted on his tongue as the rich, salty flavor of the gravy perfectly complemented the savory fat of the boar, while a subtle spicy kick lingered in the back of his throat.
It was genuinely incredible... as usual.
Silas swallowed the food and looked up at the woman.
"Morwenna," Silas said seriously. "This is actually good."
Morwenna froze.
A bright crimson blush instantly exploded across her dark cheeks.
Her stormy gray eyes widened in shock.
"I-It is?" Morwenna stammered, her tough pirate persona entirely shattering in a single second.
"Yeah," Silas confirmed, taking another massive bite of the meat. "The spice blend is perfect. I didn’t know you could actually cook."
Morwenna gripped the edges of her frilly white apron, her entire body physically trembling with joy.
’He praised me!’
She completely forgot about the humiliating tea lessons with Eluned and she forgot about the apron too.
Her stormy gray eyes practically turned into sparkling stars.
"I can cook!" Morwenna declared proudly, puffing out her chest. "I cooked all the time on the high seas! I can make you whatever you want, My Lord! Just say the word!"
Eluned sat next to Silas, hiding an amused thoroughly smug smile behind her crystal goblet of water.
’Hook, line, and sinker.’
Evelyn slowly reached out and pulled a plate toward herself as she took a bite of the buttered root vegetables.
Her dark eyes widened as well.
"Holy shit," Evelyn mumbled, aggressively scooping more onto her fork. "This is better than some of the restaurants in Central City."
Elm slowly pulled her face away from Evelyn’s hoodie.
The white-haired Hero tentatively reached out, picking up a warm roll of bread.
She took a tiny bite.
The soft, buttery texture completely overwhelmed her senses.
She had been living off synthesized tasteless nutrient fluid pumped directly through a feeding tube for quite a long time so tears literally welled up in Elm’s silver eyes.
"It’s so good," Elm whispered, taking another desperate bite of the bread.𝒻𝑟ℯℯ𝑤𝑒𝑏𝑛𝘰𝓋𝑒𝓁.𝒸𝑜𝘮
Eluned smoothly set her crystal goblet down on the mahogany table and then she turned her stunning emerald eyes toward the white-haired Hero.
"It is wonderful to finally meet you, Elm," Eluned spoke, her melodic voice completely filling the quiet dining room.
Elm flinched slightly, suddenly aware of the supreme SSS-Rank aura radiating naturally from the green-haired woman sitting across from her.
"I am Eluned," the Nature Goddess introduced herself with a warm, welcoming smile. "I am Lord Silas’s First Hero and the very first summon of the Blessed Land."
Elm’s silver eyes widened in quiet realization.
She looked at the ingrained unbreakable bond radiating between Silas and Eluned.
’I can feel the connection between their souls...’
Elm slowly sat up straighter in her chair.
"I... I am Evelyn’s First Hero," Elm replied softly, her voice carrying a deep quiet pride. "The very first summon of The Unmovable Wall."
Eluned nodded gracefully.

"I know," Eluned agreed. "Our Lord told me what you did on the battlefield today. You willingly sacrificed your own core to protect your territory and you burned your own soul to give your Lord a chance at victory."
Elm lowered her gaze to the wooden table with her hands clutching the piece of bread.
"I failed," Elm whispered.

"You did not fail," Eluned corrected her firmly. "You proved your loyalty. A territory is not measured entirely by its physical walls or its artillery cannons. It is measured by the devotion of its people. You are a true Hero, Elm."
Elm looked up, her silver eyes shimmering with fresh tears. She looked at Evelyn, who offered her a tired reassuring smile.
Elm slowly nodded, taking a deep comforting breath of the warm air.
"Thank you, Lady Eluned," Elm said respectfully.
Silas finished his plate of roasted boar, pushing it slightly toward the center of the table.
He leaned back in his heavy wooden chair.
He rested his elbows casually on the armrests with his golden-ringed eyes locking directly onto the dark-haired girl sitting across from him.
The pleasantries and the introductions were officially over.
It was time for business.
"So, Evelyn," Silas started. "Let’s talk numbers."
Evelyn groaned loudly, dropping her fork onto her plate.
"I knew this was coming," Evelyn muttered, rubbing her tired temples.
"We had an explicit verbal contract," Silas reminded her coldly. "We agreed on a strict 60-40 revenue split in my favor."
’I didn’t forget the money.’
How could he? Money ruled the world.

"The contract covered the initial broadcast day when we streamed with Lohan Sterling and Etilga Bloom," Silas recounted smoothly. "It covered all the subsequent mini-streams you ran leading up to the war to build hype."
Silas leaned forward, resting his chin on his steepled fingers.

"And most importantly, it covers the massive Lord War broadcast that just concluded," Silas finished. "The one where I successfully cured your dying First Hero and completely spared your people from execution... most at least."
Evelyn glared at him.
"You don’t have to guilt-trip me," Evelyn grumbled irritably. "I honor my contracts."
Evelyn reached into the deep pocket of her oversized hoodie and then she pulled out a sleek advanced digital datapad.
She tapped the glass screen, pulling up the restricted backend analytics of her primary Sovereign Network account.
"The metrics from today are absolutely completely insane," Evelyn explained with her mind rapidly processing the raw data.
She flipped the datapad around, sliding it across the mahogany table toward Silas.
"The Lord War broadcast peaked at exactly 1.5 billion concurrent live viewers," Evelyn revealed bluntly.
Silas kept his face completely neutral.
Internally, his brain practically detonated with greed and surprise.
’One point five BILLION?!’
That was a completely incomprehensible amount of human traffic.

"Even when Hiro’s purple domain completely blacked out the visual feed, the viewer count didn’t drop," Evelyn continued, sighing heavily to hide her own excitement. "If anything, the suspense actually drove the engagement metrics higher. People were actively flooding the super-chats and the Valoria betting pools trying to guess who was winning inside the dome."
Evelyn leaned back in her chair, crossing her arms over her chest.
"Between the raw ad revenue, the premium subscriptions, the direct super-chats, and the percentage cuts we took from the Association betting rings..." Evelyn calculated rapidly.
She stared directly into Silas’s golden eyes.
"I currently owe you exactly seventy-five million Spirit Credits." Evelyn declared flatly.
Morwenna, who was currently pouring a glass of water for Eluned, completely froze.
SPLASH!
She accidentally spilled water entirely over the mahogany table.
"Seventy-five MILLION?!" Morwenna shrieked, her brain completely short-circuiting at the number.
She didn’t know about Spirit credits but she did know that...
You could buy an entire fleet of Mythril-plated galleons with that kind of capital.
Silas didn’t even blink.
He simply nodded slowly with his expression entirely stoic.
"Transfer the funds to me when we get back to Earth, I’ll have a bit of a talk with my bank and stuff." Silas sighed.
"I will," Evelyn agreed smoothly. "Though I should say the Valoria City banking guild takes exactly twelve hours to clear a transaction of that massive magnitude, but it will be in your account."
Evelyn rubbed her face, looking thoroughly exhausted by the scale of the finances.
Silas picked up his glass of water, taking a slow, measured sip and he set the glass back down.
"Now," Silas shifted the topic completely. "There is a pressing logistical issue that we need to address immediately."
Evelyn raised an eyebrow. "What issue?"
"My disguise," Silas stated bluntly.
Evelyn blinked in confusion.

"The Lord Vespera persona was incredibly effective for combat," Silas explained, gesturing to his own face. "But I never actually prepared an official registered identity for her within the World Council databases."
’I literally just put on some armor and started swinging...’

"Right now, there are millions of people across the network desperately trying to figure out who Vespera actually is," Silas continued. "If the Valoria City auditors decide to run a deep-dive background check on my territory, they are going to immediately realize that Vespera does not legally exist."
Silas leaned forward, his golden eyes locking onto Evelyn’s dark ones.
"Which brings me back to my earlier question," Silas said. "How exactly do you handle the legal paperwork and the digital footprint for your Lord Sky persona?"
Evelyn groaned loudly.
She reached into her hoodie pocket and she pulled out her slim silver cigarette case as well as her plasma lighter.
CLICK! FWOOSH!
She lit the cigarette, taking a stressed drag of the nicotine.
Elm immediately scowled, aggressively waving her hand in front of her face to clear the gray smoke away from her nose.
"Evelyn," Elm complained weakly. "That smells terrible."

"Deal with it, Elm," Evelyn shot back irritably, exhaling a thick plume of smoke toward the ceiling. "I just lost my territory, I’m down seventy-five million credits, and now I have to play corporate consultant..."
Evelyn tapped her finger against the mahogany table.

"You can’t just fake a Lord identity in the Sovereign Realm with a simple disguise artifact," Evelyn explained, entirely dropping her casual tone and slipping into her brilliant strategic persona. "The World Council uses highly advanced biometric tracking and mana-signature registration."
"So how did you do it?" Silas pressed.
"I didn’t," Evelyn admitted bluntly. "I paid someone else to do it."
She took another heavy drag of the cigarette.

"There is an incredibly skilled illegal information broker operating deep in the undercity of Valoria," Evelyn revealed quietly. "His name is Jax, or so you could say. He specializes in digital forgery, deep-network hacking, and manufacturing bulletproof corporate identities."
Evelyn flicked a bit of ash onto her empty plate.

"Jax owes me a massive favor from my early realm-diving days," Evelyn continued. "He completely hardwired the audio filters into my streaming drones to modulate my voice. He also completely fabricated the birth records, the guild registration, and the tax history for Lord Sky."
Silas nodded slowly, fully absorbing the critical intelligence.
"If the Valoria auditors look up Lord Sky," Evelyn said proudly, "they will find a perfectly clean, thirty-year-old male commander with a flawless credit score."
"I need that exact same service for Vespera," Silas stated immediately.
Evelyn smirked around her cigarette.
"Oh, really?" Evelyn asked, leaning forward with a smug expression. "And why exactly should I give you the direct contact information for my most valuable underground asset?"

chapters.title: Chapter 335: Pledge Your Loyalty To Blessed Land
paragraphs: Silas didn’t even hesitate.
"Because I won’t charge you an extortionate medical fee for fixing your massive leadership blunder today," Silas replied coldly.
Evelyn frowned. "What blunder?"

"You literally let your First Hero burn her own soul to ashes in a suicide spell just to fuel your blind guy," Silas pointed out. "I had to step in, pull Elm back from the brink of core-death, and let my girls not execute Hiro... I cleaned up your entire mess."
Evelyn’s pale cheeks flushed a deep embarrassed crimson.
"I was stressed!" Evelyn argued defensively.
"I will also pay you exactly two million Spirit Credits for the introduction," Silas added smoothly, completely ignoring her excuse.
Evelyn’s eyes lit up instantly.
"Deal," Evelyn agreed immediately, completely selling out her underground contact without a second thought. "I will send you Jax’s encrypted comm-link frequency later or I’ll take you there rather."
Silas smirked in satisfaction.
’Business is business.’
"Pleasure doing business with you, Evelyn," Silas said calmly.
He leaned back in his chair, taking a moment to actually study the stressed black-haired girl sitting across from him.
He looked at her messy hair, her oversized hoodie, and the heavy, exhausted bags under her dark eyes.
"You know," Silas said casually. "For an incredibly ruthless and successful classic Lord, you look surprisingly young. How old are you actually?"
Evelyn exhaled a long stream of smoke.
"I’m twenty-two," Evelyn answered bluntly.
Silas blinked in genuine surprise.
"Twenty-two?" Silas repeated, raising an eyebrow.
"Yeah," Evelyn nodded. "Why? How old are you?"
"I’m eighteen," Silas replied.
Evelyn froze.
The glowing tip of her cigarette literally trembled between her fingers.
She stared at the Lord sitting across from her in disbelief.

"You’re... you’re eighteen?" Evelyn stammered. "You built this entire insane territory, you conquered our army, and you mentally broke my entire command structure... and you’re barely legally allowed to buy a drink?!"
It made her head hurt.
"Pretty much," Silas shrugged casually.
He offered her a mocking grin.

"So, you’re twenty-two," Silas continued, deciding to ruthlessly press his advantage. "That is basically a fossil in this realm. Tell me, Evelyn... at your incredibly advanced age, why don’t you have a husband yet?"
Evelyn’s jaw dropped open.
Her dark eyes flared with rage.
"Excuse me?!" Evelyn shrieked, slamming her hands violently against the mahogany table.

"I mean, you’re wearing an oversized hoodie and smoking cheap cigarettes while running a mobile fortress," Silas roasted her flawlessly. "It just seems like you’ve completely given up on the Valoria dating market..."
"I WILL FUCKING KILL YOU!" Evelyn screamed, lunging forward aggressively across the table.
She completely tried to grab Silas by the collar of his black tunic.
Elm panicked instantly.
The white-haired Hero desperately grabbed Evelyn by the back of her gray hoodie, physically hauling her Lord back into her wooden chair with surprising strength.
"My Lord, please calm down!" Elm begged, completely mortified by the sudden outburst.
"He called me a fossil!" Evelyn yelled, pointing a shaking, furious finger at the highly amused Warlord. "I am in the prime of my youth! I have flawless skin!"
"Sure," Silas mocked her gently.

"I am a responsible adult!" Evelyn argued defensively, aggressively smoothing down her wrinkled hoodie. "I don’t have time for a stupid husband! I am actively providing for my little brother back on Earth! I send almost all of my clean profits back home to pay for his tuition!"
Silas’s smirk faded slightly.
He looked at Evelyn with a sudden new level of genuine respect.
’She’s funding her brother’s education?’
Beneath the arrogant Lord persona, the smoking habit, and the massive mobile fortress, she was just an older sister trying to keep her family afloat in a brutal unforgiving universe.
"That’s actually commendable, Evelyn," Silas told her honestly.
Evelyn crossed her arms tightly over her chest, aggressively looking away from him.
"Shut up," Evelyn mumbled, her cheeks burning bright red. "Don’t act nice now after you called me a spinster."
KNOCK! KNOCK!
The heavy sound of metal gauntlets striking the oak doors echoed through the dining room.
The massive double doors were slowly pushed open.
Gunnhild stepped heavily into the room.
The woman was flanked by two new faces.
Walking nervously behind the towering blonde warrior were Lupina and Morrighan.
The wolf-girl and the demoness had been stripped of their heavy combat armor.
They were currently wearing simple clean gray tunics and dark trousers provided by the girls that were free.
Lupina was still aggressively chewing on a massive piece of baked bread with her furry ears twitching nervously as she scanned the luxurious dining room.
Morrighan walked calmly, her dark demonic eyes sweeping across the room with a cautious gaze.
Gunnhild marched them directly up to the edge of the mahogany table.
"My Lord," Gunnhild announced loudly, saluting Silas by slamming her fist over her heart. "I have brought the newly acquired women as you requested."
Lupina and Morrighan immediately stopped walking.
They both stared in complete utter confusion at the young muscular golden-eyed man sitting confidently at the head of the table.
"Wait," Lupina mumbled around her mouthful of bread.
The wolf-girl pointed a furry finger directly at Silas.
"Who is this guy?" Lupina asked, her tail drooping in confusion. "Where is the crazy one-armed woman who kicked our asses?"
Silas let out a soft sigh.
He slowly stood up from his heavy wooden chair.
He looked directly at the two defeated Heroes of The Unmovable Wall.
"I am Silas Graves," Silas introduced himself, his deep voice carrying the undeniable authority of the Blessed Land. "I am the Lord of this territory."
Lupina’s jaw dropped entirely open with a piece of half-chewed bread falling directly out of her mouth onto the carpet.
"You’re a man?!" Lupina shrieked in absolute shock.
"The Vespera persona was a highly advanced combat disguise," Silas explained bluntly. "It was entirely necessary for misdirection during the broadcast."
Morrighan, the demonic Hero, didn’t look surprised at all. She stood perfectly still with her arms crossed casually over her gray tunic.
"I already knew you were a man," Morrighan stated smoothly.
Silas raised a skeptical eyebrow.

"Oh?" Silas asked. "And how exactly did you figure that out? My disguise ring is a Tier-4 artifact forged by a dwarf master according to what Thora said... It flawlessly masks my vocal chords, my physical mass, and my entire mana signature."
Morrighan offered an amused smirk.
"Your artifact might be flawless," Morrighan replied dryly. "But your acting is absolutely terrible."
Silas frowned. "Excuse me?"

"Your voice and mana were perfectly masked," Morrighan pointed out bluntly, roasting his performance. "But your idle body language is quite male though only for eyes that pay attention. You walk like an aggressive warrior who is used to carrying weapons."
Morrighan casually leaned against the back of an empty wooden chair.
"Furthermore," Morrighan continued mercilessly. "When you were standing next to the dragon and talking..."
Morrighan offered a deadpan brutal stare.
"...you casually reached down and adjusted a package that wasn’t even there."
Evelyn choked on her cigarette smoke.
She burst into a fit of aggressive hacking laughter, covering her mouth with her hands.
"He adjusted his phantom balls!" Evelyn cackled loudly, completely losing her composure.
Elm giggled softly beside her, desperately trying to hide her smile behind her hands.
Even Eluned and Morwenna couldn’t hold it in, completely breaking their pristine composure as they burst into a chorus of snorts and loud laughter from across the table.
Silas stood at the head of the table.
His usually stoic face flushed a deep uncharacteristically bright shade of red.
’Fucking hell...’
He had completely forgotten to suppress his subconscious male habits while wearing the female armor.

"And finally," Morrighan finished her brutal critique. "Your silver breastplate was flat... There was zero extra room in that chest piece as no self-respecting female warrior with that much power would wear armor that restrictive without custom padding."
Silas gritted his teeth, a bit humiliated by the demoness’s flawless logic.
"Noted," Silas replied stiffly, aggressively clearing his throat to regain his composure. "I will work on my physical acting."
He stepped out from behind the table as he walked slowly and deliberately toward the two newly acquired Heroes.

"You were defeated on the battlefield," Silas declared with his voice dropping all traces of humor. "Your previous Lord has officially surrendered the Lord War. By the ancient laws of the Sovereign Realm, your contracts have been permanently severed."
Lupina swallowed hard with her furry ears folding completely flat against her head in terror.
Morrighan stood perfectly still, meeting his golden gaze without flinching.

"You now belong to the Blessed Land," Silas stated. "I am offering you a singular choice. You can swear unbreakable loyalty to my banner right here and now, or you can walk out those gates and take your chances as rogue units in the Unknown Zone as of right now."
The choice was completely obvious.
Rogue units without a Lord’s mana tether usually died within a week in the wild.
Morrighan didn’t hesitate for a single second.
The demoness dropped gracefully to one knee on the thick carpet. She bowed her head deeply, pressing her right hand firmly over her heart.
"I, Morrighan," she swore formally, her voice echoing with dark mana. "Pledge my loyalty and my blade to you. Your enemies are my enemies and your will is my command."
Lupina quickly scrambled to her knees right beside her partner.

"I-I swear too!" Lupina stammered nervously with her tail tucked firmly between her legs. "I pledge my loyalty to you, Lord Silas! Please just don’t let that crazy blonde woman shove any more bread in my mouth!"
Gunnhild snorted loudly from the doorway, crossing her armored arms over her chest.
"Welcome to the Vanguard, fresh meat," Gunnhild laughed as she left immediately after.
Silas watched the two units formally bind their souls to his territory. He could instantly feel the surge of raw mana flowing seamlessly into his Gold Core as their contracts finalized.
It was an incredibly lucrative acquisition.
Silas nodded in satisfaction.
"Stand up," Silas ordered them. "Once we’re out, Gunnhild will show you to your new quarters in the barracks but stay outside for now."
Morrighan and Lupina stood up respectfully.
They quickly followed the towering Berserker out of the dining room with the heavy oak doors closing firmly behind them.
Silas turned slowly around.
He looked directly across the mahogany table at Evelyn.
The black-haired Lord was leaning back in her chair, watching him with a complicated and respectful expression.
Silas offered her a sharp grin.
"Now," Silas said smoothly with his golden eyes flashing. "According to our official broadcast wager..."
Evelyn groaned, completely burying her face in her hands.
"You owe me exactly seventy female combatants from your remaining army roster," Silas reminded her flawlessly.
He walked back toward the table, adjusting the sleeves of his black tunic.
"Let’s go pick them up."
The heavy polished oak doors of the Keep swung open, letting a rush of crisp morning air into the foyer.
Silas stepped out onto the paved stone pathway.
He took a deep breath, letting the clean untainted mana of the Blessed Land fill his lungs. Behind him, the sound of dragging exhausted combat boots echoed against the stone.
Evelyn walked out directly behind him.
She was still swimming in her oversized gray hoodie, the fabric heavily stained with soot, ash, and dried mud from the ruined battlefield.
Her long black hair was a tangled mess, and her shoulders were slumped under the crushing weight of her territorial defeat.
Elm followed closely beside her Lord.
The white-haired Hero looked infinitely better than she had an hour ago.

The healthy color had completely returned to her pale cheeks, but her crystalline silver eyes still darted nervously around the unfamiliar territory, taking in the massive stone walls and the towering architecture.
Out in the wide central courtyard, several of the girls were lounging on the lush green grass.
Gunnhild was sitting heavily on a wooden supply crate.
The woman had her sword resting across her lap, and she was aggressively polishing the curved mythril edge with a thick leather cloth.
A few of the other women who had helped distribute the hot food to the prisoners were resting nearby, passing around wooden canteens of water and chatting quietly as Morrighan and Lupina joined them.
Silas raised his hand.
"Gunnhild," Silas called out with his deep voice carrying easily across the courtyard.
The woman instantly snapped to attention. She dropped her polishing cloth, grabbed her weapon, and stood up straight.
"Yes, My Lord!" Gunnhild responded loudly.
"Go out to the main gates," Silas ordered. "Gather the Unmovable Wall women who are still lounging outside on the grass. Bring them all into the main courtyard."
Gunnhild offered a sharp grin.
"Right away, Boss," Gunnhild said. She whistled loudly, signaling the other Vanguard women to get on their feet.
The group quickly fell into line and jogged off toward the massive steel-weave gates to round up the other people.
Silas turned around on the stone path as he looked down at the exhausted black-haired girl standing next to him.

"So, Evelyn," Silas started smoothly, shifting right back into business. "About the wager. Like I said, you owe me seventy women. Do you want to select them from your ranks, or can I handpick the recruits myself?"

chapters.title: Chapter 336: A Choice
paragraphs: Evelyn let out a long ragged sigh.
She aggressively rubbed her temples with her soot-stained fingers.
Her head was pounding with a vicious throbbing migraine.
She didn’t want to make roster decisions right now... She didn’t want to play the ruthless Lord calculating unit values either.
All she wanted to do was find a dark, quiet room and sleep for an entire week.
"Just let me handle it, Silas," Evelyn muttered tiredly.
She looked up at him.
Her dark eyes carried a heavy undeniable weight. She was incredibly grateful to Silas for saving Elm.
He had miraculously cured her oldest friend’s shattered core when he had zero obligation to do so.
He could have just let Elm die and taken the territory, but he chose to heal her.
But the aftereffects of this Lord War were catastrophic for her people.
The Unmovable Wall’s infrastructure was damaged, the mana reserves were drained, and her troops were battered, demoralized, and deeply exhausted.
"Silas," Evelyn asked quietly with her voice losing its usual sarcastic edge. "Can I ask for a massive favor?"
Silas crossed his arms over his black tunic.
"Depends on the favor," Silas replied.

"I need time," Evelyn admitted, looking down at the paved stones. "I need permission to keep my people stationed around the borders of the Blessed Land for a week at most... Just until I can gather everyone up, treat the wounded, and reorganize my broken command structure. We can’t move the mobile fortress in this state."
Silas looked at her for a moment. He didn’t even need to consult his internal thoughts for this one.
It was a perfectly reasonable logistical request.
"Granted," Silas nodded. "Take the week. You can park the fortress on the western ridge where you guys stayed before."
Evelyn let out a massive breath of relief, the tension leaving her shoulders.
"I even have a place for your people, the women though to stay inside the walls if they want off the treads," Silas added casually. "I just finished building a new residential complex."
Evelyn frowned. Her stubborn independent pride immediately flared up.
"No," Evelyn rejected the offer instantly, shaking her head. "That’s too much. We can just stay in our own territory. The mobile fortress still has functional barracks as we don’t need charity."
She didn’t want to accept housing handouts from the Lord who had just crushed her entire army on a global broadcast.
POK!
Elm suddenly elbowed Evelyn hard in the ribs.
"Ow!" Evelyn yelped, clutching her side and glaring at her First Hero. "What was that for?!"
Elm stared right back at her with unwavering seriousness.

"We are staying here," Elm told her Lord firmly, leaving no room for debate. "Lord Silas just saved my life when he had absolutely zero obligation to do so. We are not going to insult his hospitality by running away to pout in the fortress. Accept the offer, Evelyn."
Evelyn opened her mouth to argue, ready to defend the honor of her territory.
But she looked into Elm’s stubborn silver eyes and realized it was a losing battle.
Elm had just spent a long time floating in a freezing glass tube... she wasn’t about to go sleep back there.
Evelyn snapped her mouth shut.
She pouted angrily, crossing her arms and looking away from Silas with an irritated huff.
"Fine," Evelyn grumbled. "We will stay."
Her childish pout quickly faded, replaced by the serious expression of a commander as she turned to face her First Hero.
"Elm," Evelyn ordered quietly. "Go back out to the battlefield right now... Secure Hiro and the other heavily wounded commanders."
Elm nodded immediately, standing at attention.

"Get them back into the Unmovable Wall medical bays before they hurt themselves trying to train or march out of stubborn pride," Evelyn instructed. "Make sure the healers are treating them immediately. Lock them in the med-bay if you have to."
"Understood, My Lord," Elm said respectfully.
The white-haired Hero turned around and jogged quickly down the path toward the main gates.
Evelyn watched her go. Once Elm was out of earshot, Evelyn let out another exhausted sigh.
She looked down at her muddy combat boots with her shoulders sagging.
"There were so many casualties today," Evelyn whispered softly.
Her voice cracked slightly.
For the first time since they had met, the successful Lord Sky sounded incredibly vulnerable.

"It has been a very long time since I felt like a rookie," Evelyn confessed, her dark eyes reflecting the trauma of the battlefield. "I have conquered a lot of Zones but watching your Vanguard dismantle my forces..."
She ran her trembling hand through her messy black hair.

"I realize now that from the very beginning, I had no hope of defeating the Blessed Land," Evelyn admitted bitterly. "My tactics were useless and my stats didn’t matter since we were playing an entirely different game."
She clenched her fists inside the pockets of her hoodie.
"Perhaps if I had realized that earlier..." Evelyn muttered, her voice thick with guilt. "If I had just swallowed my damn pride and surrendered an hour sooner, there wouldn’t be so much dea—"
"Stop."
Silas’s deep voice cut through her spiraling thoughts like a steel blade.
Evelyn blinked, looking up at him in surprise.
Silas stood on the stone path with his hands casually in his pockets, his golden-ringed eyes looking down at her with a calm look.
"It is not my place to say this," Silas told her bluntly. "I am not your commander, and I don’t run your territory. But you shouldn’t think too much about the ’what ifs’..."
Evelyn stared at him, caught off guard by his sudden intervention.

"You made the best tactical decision you could with the intelligence you had at the time," Silas pointed out logically. "You didn’t know the extent of my Vanguard’s power so you fought hard. You trusted your heroes and you lost. That is just how the Sovereign Realm works."
He offered her a smirk.
"Besides," Silas joked, his tone lightening up considerably. "You are already old enough as it is. If you stress out any more over things you can’t control, you are going to start losing your hair."
Evelyn froze.
Her dark eyes went incredibly wide with indignation as the guilt instantly evaporated, replaced entirely by offended rage.
"I am twenty-two!" Evelyn shrieked at the top of her lungs. She stepped forward and swung her fist aggressively at his shoulder.
WHACK!
Silas didn’t even try to dodge. He didn’t flinch as her unarmored knuckles bounced harmlessly off his dense muscles.
"Stop calling me old, you stupid teenager!" Evelyn yelled, winding up for another punch. "I am in the prime of my life and I have an immaculate skincare routine!"
"Yeah yeah..."
Silas just laughed, easily catching her wrist in his large hand before she could hit him again.
A few yards away, perfectly hidden behind the thick wooden pillar of the Keep’s expansive front porch, two powerful women were completely frozen in terror.
Eluned and Morwenna had been secretly eavesdropping on the conversation.
Both women suddenly broke out into a cold panicked sweat.
Morwenna swallowed hard, her hand nervously gripping the hilt of her cutlass.
’She is twenty-two...’ Morwenna thought, her stormy gray eyes wide with panic.
Eluned gripped the wooden pillar so tightly her knuckles turned white.
’And he thinks that is old...’ Eluned realized in absolute horror.
They were both ancient immortal beings.
Morwenna had sailed the phantom seas and pillaged the oceans for well over centuries.
Eluned was a literal Nature Goddess who had existed for countless generations, watching forests rise and fall.
’Does this mean he is going to start making jokes about our age too?!’ Morwenna mouthed silently to the First Wife with her pirate bravado completely shattered.
Eluned furiously shook her head, her beautiful emerald eyes filled with terrified dread.
’We take our real ages to the grave,’ Eluned mouthed back aggressively. ’If he asks, I am twenty-one.’
Out in the courtyard, the synchronized sound of marching boots echoed across the stone pathways, saving Silas from dealing with a potentially lethal domestic crisis.
Gunnhild and the girls had returned from the gates.
They were leading a massive group of women from the Unmovable Wall directly into the center of the Keep’s courtyard.
There were well over a hundred women gathered on the grass.
They made up almost the entirety of the surviving female faction from Evelyn’s army.
There were heavily armored knights carrying dented shields, agile scouts with torn cloaks, and a large group of soot-stained dwarven blacksmiths clutching their heavy hammers.
They looked exhausted.
Their armors were heavily dented, their uniforms were torn from the elemental blasts, and many of them sported fresh white bandages wrapped tightly around their arms and heads.
They stopped marching, forming up in the center of the grassy courtyard.
A tense heavy silence fell over the massive group.
They all looked up at Silas standing on the pathway.
Their expressions were incredibly varied. Some looked at him with blatant wide-eyed fear. Some looked at him with quiet simmering resentment and some looked at him with undeniable awe.
It seemed he was the one who had commanded the monsters that decisively won the Lord War against their supposedly invincible mobile fortress.
By the brutal laws of the Sovereign Realm, he now had the absolute right to dictate exactly what happened to them.
Then, the women shifted their collective gaze.
They looked past Silas and saw Evelyn standing there in her oversized gray hoodie.
The atmosphere in the courtyard instantly shifted.
The fear and the resentment completely melted away. It was replaced by a deep sorrow.
They looked at their Lord with heartbreaking apologies written all over their dirty faces. They felt incredibly guilty for failing to hold the line as they felt like they had let her down.
Silas watched the silent exchange carefully.
He liked what he saw... He liked it a lot.
These women weren’t mindless mercenaries who only cared about their next paycheck or survival.
They possessed genuine fierce loyalty to their commander and that in itself was a very valuable trait.
Evelyn stepped forward, pulling her hand out of Silas’s grip. She looked out at her battered broken soldiers.
"I am sorry," Evelyn spoke loudly, her voice carrying clearly across the quiet courtyard. "I led you into a battle we could not win."
The women immediately shook their heads.
"Do not apologize, My Lord!" a tall female knight called out from the front row, slamming her fist over her dented breastplate. "We failed to protect the Vanguard!"
"You gave us everything, Lord Sky!" another scout shouted fiercely from the back. "You built the fortress for us!"
"We were blessed just to know you!" a stout dwarven woman yelled, slamming her heavy iron hammer against her steel shield. "We’d ride the treads to hell for you!"
Evelyn smiled sadly, fighting back the tears welling in her dark eyes.
She stepped back, giving Silas the floor. She had led them as far as she could.
...Now, it was up to him.
Silas stepped forward.
He cleared his throat.
"Attention," Silas commanded.
His deep voice instantly silenced the murmuring crowd as the aura of a Lord radiated naturally from his frame, completely commanding the space.
"I am Silas Graves," Silas introduced himself formally.
A ripple of extreme visible confusion swept through the ranks of the Unmovable Wall soldiers.
They looked around frantically. They searched the courtyard for the terrifying, one-armed woman in silver armor who had decimated their front lines.
"I am Lord Vespera as well," Silas stated bluntly, dropping the bomb.
The women gasped collectively.

"The Vespera identity was a combat disguise used for the broadcast," Silas explained smoothly, not offering any apologies for the deception. "This is the true me. I am the Lord of the Blessed Land..."
He let the massive revelation sink in for a moment.
He watched their shocked faces process the reality that they had been beaten by him.

"I am well aware that this transition is quite abrupt," Silas continued, pacing slowly and deliberately in front of the crowd. "But as of right now, you need to know the terms of the wager that ended this war."
He stopped pacing and looked directly at the front row of knights.
"Your Lord made a choice before the battle began," Silas revealed. "She agreed that if the Blessed Land won the Lord War, she would give me seventy women from your ranks as compensation."
A heavy anxious murmur broke out among the soldiers.
They looked at each other nervously, wondering who was going to be dragged away in chains to serve the enemy Lord.
"I am now calling in that debt," Silas declared loudly.
He raised his hand, pointing to the empty pristine patch of green grass on the left side of the courtyard.
"But... I am giving you a choice," Silas told them.

sentences.text: Evelyn let out a long ragged sigh.
She aggressively rubbed her temples with her soot-stained fingers.
Her head was pounding with a vicious throbbing migraine.
She didn’t want to make roster decisions right now...
She didn’t want to play the ruthless Lord calculating unit values either.
All she wanted to do was find a dark, quiet room and sleep for an entire week.
"Just let me handle it, Silas," Evelyn muttered tiredly.
She looked up at him.
Her dark eyes carried a heavy undeniable weight.
She was incredibly grateful to Silas for saving Elm.
He had miraculously cured her oldest friend’s shattered core when he had zero obligation to do so.
He could have just let Elm die and taken the territory, but he chose to heal her.
But the aftereffects of this Lord War were catastrophic for her people.
The Unmovable Wall’s infrastructure was damaged, the mana reserves were drained, and her troops were battered, demoralized, and deeply exhausted.
"Silas," Evelyn asked quietly with her voice losing its usual sarcastic edge.
"Can I ask for a massive favor?"
Silas crossed his arms over his black tunic.
"Depends on the favor," Silas replied.
"I need time," Evelyn admitted, looking down at the paved stones.
"I need permission to keep my people stationed around the borders of the Blessed Land for a week at most...
Just until I can gather everyone up, treat the wounded, and reorganize my broken command structure.
We can’t move the mobile fortress in this state."
Silas looked at her for a moment.
He didn’t even need to consult his internal thoughts for this one.
It was a perfectly reasonable logistical request.
"Granted," Silas nodded.
"Take the week.
You can park the fortress on the western ridge where you guys stayed before."
Evelyn let out a massive breath of relief, the tension leaving her shoulders.
"I even have a place for your people, the women though to stay inside the walls if they want off the treads," Silas added casually.
"I just finished building a new residential complex."
Evelyn frowned.
Her stubborn independent pride immediately flared up.
"No," Evelyn rejected the offer instantly, shaking her head.
"That’s too much.
We can just stay in our own territory.
The mobile fortress still has functional barracks as we don’t need charity."
She didn’t want to accept housing handouts from the Lord who had just crushed her entire army on a global broadcast.
POK!
Elm suddenly elbowed Evelyn hard in the ribs.
"Ow!" Evelyn yelped, clutching her side and glaring at her First Hero.
"What was that for?!"
Elm stared right back at her with unwavering seriousness.
"We are staying here," Elm told her Lord firmly, leaving no room for debate.
"Lord Silas just saved my life when he had absolutely zero obligation to do so.
We are not going to insult his hospitality by running away to pout in the fortress.
Accept the offer, Evelyn."
Evelyn opened her mouth to argue, ready to defend the honor of her territory.
But she looked into Elm’s stubborn silver eyes and realized it was a losing battle.
Elm had just spent a long time floating in a freezing glass tube... she wasn’t about to go sleep back there.
Evelyn snapped her mouth shut.
She pouted angrily, crossing her arms and looking away from Silas with an irritated huff.
"Fine," Evelyn grumbled.
"We will stay."
Her childish pout quickly faded, replaced by the serious expression of a commander as she turned to face her First Hero.
"Elm," Evelyn ordered quietly.
"Go back out to the battlefield right now...
Secure Hiro and the other heavily wounded commanders."
Elm nodded immediately, standing at attention.
"Get them back into the Unmovable Wall medical bays before they hurt themselves trying to train or march out of stubborn pride," Evelyn instructed.
"Make sure the healers are treating them immediately.
Lock them in the med-bay if you have to."
"Understood, My Lord," Elm said respectfully.
The white-haired Hero turned around and jogged quickly down the path toward the main gates.
Evelyn watched her go.
Once Elm was out of earshot, Evelyn let out another exhausted sigh.
She looked down at her muddy combat boots with her shoulders sagging.
"There were so many casualties today," Evelyn whispered softly.
Her voice cracked slightly.
For the first time since they had met, the successful Lord Sky sounded incredibly vulnerable.
"It has been a very long time since I felt like a rookie," Evelyn confessed, her dark eyes reflecting the trauma of the battlefield.
"I have conquered a lot of Zones but watching your Vanguard dismantle my forces..."
She ran her trembling hand through her messy black hair.
"I realize now that from the very beginning, I had no hope of defeating the Blessed Land," Evelyn admitted bitterly.
"My tactics were useless and my stats didn’t matter since we were playing an entirely different game."
She clenched her fists inside the pockets of her hoodie.
"Perhaps if I had realized that earlier..." Evelyn muttered, her voice thick with guilt.
"If I had just swallowed my damn pride and surrendered an hour sooner, there wouldn’t be so much dea—"
"Stop."
Silas’s deep voice cut through her spiraling thoughts like a steel blade.
Evelyn blinked, looking up at him in surprise.
Silas stood on the stone path with his hands casually in his pockets, his golden-ringed eyes looking down at her with a calm look.
"It is not my place to say this," Silas told her bluntly.
"I am not your commander, and I don’t run your territory.
But you shouldn’t think too much about the ’what ifs’..."
Evelyn stared at him, caught off guard by his sudden intervention.
"You made the best tactical decision you could with the intelligence you had at the time," Silas pointed out logically.
"You didn’t know the extent of my Vanguard’s power so you fought hard.
You trusted your heroes and you lost.
That is just how the Sovereign Realm works."
He offered her a smirk.
"Besides," Silas joked, his tone lightening up considerably.
"You are already old enough as it is.
If you stress out any more over things you can’t control, you are going to start losing your hair."
Evelyn froze.
Her dark eyes went incredibly wide with indignation as the guilt instantly evaporated, replaced entirely by offended rage.
"I am twenty-two!" Evelyn shrieked at the top of her lungs.
She stepped forward and swung her fist aggressively at his shoulder.
WHACK!
Silas didn’t even try to dodge.
He didn’t flinch as her unarmored knuckles bounced harmlessly off his dense muscles.
"Stop calling me old, you stupid teenager!" Evelyn yelled, winding up for another punch.
"I am in the prime of my life and I have an immaculate skincare routine!"
"Yeah yeah..."
Silas just laughed, easily catching her wrist in his large hand before she could hit him again.
A few yards away, perfectly hidden behind the thick wooden pillar of the Keep’s expansive front porch, two powerful women were completely frozen in terror.
Eluned and Morwenna had been secretly eavesdropping on the conversation.
Both women suddenly broke out into a cold panicked sweat.
Morwenna swallowed hard, her hand nervously gripping the hilt of her cutlass.
’She is twenty-two...’ Morwenna thought, her stormy gray eyes wide with panic.
Eluned gripped the wooden pillar so tightly her knuckles turned white.
’And he thinks that is old...’ Eluned realized in absolute horror.
They were both ancient immortal beings.
Morwenna had sailed the phantom seas and pillaged the oceans for well over centuries.
Eluned was a literal Nature Goddess who had existed for countless generations, watching forests rise and fall.
’Does this mean he is going to start making jokes about our age too?!’ Morwenna mouthed silently to the First Wife with her pirate bravado completely shattered.

chapters.title: Chapter 337: New Additions To Blessed Land
paragraphs: He didn’t want to drag them by force as he didn’t want to build his territory on resentment.

"You can either join the Blessed Land right here, right now," Silas offered, "or you can stay where you are and remain with the Unmovable Wall. I cannot, and will not, force you to cross over if your heart is not in it."
He paused, looking specifically at the group of soot-stained dwarves clutching their hammers.

"Though I will admit," Silas added strategically with a smirk touching his lips. "My Master Smith is currently drowning in raw materials, and I am in desperate need of highly skilled dwarven craftsmen."
Silas crossed his arms.
He waited.
He wasn’t planning on cultivating a bunch of mindless resentful slaves. These were all people who had heads, emotions, and feelings.
That was exactly why he had allowed the Unmovable Wall to park their fortress and stay here for a week.
He wanted them to naturally observe how the Blessed Land women acted.
He wanted them to see the food, the safety, and the camaraderie.
He knew that over time, seeing the luxury and freedom his territory provided, they would willingly enter his ranks of their own power.
However, that didn’t seem to be a problem right now.
A large group of heavily muscled dwarven women immediately broke ranks.
They marched straight over to the left side of the courtyard without a single second of hesitation.

"We go where the forge is hot, Lord Silas!" one of the dwarves grunted loudly, hoisting her heavy hammer over her shoulder. "Lord Sky was good to us, but the Unmovable Wall only has two forges... We want to strike mythril!"
As the dwarves moved, the rest of the women began to follow.
They split from the main forces with surprising organized efficiency.
It was almost as though they had already discussed this among themselves while sitting out in the mud.
They didn’t argue and they didn’t cry or scream about betrayal.
They simply patted their comrades on the shoulders, gave quick, tight hugs, and walked confidently over to the designated spot on the left.
Within two minutes, exactly seventy women stood entirely separate from the main force.
A tall girl with short brown hair and a dented chestplate stepped up from the main group.
She offered Silas a crisp and perfectly executed military salute.
"Lord Graves," the girl reported clearly. "We were already made aware of these wager terms by Lord Sky’s secondary commanders while we were being treated on the field."
She gestured to the seventy women standing proudly on the left.
"We had already discussed the logistics and decided exactly who would go before we even marched into your courtyard," the girl explained.
She offered a small proud smile.

"We did not want to make too much of a fuss about it in front of you," she continued respectfully. "We of The Unmovable Wall are not the kind of people to cause trouble over an honorable wager. Our Lord gave her word, and we will honor her debt..."
Silas raised an eyebrow.
He was genuinely impressed.
The discipline, maturity, and professionalism of Evelyn’s troops were top-tier.
...They were taking their defeat with incredible grace.
"Thank you," Silas said respectfully, returning her nod.
He turned his head toward the massive stone structure of the barracks.
"Brida!" Silas called out loudly.
BANG!
The heavy wooden door of the barracks slammed violently open.
Brida stepped out into the bright morning sun.
The Grand Titan Bastion was not wearing her massive multi-ton adamantine armor as she was dressed casually instead.
"Hehehe~"

She wore a ridiculously big white singlet that stretched tightly over her massive muscles and loose cloth shorts and she was aggressively massaging her wet hair with a thick white towel, having clearly just stepped out of a hot shower.
She walked lazily over to Silas with her heavy muscles flexing effortlessly with every step.
"Yeah, Boss?" Brida yawned, tossing the wet towel casually over her broad shoulder.
Silas pointed to the seventy women standing proudly on the left.
"Take charge of our new recruits," Silas ordered.
Brida looked at the massive group of battered soldiers, scouts, and dwarves.
She cracked a wide grin, cracking her thick knuckles loudly.
"You got it," Brida laughed.
She walked heavily over to the recruits, towering over almost all of them like a literal mountain of muscle.
"Alright, listen up!" Brida bellowed, her booming voice echoing off the Keep walls.
She pointed a thick calloused finger back at the barracks.
"The seventy of you who just joined the Blessed Land are coming with me," Brida commanded.
She looked past the crowd, scanning the faces until she spotted two familiar figures standing near Gunnhild.
"Morrighan! Lupina!" Brida shouted loudly. "Get your asses over here!"
The demoness and the wolf-girl quickly jogged over to join the group, looking slightly intimidated by the towering Bastion.
"That makes seventy-two," Brida noted, doing the quick math in her head.
She rested her hands on her hips, looking down at the recruits.

"You are officially Blessed Land recruits now," Brida told them bluntly. "You will be staying in the barracks for the time being. You follow my orders and you follow the Lord’s orders as well. Follow me, and do not lag behind."
Brida turned around and started marching heavily toward the massive stone barracks building.
The seventy-two women immediately fell into line.
They followed the towering woman without a single word of complaint, eager to get inside and see their new bunks.
As the recruits marched away, the sound of rapid footsteps approached from the main gates.
Elm had arrived back in the courtyard.
The white-haired Hero jogged up to Evelyn, panting slightly.
She offered a quick, sharp nod to confirm that Hiro and the other commanders had been securely put in the fortress medical bays.
Silas turned his attention to the remaining women from the Unmovable Wall.
There were about thirty or so soldiers left standing in the grass, the ones who had chosen to stay with Evelyn.
"The rest of you," Silas announced calmly. "Follow me."
He didn’t wait for a response. Silas turned and began walking down the paved stone path that cut deep through the center of the territory.
Evelyn and Elm quickly fell into step right behind him. The thirty surviving soldiers formed up into a loose column and followed their Lord.
They began moving across the Blessed Land.
As they walked, the defensive tension slowly began to leave the soldiers’ shoulders.
They stopped marching like prisoners and started looking around with genuine curiosity.
"Whoa..." one of the knights muttered softly, her eyes going wide.
Evelyn and Elm were equally stunned.
They commented quietly to each other, pointing at the structures as they took in the undeniable beauty of the territory.
The Unmovable Wall was a massive, vibrating cage of iron, steel, and suffocating smog.
It was very functional, but it was incredibly bleak.
The Blessed Land oh the other hand was a vibrant living paradise.
Lush, thick green grass carpeted the ground perfectly.
Massive, magical mana-fruit trees lined the paved pathways with their heavy branches sagging with glowing red apples that radiated pure energy.
The air smelled like fresh blooming flowers and clean soil instead of burning engine oil and exhaust.
"It is so green," Elm whispered in absolute awe, her silver eyes reflecting the sunlight. "I haven’t seen real grass in such a long time."
They walked past the grand multi-story stone structure of the Territory Library.
Evelyn spotted several of the Vanguard girls sitting comfortably on the outdoor wooden benches.
They were casually reading thick leather-bound books in the sunlight, sipping tea and chatting.
They didn’t look like soldiers waiting for the next attack as they looked incredibly relaxed and at peace.
Silas smiled faintly as he heard Evelyn’s quiet gasp of surprise behind him.
He knew exactly what he was doing. He wasn’t just giving them a tour as he was showing them a significantly better life.
He was planting the seeds.
’In case some extra people want to join us...’
They continued down the path until they reached the newly constructed residential sector.
Silas stopped walking.
He stood directly in front of the massive towering Obsidian-Slate living quarters.
There were four identical, sprawling three-story luxury complexes standing proudly on the manicured grass.
The dark stone walls gleamed with a subtle purple hue in the sunlight as thick ironwood columns framed the entrances, and wide glass balconies lined the upper floors.
The thirty Unmovable Wall soldiers stared up at the architectural majesty of the buildings with their jaws collectively dropping.
Silas turned around to face Evelyn.
He reached into his tunic pocket and pulled out a heavy iron key ring.
He tossed it smoothly through the air.
JINGLE!
Evelyn caught the heavy keys clumsily against her chest, looking down at them in confusion.
"I am giving you and your people the fourth building," Silas told her, pointing to the massive complex on the far right.
Evelyn stared at the keys in her hand, completely dumbfounded.
"This entire building?" Evelyn asked in disbelief. "Just for us?"
"Yes," Silas confirmed calmly.
He crossed his arms over his black tunic.
"Each suite inside has a private runic bath with perfectly heated water," Silas explained casually. "There are fresh clean linens on the beds, and the walls are fully insulated against the weather."
The Unmovable Wall soldiers standing behind Evelyn literally gasped out loud.
Hot water... Private rooms... Real, soft beds?
It sounded like unattainable heaven to soldiers who had been sleeping on vibrating cots inside a metal hull.
"My only rule is that you keep the place neat," Silas warned them cleanly. "Do not track mud on my hardwood floors."
Evelyn gripped the keys incredibly tightly.
She looked up at Silas.
Her dark eyes were filled with genuine, and overwhelming gratitude. He hadn’t just given them a place to sleep... he had given them luxury after the worst day of their lives.
"Thank you, Silas," Evelyn said softly with her voice carrying sincerity.
Silas nodded.
He took a long look at the exhausted, soot-stained faces of everyone gathered around him.
They had bled today and they had fought incredibly hard so they deserved a break from the brutal reality of the Sovereign Realm.
"You all should go inside and clean up," Silas announced loudly to the group. "Wash the mud off. Soak in the hot water. Get some rest."
He offered them a genuine grin that completely banished his intimidating aura.
"And when you are done," Silas added warmly. "Come down to the main Mess Hall in the Barracks."
Evelyn raised an eyebrow, tilting her head.
"Why?" Evelyn asked.
"Because we are going to have a party," Silas declared.
The party in the main Mess Hall was deafening.
It was genuinely unknown how the massive wooden building was able to contain so many women at once without the walls physically bursting outward from the pressure.
But that didn’t matter...
The volume of noise was incredible.
Over a hundred and fifty women were packed tightly into the expansive high-ceilinged hall.
Every single long oak table was full as the women were eating a lot, drinking deeply, and laughing at the top of their lungs.
The suffocating tension of the Lord War had completely vanished.
It was entirely replaced by the universal unifying camaraderie of a massive well-earned feast.
At the far end of the hall, a large group of the newly recruited dwarven women were literally standing on top of the sturdy oak tables.
They had locked arms tightly together and were stomping their heavy boots, singing a loud rowdy dwarven tavern song.
"HEAVE THE IRON, STRIKE THE STONE!" they bellowed merrily, their voices shaking the rafters.
Thora was in her undisputed element.
The Master Smith was actively carting a massive heavy wooden barrel of alcohol across the room, completely ignoring the weight.
She was aggressively slamming heavy wooden tankards down onto the tables with boisterous enthusiasm.
"Everyone, take one!" Thora shouted gleefully over the loud singing. "Come on, drink one! It’s fresh from the brewery! Don’t be shy!"
She was handing out massive overflowing cups of highly concentrated Blessed Drinks.
It didn’t matter who they were.
It didn’t matter if they were the exhausted women who had stayed with the Unmovable Wall, the Blessed Land soldiers, or the brand-new recruits.
Everyone got a drink.
The Unmovable Wall soldiers looked at the glowing white liquid hesitantly at first.
Then, they took a small sip.
GULP!
The exact second the magical liquid hit their stomachs, a blinding warm wave of pure refreshing mana washed entirely over their exhausted cores.
"Oh my goddess," one of Evelyn’s heavily bruised knights groaned aloud.
She let out a massive shuddering sigh of relief as her sore, aching muscles instantly relaxed.
The lingering painful bruises on her arms completely faded away into nothingness.
It was simply too much enjoyment to process at once.
Especially when combined with the food.
At a table near the center of the hall, Talira was completely losing her mind.
