A tall girl with short brown hair and a dented chestplate stepped up from the main group.
She offered Silas a crisp and perfectly executed military salute.
"Lord Graves," the girl reported clearly.
"We were already made aware of these wager terms by Lord Sky’s secondary commanders while we were being treated on the field."
She gestured to the seventy women standing proudly on the left.
"We had already discussed the logistics and decided exactly who would go before we even marched into your courtyard," the girl explained.
She offered a small proud smile.
"We did not want to make too much of a fuss about it in front of you," she continued respectfully.
"We of The Unmovable Wall are not the kind of people to cause trouble over an honorable wager.
Our Lord gave her word, and we will honor her debt..."
Silas raised an eyebrow.
He was genuinely impressed.
The discipline, maturity, and professionalism of Evelyn’s troops were top-tier.
...They were taking their defeat with incredible grace.
"Thank you," Silas said respectfully, returning her nod.
He turned his head toward the massive stone structure of the barracks.
"Brida!" Silas called out loudly.
BANG!
The heavy wooden door of the barracks slammed violently open.
Brida stepped out into the bright morning sun.
The Grand Titan Bastion was not wearing her massive multi-ton adamantine armor as she was dressed casually instead.
"Hehehe~"

She wore a ridiculously big white singlet that stretched tightly over her massive muscles and loose cloth shorts and she was aggressively massaging her wet hair with a thick white towel, having clearly just stepped out of a hot shower.
She walked lazily over to Silas with her heavy muscles flexing effortlessly with every step.
"Yeah, Boss?" Brida yawned, tossing the wet towel casually over her broad shoulder.
Silas pointed to the seventy women standing proudly on the left.
"Take charge of our new recruits," Silas ordered.
Brida looked at the massive group of battered soldiers, scouts, and dwarves.
She cracked a wide grin, cracking her thick knuckles loudly.
"You got it," Brida laughed.
She walked heavily over to the recruits, towering over almost all of them like a literal mountain of muscle.
"Alright, listen up!" Brida bellowed, her booming voice echoing off the Keep walls.
She pointed a thick calloused finger back at the barracks.
"The seventy of you who just joined the Blessed Land are coming with me," Brida commanded.
She looked past the crowd, scanning the faces until she spotted two familiar figures standing near Gunnhild.
"Morrighan!
Lupina!" Brida shouted loudly.
"Get your asses over here!"
The demoness and the wolf-girl quickly jogged over to join the group, looking slightly intimidated by the towering Bastion.
"That makes seventy-two," Brida noted, doing the quick math in her head.
She rested her hands on her hips, looking down at the recruits.
"You are officially Blessed Land recruits now," Brida told them bluntly.
"You will be staying in the barracks for the time being.
You follow my orders and you follow the Lord’s orders as well.
Follow me, and do not lag behind."
Brida turned around and started marching heavily toward the massive stone barracks building.
The seventy-two women immediately fell into line.
They followed the towering woman without a single word of complaint, eager to get inside and see their new bunks.
As the recruits marched away, the sound of rapid footsteps approached from the main gates.
Elm had arrived back in the courtyard.
The white-haired Hero jogged up to Evelyn, panting slightly.
She offered a quick, sharp nod to confirm that Hiro and the other commanders had been securely put in the fortress medical bays.
Silas turned his attention to the remaining women from the Unmovable Wall.
There were about thirty or so soldiers left standing in the grass, the ones who had chosen to stay with Evelyn.
"The rest of you," Silas announced calmly.
"Follow me."
He didn’t wait for a response.
Silas turned and began walking down the paved stone path that cut deep through the center of the territory.
Evelyn and Elm quickly fell into step right behind him.
The thirty surviving soldiers formed up into a loose column and followed their Lord.
They began moving across the Blessed Land.
As they walked, the defensive tension slowly began to leave the soldiers’ shoulders.
They stopped marching like prisoners and started looking around with genuine curiosity.
"Whoa..." one of the knights muttered softly, her eyes going wide.
Evelyn and Elm were equally stunned.
They commented quietly to each other, pointing at the structures as they took in the undeniable beauty of the territory.
The Unmovable Wall was a massive, vibrating cage of iron, steel, and suffocating smog.
It was very functional, but it was incredibly bleak.
The Blessed Land oh the other hand was a vibrant living paradise.
Lush, thick green grass carpeted the ground perfectly.
Massive, magical mana-fruit trees lined the paved pathways with their heavy branches sagging with glowing red apples that radiated pure energy.
The air smelled like fresh blooming flowers and clean soil instead of burning engine oil and exhaust.
"It is so green," Elm whispered in absolute awe, her silver eyes reflecting the sunlight.
"I haven’t seen real grass in such a long time."
They walked past the grand multi-story stone structure of the Territory Library.
Evelyn spotted several of the Vanguard girls sitting comfortably on the outdoor wooden benches.
They were casually reading thick leather-bound books in the sunlight, sipping tea and chatting.
They didn’t look like soldiers waiting for the next attack as they looked incredibly relaxed and at peace.
Silas smiled faintly as he heard Evelyn’s quiet gasp of surprise behind him.
He knew exactly what he was doing.
He wasn’t just giving them a tour as he was showing them a significantly better life.
He was planting the seeds.
’In case some extra people want to join us...’
They continued down the path until they reached the newly constructed residential sector.
Silas stopped walking.
He stood directly in front of the massive towering Obsidian-Slate living quarters.
There were four identical, sprawling three-story luxury complexes standing proudly on the manicured grass.
The dark stone walls gleamed with a subtle purple hue in the sunlight as thick ironwood columns framed the entrances, and wide glass balconies lined the upper floors.
The thirty Unmovable Wall soldiers stared up at the architectural majesty of the buildings with their jaws collectively dropping.
Silas turned around to face Evelyn.
He reached into his tunic pocket and pulled out a heavy iron key ring.
He tossed it smoothly through the air.
JINGLE!
Evelyn caught the heavy keys clumsily against her chest, looking down at them in confusion.
"I am giving you and your people the fourth building," Silas told her, pointing to the massive complex on the far right.
Evelyn stared at the keys in her hand, completely dumbfounded.
"This entire building?" Evelyn asked in disbelief.
"Just for us?"
"Yes," Silas confirmed calmly.
He crossed his arms over his black tunic.
"Each suite inside has a private runic bath with perfectly heated water," Silas explained casually.
"There are fresh clean linens on the beds, and the walls are fully insulated against the weather."
The Unmovable Wall soldiers standing behind Evelyn literally gasped out loud.
Hot water...
Private rooms...
Real, soft beds?
It sounded like unattainable heaven to soldiers who had been sleeping on vibrating cots inside a metal hull.
"My only rule is that you keep the place neat," Silas warned them cleanly.
"Do not track mud on my hardwood floors."
Evelyn gripped the keys incredibly tightly.
She looked up at Silas.
Her dark eyes were filled with genuine, and overwhelming gratitude.
He hadn’t just given them a place to sleep... he had given them luxury after the worst day of their lives.
"Thank you, Silas," Evelyn said softly with her voice carrying sincerity.
Silas nodded.
He took a long look at the exhausted, soot-stained faces of everyone gathered around him.
They had bled today and they had fought incredibly hard so they deserved a break from the brutal reality of the Sovereign Realm.
"You all should go inside and clean up," Silas announced loudly to the group.
"Wash the mud off.
Soak in the hot water.
Get some rest."
He offered them a genuine grin that completely banished his intimidating aura.
"And when you are done," Silas added warmly.
"Come down to the main Mess Hall in the Barracks."
Evelyn raised an eyebrow, tilting her head.
"Why?" Evelyn asked.
"Because we are going to have a party," Silas declared.
The party in the main Mess Hall was deafening.
It was genuinely unknown how the massive wooden building was able to contain so many women at once without the walls physically bursting outward from the pressure.
But that didn’t matter...
The volume of noise was incredible.
Over a hundred and fifty women were packed tightly into the expansive high-ceilinged hall.
Every single long oak table was full as the women were eating a lot, drinking deeply, and laughing at the top of their lungs.
The suffocating tension of the Lord War had completely vanished.
It was entirely replaced by the universal unifying camaraderie of a massive well-earned feast.
At the far end of the hall, a large group of the newly recruited dwarven women were literally standing on top of the sturdy oak tables.
They had locked arms tightly together and were stomping their heavy boots, singing a loud rowdy dwarven tavern song.
"HEAVE THE IRON, STRIKE THE STONE!" they bellowed merrily, their voices shaking the rafters.
Thora was in her undisputed element.
The Master Smith was actively carting a massive heavy wooden barrel of alcohol across the room, completely ignoring the weight.
She was aggressively slamming heavy wooden tankards down onto the tables with boisterous enthusiasm.
"Everyone, take one!" Thora shouted gleefully over the loud singing.
"Come on, drink one!
It’s fresh from the brewery!
Don’t be shy!"
She was handing out massive overflowing cups of highly concentrated Blessed Drinks.
It didn’t matter who they were.
It didn’t matter if they were the exhausted women who had stayed with the Unmovable Wall, the Blessed Land soldiers, or the brand-new recruits.
Everyone got a drink.
The Unmovable Wall soldiers looked at the glowing white liquid hesitantly at first.
Then, they took a small sip.
GULP!
The exact second the magical liquid hit their stomachs, a blinding warm wave of pure refreshing mana washed entirely over their exhausted cores.
"Oh my goddess," one of Evelyn’s heavily bruised knights groaned aloud.
She let out a massive shuddering sigh of relief as her sore, aching muscles instantly relaxed.
The lingering painful bruises on her arms completely faded away into nothingness.
It was simply too much enjoyment to process at once.
Especially when combined with the food.
At a table near the center of the hall, Talira was completely losing her mind.

chapters.title: Chapter 338: Addiction
paragraphs: The primordial dragon was sitting properly in her humanoid form, but she was eating like a completely starved feral beast.
She had actively piled literal mountains of roasted chicken onto her large wooden plate.
CHOMP!
"Hahahahaa!"
She tore through the roasted meat with terrifying draconic speed, completely ignoring the bones as she crushed them between her teeth.
Talira wiped a thick streak of hot grease from her chin and pointed a half-eaten chicken leg directly across the table.
Kaelia was sitting directly opposite her, wearing her pristine clean maid uniform, watching the dragon eat with wide eyes.
"You are a god," Talira mumbled aggressively through a massive mouthful of food.
Talira swallowed hard, thumping her chest.
"You completely outdid yourself, Kaelia," Talira praised the maid loudly. "This is the best chicken I have ever tasted in my entire long life."
Kaelia’s face instantly flushed a bright and incredibly adorable red.
The chef hid her face entirely behind her hands, giggling shyly at the highly aggressive compliment.
"Thank you, Talira," Kaelia whispered happily, her eyes shining with pride.
Meanwhile, over in the far dimly lit corner of the Mess Hall.
A massive loud crowd had formed tightly around a solitary round table.
"PUSH!" someone screamed wildly from the back.
"BREAK HER DAMN ARM!" another voice yelled aggressively.
Eluned and Morwenna were having a vicious competitive arm-wrestling match.
Both of the ancient SSS-Rank powerhouses were completely drunk on the highly concentrated Blessed Drinks.
Their elbows were planted firmly and aggressively on the groaning wooden table.

Their hands were locked tightly together in an iron grip as the terrifying physical pressure generated between them was actually warping the air around the table, causing the wood to crack and splinter under their elbows.
"You are getting weak in your old age, pirate!" Eluned sneered loudly, her melodic voice completely gone.
The Nature Goddess’s beautiful emerald eyes were slightly glazed over, and her usually pristine cheeks were flushed a deep intoxicated pink from the alcohol.
"Shut your mouth, you overgrown weed!" Morwenna roared back furiously, her hair flying wildly around her flushed face.
The Dread Queen gritted her teeth with the veins bulging in her neck as she desperately tried to push Eluned’s arm down to the wood.
They were hurling creative personal insults directly at each other.
"Your ship probably smells like rotten fish and bad decisions!" Eluned taunted viciously, pushing slightly harder and gaining an inch.
"Your precious mana-apples taste like dirt!" Morwenna shrieked in rage, refusing to yield a single millimeter, desperately holding the line.
Standing right next to the table, completely caught up in the hype of the match, was Elm.
The normally quiet highly reserved white-haired Hero was slamming her small fists excitedly on the wooden table, bouncing on the balls of her feet.
"Break her wrist, Eluned!" Elm cheered wildly, fully and entirely supporting her new best friend. "Slam it through the table!"
"Don’t encourage her, Elm!" Lupina yelled loudly from the other side of the crowd, pumping her fist and cheering aggressively for the pirate. "Come on, Morwenna! Snap the twig!"
Sitting entirely alone in a quiet elevated booth in the opposite corner of the room.
Evelyn watched the chaos unfolding before her.
She had a warm wooden cup of the glowing Blessed Drink resting comfortably in her hands.
She took a slow measured sip, feeling the incredible potent warmth completely soothe her exhausted nerves and heal her minor scrapes.
Evelyn looked at the stout dwarves singing rowdily on the tables, she looked at Talira happily eating her literal body weight in roasted chicken.
She looked at the elegant Eluned and the terrifying Morwenna screaming petty insults at each other like college freshmen over a drunken arm-wrestling match.
Evelyn let out a long but deeply amused sigh.
’Since when did everyone become a barbarian?’ Evelyn thought to herself.
Her disciplined militaristic mobile fortress had never, ever seen a party like this.
Her soldiers were usually too stressed about fuel, too tired from repairing treads, or too scared of the Zones to ever truly let loose.
But as she watched her oldest friend, Elm, laughing hysterically and cheering with the other Blessed Land girls without a single care in the world.
Evelyn couldn’t help but smile.
A genuine relaxed smile touched her lips as the heavy burden of leadership felt incredibly light in this room.
They were having fun... They were safe and they were alive. That was what actually mattered at the end of the day.
CREAAAK!
The heavy wooden bench across from her suddenly creaked under a new weight.
Silas sat down exactly opposite her in the quiet booth.
He was holding massive fresh tankards of the Blessed Drink. He slid one smoothly across the scratched wooden table toward her.𝓯𝓻𝒆𝙚𝒘𝓮𝙗𝓷𝒐𝓿𝙚𝒍.𝙘𝓸𝙢
Silas leaned back heavily against the booth, crossing his arms casually over his black tunic.
He looked at the relaxed smiling black-haired Lord.
"So," Silas said smoothly, his golden-ringed eyes locking onto hers. "When are we going back to Earth?"
Evelyn slowly ran a hand through her messy black hair as she stared across the scratched wooden table of the Mess Hall.
"When do you want to go back?" Evelyn asked.
Her voice was barely audible over the roaring deafening noise of the dwarven women singing on the tables.
She was completely confident that her people would be able to handle themselves.
Elm was here. Her secondary commanders were currently resting in their new luxury suites.
The Unmovable Wall was parked securely on the western ridge but it was clear that Silas was in a massive hurry.
He wanted to prepare his Vespera identity as soon as possible before the World Council auditors started sniffing around his territory’s digital footprint.
Silas leaned forward, resting his forearms on the sticky wood.
"Why not tomorrow?" Silas suggested pragmatically.
He took a slow measured sip from his wooden tankard.
"We can do it early in the afternoon or something," Silas continued. "I’m not exactly aware of what day tomorrow is back on Earth, though."
Evelyn interrupted him with a tired sigh.
"It’s Tuesday," Evelyn told him bluntly.
Silas nodded.
"Tuesday works," Evelyn confirmed, rubbing her tired eyes. "That’s completely fine. Jax will definitely be around... He never leaves his underground rig during the week."
"Perfect," Silas agreed.
He set his tankard down.
"Where should we meet up in Valoria City?" Silas asked.
Evelyn tilted her head left and right, stretching her stiff neck muscles.
She reached across her plate and picked up a massive piece of roasted chicken.
CHOMP!
She took a massive bite, chewing thoughtfully as she processed his question.
A sudden petty thought crossed her brilliant mind as Evelyn swallowed the chicken.
"I can just come over to your place," Evelyn suggested casually.
"Gah!"
Silas violently choked on the mouthful of Blessed Drink he had just chugged down.
He slammed his hand against his chest, coughing aggressively as the glowing liquid went down the wrong pipe.
"Excuse me?" Silas wheezed with his golden-ringed eyes watering slightly. Evelyn offered him a terrifying and perfectly sweet smile.
"Is that an issue?" Evelyn asked innocently.
She leaned forward, resting her chin on her hands.
"I mean, I think it’s only fair for all of the trouble you’ve caused me today," Evelyn pointed out smoothly. "You completely blew up my front lines so I owe you a visit."
She tapped her fingers against the table.
"Just give me your private network number," Evelyn demanded. "You can turn on your location tracker tomorrow afternoon, and I will come directly over to your house."
Silas stared at her.
He could instantly read exactly what she was doing.
Evelyn was incredibly intrigued about where he actually lived on Earth.
He had ruthlessly joked around with her age earlier, calling her a twenty-two-year-old fossil.
She was planning to joke around with his living conditions.
’She wants to see if I live in a dumpster...’ Silas realized internally.
If his Earth apartment was a dump, she was going to ruthlessly mock him for the rest of his life.
That was only fair in the unwritten rules of banter. Silas finally caught his breath, wiping his mouth with the back of his hand.
"Fine," Silas agreed to her conditions.
He reached across the table.
Evelyn handed him her advanced custom-built datapad.
TAP! TAP! TAP!
Silas quickly punched in his private contact number and slid the heavy device back across the wood.
Evelyn looked at the number and saved it.
"Thank you," Evelyn said with her smug grin widening.
She grabbed another piece of chicken from her plate.
"By the way, compliment your chef for me," Evelyn mumbled through a mouthful of meat. "This food is absolutely incredible."
Silas smirked.
"I will pass it along to Kaelia," Silas noted.
Evelyn swallowed hard, wiping her greasy fingers on a napkin.
She looked directly at him, her dark eyes sparkling with mockery.
"Oh, and one more thing," Evelyn added casually.
"What?" Silas asked, his eyes narrowing.
"Tomorrow, before we meet Jax, we are also going to have to go to the main Valoria City bank to do the seventy-five million credit transaction properly," Evelyn explained.
She offered a sympathetic fake pout.
"Since you are so young," Evelyn teased mercilessly. "I might have to sign as your legal adult guardian for the transfer."
Silas’s right eyebrow twitched violently.
"Fuck you," Silas stated bluntly.
Evelyn burst out laughing.
It was a loud genuine laugh that echoed over the noise of the singing dwarves.
She threw her head back, completely losing her aristocratic Lord Sky composure.
Still laughing, she grabbed her wooden tankard.
’Uh whatever... Let’s just get this drink down.
She took a massive swing of the highly concentrated Blessed Drink.
GLUG!
The exact second the raw magical alcohol hit her throat, her entire body physically locked up.
"Ack—"
Evelyn coughed violently, slamming the wooden cup back down onto the table.
Her pale face instantly flushed a vibrant burning red.
"Holy shit," Evelyn gasped, wiping her mouth. Her eyes were completely wide.
"This is good," Evelyn slurred, her words instantly blending together. "But it is really, really strong..."
Her core had been completely drained during the Lord War so she had zero internal mana reserves left to process the power of the magical alcohol.
"Uhh, Evelyn?" Silas noted, leaning forward.
’Ah fuck... I took the strong ones.’
Thora was distributing a weakened version and the stronger version, since he couldn’t take drunk, he had taken the stronger version and as a result, he handed one over to Evelyn.
Her dark eyes rolled completely into the back of her head.
THUD!
Evelyn slumped heavily forward with her face planting directly onto the scratched wooden table.
She instantly lost consciousness as soft exhausted snores began to escape her lips.
Silas stared at the unconscious Lord of The Unmovable Wall lying face-down next to a pile of chicken bones.
"Lightweight," Silas muttered.
The world was completely blurry.
When Evelyn finally began to wake up, she felt like she was floating.
The roaring deafening noise of the Mess Hall was gone.
It was completely replaced by the soft sound of heavy boots crunching against paved stone.
She was currently being carried and Evelyn blinked her heavy eyelids while looking up.
Silas was holding her effortlessly in his arms, carrying her princess-style.
His broad muscular chest radiated an incredible comforting amount of physical heat against the freezing night air.
He wasn’t breathing hard as to a Lord of his level, Evelyn’s petite frame weighed nothing.
"Is this the room?" Silas’s deep voice echoed above her.
"Yes, it is."
Evelyn slowly turned her blurry head.
Elm was walking right beside them, her white hair glowing in the moonlight.
CLICK!
The sound of a heavy iron key turning in a lock echoed clearly as the thick wooden door to the luxury suite opened.
Silas carried Evelyn directly into the dark, quiet room.
"Finally... she’s a bit light though, does she even eat?"
’Fuu... fucker.’
He walked over to the massive plush king-sized bed as he gently let her down onto the thick down mattress.
FWUMP!
Evelyn collapsed into the soft pillows with her limbs feeling like dead lead.
She couldn’t move her arms as her head was spinning aggressively from the magical alcohol.
Silas stood up straight, rolling his shoulders to release the slight tension.
He let out a soft tired sigh then he turned around, looking at the white-haired Hero standing near the doorway.
"Goodnight, Elm," Silas said quietly, not wanting to wake the other resting soldiers in the complex.
"Goodnight, Lord Silas," Elm replied respectfully, bowing her head. "Thank you for carrying her."
Silas nodded.
He turned toward the door, completely ready to leave and finally get some sleep himself.
However, as he was just about to take a step...
A trembling hand forcefully clutched the fabric of his black tunic.
Silas stopped as he looked down and Evelyn had rolled over on the bed.
Her dark blurry eyes were entirely half-open, staring up at him in the dim light of the room as her fingers were gripping his shirt with desperate pathetic strength.
"My... cigarettes..." Evelyn slurred with her voice shaking violently.
She tried to pull herself up, her free hand patting the empty pockets of her oversized gray hoodie.
"Where are they...?" Evelyn breathed out, her chest heaving. "I need one."

He had ruthlessly joked around with her age earlier, calling her a twenty-two-year-old fossil.
She was planning to joke around with his living conditions.
’She wants to see if I live in a dumpster...’ Silas realized internally.
If his Earth apartment was a dump, she was going to ruthlessly mock him for the rest of his life.
That was only fair in the unwritten rules of banter.
Silas finally caught his breath, wiping his mouth with the back of his hand.
"Fine," Silas agreed to her conditions.
He reached across the table.
Evelyn handed him her advanced custom-built datapad.
TAP!
TAP!
TAP!
Silas quickly punched in his private contact number and slid the heavy device back across the wood.
Evelyn looked at the number and saved it.
"Thank you," Evelyn said with her smug grin widening.
She grabbed another piece of chicken from her plate.
"By the way, compliment your chef for me," Evelyn mumbled through a mouthful of meat.
"This food is absolutely incredible."
Silas smirked.
"I will pass it along to Kaelia," Silas noted.
Evelyn swallowed hard, wiping her greasy fingers on a napkin.
She looked directly at him, her dark eyes sparkling with mockery.
"Oh, and one more thing," Evelyn added casually.
"What?" Silas asked, his eyes narrowing.
"Tomorrow, before we meet Jax, we are also going to have to go to the main Valoria City bank to do the seventy-five million credit transaction properly," Evelyn explained.
She offered a sympathetic fake pout.
"Since you are so young," Evelyn teased mercilessly.
"I might have to sign as your legal adult guardian for the transfer."
Silas’s right eyebrow twitched violently.
"Fuck you," Silas stated bluntly.
Evelyn burst out laughing.
It was a loud genuine laugh that echoed over the noise of the singing dwarves.
She threw her head back, completely losing her aristocratic Lord Sky composure.
Still laughing, she grabbed her wooden tankard.
’Uh whatever...
Let’s just get this drink down.
She took a massive swing of the highly concentrated Blessed Drink.
GLUG!
The exact second the raw magical alcohol hit her throat, her entire body physically locked up.
"Ack—"
Evelyn coughed violently, slamming the wooden cup back down onto the table.
Her pale face instantly flushed a vibrant burning red.
"Holy shit," Evelyn gasped, wiping her mouth.
Her eyes were completely wide.
"This is good," Evelyn slurred, her words instantly blending together.
"But it is really, really strong..."
Her core had been completely drained during the Lord War so she had zero internal mana reserves left to process the power of the magical alcohol.
"Uhh, Evelyn?" Silas noted, leaning forward.
’Ah fuck...
I took the strong ones.’
Thora was distributing a weakened version and the stronger version, since he couldn’t take drunk, he had taken the stronger version and as a result, he handed one over to Evelyn.
Her dark eyes rolled completely into the back of her head.
THUD!
Evelyn slumped heavily forward with her face planting directly onto the scratched wooden table.
She instantly lost consciousness as soft exhausted snores began to escape her lips.
Silas stared at the unconscious Lord of The Unmovable Wall lying face-down next to a pile of chicken bones.
"Lightweight," Silas muttered.
The world was completely blurry.
When Evelyn finally began to wake up, she felt like she was floating.
The roaring deafening noise of the Mess Hall was gone.
It was completely replaced by the soft sound of heavy boots crunching against paved stone.
She was currently being carried and Evelyn blinked her heavy eyelids while looking up.
Silas was holding her effortlessly in his arms, carrying her princess-style.
His broad muscular chest radiated an incredible comforting amount of physical heat against the freezing night air.
He wasn’t breathing hard as to a Lord of his level, Evelyn’s petite frame weighed nothing.
"Is this the room?" Silas’s deep voice echoed above her.
"Yes, it is."
Evelyn slowly turned her blurry head.
Elm was walking right beside them, her white hair glowing in the moonlight.
CLICK!
The sound of a heavy iron key turning in a lock echoed clearly as the thick wooden door to the luxury suite opened.
Silas carried Evelyn directly into the dark, quiet room.
"Finally... she’s a bit light though, does she even eat?"
’Fuu... fucker.’
He walked over to the massive plush king-sized bed as he gently let her down onto the thick down mattress.
FWUMP!
Evelyn collapsed into the soft pillows with her limbs feeling like dead lead.
She couldn’t move her arms as her head was spinning aggressively from the magical alcohol.
Silas stood up straight, rolling his shoulders to release the slight tension.
He let out a soft tired sigh then he turned around, looking at the white-haired Hero standing near the doorway.
"Goodnight, Elm," Silas said quietly, not wanting to wake the other resting soldiers in the complex.
"Goodnight, Lord Silas," Elm replied respectfully, bowing her head.
"Thank you for carrying her."
Silas nodded.
He turned toward the door, completely ready to leave and finally get some sleep himself.
However, as he was just about to take a step...
A trembling hand forcefully clutched the fabric of his black tunic.
Silas stopped as he looked down and Evelyn had rolled over on the bed.
Her dark blurry eyes were entirely half-open, staring up at him in the dim light of the room as her fingers were gripping his shirt with desperate pathetic strength.
"My... cigarettes..." Evelyn slurred with her voice shaking violently.
She tried to pull herself up, her free hand patting the empty pockets of her oversized gray hoodie.
"Where are they...?" Evelyn breathed out, her chest heaving.
"I need one."

chapters.title: Chapter 339: Return To Earth
paragraphs: Silas looked down at her trembling form.
Her nicotine withdrawal, combined with the extreme mana exhaustion and the magical alcohol was sending her nervous system into complete shock.
She looked pathetic.
Silas reached down and firmly grabbed her wrist.
He gently pried her trembling fingers off his black tunic.
"Smoking isn’t good for you, Evelyn," Silas told her bluntly with his golden eyes completely cold as he placed her hand back down onto the mattress.
"It will do more harm than good," Silas stated pragmatically. "Especially in your current physical state. You need sleep, not poison."
Evelyn glared at him.
"Bullshit," Evelyn hissed aggressively, trying to sit up again.
Her teeth were chattering.

"You don’t understand," Evelyn gasped out, her eyes entirely frantic. "I need it. It slows my brain down. I can’t stop thinking about the bodies. I can’t stop thinking about the blood... Give me my damn lighter, Silas."
She reached for him again.
POK!
A slender pale hand suddenly reached out from the darkness.
Elm brought two fingers down and sharply tapped Evelyn directly on the forehead.
A microscopic burst of concentrated sleep magic surged directly into Evelyn’s brain and Evelyn’s eyes instantly rolled back.
She slumped heavily back onto the pillows, falling into a deep dreamless induced sleep as the suite fell completely silent.
Silas stood next to the bed, looking at the unconscious girl while Elm stood on the other side of the mattress.
The white-haired Hero stared down at her Lord, her silver eyes filled with heartbreaking guilt.
"It is mostly my fault," Elm whispered softly to the quiet room. Silas looked up at her as Elm reached down, gently pulling the heavy woolen blanket up over Evelyn’s shivering shoulders.
"When we first started out our journey which was in an Unknown Zone," Elm explained with her voice cracking slightly. "We were constantly under attack. We never slept as the stress was killing her."
Elm gently brushed a strand of black hair out of Evelyn’s face.

"She started smoking just to stay awake on the night watches," Elm confessed bitterly. "If I had just stopped her during our earlier days... if I had been stronger and taken the night shifts myself... this whole thing wouldn’t be happening. I let her ruin her own body to protect me."
Silas listened to the Hero’s confession.
He looked at Elm’s guilty tear-filled silver eyes but he didn’t offer her empty platitudes.
"She is the Lord, Elm," Silas stated firmly, his deep voice anchoring the room. "She made her own choices to protect her people so you cannot bear the weight of her decisions."
Elm looked up at him, wiping a tear from her cheek.
"You did your job today," Silas assured her cleanly. "You gave everything you had. Now, let her rest."
Silas turned around and walked to the heavy oak door.
"Take care of your Lord, Elm," Silas ordered quietly.
"I will," Elm promised fiercely.
Silas stepped out of the room.
CLICK!
He closed the heavy wooden door firmly behind him.
Silas walked out of the residential complex as he stepped directly into the freezing biting evening wind of the Umbral Basin.
He shoved his hands deep into the pockets of his dark trousers, walking slowly down the paved stone pathway toward the Keep.
The territory was entirely silent as the massive Lord War was truly over.
Silas looked up at the dark, starry sky above the Blessed Land.
He didn’t hate Evelyn...
On the contrary, he actually liked her pretty well.
She was a brilliant tactician, a fiercely loyal Lord and she didn’t put up with any of the arrogant high-society bullshit that plagued successful people.
But all of that desperate pathetic talk about smoking in the bedroom... It left a bitter disgusting taste in his mouth.
It reminded him entirely of everything he had left behind.
It reminded him of all the bleak depressing reality he had endured before he had reincarnated into the body of Silas Graves.
’Even while I was in the slums...’
Earth was a decaying world.
’There was nothing good waiting at the front of it all.’ Silas thought with his boots crunching on the stone path.
He remembered the hospital rooms.
He remembered the smell of the sterile bleach and the endless beeping monitors.
He remembered watching people completely destroy their own bodies with terrible habits, desperately chasing a temporary high to escape the grinding misery of modern life.
It didn’t really matter if this world’s Earth had a vastly greater amount of medical power.
It didn’t matter if they had potions, healing magic, and Lord Cores.
’It is all the exact same thing at the end of the day,’ Silas thought.
Death always collected its debts.
If you constantly poisoned your own core, if you constantly relied on a crutch to escape reality, you would eventually break.
Evelyn was strong but she was actively killing herself to manage her stress.
Silas exhaled a long breath into the freezing air.
’None of my business though...’
He reached the towering massive oak doors of the Keep as he pushed the heavy iron handles open and stepped inside the grand foyer.
He closed the doors firmly behind him.
THUD!
The Keep was completely silent as the roaring hearth fires had burned down to glowing red embers.
Silas looked around the empty shadowy halls.𝘧𝓇𝑒𝑒𝑤ℯ𝑏𝓃𝘰𝑣ℯ𝘭.𝘤ℴ𝘮
’Right...’ Silas remembered internally.
He had ordered Aeliana, Rowenna, and Kadi to stay down in the massive stone barracks for the night.
They were down there explicitly to watch over the seventy-two new Unmovable Wall recruits, just in case any of the prisoners decided to get bold and start a riot in the dark.
Not that it actually mattered.
Brida and Gunnhild were down there too. If a riot started, the Titan Bastion would literally throw the perpetrators through a stone wall.
Silas walked slowly up the grand, curving marble staircase.
He reached the second-floor landing and walked down the plush carpeted hallway toward his bedroom.
As he turned the final corner, he stopped.
Standing perfectly still outside his heavy wooden bedroom door was Eluned.
The Nature Goddess looked absolutely breathtaking in the dim candlelight of the hallway.
She was still wearing her elegant green sundress, the fabric clinging perfectly to her stunning hourglass curves as her flowing silver-green hair spilled flawlessly over her shoulders.
She no longer had that aggressive flushed drunk look on her cheeks from the Mess Hall arm-wrestling match.
The Blessed Drinks processed quickly through SSS-Rank cores so she was completely sober.
And she looked at him with an expression of overwhelming devotion.
"Welcome back, My Lord," Eluned greeted him softly.
Her melodic voice sent an instant electric shiver directly down Silas’s spine.
"Elu..." Silas breathed out, stepping closer to her.
Eluned didn’t wait for him to finish as she stepped forward and wrapped her soft, slender arms entirely around his muscular neck.
She hugged him tightly, pressing her warm body flawlessly against his chest.
"Congratulations on winning the war," Eluned whispered sincerely into his ear. "You were magnificent today."
Silas wrapped his arms around her waist, pulling her flush against him.
He buried his face in her hair, breathing in the intoxicating addictive scent of fresh rain and blooming flowers.
Eluned slowly pulled her head back just an inch.
She leaned her soft warm lips directly against the shell of his ear.
"Would you like your favorite food tonight...?" Eluned whispered, her voice dropping into a dangerous seductive tone.
She gently bit his earlobe.
"...Which is me?"
Silas completely froze.
His composure shattered into a million pieces.
Just hearing her whisper those words in that specific sultry tone made him instantly hard against the fabric of his trousers.
The overwhelming pent-up adrenaline from the battlefield, the stress of the negotiations, and the intense physical proximity entirely overrode his brain.
Silas didn’t say a single word.
He grabbed the heavy brass handle of his bedroom door and he pushed it violently open.
BANG!
Silas and Eluned completely stumbled through the doorway with their mouths entirely locked together in a desperate ferocious kiss.
Silas kicked the heavy wooden door firmly shut behind them.
CLICK!
They didn’t even make it three steps into the room before the clothes started flying.
Silas aggressively gripped the delicate fabric of her green sundress, pulling it smoothly over her head and tossing it carelessly onto the floor.
Eluned frantically unbuttoned his black tunic with her soft hands desperately mapping the hard muscles of his chest and abdomen and in mere moments, they fell onto the massive, plush mattress.
FWUMP!
The entire massive wooden bed frame violently groaned under the sudden, intense physical impact.
"Silas~ Go hard~" Eluned moaned softly against his lips, her emerald eyes glowing with raw lust.
Silas pinned her wrists gently but firmly to the pillows, positioning himself perfectly between her soft thighs.
He didn’t hold back as he drove forward.
"Ahhn~!"
Eluned let out a loud high-pitched gasp as he fully entered her with her back arching entirely off the mattress.
Soon, the only sound echoing in the massive dimly lit master bedroom was the loud moaning of the Nature Goddess as Silas thrusted relentlessly into her.
The bed frame violently slammed against the far wall with every single powerful movement.
THUD! PAH! THUD!
It was a primal unrestrained celebration of victory.
’I see...’
However, inside the massive pitch-black walk-in wardrobe of the master bedroom.
Morwenna was completely trapped.
The pirate was sitting heavily on the dark wooden floor of the closet, surrounded entirely by Silas’s clean tunics and heavy leather coats.
She had sneaked into his room earlier in the evening...
She had meticulously planned to ambush him, fully intending to use the seductive lessons she had supposedly learned to completely force her way into his bed.
But Eluned had arrived first and now, Morwenna was stuck.
’How did she manage to do it?’
She didn’t dare use her magic to escape.
The mana of teleporting out of the room would instantly alert Eluned’s SSS-Rank senses, and she would never live down the humiliation of being caught hiding in the closet like a creepy voyeur.
So, Morwenna sat in the dark and she listened.
She had enhanced S-Rank hearing after all and she couldn’t turn it off unless she purposely made herself deaf so...
She heard absolutely everything.
PAH! PAH! PAH!
She heard the wet slippery sound of their bodies slapping together.
"Elu~ You’re tighter than usual~"
She heard Silas’s deep breathless grunts.
She heard Eluned... her elegant and perfectly composed Goddess friend screaming and moaning like a feral beast.
"Yes... harder... Silas, please~" Eluned’s voice echoed clearly through the wooden slats of the closet door. "Cum in meeee~"
Morwenna let out a silent terrified gulp.
Her stormy gray eyes were wide as saucers in the darkness.

The terrifying force of each of Silas’s thrusts literally vibrated through the floorboards and the physical shockwaves hit Morwenna exactly where she was sitting as the pirate captain’s breathing grew incredibly shallow.
"Haah~"
Her heart hammered violently against her ribs.
A completely foreign overwhelming heat began to spread rapidly through her lower abdomen.
The spot between her legs suddenly became incredibly wet.
’It’s wetter than usual... am I turned on from getting my opportunity stolen?’
Morwenna’s hand trembled violently as she slowly reached down and she touched the damp fabric of her dark trousers.
She had never ever experienced this before.
’Is this...’ Morwenna thought frantically with her face burning hotter than a furnace in the pitch-black closet as she leaned through the cracks to see.
’Is this... sex?!’
On that day, Morwenna realized she had a kink...
She had a kink for being cucked.
[The next Afternoon]
FLASH!
Silas materialized silently in the center of his Earth apartment.
The transition from the Sovereign Realm back to his building in Silverleaf was entirely seamless, devoid of any violent flashing lights or portal noise.
He stood in the middle of his quiet moderately furnished living room.
"Elu really drained me..." Silas muttered aloud to the empty room.
His legs were genuinely trembling.
The Nature Goddess had zero limits once she got going.
Her SSS-Rank Vitality meant she never got tired, while his newly advanced Gold Core was forced to work overtime just to keep up with her demands.
He had barely slept two hours but so far, the transition was good.
Evelyn had left the Sovereign Realm an hour before him, heading back to her own location on Earth to prep for their afternoon meeting.
Silas walked slowly toward the couch, running a calloused hand through his messy dark hair.
He grabbed the hem of his black shirt.
SWISH!
He pulled the shirt smoothly over his head, tossing it casually over the back of the living room sofa.
It was a comfortable habit that he had recently developed.
’It’s my house,’ Silas reasoned pragmatically. ’Why the hell should I be covering myself up?’
He walked over to the small coffee table as he picked up his sleek Earth smartphone.
The screen instantly lit up, flooded entirely with notifications.
He checked his messages.
Two completely unknown numbers had been aggressively messaging him since yesterday.
’I cannot deal with this shit right now,’ Silas thought, dismissing the notifications completely without looking at them.
He had seventy-five million credits to launder and a fake identity to build today.
DING!
Another text message popped up on the top of the screen.
This one was from the number he had manually entered into Evelyn’s datapad back in the Mess Hall.
He quickly saved the contact.
[Evelyn]: Turn on your location.

He pulled the shirt smoothly over his head, tossing it casually over the back of the living room sofa.
It was a comfortable habit that he had recently developed.
’It’s my house,’ Silas reasoned pragmatically. ’Why the hell should I be covering myself up?’
He walked over to the small coffee table as he picked up his sleek Earth smartphone.
The screen instantly lit up, flooded entirely with notifications.
He checked his messages.
Two completely unknown numbers had been aggressively messaging him since yesterday.
’I cannot deal with this shit right now,’ Silas thought, dismissing the notifications completely without looking at them.
He had seventy-five million credits to launder and a fake identity to build today.
DING!
Another text message popped up on the top of the screen.
This one was from the number he had manually entered into Evelyn’s datapad back in the Mess Hall.
He quickly saved the contact.
[Evelyn]: Turn on your location.

chapters.title: Chapter 340: Return To Earth [II]
paragraphs: Silas smirked with the banter instantly kicking in. He couldn’t help himself... It wasn’t his fault that Evelyn was so easy to bully after all.
He tapped the screen.
[Silas]: Sure Ma’am.
[Evelyn]: 🖕
He toggled the GPS location sharing feature on his phone, pinging his exact coordinates in Silverleaf directly to her device.
Silas then put the phone in his pocket as he sighed while rolling his stiff shoulders.
’I’m quite tired...’
His throat was completely dry from the intense activities of the previous night and sure Aeli had made him the usual juice but it was time for some proper water.
He turned around and walked slowly downstairs toward the main kitchen to pour himself a cold cup of water from the sink.
As he reached the bottom of the wooden stairs, he paused.
He sniffed the air.
The house sure did smell strange today.
There was a pleasant aroma of cooking oil, soy sauce, and fresh vegetables drifting through the hallway.

’Is Martha around?’ Silas pondered internally, thinking of the older woman who managed the building. She was his servant after all, so that was a stupid question. ’Of course she’s around but still... what are they doing?’
He walked completely barefoot into the kitchen and as he stepped onto the tiled floor.
Suddenly, a small figure completely ran around the corner of the kitchen island, carrying a basket of fresh groceries.
They literally ran right into his bare chest.
Silas didn’t even flinch with his body absorbing the microscopic impact but as he looked down, he realized that it wasn’t Martha.
It was a young girl who looked to be exactly around his little sister Lia’s age.
She was incredibly cute, with soft round cheeks and a petite frame.
’Hm... She seems very familiar but why is she at my place? One of my distant relatives? No I’m not sure if she’s on the registry.
She looked very Asian, with long beautiful black hair that fell perfectly down her back.
But her most striking feature was her eyes.
She had bright vivid purple eyes that widened into massive saucers as she stared directly at him.
Kaede looked up.
She saw a towering muscular man standing shirtless in the middle of the kitchen.
Kaede blinked twice as she dropped the grocery basket onto the floor.
"Eeeeeeeek!" Kaede screamed at the top of her lungs, covering her bright red face with her hands.
Silas stood perfectly still, closing his eyes as the high-pitched scream echoed painfully through his skull.
’Fuck...’ Silas thought tiredly.
The piercing high-pitched scream echoed off the pristine ceramic tiles of the kitchen, shattering the peaceful silence of the Silverleaf apartment.
’Does she not stop screaming?’
Silas now stood perfectly still in front of his own kitchen island, holding an empty glass in his hand.
His brain, exhausted from a brutal Lord War, diplomatic negotiations, and a grueling intense night with an SSS-Rank Nature Goddess, practically flatlined.
He stared down at the terrified ten-year-old girl with long black hair and bright purple eyes who had just dropped a basket of fresh groceries all over the floor.

’Who am I?’ Silas complained bitterly in his own thoughts, letting out a long heavy exhale as he pinched the bridge of his nose. ’I am the Lord of the Blessed Land and the owner of this damn place so why am I currently standing barefoot in my own kitchen, getting screamed at like a B-list horror movie villain?’
The volume of Kaede’s scream instantly alerted the rest of the household as rapid panicked footsteps thundered down the wooden staircase and across the living room hardwood.
"What happened?! Who’s hurt?!" Martha yelled, bursting around the kitchen corner with terrifying motherly speed.
The dedicated housekeeper was actively brandishing a heavy steel frying pan like a lethal blunt-force weapon with her eyes darting frantically around the room looking for an intruder.
Lia sprinted into the kitchen right behind her, completely out of breath. Her dark pigtails bounced wildly as she scanned the area, fully expecting a rogue monster or an assassin.
Penelope brought up the rear, the haughty violet-eyed noble girl skidding to a halt on the tiles, looking very alarmed.
They all froze, staring at the shirtless young man standing near the sink.
"Big Brother!" Lia gasped, her dark eyes instantly lighting up with joy.
Before Silas could even put his glass down, his eleven-year-old sister launched herself across the kitchen.
She collided with his abdomen, wrapping her arms tightly around his waist in a massive crushing hug.
Silas let out a soft grunt as the air was forced from his lungs, but a genuine warm smile immediately broke through his exhausted exterior.
"I’m back, squirt," Silas chuckled softly, resting his large calloused hand on top of Lia’s head and gently ruffling her dark hair.
All of the cold tension from the Sovereign Realm completely melted away the exact second he held his little sister.
Martha immediately lowered her heavy steel frying pan, letting out a massive shuddering sigh of relief.
The older woman placed a hand over her racing heart, offering him a warm affectionate smile.
"Welcome home, Master Silas," Martha greeted him, her eyes shining with quiet happiness. "We were all so incredibly worried about you... You’ve been gone for over a week."
Over near the dropped grocery basket, Kaede was still cowering slightly with her hands covering her blushing cheeks.
She peered through the gaps in her fingers at the towering intimidating guy who looked like a literal statue.
Penelope let out an exasperated sigh.
The purple-haired noble girl reached out and gently patted Kaede on the shoulder, shaking her head.
"Calm down, Kaede, and stop screaming," Penelope instructed with a dry matter-of-fact tone. "You aren’t being kidnapped. Look at him. That is obviously Lia’s big brother."
Kaede slowly lowered her hands, blinking her bright purple eyes in rapid succession.
She looked at Lia hugging his waist, and then she looked back up at Silas’s face.
Lia finally pulled back from the hug, looking up at him with a beaming radiant smile.
She quickly turned around, gesturing proudly toward her two friends.

"Big Brother, these are my best friends from Valoria Academy!" Lia introduced them excitedly, her voice bubbling with pure enthusiasm. "This is Kaede, and this is Penelope! They’ve been coming over to hang out and study with me while you were away in the Sovereign Realm."
Silas looked over at the two young girls.
He took in Penelope’s sharp posture and Kaede’s slightly embarrassed fidgeting demeanor.
His instincts instantly recognized the high-tier magical fabrics of their academy uniforms and the subtle expensive jewelry they wore, but he didn’t care about their backgrounds.
’Well I already know Penelope but not Kaede... she seems familiar like I’ve seen her online or something.’
He only cared that they were treating his little sister well.
"It’s very nice to finally meet you both," Silas said smoothly "I am Silas Graves."
Kaede completely flushed a bright vibrant red, hurriedly offering a quick, incredibly polite bow.
Penelope offered a composed elegant curtsy, thoroughly impressed by the imposing presence of Lia’s guardian. She didn’t get to analyze him properly the last time they met after all.

"Thank you both for coming over and keeping Lia company," Silas continued, offering them a genuine appreciative smile. "I know my sister can be a bit of a nerd sometimes, so I appreciate you being such good friends to her."
"Hey!" Lia protested loudly, puffing out her cheeks in sheer indignation.
Silas chuckled, reaching out and affectionately pinching Lia’s soft cheek. He stretched the skin playfully, ignoring her annoyed swatting.
"I just hope my sudden appearance isn’t disturbing your study session," Silas added politely, looking between the girls. "I didn’t expect to walk into a full house."
"Oh, n-not at all, Mr. Graves!" Kaede stammered quickly, waving her hands in front of her chest. "We were just getting snacks for our project! You aren’t disturbing us!"

"You really don’t have to call me ’Mr. Graves’," Silas bantered easily, releasing Lia’s cheek and leaning back against the kitchen counter. "It makes me sound like an eighty-year-old guild master... Silas is completely fine."
Penelope and Kaede both relaxed instantly with a small comfortable smile forming on their faces as they watched the siblings interact.
The intimidating terrifying aura Silas had radiated just a minute ago was entirely gone.
Seeing him joke around and casually tease his little sister proved that they truly were a tight-knit family.
Lia, however, suddenly crossed her arms over her chest. She looked Silas up and down, her dark eyes narrowing with strict critical disapproval.

"You should have some shame, Big Brother," Lia scolded him, tapping her foot against the tiles. "You can’t just walk around the house while you’re entirely shirtless! We have guests over! Put some clothes on!"
Silas blinked, looking down at his own bare muscled torso. He let out a long sigh.

"It is literally my house, Lia," Silas defended his rights. "I pay the rent, I pay the utility bills, and I just got back. If I want to walk to my own kitchen sink without a shirt on, I have earned that right... If you want me to wear a shirt, get your own house."
Martha stepped forward, completely ignoring his flawless logic.
The middle-aged maid had fully shifted into her unstoppable authoritative mother-hen mode.

"None of that matters right now," Martha declared smoothly, placing her hands on her hips. "You look exhausted, and you definitely haven’t eaten a proper home-cooked meal in days. I suggest you go sit with the girls in the main dining room right now, and I will serve you some hot food."
The older woman seemed incredibly, visibly excited about the prospect of finally serving her Master again.
"I appreciate it, Martha, but I can’t stay long," Silas started to argue, raising a hand. "I am actually preparing to meet up with someone important in the city later this afternoon, and—"
Martha didn’t listen to a single word he just said.
She walked directly behind the towering eighteen-year-old Lord, placing her hands firmly on his broad bare back.
With surprising physical strength, she began actively shoving him out of the kitchen and toward the hallway.

"You have been gone for far too long, Master Silas!" Martha scolded him affectionately, completely shutting down his protests. "You are going to E-A-T... That is exactly what you pay me a generous salary for! I am your maid, and you are going to eat my cooking!"
Silas let out a deep defeated sigh.
He had the physical stats to rip a steel vault door off its hinges with his bare hands but against Martha’s stubborn authority, he was completely and utterly powerless.
"Alright, alright, I surrender," Silas agreed tiredly, letting himself be pushed.
Lia, Kaede, and Penelope instantly giggled at the Lord’s defeat.
The three girls quickly ran up and grabbed his arms, happily pulling Silas along the hallway and dragging him directly into the main dining room.
As Silas allowed himself to be dragged into the spacious room, he immediately noticed a massive advanced holographic projection floating directly above his oak dining table.
Silas paused, narrowing his eyes as he looked at the glowing blue data streams, complex geometric graphs, and massive blocks of text hovering in the air.𝗳𝚛𝗲𝕖𝚠𝚎𝚋𝗻𝗼𝕧𝗲𝐥.𝚌𝚘𝐦
The level of detail on the projection was staggering, detailing supply chain metrics, topographical layouts, and infrastructure designs.
"What exactly is this?" Silas asked, pulling out a wooden chair and taking a seat at the head of the table.
The three girls scrambled to take their seats around the projection.
Lia pulled her heavy leather notebook toward her chest, looking up at him with bright eager eyes.

"It’s our mandatory group project for Valoria Academy," Lia explained proudly, gesturing to the floating text. "We have to write a comprehensive detailed thesis on Territory Logistics. We’re trying to figure out the best way to handle supply lines and infrastructure for a developing zone."
Kaede, who had been sitting quietly and acting pretty shy up until this point, leaned forward slightly.
Her bright purple eyes were filled with genuine, burning curiosity as she looked at the muscular man sitting across from her.

"Lia told us that you went into the Sovereign Realm to build a territory," Kaede asked softly, fidgeting with her pen. "Are you a Lord, Silas? Could you tell us how you handle your own territory? The textbooks are so boring, and we really want a high grade."
Lia vigorously nodded her head, supporting her friend’s point. She looked at her Brother with massive pleading puppy-dog eyes.
"Please, Big Brother?" Lia begged sweetly. "Just a few tips? Your real-world experience is way better than anything the Professor could ever teach us!"
Silas looked at the three young girls staring at him with such intense desperation.
He let out a long slow sigh, aggressively running a hand through his messy dark hair.
He was tired, but he couldn’t bring himself to say no to his sister.

"Fine," Silas relented, leaning back in his chair and crossing his arms over his bare chest. "I will only help a little bit. I am not doing your homework for you. Lay whatever specific questions you have directly on me."

chapters.title: Chapter 341: Harper’s Appearance
paragraphs: The three girls instantly smiled, their faces lighting up with academic triumph.
Penelope immediately took charge of the interface.
The purple-haired noble girl reached out, smoothly dragging the glowing blue hologram directly to her side of the table.
She tapped a specific section regarding resource management and looked at Silas with an analytical business-oriented gaze.

"Alright, let’s start with raw resource acquisition," Penelope pitched her question like a seasoned corporate auditor. "If you discover a massive valuable area filled with raw ores near your territory’s borders, how much of a percentage cut do you typically have to give the Central City Guilds in order to legally employ their help with the excavation and registration process?"
Silas blinked.
He sat perfectly still in his wooden chair.
His brain completely short-circuited as he processed the unbelievable absurdity of the question.
’Uh...’ Silas thought, his golden-ringed eyes staring blankly at the haughty noble girl. ’We give our private mines to Central City? What the fuck now?’
It had been quite a while since he had personally sat through the basic Lord theory classes back at the academy before his awakening.
But even still, did these textbooks actually expect him to hand over his incredibly valuable resources?
Did they really expect him to casually sign away the mythril and obsidian veins located deep inside the Umbral Basin just to pay some arrogant, bureaucratic guild for ’registration’?
’I would literally rather die,’ Silas realized internally. ’I would rather burn Central City to the ground with dragon fire than give them a single ounce of my territory’s material.’
Silas remained completely silent for a few seconds too long, his face locked in an expression of deadpan disbelief.
Lia noticed his blank stare and instantly puffed out her cheeks.
"You’re a dummy, Big Brother!" Lia called him out playfully, tossing a crumbled-up piece of paper at his chest. "You don’t even know the standard tax brackets for your own mines!"
Kaede, however, was observant. She noticed the specific glint in Silas’s eyes and immediately raised her hand.
"Wait, no, it’s not that he doesn’t know," Kaede corrected Lia, her purple eyes widening with sudden realization.
She looked directly at Silas, leaning eagerly across the table. "Silas... is your territory stationed deep inside an Unknown Zone?"
Silas slowly nodded, his deadpan expression fading into a dangerous smirk.
"It is," Silas confirmed cleanly. "I am stationed off the grid."
The three girls instantly went completely quiet as the silence in the dining room was deafening.
They stared at him with awe.
Operating a territory in the Known Zones near Central City was basically like running a corporate franchise... you paid taxes, you followed rules, and you hired guilds.
But operating a territory in the savage, blood-soaked Unknown Zones meant you were an undisputed king answering to no one but the monsters at your gates.
"Oh my god..." Kaede whispered, breaking the silence.
She looked at Penelope and Lia, her voice trembling with excitement.
"Unknown Zone territories aren’t legally bound to pay any sort of tax or percentage cuts for whatever raw resources they find! They have total sovereignty over them!"
The exact second the realization hit them, chaos erupted.
The three girls practically abandoned their chairs.
They swarmed the head of the table, entirely surrounding Silas with glittering obsessive eyes.
They started aggressively peppering him with a barrage of complex rapid-fire logistical questions.
"How do you handle local monster migrations without Central City wards?!" Penelope demanded with her pen flying across her notebook.
"What is your caloric burn rate for a Vanguard unit?!" Lia asked frantically, tapping her datapad.
"Do you build luxury baths for your troops to maintain their psychological morale?!" Kaede yelled over the others, prioritizing the aesthetic aesthetics of warfare.

"Hold on, slow down!" Silas coughed loudly, raising his hands defensively as he tried to handle the overwhelming multi-directional assault of middle-school academia. "One question at a time! And yes, Kaede, I literally just built four massive residential complexes with heated clawfoot soaking tubs for my people."
"I KNEW IT!" Kaede cheered victoriously, pointing a triumphant finger at Penelope. "I told you luxury plumbing was a critical survival metric!"
Before Penelope could argue against the viability of bathtubs, the kitchen doors swung completely open.
"Alright, girls, calm down and give him some room to breathe," Martha announced warmly while cutting through the chaos.
The housekeeper marched into the dining room carrying a massive, incredibly wide silver serving tray.
The sheer volume of food she was balancing was staggering.
She gracefully lowered the heavy tray onto the center of the oak table, completely pushing the holographic projector to the side.
Martha began rapidly displaying the meals upon the table, talking passionately about every single dish she had prepared for him.

"I have a seasoned medium-rare basilisk steak with garlic butter," Martha listed off, setting down a sizzling cast-iron skillet that smelled like heaven. "I also made a rich hearty root vegetable stew for your stamina, an entire platter of spicy roasted noodles, and freshly baked garlic bread."
Silas stared at the massive mountain of perfectly cooked food. It was enough to feed an entire squad of heavy infantrymen.
"Martha," Silas said, blinking in genuine surprise. "Isn’t this way too much for one person?"
The woman completely ignored his protest.
She reached back onto the tray and immediately dropped a massive decadent chocolate lava cake covered in powdered sugar directly next to his steak.
Martha’s face instantly flushed a bright vibrant shade of crimson.

paragraphs: "No," Harper refused instantly, leaning in even closer until her face was mere inches from his.
She offered him a seductive and incredibly demanding smile. "Are you up for it right now?"
"Up for what?!" Silas demanded, he was confused.
"A date!" Harper declared shamelessly, practically vibrating with excitement. "I want you to take me on a date right now, Silas!"
Before Silas could ruthlessly reject her sudden aggressive romantic ambush, the sound of slow hesitant footsteps echoed from the dining room archway.
"Big Sister...?"
A small incredibly shaky voice cut through the tense atmosphere of the hallway.
Harper completely paused.
Her seductive smile instantly froze on her face and her glowing purple eyes widened in panic as she recognized the voice.
Harper slowly turned her head over her shoulder, looking toward the dining room.
Standing in the archway, holding her leather academy notebook against her chest, was Penelope.
The haughty violet-eyed noble girl was staring directly at the incredibly compromising position on the floor.
She saw her ruthless corporate-mogul older sister actively straddling the bare muscular hips of her best friend’s brother.
Penelope’s face was completely flushed.
She blushed heavily at her sister’s embarrassing attitude, biting her lower lip in shock.
A violently bright red hue instantly shot straight up Harper’s neck, completely taking over her entire face.
The ruthless Lord of Valoria City looked absolutely terrified.
Penelope adjusted her grip on her notebook, staring down at her older sister with a critical deadpan expression.
"S-So..." Penelope stuttered out. "...this is the highly important ’business meeting’ you told me you were going to after school, huh?"
Harper slowly pushed herself off the polished hardwood floor of the entryway.

She rested her manicured hands flat against Silas’s broad bare chest for just a second longer than was strictly necessary, feeling the steady powerful rhythm of his heartbeat thudding beneath her palms.
The thudding of his Core radiated a comforting physical heat that made her fingertips tingle with residual static.
"I was just made aware of Silas’s return to Earth not too long ago," Harper admitted with her voice uncharacteristically soft and slightly breathless.
She looked down at Silas as he began to push himself up from the ground.
As the Lord shifted his weight, the deep chiseled ridges of his abdominal muscles flexed beautifully under the dim hallway lighting.
For some strange and intensely overwhelming reason, Harper felt a sudden burning urge to lean forward and press her lips directly against his stomach.
’Hehehe~’
She quickly shook her head, forcing the inappropriate degenerate thought to the back of her mind before her face could flush any redder.

"You left your network location tracker on," Harper pointed out, brushing a stray lock of vibrant purple hair behind her ear to regain her corporate composure. "I saw the ping register on my private datapad and came over here immediately."
"Yes, I did," Silas replied, finally getting to his feet and brushing invisible dust off his dark trousers.
He didn’t bother elaborating on the fact that he had actually turned the digital tracker on for Evelyn, not her.
Silas simply rolled his stiff shoulders with the joints popping loudly in the quiet hallway, and gestured back toward the warm inviting light spilling from the dining room archway.

"I am waiting on someone to arrive for a business meeting," Silas informed her casually as he began walking back down the corridor. "Come on in. Martha made enough food to feed an entire Vanguard garrison, and I doubt I can finish it all myself."
Harper tilted her head, her curiosity instantly piqued.
She wondered who on earth Silas was expecting this late in the afternoon, especially since he had just returned from the Sovereign Realm, who was so important?
She quickly smoothed down the wrinkles in her tailored black corporate suit and hurried after him, following his towering frame toward the kitchen.
As they walked past the kitchen boundary, Martha was standing near the doorway, gently closing the heavy front door that Harper had left wide open in her frantic rush.
The dedicated housekeeper paused, her experienced eyes scanning the beautiful purple-haired woman trailing closely behind her Master.
’Wait a minute...’ Martha thought, her eyes widening in sudden realization. ’Isn’t that Penelope’s big sister?’
Martha actively kept up with the Valoria City corporate news networks.
It was impossible not to know who Harper Valeriana Whitmore was at this current point in time.
The young woman was pretty much the brand-new, undisputed owner of several massive Lord Association Buildings located directly in the commercial district.𝘧𝘳𝘦ℯ𝓌𝘦𝒷𝘯𝑜𝑣𝘦𝓁.𝒸𝘰𝓂
She had inherited a sprawling unfathomable financial empire overnight after her father’s tragic demise, meaning the girl currently staring longingly at her Master’s back was seriously rich.
’Is this Master Silas’s actual girlfriend?’ Martha pondered internally, tapping her chin thoughtfully with a crisp white kitchen towel.

Given how fiercely clingy the woman had been in the hallway, literally throwing herself onto the floor without a single second of hesitation for her expensive suit, it certainly looked like a committed romantic relationship.
Martha nodded to herself in profound, undeniable approval.
This wasn’t bad taste at all... In fact, Harper was a very strong, beautiful woman with a top-tier core and a booming real estate portfolio.
’It is clear that they would have wonderfully strong children,’ Martha concluded, her instincts running completely wild with future generational planning.
She was already mentally measuring the guest room for a nursery.
Silas walked into the dining room and immediately sat back down at the head of the heavy oak table.
Without missing a single beat, he picked up his fork and knife, digging right back into the massive sizzling basilisk steak Martha had prepared.
He ate with the focused efficiency of a starved beast, consuming the dense magical meat to replenish his drained reserves.
Harper walked into the room right behind him.
The three young girls sitting around the holographic projector instantly looked up from their digital notes, their eyes wide with genuine surprise.
Penelope nearly dropped her expensive fountain pen.
She stared at her older sister in disbelief, still reeling from the deeply compromising scene she had just witnessed out in the hallway.
Harper completely ignored her younger sister’s intensely judgmental stare and gracefully took an empty wooden chair next to Silas.
She crossed her long legs, resting her elbow on the table as she took a look at the massive, glowing blue hologram hovering over their leather notebooks.

"Territory Logistics?" Harper read the title of the projection with a confident knowing smile touching her lips. "If you girls have any specific questions about supply chains, tax brackets, or resource management, you should just ask me. I literally run four separate guild hubs."
Penelope immediately puffed out her cheeks, crossing her arms over her chest with a fierce pout.
She didn’t want her older sister crashing her private study session and showing off her wealth in front of her academy friends.
"We are doing just fine on our own, Harper," Penelope grumbled defensively, her violet eyes narrowing into a sharp glare.
Harper laughed softly, reaching across the table and gently pinching Penelope’s pouting cheek.
"You are so incredibly cute when you try to act tough, Pen."
Harper then turned her vibrant purple eyes toward Lia and Kaede, offering them a bright genuine smile that lacked any of her usual cutthroat CEO edge.
"Thank you both for being such good friends with her," Harper said sincerely. "Penelope can be quite a strange stubborn girl sometimes, so I appreciate you dealing with her eccentricities."
Penelope’s face instantly flushed a brilliant burning shade of crimson.
She swatted her sister’s hand away, completely mortified by the sudden display of familial affection in front of her peers.
"Move away, you are embarrassing me!" Penelope hissed quietly, shrinking down into her wooden chair and trying to hide behind her textbook.
Harper just smiled wider, affectionately patting her younger sister on the top of the head.
Usually, the relationship between the two Whitmore sisters was not that good.
They had been raised in a toxic cutthroat environment by a ruthless father who constantly pitted them against each other for his approval.
But after Harper inherited the empire and secured their ultimate freedom, something fundamental changed.
Even though she was currently drowning in endless corporate paperwork and didn’t have much free time, Harper made a genuine concerted attempt to be a better big sister.
Penelope would rather swallow a live grenade than ever admit it to Harper’s face, but deep down, the younger girl actually really liked the attention.
Harper sat back in her chair and finally reached for the lapels of the dark, heavy garment draped over her shoulders.
She smoothly slipped her arms out of the sleeves, pulling off the trench coat she had worn to the apartment to shield against the chill.
Harper leaned over the table, handing the heavy fabric directly over to Silas.
"Here," Harper said, winking playfully at the Lord as she passed it over. "I brought it back in one piece. And just so you know, it smells completely like me now."
Silas paused his aggressive eating.

He put his fork down and took the heavy trench coat from her hands as he looked at the flawless runic stitching, the reinforced defensive seams, and the pristine dark leather, letting out a soft tired sigh.
"Thank you, Harper," Silas told her honestly. "I genuinely wasn’t sure you were ever going to return this. People tend to keep gear when one lends it out."
Harper gasped, placing a hand over her chest in feigned dramatic offense.

"What kind of thief do you take me for?" Harper teased, her purple eyes sparkling with pure mischief. "Of course I will return it... A Whitmore always pays her debts, especially to the man who saved her life."
’Whitmore, huh? Did she get a surname or what...?’
Well Silas hadn’t known much about her originally so he couldn’t be sure.
Kaede, who had been watching the entire exchange with the focused, unblinking intensity of a hawk, suddenly leaned forward.
The ten-year-old girl rested her chin on her hands, her bright purple eyes completely filled with burning curiosity.
She desperately wanted the gossip.

"So..." Kaede dragged out the word, looking back and forth between the billionaire CEO and the shirtless man sitting at the head of the table. "Are you perhaps very, very close with Lia’s big brother?"
A soft incredibly dreamy smile appeared on Harper’s beautiful face.
She leaned back in her chair, staring at Silas with an expression of pure affection that made the Lord’s spine tingle with incoming dread.
"Close doesn’t even begin to cover it," Harper answered in a sultry dramatic whisper, making sure all the girls could hear her perfectly. "You see, girls... he has seen me naked."
"Gah!"
Silas violently choked on a piece of basilisk steak.
He slammed his fist against his chest, grabbing his glass of water and chugging it desperately to clear his airway.
"That was completely unintentional!" Silas defended himself loudly, his face flushing with embarrassment. "I was just trying to keep you alive!"
Harper simply shrugged her shoulders with an undeniably bright blush spreading across her own cheeks despite her bold confident words.

"I don’t mind," Harper admitted softly, tracing the smooth edge of the wooden table with her index finger. "But he did see everything, and he didn’t even try to take responsibility for it afterward. The fact that it already happened is proof enough of our deep bond..."
The dining room instantly erupted into chaos.
"I need more sauce! Tell me everything!" Kaede demanded excitedly, practically vibrating in her chair as she demanded the full romantic backstory of the dungeon dive.
"You are a massive pervert, Big Brother!" Lia yelled accusingly, pointing her expensive fountain pen at Silas with a look of disgust. "I can’t believe you did that!"
Penelope simply groaned, burying her flushing face entirely in her hands as she prayed for the wooden floorboards to open up and swallow her whole.
Her older sister was undeniably shameless.
Over by the kitchen archway, Martha was watching the scene unfold with wide panicked eyes.
The housekeeper was actively giving Silas complex, frantic hand signals from across the room, demanding an explanation.

’Ah! Master Silas saw the billionaire CEO naked in a dungeon?!’ Martha thought with her mind spinning wildly with the dramatic implications. ’And he doesn’t want to take responsibility for compromising a maiden’s honor? Did I perhaps make a wrong choice in believing my Master was a pure chivalrous gentleman?’
