Her seductive smile instantly froze on her face and her glowing purple eyes widened in panic as she recognized the voice.
Harper slowly turned her head over her shoulder, looking toward the dining room.
Standing in the archway, holding her leather academy notebook against her chest, was Penelope.
The haughty violet-eyed noble girl was staring directly at the incredibly compromising position on the floor.
She saw her ruthless corporate-mogul older sister actively straddling the bare muscular hips of her best friend’s brother.
Penelope’s face was completely flushed.
She blushed heavily at her sister’s embarrassing attitude, biting her lower lip in shock.
A violently bright red hue instantly shot straight up Harper’s neck, completely taking over her entire face.
The ruthless Lord of Valoria City looked absolutely terrified.
Penelope adjusted her grip on her notebook, staring down at her older sister with a critical deadpan expression.
"S-So..." Penelope stuttered out.
"...this is the highly important ’business meeting’ you told me you were going to after school, huh?"
Harper slowly pushed herself off the polished hardwood floor of the entryway.

She rested her manicured hands flat against Silas’s broad bare chest for just a second longer than was strictly necessary, feeling the steady powerful rhythm of his heartbeat thudding beneath her palms.
The thudding of his Core radiated a comforting physical heat that made her fingertips tingle with residual static.
"I was just made aware of Silas’s return to Earth not too long ago," Harper admitted with her voice uncharacteristically soft and slightly breathless.
She looked down at Silas as he began to push himself up from the ground.
As the Lord shifted his weight, the deep chiseled ridges of his abdominal muscles flexed beautifully under the dim hallway lighting.
For some strange and intensely overwhelming reason, Harper felt a sudden burning urge to lean forward and press her lips directly against his stomach.
’Hehehe~’
She quickly shook her head, forcing the inappropriate degenerate thought to the back of her mind before her face could flush any redder.
"You left your network location tracker on," Harper pointed out, brushing a stray lock of vibrant purple hair behind her ear to regain her corporate composure.
"I saw the ping register on my private datapad and came over here immediately."
"Yes, I did," Silas replied, finally getting to his feet and brushing invisible dust off his dark trousers.
He didn’t bother elaborating on the fact that he had actually turned the digital tracker on for Evelyn, not her.
Silas simply rolled his stiff shoulders with the joints popping loudly in the quiet hallway, and gestured back toward the warm inviting light spilling from the dining room archway.
"I am waiting on someone to arrive for a business meeting," Silas informed her casually as he began walking back down the corridor.
"Come on in.
Martha made enough food to feed an entire Vanguard garrison, and I doubt I can finish it all myself."
Harper tilted her head, her curiosity instantly piqued.
She wondered who on earth Silas was expecting this late in the afternoon, especially since he had just returned from the Sovereign Realm, who was so important?
She quickly smoothed down the wrinkles in her tailored black corporate suit and hurried after him, following his towering frame toward the kitchen.
As they walked past the kitchen boundary, Martha was standing near the doorway, gently closing the heavy front door that Harper had left wide open in her frantic rush.
The dedicated housekeeper paused, her experienced eyes scanning the beautiful purple-haired woman trailing closely behind her Master.
’Wait a minute...’ Martha thought, her eyes widening in sudden realization. ’Isn’t that Penelope’s big sister?’
Martha actively kept up with the Valoria City corporate news networks.
It was impossible not to know who Harper Valeriana Whitmore was at this current point in time.
The young woman was pretty much the brand-new, undisputed owner of several massive Lord Association Buildings located directly in the commercial district.𝘧𝘳𝘦ℯ𝓌𝘦𝒷𝘯𝑜𝑣𝘦𝓁.𝒸𝘰𝓂
She had inherited a sprawling unfathomable financial empire overnight after her father’s tragic demise, meaning the girl currently staring longingly at her Master’s back was seriously rich.
’Is this Master Silas’s actual girlfriend?’ Martha pondered internally, tapping her chin thoughtfully with a crisp white kitchen towel.

Given how fiercely clingy the woman had been in the hallway, literally throwing herself onto the floor without a single second of hesitation for her expensive suit, it certainly looked like a committed romantic relationship.
Martha nodded to herself in profound, undeniable approval.
This wasn’t bad taste at all...
In fact, Harper was a very strong, beautiful woman with a top-tier core and a booming real estate portfolio.
’It is clear that they would have wonderfully strong children,’ Martha concluded, her instincts running completely wild with future generational planning.
She was already mentally measuring the guest room for a nursery.
Silas walked into the dining room and immediately sat back down at the head of the heavy oak table.
Without missing a single beat, he picked up his fork and knife, digging right back into the massive sizzling basilisk steak Martha had prepared.
He ate with the focused efficiency of a starved beast, consuming the dense magical meat to replenish his drained reserves.
Harper walked into the room right behind him.
The three young girls sitting around the holographic projector instantly looked up from their digital notes, their eyes wide with genuine surprise.
Penelope nearly dropped her expensive fountain pen.
She stared at her older sister in disbelief, still reeling from the deeply compromising scene she had just witnessed out in the hallway.
Harper completely ignored her younger sister’s intensely judgmental stare and gracefully took an empty wooden chair next to Silas.
She crossed her long legs, resting her elbow on the table as she took a look at the massive, glowing blue hologram hovering over their leather notebooks.
"Territory Logistics?" Harper read the title of the projection with a confident knowing smile touching her lips.
"If you girls have any specific questions about supply chains, tax brackets, or resource management, you should just ask me.
I literally run four separate guild hubs."
Penelope immediately puffed out her cheeks, crossing her arms over her chest with a fierce pout.
She didn’t want her older sister crashing her private study session and showing off her wealth in front of her academy friends.
"We are doing just fine on our own, Harper," Penelope grumbled defensively, her violet eyes narrowing into a sharp glare.
Harper laughed softly, reaching across the table and gently pinching Penelope’s pouting cheek.
"You are so incredibly cute when you try to act tough, Pen."
Harper then turned her vibrant purple eyes toward Lia and Kaede, offering them a bright genuine smile that lacked any of her usual cutthroat CEO edge.
"Thank you both for being such good friends with her," Harper said sincerely.
"Penelope can be quite a strange stubborn girl sometimes, so I appreciate you dealing with her eccentricities."
Penelope’s face instantly flushed a brilliant burning shade of crimson.
She swatted her sister’s hand away, completely mortified by the sudden display of familial affection in front of her peers.
"Move away, you are embarrassing me!" Penelope hissed quietly, shrinking down into her wooden chair and trying to hide behind her textbook.
Harper just smiled wider, affectionately patting her younger sister on the top of the head.
Usually, the relationship between the two Whitmore sisters was not that good.
They had been raised in a toxic cutthroat environment by a ruthless father who constantly pitted them against each other for his approval.
But after Harper inherited the empire and secured their ultimate freedom, something fundamental changed.
Even though she was currently drowning in endless corporate paperwork and didn’t have much free time, Harper made a genuine concerted attempt to be a better big sister.
Penelope would rather swallow a live grenade than ever admit it to Harper’s face, but deep down, the younger girl actually really liked the attention.
Harper sat back in her chair and finally reached for the lapels of the dark, heavy garment draped over her shoulders.
She smoothly slipped her arms out of the sleeves, pulling off the trench coat she had worn to the apartment to shield against the chill.
Harper leaned over the table, handing the heavy fabric directly over to Silas.
"Here," Harper said, winking playfully at the Lord as she passed it over.
"I brought it back in one piece.
And just so you know, it smells completely like me now."
Silas paused his aggressive eating.

He put his fork down and took the heavy trench coat from her hands as he looked at the flawless runic stitching, the reinforced defensive seams, and the pristine dark leather, letting out a soft tired sigh.
"Thank you, Harper," Silas told her honestly.
"I genuinely wasn’t sure you were ever going to return this.
People tend to keep gear when one lends it out."
Harper gasped, placing a hand over her chest in feigned dramatic offense.
"What kind of thief do you take me for?" Harper teased, her purple eyes sparkling with pure mischief.
"Of course I will return it...
A Whitmore always pays her debts, especially to the man who saved her life."
’Whitmore, huh?
Did she get a surname or what...?’
Well Silas hadn’t known much about her originally so he couldn’t be sure.
Kaede, who had been watching the entire exchange with the focused, unblinking intensity of a hawk, suddenly leaned forward.
The ten-year-old girl rested her chin on her hands, her bright purple eyes completely filled with burning curiosity.
She desperately wanted the gossip.
"So..." Kaede dragged out the word, looking back and forth between the billionaire CEO and the shirtless man sitting at the head of the table.
"Are you perhaps very, very close with Lia’s big brother?"
A soft incredibly dreamy smile appeared on Harper’s beautiful face.
She leaned back in her chair, staring at Silas with an expression of pure affection that made the Lord’s spine tingle with incoming dread.
"Close doesn’t even begin to cover it," Harper answered in a sultry dramatic whisper, making sure all the girls could hear her perfectly.
"You see, girls... he has seen me naked."
"Gah!"
Silas violently choked on a piece of basilisk steak.
He slammed his fist against his chest, grabbing his glass of water and chugging it desperately to clear his airway.
"That was completely unintentional!" Silas defended himself loudly, his face flushing with embarrassment.
"I was just trying to keep you alive!"
Harper simply shrugged her shoulders with an undeniably bright blush spreading across her own cheeks despite her bold confident words.
"I don’t mind," Harper admitted softly, tracing the smooth edge of the wooden table with her index finger.
"But he did see everything, and he didn’t even try to take responsibility for it afterward.
The fact that it already happened is proof enough of our deep bond..."
The dining room instantly erupted into chaos.
"I need more sauce!
Tell me everything!" Kaede demanded excitedly, practically vibrating in her chair as she demanded the full romantic backstory of the dungeon dive.
"You are a massive pervert, Big Brother!" Lia yelled accusingly, pointing her expensive fountain pen at Silas with a look of disgust.
"I can’t believe you did that!"
Penelope simply groaned, burying her flushing face entirely in her hands as she prayed for the wooden floorboards to open up and swallow her whole.
Her older sister was undeniably shameless.
Over by the kitchen archway, Martha was watching the scene unfold with wide panicked eyes.
The housekeeper was actively giving Silas complex, frantic hand signals from across the room, demanding an explanation.
’Ah!

Master Silas saw the billionaire CEO naked in a dungeon?!’ Martha thought with her mind spinning wildly with the dramatic implications. ’And he doesn’t want to take responsibility for compromising a maiden’s honor?
Did I perhaps make a wrong choice in believing my Master was a pure chivalrous gentleman?’

chapters.title: Chapter 343: Evelyn... Arrives
paragraphs: Silas looked around the chaotic dining room.
He looked at the accusing glare of his little sister, the terrified embarrassment of Penelope, the gossip-hungry eyes of Kaede, and the deeply judgmental hand signals of his own maid.
He let out a long exhausted sigh.
There was only one way to shut this entire circus down before it spiraled out of control.
Silas turned his head, locking his golden-ringed eyes directly onto Harper.
"Fine," Silas told her bluntly with his deep voice easily cutting through the noise of the cheering girls. "I will accept your date, okay? Just stop telling my sister about the Secret Realm stuff."
Harper blinked.
Her jaw dropped slightly, and her glowing purple eyes widened in unexpected shock.
She stared at him as he calmly picked his fork back up and resumed eating his steak as though he were a mechanical machine, methodically taking down the massive mountain of food on his plate.
’I... uh...’ Harper thought frantically, her heart suddenly hammering against her ribs like a trapped bird. ’I didn’t think it would happen this quickly!’
She had expected him to reject her, to push her away, or to cite his busy schedule as an excuse to delay.
The sudden unceremonious acceptance caught her off guard.
’Is he in a rush or something?’ Harper wondered, her brilliant strategic mind analyzing his rapid machine-like eating behavior.
He had mentioned out in the hallway that he had someone to meet this afternoon.
That specific detail suddenly made her intensely interested in exactly who this mystery person was.
Who was so important that Silas was trying to clear his schedule this rapidly?
But regardless of his hidden motives, she had won the primary battle.
Harper smiled, a genuine radiant expression of pure happiness illuminating her face.
"Thank you, Silas," Harper said softly, her voice trembling slightly with excitement.
She leaned slightly closer to him. "When should we go? I can clear my entire corporate schedule for the rest of the week."
’A stalker like you has a schedule?’
Silas didn’t look up from his plate, slicing a piece of garlic bread.
"You decide on a time and text the details to my network number," Silas instructed cleanly.
He didn’t tell her out loud, but his sensory perception was currently flaring.
He could feel a very familiar, distinctly nicotine-laced mana signature rapidly approaching the front of his apartment building.
Evelyn was finally here.
KNOCK! KNOCK!
The sharp heavy sound of knuckles rapping against the front door echoed down the hallway.
’That’s probably her,’ Silas thought, putting his fork down and wiping his mouth with a white napkin.
They needed to get to the Valoria City bank immediately to process the seventy-five million credit transfer, and then head over to the undercity to meet Evelyn’s information broker, Jax.
The faster he met with the underground contact and secured a bulletproof identity for Vespera, the faster the suffocating anxiety building in his chest would dissipate.
He couldn’t risk the World Council uncovering his deception.
Silas stood up from the oak table, pushing his chair back.
"If you girls have any more questions about the logistics project, ask Harper," Silas told the study group. "She actually runs a territory in the Known Zones I think."
He looked over at the kitchen archway, intending to ask Martha to grab him a fresh clean shirt from his bedroom upstairs.
But his eyes fell on the dark trench coat resting on the back of his chair.
"Whatever..."
Silas grabbed the heavy coat and smoothly slid his muscular arms into the sleeves.

He pulled the lapels tight over his bare chest. Sure, the fabric smelled distinctly like Harper’s expensive lavender perfume but she smelled genuinely great, so he didn’t mind the scent in the slightest.
"Thanks for fixing the coat," Silas complimented her casually, adjusting the reinforced collar around his neck. "It feels sturdier than before."
He turned and walked purposefully out of the dining room, heading straight for the front entrance.
Harper watched his broad shoulders disappear down the hallway with her heart fluttering wildly at the casual compliment.
She was captivated by his presence.
Silas reached the front door and pulled the heavy brass handle open.
Standing on the porch was Evelyn.
The Lord of The Unmovable Wall was wearing a fresh clean oversized black hoodie and dark cargo pants.
"Do you only wear hoodies?"
Her black hair was pulled up into a messy bun, and she looked thoroughly exhausted from the events of the day.
"No."
She took a long deep drag from the slim silver cigarette resting between her lips.
FWOOSH.
Evelyn unceremoniously puffed a thick cloud of gray toxic smoke directly into Silas’s face as he opened the door.
"You live in a pretty nice place for a teenager," Evelyn noted dryly, her dark eyes scanning the pristine exterior of the Silverleaf apartment complex.
Silas stepped out onto the porch, waving a hand to clear the toxic smoke away from his face.
He reached back and pulled the heavy front door firmly shut behind him.
"Stop smoking on my property," Silas ordered cleanly. "And thanks for the compliment, though you obviously can’t relate since you live in a rusty metal box."
Evelyn’s eyes narrowed into a fierce irritated glare at the flawless roast.
"Fucker," Evelyn cursed bluntly, flipping him off as she turned around and started walking down the porch steps.
Inside the apartment, just as the heavy wooden door was closing, Harper had rushed out into the hallway.
The purple-haired Lord blinked in surprise when she heard the distinct, voice of another woman interacting with Silas.
She quickly ran over to the front door, grabbing the handle and pulling it open just a crack to peer outside.
She looked through the narrow gap, watching Silas and the strange hoodie-wearing girl walking off toward the sidewalk together.
Harper desperately wanted to open the door fully.
She wanted to step out onto the porch, announce her presence with a flare of lightning, and demand to know exactly who this woman was.
However, just before they reached the end of the front walkway, Evelyn paused.
The black-haired Lord turned her head slightly, looking back over her shoulder directly at the cracked front door.
Evelyn’s dark eyes locked flawlessly onto Harper’s glowing purple ones hiding in the shadows.
Harper could swear, upon her life as a Lord, that she saw the strange woman’s lips twitch upward into an arrogant mocking smirk, as though she were playing a hilariously funny prank on a rival.
Then, Evelyn faced forward again, and the heavy front door swung completely shut.
Harper stood alone in the quiet hallway with her hands clenched into tight fists.
Her mind was racing a mile a minute.
It was painfully obvious that this mystery person was incredibly important to Silas, given how quickly he had left his own welcome-home meal to meet her.
But it didn’t seem like they were going on a romantic date, especially since Silas and Harper were supposed to be going on an official date very soon.
Harper let out a long conflicted sigh.
’That woman seems to be a massive smoking addict,’ Harper analyzed the brief encounter, remembering the thick cloud of gray smoke lingering on the porch.
Silas was a health-conscious Lord who relied on peak physical performance to survive.
From everything Harper had researched and observed about him, he definitely didn’t like women who poisoned their own bodies with terrible habits.
He preferred strength, vitality, and purity of core.
’It won’t work out between them,’ Harper thought, a fierce undeniable wave of possessiveness washing over her soul.
She unclenched her fists, her purple eyes glowing with the raw untamed power of a woman genuinely in love.
She had fought her own family, survived a god, and claimed a billionaire’s empire.
She wasn’t going to lose the man she loved to some random sleep-deprived girl in a dirty hoodie.
’At the end of the day, Silas belongs to me...’ Harper declared in her heart, sealing her own romantic resolve.
She turned around and walked back toward the kitchen archway. She offered Martha a bright impeccably polite smile.

"Excuse me, Martha," Harper requested sweetly, her eyes gleaming with sudden strange intensity. "Does Silas happen to have any more of his coats or shirts in his closet? I want to... see all of them."
Martha stared at the beautiful billionaire CEO, clutching her white towel in deadpan disbelief.
’This woman is really, really weird,’ Martha thought, silently judging the elite class of Valoria City.
Silas and Evelyn walked silently down the pristine concrete sidewalk, leaving the manicured lawns of the Silverleaf apartment complex behind them.
The late afternoon sun was beginning to dip below the towering skyscrapers of Valoria City, casting long golden shadows across the quiet residential street.
The noise of distant traffic and passing transport shuttles filled the air which was a stark contrast to the magical silence of the Umbral Basin.
As they approached the main intersection, Evelyn’s dark eyes locked onto a vehicle parked illegally right against the curb.
It was a midnight-black luxury supercar.
The chassis was plated in refined mythril-alloy, the windows were tinted with privacy wards, and the tires hummed with subtle gravitational magic.
It was the exact gift that Elora had bought for Silas to secure his favor.
Evelyn stopped walking.
She stared at the breathtakingly expensive machine with her mind immediately calculating its market value.
"You really splurged a massive amount of money on a ride, didn’t you?" Evelyn noted, crossing her arms over her hoodie and looking at him skeptically.
Silas shoved his hands deep into the pockets of his dark trench coat.
"I wasn’t the one who bought it," Silas corrected her smoothly. "It was a gift from an associate."
Evelyn tilted her head, her brilliant mind instantly connecting the dots.
She was a tactician so she could easily get a read on Silas’s operational methods.
She had just seen that beautiful incredibly wealthy woman back in the hallway... the infamous Harper Whitmore, the brand-new billionaire owner of four Lord Association Buildings.
And now, she was staring at an eight-million-credit supercar that Silas claimed was a "gift."
’He is exactly the kind of man that makes wealthy women spend fortunes on his stuff,’ Evelyn concluded in her mind, completely misinterpreting the situation.
In her eyes, Silas was ruthlessly exploiting that poor lovesick billionaire woman for her vast corporate wealth in order to fund his rapid territory expansion.
He had no formal backing, no noble family, and no corporate sponsors.
Seducing one of the richest heiresses in Valoria City was the perfect strategy to secure endless capital.
’As expected of this ruthless fucker,’ Evelyn thought, feeling a strange, twisted sense of professional respect for his audacious grift.
She stepped closer to him and aggressively elbowed him hard in the ribs.
"Smooth operator," Evelyn muttered sarcastically, taking another long drag from her cigarette and puffing the smoke into the air.
"Hm?" Silas grunted, rubbing his side and looking down at her in complete confusion.
He had no idea what she was talking about or why she was suddenly praising him.
He let out a tired sigh, deciding not to question the complex inner workings of her nicotine-addled brain.
"So," Silas asked, looking up and down the empty residential street. "How exactly are we getting around the city today to meet your underground contact? Are we taking the supercar?"
Evelyn shook her head, flicking a bit of gray ash onto the pristine sidewalk.

"No," Evelyn replied bluntly. "We need to stay under the radar if we are going deep into the undercity to meet Jax. Driving an eight-million-credit mythril beacon is a terrible idea. It draws too much attention so I already called us a ride."
Silas raised a skeptical eyebrow. "You called a ride?"
Right on cue, a beat-up aggressively yellow, standard Valoria City public transit cab rattled around the street corner.
The combustion engine sputtered loudly, emitting a thick cloud of dark terrible-smelling exhaust as it screeched to a halt right in front of them.
The back door featured a massive, peeling advertisement for a cheap healing potion brand, and one of the hubcaps was entirely missing.
Silas stared at the depressing broken-down public cab.
He looked at Evelyn, who was standing there with her hands securely in her pockets, waiting for him to open the dented door.
"Pfft."
A sharp laugh escaped Silas’s lips.
He tried to cover his mouth with his hand, but he couldn’t hold it back.
He began laughing out loud at the pathetic contrast between the luxury he had just left and the broke-Lord reality standing in front of him.
’And she’s a multi-millionaire too...’
Evelyn’s pale face instantly flushed a violent furious shade of crimson. Her dark eyes flared with rage at his mockery.
"I’ll kill you, fucker!" Evelyn screamed, throwing her cigarette onto the ground and lunging aggressively at him.

It was the exact gift that Elora had bought for Silas to secure his favor.
Evelyn stopped walking.
She stared at the breathtakingly expensive machine with her mind immediately calculating its market value.
"You really splurged a massive amount of money on a ride, didn’t you?" Evelyn noted, crossing her arms over her hoodie and looking at him skeptically.
Silas shoved his hands deep into the pockets of his dark trench coat.
"I wasn’t the one who bought it," Silas corrected her smoothly.
"It was a gift from an associate."
Evelyn tilted her head, her brilliant mind instantly connecting the dots.
She was a tactician so she could easily get a read on Silas’s operational methods.
She had just seen that beautiful incredibly wealthy woman back in the hallway... the infamous Harper Whitmore, the brand-new billionaire owner of four Lord Association Buildings.
And now, she was staring at an eight-million-credit supercar that Silas claimed was a "gift."
’He is exactly the kind of man that makes wealthy women spend fortunes on his stuff,’ Evelyn concluded in her mind, completely misinterpreting the situation.
In her eyes, Silas was ruthlessly exploiting that poor lovesick billionaire woman for her vast corporate wealth in order to fund his rapid territory expansion.
He had no formal backing, no noble family, and no corporate sponsors.
Seducing one of the richest heiresses in Valoria City was the perfect strategy to secure endless capital.
’As expected of this ruthless fucker,’ Evelyn thought, feeling a strange, twisted sense of professional respect for his audacious grift.
She stepped closer to him and aggressively elbowed him hard in the ribs.
"Smooth operator," Evelyn muttered sarcastically, taking another long drag from her cigarette and puffing the smoke into the air.
"Hm?" Silas grunted, rubbing his side and looking down at her in complete confusion.
He had no idea what she was talking about or why she was suddenly praising him.
He let out a tired sigh, deciding not to question the complex inner workings of her nicotine-addled brain.
"So," Silas asked, looking up and down the empty residential street.
"How exactly are we getting around the city today to meet your underground contact?
Are we taking the supercar?"
Evelyn shook her head, flicking a bit of gray ash onto the pristine sidewalk.
"No," Evelyn replied bluntly.
"We need to stay under the radar if we are going deep into the undercity to meet Jax.
Driving an eight-million-credit mythril beacon is a terrible idea.
It draws too much attention so I already called us a ride."
Silas raised a skeptical eyebrow.
"You called a ride?"
Right on cue, a beat-up aggressively yellow, standard Valoria City public transit cab rattled around the street corner.
The combustion engine sputtered loudly, emitting a thick cloud of dark terrible-smelling exhaust as it screeched to a halt right in front of them.
The back door featured a massive, peeling advertisement for a cheap healing potion brand, and one of the hubcaps was entirely missing.
Silas stared at the depressing broken-down public cab.
He looked at Evelyn, who was standing there with her hands securely in her pockets, waiting for him to open the dented door.
"Pfft."
A sharp laugh escaped Silas’s lips.
He tried to cover his mouth with his hand, but he couldn’t hold it back.
He began laughing out loud at the pathetic contrast between the luxury he had just left and the broke-Lord reality standing in front of him.
’And she’s a multi-millionaire too...’
Evelyn’s pale face instantly flushed a violent furious shade of crimson.
Her dark eyes flared with rage at his mockery.
"I’ll kill you, fucker!" Evelyn screamed, throwing her cigarette onto the ground and lunging aggressively at him.

chapters.title: Chapter 344: Ice Cream In A Beat Down Cab
paragraphs: The beat-up yellow public transit cab rattled loudly as it pulled away from the curb with its failing combustion engine coughing a thick cloud of dark exhaust into the late afternoon air.
Silas and Evelyn were securely in the back seat, leaving the quiet manicured streets of the Silverleaf apartment complex behind them.
Just seconds after their terrible ride turned the corner and disappeared from view, a completely different class of vehicle glided smoothly into the neighborhood.
A sleek elongated luxury limousine, plated entirely in polished obsidian and trimmed with silver runic etchings, pulled silently up to the curb.
The vehicle came to a flawless stop directly in front of Silas’s apartment building.
The driver’s side door opened, and a tall impeccably dressed butler in a tailored black suit stepped out onto the concrete.
He walked briskly around the rear of the vehicle and respectfully opened the passenger door.
A young woman stepped out into the Valoria City sunlight.
Seraphina Bloom adjusted the collar of her designer crimson blazer with her movements radiating the undeniable elegance of high-society nobility.
She reached up with a manicured hand, smoothly running her fingers through her vibrant cascading crimson hair.
Her sharp beautiful features were locked into an expression of intense focused determination.

’He left his location tracker on earlier, even though it just turned off,’ Seraphina thought to herself, her mind racing as she stared at the front door of the apartment building. ’That was a clear indication that he was around here. I know I have the right address...’
"I wish you the best of luck, Lady Seraphina," the butler offered politely, bowing his head as he held the limousine door.
Seraphina completely ignored him.

She didn’t have time for pleasantries with the hired help as she clutched a thick leather folder filled with legal documents tightly against her chest and walked forward with her expensive heels clicking sharply against the paved stone walkway leading up to Silas’s porch.
She had been searching for him for quite a while now.
Ever since the chaotic events inside Ititius’s Secret Realm, Silas had seemingly vanished from social circles.
The Lord had practically fallen off the grid, retreating into the depths of the Sovereign to build his territory.
Seraphina had been genuinely worried about him, though she would never willingly admit that vulnerability out loud to anyone.
She continued walking up the porch steps with her mind flashing back to the specific compromising incident that had tied their fates together.
During the Secret Realm expedition, Silas had seen her entirely naked. He had witnessed everything, completely stripping away her noble dignity just to pee.
In the traditional rigid culture of the elite noble families, an event like that carried massive consequences.
She had already talked it out at length with her Mother and Father. The conclusion was unyielding.
Silas Graves would have to marry her to preserve the honor of the Bloom family.
’I am fully prepared to treat you exactly as you deserve to be treated,’ Seraphina thought with a sudden wave of warmth spreading through her chest as her thighs pressed together slightly.
Despite the forced nature of the arrangement, she didn’t actually hate the idea.
Silas was fiercely strong, incredibly capable, and undeniably handsome.
As long as he treated her well and fulfilled his duties as a proper husband, she would treat him incredibly well as a wife.
She would manage his household, support his territorial expansion, and maybe, eventually, she would even bear his children to secure their legacy.
She certainly wouldn’t end up like her own parents.
She silently swore that she would never publicly disgrace Silas online like her mother, Etilga, had done to her father.
Those two had a bizarre toxic dynamic that constantly spilled into the Valoria City tabloids.
Seraphina wanted a stable powerful partnership.
’I want Silas...’ Seraphina resolved fiercely in her heart, gripping the leather folder even tighter. ’And I will get him.’
She reached the heavy front door and raised her hand. She knocked firmly three times on the thick wood, projecting an aura of complete confidence.
She waited, fully expecting the rugged dark-haired Lord to open the door and look at her in surprise.
She had her opening lines perfectly rehearsed... She was going to be assertive and irresistibly charming.
CLICK!
The heavy brass handle turned, and the door slowly swung inward.
Seraphina’s elegant smile instantly died on her face.
Standing in the doorway was not Silas Graves. It was a stunningly beautiful woman with vibrant purple hair.
To make matters infinitely worse, the woman was currently wearing an oversized comfortable dark hoodie that clearly belonged to Silas, hanging loosely over her shoulders in a deeply intimate manner.
Harper stared back at the red-haired noble, her glowing purple eyes narrowing into a fierce territorial glare.
She instantly recognized Seraphina.
The air on the porch instantly dropped twenty degrees, crackling with the invisible suffocating pressure of two powerful jealous women.
Seraphina’s grip on her leather folder tightened until her knuckles turned white.
Her crimson eyes flared with pure hostility as she took in Harper’s disheveled comfortable appearance inside Silas’s home.
"Bitch," Seraphina spat venomously, completely dropping her noble elegance. "What the hell are you doing at his house?"
A long distance away from the brewing domestic war zone at the Silverleaf apartment, the beat-up yellow public transit cab violently hit a massive pothole.
"Ugh," Silas grunted, bracing his hands against the sticky peeling vinyl of the passenger seat to keep from bouncing his head off the low ceiling.
The suspension on the vehicle was shot.
Every single bump in the Valoria City asphalt sent a jarring uncomfortable shockwave directly up his spine.
The air conditioning was broken, blowing lukewarm, musty air that smelled faintly of cheap stale beer into the cramped back seat.
Silas turned his head, glaring at Evelyn.

The black-haired Lord of The Unmovable Wall was sitting next to him with her knees pulled up slightly in the cramped space, staring casually out the smudged window as if this were a perfectly normal way to travel.
"I have a very serious question," Silas stated, his deep voice carrying a heavy layer of judgment over the rattling engine noise.
Evelyn didn’t look away from the window. "What?"
"If you are supposedly so incredibly rich," Silas pointed out, gesturing wildly at the terrible interior of the cab. "Why in the world are we riding in a metal deathtrap that smells like a wet dog?"
Evelyn finally turned her head, offering him a completely indifferent shrug.

"We could have easily ordered a private guild-certified armored transport," Evelyn admitted smoothly, not looking the least bit bothered by the sticky seats. "But those premium cabs are just too costly for a simple cross-town trip... They charge a massive base fee just to unlock the doors, plus a premium rate per mile based on the threat level of the district."
Silas stared at her in deadpan disbelief.
"Evelyn," Silas said slowly, making sure she heard every word. "You are a multi-millionaire... You own a fortress the size of a city block so I think you can afford a base fee."

"Wealth is accumulated through strict financial discipline, Silas," Evelyn lectured him dryly, leaning back against the uncomfortable vinyl. "You don’t stay rich by throwing away credits on useless luxury when a standard transit cab gets you to the exact same destination."
"This thing might actually explode before we reach the destination," Silas countered, gripping the door handle as the cab violently swerved to avoid a stray utility drone in the street.
Before Evelyn could argue her stingy financial philosophies any further, the cab lurched forward and slammed to a halt.
The screech of the worn brake pads was deafening.
Silas looked out the front windshield.
The massive sprawling commercial district of Valoria City was completely deadlocked in a brutal afternoon traffic jam.
Hundreds of hovering transports, armored cargo trucks, and luxury sedans were packed tightly together between the towering skyscrapers, none of them moving an inch.
The cab driver, a gruff older man with cybernetic implants on his neck, turned around and slid the scratched plexiglass divider open.
"Central intersection is blocked by a guild parade, kids," the driver grunted, chewing on a toothpick. "We are gonna be sitting here for at least twenty minutes before the enforcers clear the lanes."
Evelyn groaned loudly, letting her head fall back against the seat. "Perfect. Just what I needed today."
Silas let out a tired sigh, unbuttoning the top of his dark trench coat to vent some of the stifling heat trapped in the cabin.
He looked out his window at the crowded sidewalk.
Right next to their stalled cab, an entrepreneurial street vendor had set up a glowing frost-warded cart.
The vendor was actively scooping large, colorful servings of magically chilled ice cream for the pedestrians stuck in the traffic.
’That’s not a bad idea...’
If he was going to be trapped in a hot terrible-smelling box, he was at least going to be comfortable.
Silas rolled down his window, leaning his head out into the bustling street.
"Hey," Silas called out to the vendor, holding up a crisp silver credit note. "Two large cups of the frost-berry."
The vendor eagerly trotted over, exchanging the cold treats for the currency through the open window.
Silas rolled the glass back up and turned to Evelyn. He held out one of the large, sweating paper cups filled with bright blue, magically chilled ice cream.
Evelyn blinked in surprise, staring at the offering.
"What is this?" Evelyn asked defensively, eyeing the cup like it might be a trap.

"It is ice cream, Evelyn," Silas replied dryly, shoving it directly into her hands. "Eat it before it melts all over your hoodie. Consider it a peace offering for dragging you out of the Sovereign Realm."
Evelyn took the cup with her dark eyes narrowing suspiciously as she inspected the frost-berry treat.
She grabbed the small wooden spoon and took a cautious tiny bite.
The exact second the magical sub-zero sweetness hit her tongue, her entire demeanor shifted.
The stress of the Lord War and the crushing exhaustion seemed to momentarily melt away from her pale face.
Her eyes widened, and she immediately scooped a massive unceremonious bite into her mouth.
Silas watched her eat with an amused smirk.
For a Lord who commanded an army of heavy infantry, she looked surprisingly innocent eating ice cream in the back of a broken-down cab.
"Brain freeze," Evelyn suddenly hissed, squeezing her eyes tightly shut and pressing a hand firmly against her forehead as the magical cold rapidly assaulted her sinuses.
Silas couldn’t help it.
He burst out laughing.
"You are supposed to eat it slowly, you idiot," Silas mocked her playfully, taking a calm bite of his own treat.
Evelyn glared at him through one open eye with her face flushed from the cold.
"Shut up," Evelyn mumbled irritably, though there was no real venom in her voice.
She took another significantly smaller bite.
They sat together in the cramped uncomfortable back seat, making surprisingly easy small talk as the traffic slowly began to crawl forward.
They complained about the absurd Valoria City zoning laws, mocked the garish, overly expensive outfits of the nobles walking past their cab, and shared a rare quiet moment of genuine camaraderie.
Despite their massive globally broadcast war just hours prior, they actually enjoyed each other’s company.
They both shared the same modern mindset that completely rejected the dramatic nonsense of the Sovereign Realm.
Eventually, the traffic cleared, and the cab sped up, weaving through the towering commercial sector.
"We’re here," the driver announced, pulling up to the curb.
They had arrived outside the Valoria City Central Bank.
It was a massive intimidating structure built entirely from reinforced white marble and gleaming gold pillars.
Heavily armed security golems patrolled the front steps, and the entrance hummed with dense visible layers of anti-theft magical wards.
Silas and Evelyn stepped out of the terrible cab.
Silas tossed a few extra credits through the front window to pay the driver, not waiting for the change.
They walked over to a nearby public disposal chute, discarding their empty ice cream cups, and marched together up the grand marble steps of the bank.
"Finally..."
The interior of the Valoria City Bank was overwhelming.
The ceiling vaulted hundreds of feet into the air, painted with intricate murals of the founding Lords.
The main floor was packed with thousands of ordinary citizens, low-tier merchants, and mercenaries, all waiting miserably in endlessly long winding lines to see a teller.
Silas looked at the massive crowd, preparing himself for hours of mind-numbing waiting.
"Follow me," Evelyn ordered smoothly, completely bypassing the massive crowd.

chapters.title: Chapter 345 - 75 Million Credits Richer
paragraphs: She walked with undeniable confidence directly toward a roped-off guarded section on the far side of the grand hall.
Two massive iron golems stepped forward to block her path, their glowing red eyes scanning her unimpressive oversized gray hoodie.
Evelyn simply reached into her pocket and pulled out a banking emblem.
The exact second the golems registered the authenticity of the Lord insignia, they instantly stepped aside, bowing their massive metal heads in deep respect.

"Lords have special line-cutting privileges," Evelyn explained casually to Silas as they walked past the velvet ropes. "Time is money, and the World knows we don’t have time to wait behind normal people."
They approached the pristine polished mahogany desk of a senior cashier.
The man behind the glass partition wore a crisp tailored suit and a polite smile.
"Welcome, Honored Lords," the cashier greeted them warmly. "How may the Valoria Central Bank assist your expanding territories today?"
Evelyn leaned against the counter, sliding her datapad across the smooth wood.
"I need to authorize a direct immediate capital transfer from my primary holding accounts to his designated one." Evelyn instructed smoothly, gesturing to Silas standing beside her.
The cashier nodded efficiently, picking up the datapad to review the digital paperwork.
"Of course, My Lady. A simple capital transfer is routine. Let me just confirm the sum of the transaction and we will have that processed for—"
The cashier’s voice abruptly died in his throat.
His eyes bugged out of his skull, bulging wildly behind his wire-rimmed glasses.
He stared at the glowing blue numbers on the datapad screen, his brain completely failing to process the terrifying scale of the wealth.
"S-Seventy-five... million... Spirit Credits?" the cashier stammered, his hands beginning to physically tremble as he held the device.
He nervously looked up from the screen, his gaze shifting directly to Silas.
He took in the rugged handsome face, his dark trench coat, and his clear undeniable youth.

"M-My Lord," the cashier addressed Silas, his voice cracking violently under the pressure. "Please forgive my profound intrusion, but... you appear to be quite young. A transaction of this unfathomable magnitude usually requires a verified adult guarantor, or a senior guild representative to physically co-sign the release of funds to prevent fraudulent coercion."
Silas stared at the trembling man with a cold deadpan expression.
Evelyn didn’t miss a beat.
She leaned against the mahogany counter, offering Silas an arrogant mocking grin that radiated pure spite.

"Oh, dear me," Evelyn dramatically sighed, placing a hand over her heart. "It seems my poor, inexperienced little Lord needs a grown-up to hold his hand through the scary bank procedures. Don’t worry, kid. I will gladly sign the guardian waiver for you."
Silas rolled his eyes so hard it actually hurt his nerves. He crossed his arms, refusing to give her the satisfaction of a verbal reaction.

"This amount of capital far exceeds my clearance tier," the cashier apologized frantically, sweating profusely as he handed the datapad back to Evelyn. "I am not authorized to move seventy-five million credits without an executive override. You will have to go upstairs to the Manager’s private office for approval..."
"Fine," Evelyn replied cleanly, taking the datapad back. "Show us the way."

A polite, impeccably dressed receptionist materialized from a side door, quickly guiding the two Lords away from the main floor and toward a private, rune-powered elevator located in the back of the building.
The heavy brass doors of the elevator closed, sealing them inside the quiet, ascending magical chamber.
Silas turned to Evelyn as the elevator rapidly climbed toward the executive floors.
He crossed his arms over his chest with his mind piecing together the logistical nightmare of what they were currently doing.

"Evelyn, explain something to me," Silas demanded quietly, his voice low so the security crystals wouldn’t pick up the audio. "How the hell do you manage to make all of this money look entirely legal on paper without revealing that you are actually Lord Sky?"
He knew she used a male disguise artifact and voice modulators on her streams.
But banking required deep verification.

"And furthermore," Silas pressed, "why does the Valoria Bank just blindly go along with transferring seventy-five million credits from a mysterious stream account without raising massive red flags with like anyone?"
Evelyn stepped closer to him in the cramped elevator, leaning in so she could whisper directly into his ear.

"It’s called corporate layering, Silas," Evelyn explained softly, her brilliant mind flexing its corporate muscles. "I don’t just dump all my stream revenue into a single savings account under my real name... I use Jax, my underground broker, to filter the capital through dozens of offshore shell companies located in the neutral zones."
She smirked proudly, tapping her datapad against her leg.

"On paper, the bank doesn’t see Evelyn the Lord, or Lord Sky the streamer," she continued whispering. "They see a massive diversified business mogul who controls a vast network of mercenary guilds and resource extraction fronts... They don’t ask questions because my shell companies pay astronomical consistent taxes to the city."
Silas listened intently to her brilliant financial maneuvering.
As she whispered, he couldn’t help but notice the scent wafting from her breath.
The mixture of the cheap toxic tobacco she constantly smoked, combined with the lingering sweetness of the frost-berry ice cream they had just eaten, was a truly chaotic experience.
Silas leaned back slightly, wrinkling his nose in blunt disgust.
"Your breath smells terrible," Silas stated, ruining the secretive spy moment.
Evelyn’s proud smirk instantly vanished.
Her dark eyes flared with sudden violent offense as she clenched her fist, stepping aggressively forward, looking ready to punch him squarely in his smug handsome face.
DING!
The elevator doors chimed and slid smoothly open, completely saving Silas from a domestic assault.
"You are a dead man," Evelyn hissed venomously under her breath as she stepped out into the plush carpeted executive hallway.
They were greeted by another receptionist, who quickly and respectfully escorted them down the wide corridor and opened the heavy double oak doors to the Branch Manager’s private office.
The office was breathtakingly luxurious.
The walls were lined with rare, imported mahogany bookshelves, and the floor was covered in a thick, sound-dampening magical rug.
Behind a massive, polished obsidian desk sat an older distinguished man with green hair and sharp intelligent eyes.
"Evelyn, my dear," the Manager greeted her warmly, standing up from his plush leather chair with a wide, welcoming smile.
"Mr. Thorne," Evelyn replied smoothly, entirely dropping her aggressive, hoodie-wearing persona and instantly slipping into the polished charismatic role of a corporate elite.
Silas watched the transformation with genuine respect. She navigated the treacherous waters of high-society business flawlessly.
"I will do the talking here," Evelyn muttered out of the corner of her mouth to Silas before stepping forward to shake the Manager’s hand.

"It is always a pleasure to see you," Mr. Thorne said, gesturing to the plush leather guest chairs in front of his desk. "Please, sit. Can I offer you a drink? I have a vintage elven wine that just arrived from the eastern border."
"That would be wonderful, thank you," Evelyn accepted graciously, taking a seat.
Silas sat down beside her, keeping his face neutral and stoic.
Mr. Thorne poured three crystal glasses of the glowing, amber-colored wine, sliding them across the obsidian desk. He sat back down, steepling his fingers together.

"So, Evelyn," Mr. Thorne began, his sharp eyes flicking briefly toward Silas. "My tellers downstairs informed me that you are requesting a rather substantial capital transfer today. Seventy-five million credits is not a sum we move lightly without understanding the nature of the business... The World Council auditors are incredibly strict this quarter."
Evelyn didn’t even flinch. She took a slow, elegant sip of her wine, setting the crystal glass down gently.

"It is a straightforward corporate acquisition, Mr. Thorne," Evelyn lied smoothly, her voice radiating confident authority. She gestured gracefully toward Silas. "This is Silas Graves... His developing territory in the outer sectors deals heavily in rare resource extraction. Specifically, high-grade mythril and obsidian."
Mr. Thorne raised an eyebrow, looking at Silas with newfound professional respect. "Is that so?"

"Indeed," Evelyn continued flawlessly, weaving her fabricated excuse. "Over the past few months, my logistics companies have supplied his remote territory with quite a lot of heavy machinery, refined fuel, and specialized mercenary contracts to secure his borders. This transfer is simply the final consolidated payout for those accumulated resource debts."
Silas sat perfectly still, actively trying not to look impressed. She was spinning a brilliant believable web of lies right to the manager’s face.

"I see," Mr. Thorne nodded slowly with his analytical mind processing the business logic. "A massive single-sum payout to avoid the recurring taxation fees of multiple smaller transfers. Very clever, Evelyn. Very efficient."
Mr. Thorne reached out and pulled a heavy, runic ledger toward himself, picking up a glowing stylus.
"Well, given your flawless credit history with our institution, and the clear business utility of this transaction, I see no reason to delay," Mr. Thorne declared warmly.
He rapidly signed his name across the digital ledger, injecting a pulse of his own verification mana into the system.

"I am authorizing the transfer immediately," the Manager confirmed, pushing a button on his desk. "I will let you execute the final prompt on your end without freezing the holding accounts for review."
Evelyn smiled brightly, her shoulders dropping a fraction of an inch in sheer relief.
"Thank you, Mr. Thorne. You are a lifesaver," Evelyn said graciously.
The tension of the meeting finally broken, Evelyn instinctively reached into the deep pocket of her gray hoodie.
She pulled out her slim silver cigarette case and her plasma lighter. She popped a cigarette between her lips and flicked the lighter.
FWOOSH!
She took a deep drag, exhaling a thin stream of gray smoke into the luxurious, air-conditioned office.
Mr. Thorne stopped smiling. The older man leaned back in his leather chair, looking at her with a gentle frown.
"Evelyn," Mr. Thorne admonished her softly. "That smoking really isn’t good for your health, my dear. You have far too bright of a future ahead of you to ruin your lungs with that terrible habit."
Evelyn paused, staring at the glowing cherry of the cigarette. Her dark eyes clouded briefly with a heavy, unspoken burden.
"I know, Mr. Thorne," Evelyn replied quietly, her voice losing its corporate polish for just a second. "I know."
She picked up her datapad from the desk.
She rapidly punched in her complex encrypted security codes and hit the final confirmation button.
BEEP!
The transfer went through instantly.
Sitting next to her, Silas felt a subtle vibration from his own coat pocket.
He pulled out his smartphone, unlocking the screen to check the Valoria Banking app.
The screen glowed brightly.
[ACCOUNT BALANCE: 75,995,500 SC]
Silas stared at the string of zeroes.
His jaw physically went slack, his mouth dropping slightly open in disbelief.
Seeing seventy-five million credits sitting liquid in his own personal account completely short-circuited his brain.
He was quite rich.
Evelyn quickly stood up from her chair, grabbing Silas by the sleeve of his trench coat before he could say anything stupid.
"Thank you again for your time, Mr. Thorne," Evelyn bid her farewells, firmly dragging the stunned Warlord toward the heavy oak doors. "We have to run. Business never sleeps."
"Safe travels, you two," the Manager waved kindly as they left.
Evelyn dragged Silas aggressively down the executive hallway, pulling him all the way to the elevators and shoving him inside.
The doors closed, sealing them in the descending box.
Evelyn immediately turned to Silas, leaning in close with a massive, incredibly smug grin plastered across her pale face.
"So," Evelyn whispered conspiratorially, her dark eyes shining with victory. "How does it feel finally having that sort of real money, Lord?"
Silas couldn’t even hide his genuine satisfaction.
He looked at the phone screen again with a sharp grin spreading across his face.
"It feels pretty damn good," Silas admitted honestly.

"That is exactly what top-tier Sovereign Network streams pay when you know how to work the algorithm," Evelyn boasted proudly, thoroughly vindicated by his reaction. "Maybe we could do more organized combat collabs in the future. We make a lethal team on camera."
Silas looked at Evelyn. He thought about the massive viewer engagement they had pulled yesterday.
It was a literal gold mine.
"Agreed," Silas nodded firmly, cementing their chaotic business partnership.
Evelyn’s face lit up with pure joy.
She aggressively pumped both of her fists high into the air, completely dropping her mature stoic persona.
"Fuck yes!" Evelyn cheered loudly in the empty elevator, doing a tiny, highly energetic victory jump.
Silas watched her celebrate.
Despite Evelyn constantly trying to act a lot more mature and ruthless than she actually was, she was still quite childish deep down.
She got genuinely excited over wins, and she cared about the people she worked with.
Silas realized, with a warm smirk, that he actually really liked that specific trait about her.
It made her human.
The elevator doors chimed and opened to the main lobby.
They walked briskly through the grand marble hall, passing the miserable lines of people, and stepped back out into the bright Valoria City sunlight.
"Alright, rich boy," Evelyn teased as they stood on the top step of the bank. "What do you want to use your massive pile of money to do first?"
Silas didn’t answer verbally. He pulled out his phone, opened the premium transportation app, and began typing rapidly.

"I am ordering a proper luxury guild cab," Silas declared firmly, making sure to pronounce the words clearly and deliberately to mock her earlier frugality. "I am not riding in another yellow death trap."
Evelyn’s jaw dropped. "You are wasting credits already?!"
"I have millions of them," Silas shot back. "I am buying legroom."
Evelyn aggressively crossed her arms, glaring at him. "You are an arrogant fucker."
Less than two minutes later, a sleek armored dark silver transport vehicle glided smoothly up to the curb.
It looked like a miniature tank designed for high-society comfort. The doors slid open automatically with a quiet hiss of pressurized air.
Silas and Evelyn climbed into the spacious incredibly comfortable leather back seats.
The air conditioning blew perfectly chilled, odorless air.
The driver, a professional separated by a thick pane of bulletproof glass, looked at them through the rearview mirror.
"Where are we heading today?" the driver asked respectfully.
Evelyn leaned forward slightly, her dark eyes narrowing with seriousness.
"Shogitown," Evelyn instructed cleanly, naming the bustling neon-lit undercity district of Valoria. "We have someone important to go meet down there."

chapters.title: Chapter 346: Shogitown [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: The sleek silver luxury transport glided through the bustling streets of Valoria City with the silent predatory grace of a deep-sea leviathan.
The chassis was forged from dense, refined mythril-alloy, designed specifically to withstand direct artillery fire from monster ambushes or spells just in case.
The tinted magically reinforced windows completely blocked out the harsh glare of the city lights, creating a dark serene environment in the spacious back seat.
The climate control system hummed with a quiet hiss of pressurized air, pumping a perfectly chilled breeze through the immaculate leather cabin.
Silas sat comfortably against the plush upholstery with his broad shoulders relaxing slightly as the vehicle navigated the complex streets of the metropolis.
He let his golden-ringed eyes drift toward the passing scenery outside.
The towering, pristine skyscrapers of the central commercial district were slowly giving way to denser and more aggressively packed architecture.
Beside him, Evelyn sat with her arms firmly crossed over her oversized gray hoodie with her knees pulled together in the massive space.
She looked out of place in the cab.
Despite her profound wealth and her status as a legendary streamer, she carried the tense coiled posture of a cornered street fighter.
She kept her dark eyes locked intensely on the GPS navigation display hovering near the driver’s partition, mentally calculating their exact coordinates.
"Approaching the drop-off sector now, Honored Lords," the driver announced.
The man was a professional driver, separated from them by a thick pane of enchanted bulletproof glass.
He checked his rearview mirror, offering a polite nod.

"We are entering the perimeter of Shogitown. Standard guild protocols prohibit luxury transports from idling in the central alleys due to the elevated risk of magical vandalism... I will have to drop you at the main crossing."
"That is fine," Evelyn instructed cleanly, her voice lacking any sort of warmth. "Just get us to the curb without drawing unnecessary attention."
The heavy transport slowed to a halt as the anti-gravitational tires settling firmly onto the damp cobblestone pavement with a soft thud.
Silas reached into the deep pocket of his dark trench coat.

He bypassed the phone that currently held his staggering new seventy-five million credit fortune and instead, his fingers brushed against a small, folded stack of physical paper cash he kept around for minor undercity transactions.
’It seems like that woman didn’t use my money... thankfully...’
He pulled out a few crisp bills, leaned forward, and smoothly slid the currency through the narrow transaction slot in the glass divider.
"Keep the change," Silas told the driver.
He didn’t wait for a receipt or a formal acknowledgment. He reached out and pushed the armored passenger door open, stepping out into the air.
"Thank you, sir," the driver replied, pocketing the cash with a genuine smile.
He looked back at the towering young man and the grumpy hoodie-wearing girl sliding across the leather seats to follow him. "You two have a wonderful evening down here. Enjoy your date!"
Evelyn, who was currently stepping out of the vehicle with one foot on the pavement, instantly froze in place.
Her pale face flushed a vivid furious shade of crimson at the casual assumption.
She slammed the heavy armored door shut with a violent burst of physical strength, glaring fiercely at the tinted windows of the transport.

"Die in a ditch, you overpriced corporate hack!" Evelyn cursed loudly, flipping off the retreating vehicle as it merged seamlessly back into the chaotic flow of city traffic and disappeared around a corner.
Silas stepped fully onto the sidewalk, completely ignoring her aggressive uncalled-for outburst.
He closed his eyes for a brief second and took a long, deep breath, letting the unique atmosphere of the district wash over him.
The air here was an overwhelming experience.
It was thick with the scent of sweet perfumes, deep-fried street meats, roasted spices, and the unmistakable feeling of mana leaking from illegal workshops.
They had arrived in Shogitown.
Silas opened his eyes, looking up at the sprawling magnificent undercity district.

It was widely considered the gritty beating heart of Valoria City’s eastern quadrant, a place where the strict suffocating laws of the World Council blurred into the chaotic gray areas of syndicate rule.
It was undeniably dangerous, but it was also incredibly beautiful.
Towering skyscrapers constructed from dark obsidian glass and rusted steel loomed overhead, their sleek modern surfaces completely covered in massive glowing neon signs.
Holographic advertisements flashed in a dozen different languages, promoting everything from cheap healing potions to black-market cybernetic enhancements.
But nestled directly beneath the imposing oppressive corporate architecture was a sprawling maze of traditional aesthetics.
Ornate wooden eaves with elegantly curved rooftops jutted out precariously over the narrow winding alleyways.
Bright red paper lanterns swayed gently in the evening breeze, strung together by thick black cables.
They cast a warm intimate glow over the damp, rain-slicked cobblestone streets, reflecting beautifully in the shallow puddles left behind by the afternoon drizzle.
And falling softly through the neon-lit air, drifting on the city wind, were thousands of delicate pink petals.
They were not cheap holographic projections or hard-light illusions.
They were real cherry blossoms.

They bloomed vibrantly from massive, magically enhanced trees that had been deliberately and stubbornly cultivated to weave their thick roots directly through the concrete and steel of the city infrastructure.
The petals drifted down gracefully in the fading sunlight, landing on the pavement, resting on the glowing hoods of hovering sports cars, and catching in the hair of the passing pedestrians.
It was a perfect fusion of ancient tradition and modern cyberpunk grit.
’And other cities are more advanced than this...’

As Silas and Evelyn stood near the curb, taking in the bustling shoulder-to-shoulder crowds of masked mercenaries, eager tourists, street vendors, and exhausted corporate workers, a young local boy wearing a traditional tunic over modern streetwear jogged past them.
"Moon Festival tonight!" the boy shouted energetically, his voice cracking slightly with excitement.
Without breaking his stride, the kid shoved a glossy brightly colored paper pamphlet directly into Silas’s chest before disappearing into the flowing crowd.
Silas blinked, his reflexes easily catching the paper before it could fall to the wet pavement.
He looked down at the pamphlet in his large calloused hand.
It featured a beautiful hand-drawn illustration of the Shogitown central plaza illuminated by thousands of floating paper lanterns.

Bold stylized text advertised an array of evening celebrations, including massive street food stalls, local martial arts tournaments, and traditional music performances that were scheduled to run late into the night.
Evelyn leaned over, peering critically at the paper in his hand. She let out a soft scoff.

"Tourist trash," Evelyn dismissed it instantly, adjusting the baggy sleeves of her oversized gray hoodie. "Come on, Silas. His place is located a few blocks deeper into the district, down in the black-market tech sectors. We need to move right now before the enforcers start their evening patrols and lock down the main thoroughfares."
Silas didn’t move.
He kept his golden-ringed eyes locked firmly on the glossy pamphlet with his thumb gently tracing the edge of the paper.
"We should stay for a bit," Silas suggested, his deep voice carrying a strange uncharacteristic softness that entirely lacked his usual edge.
Evelyn stopped walking.
She turned around, looking at him with her dark eyes narrowed in genuine confusion.
This was the exact same ruthless guy who had just butchered a mobilized army in the Sovereign Realm which was hers without breaking a sweat.
Why on earth was he suddenly interested in a noisy crowded local street fair?
"Are you out of your mind?" Evelyn asked bluntly, placing her hands on her hips. "Did you forget what we came here to do? We don’t have time for a festival."
Silas looked up from the paper.
His gaze swept slowly over the vibrant neon-lit stalls lining the bustling street.
The air was thick with the mouth-watering scent of grilled kraken skewers, sweet bean pastries, and roasted chestnuts.

"During the years that I was attending Valoria Academy," Silas explained quietly, his voice steady but carrying a weight of nostalgia. "I always wanted to come down to Shogitown... The other kids in my group, the ones with noble backing and rich parents, would constantly talk about the evening celebrations here. They talked endlessly about the atmosphere, the carnival games, and especially the food."
He folded the pamphlet neatly along its crease and slid it carefully into the deep pocket of his dark trench coat.

"But I never came," Silas admitted with a smirk touching his lips as he remembered his past. "I was too busy working three separate dead-end shifts at the lower-tier processing plants just to keep the lights on in our apartment for Lia... I didn’t have the disposable credits to waste on train tickets, let alone expensive street meat. I just looked at the holograms online. But now..."
He reached into his pocket with his fingers brushing against the cold metal of his phone.
"...now I actually have the money. I have more money than I know what to do with and I just want to see what all the fuss was about. Just for a little while."
Evelyn stared at him.
For a fraction of a second, a flicker of genuine empathy crossed her pale tired face.
She understood the grinding and humiliating weight of poverty better than almost anyone else in the Sovereign Realm.
She knew exactly what it felt like to stand on the outside looking in, desperately wanting to participate in a world that demanded wealth you didn’t possess.
But then, the suffocating stress of the day violently crashed back down onto her narrow shoulders.
She had watched her Vanguard bleed out in the mud.
Her First Hero had almost died. Her nerves were completely shot, running on pure adrenaline and lingering panic as her patience was entirely nonexistent right now.
Evelyn sneered, her deep-seated defense mechanisms instantly flaring up into aggressive hostility.

"Didn’t you explicitly state back at the bank that you wanted to get your fake identity sorted out as fast as possible?" Evelyn snapped coldly, crossing her arms defensively over her chest. "Why the hell would we waste our valuable time staying at some crowded noisy event? We have actual business to conduct, Silas."
Silas frowned slightly at her sudden tone.
"It would only be for an hour, Evelyn. He isn’t going anywhere."

"If you desperately wanted to go on a cute little festival date," Evelyn continued ruthlessly, her voice dripping with uncalled-for spite as she projected her own bitter internal frustrations directly onto him. "You should have just stayed at your pristine apartment and gone out with the rich girl you are currently ripping off."
Silas completely froze in place on the cobblestone street.
The casual conversational warmth entirely vanished from his demeanor, replaced instantly by a cold look.
His broad shoulders went rigid under his heavy leather coat, and his golden-ringed eyes darkened with sudden confusion.
"Ripping off?" Silas repeated. "What exactly are you talking about, Evelyn?"
Why was she in a tantrum too?
Evelyn didn’t answer him. She just turned her back, shoving her hands deep into her hoodie pockets, and began storming off down the crowded neon-lit sidewalk with angry stomping strides.
Silas let out an irritated breath.
’Why are women so complicated...?’
He lengthened his stride, effortlessly jogging through the dense flow of pedestrians to keep up with her frantic pace.
They passed by beautiful, ornate wooden shrines tucked cleanly between modern reinforced weapon shops, the stunning architectural contrast of the city lost on them as the tension thickened.
"Evelyn, wait," Silas demanded, easily catching up to her shoulder and matching her pace. "Explain what you meant by that. Who am I ripping off?"
Evelyn kept her dark eyes locked firmly on the wet pavement ahead, her jaw clenched tight.

"Well, you clearly have a rich billionaire heiress fawning all over you back at your house," Evelyn stated bitterly, her words spilling out in a rapid angry stream. "I saw her looking at you... Go on a date here with her or something. Play your little seduction games to fund your territory but do not involve me in your kid nonsense. I am a Lord, not a tour guide for your childhood fantasies."
Silas quieted down instantly.

sentences.text: The sleek silver luxury transport glided through the bustling streets of Valoria City with the silent predatory grace of a deep-sea leviathan.
The chassis was forged from dense, refined mythril-alloy, designed specifically to withstand direct artillery fire from monster ambushes or spells just in case.
The tinted magically reinforced windows completely blocked out the harsh glare of the city lights, creating a dark serene environment in the spacious back seat.
The climate control system hummed with a quiet hiss of pressurized air, pumping a perfectly chilled breeze through the immaculate leather cabin.
Silas sat comfortably against the plush upholstery with his broad shoulders relaxing slightly as the vehicle navigated the complex streets of the metropolis.
He let his golden-ringed eyes drift toward the passing scenery outside.
The towering, pristine skyscrapers of the central commercial district were slowly giving way to denser and more aggressively packed architecture.
Beside him, Evelyn sat with her arms firmly crossed over her oversized gray hoodie with her knees pulled together in the massive space.
She looked out of place in the cab.
Despite her profound wealth and her status as a legendary streamer, she carried the tense coiled posture of a cornered street fighter.
She kept her dark eyes locked intensely on the GPS navigation display hovering near the driver’s partition, mentally calculating their exact coordinates.
"Approaching the drop-off sector now, Honored Lords," the driver announced.
The man was a professional driver, separated from them by a thick pane of enchanted bulletproof glass.
He checked his rearview mirror, offering a polite nod.
"We are entering the perimeter of Shogitown.
Standard guild protocols prohibit luxury transports from idling in the central alleys due to the elevated risk of magical vandalism...
I will have to drop you at the main crossing."
"That is fine," Evelyn instructed cleanly, her voice lacking any sort of warmth.
"Just get us to the curb without drawing unnecessary attention."
The heavy transport slowed to a halt as the anti-gravitational tires settling firmly onto the damp cobblestone pavement with a soft thud.
Silas reached into the deep pocket of his dark trench coat.

He bypassed the phone that currently held his staggering new seventy-five million credit fortune and instead, his fingers brushed against a small, folded stack of physical paper cash he kept around for minor undercity transactions.
’It seems like that woman didn’t use my money... thankfully...’
He pulled out a few crisp bills, leaned forward, and smoothly slid the currency through the narrow transaction slot in the glass divider.
"Keep the change," Silas told the driver.
He didn’t wait for a receipt or a formal acknowledgment.
He reached out and pushed the armored passenger door open, stepping out into the air.
"Thank you, sir," the driver replied, pocketing the cash with a genuine smile.
He looked back at the towering young man and the grumpy hoodie-wearing girl sliding across the leather seats to follow him.
"You two have a wonderful evening down here.
Enjoy your date!"
Evelyn, who was currently stepping out of the vehicle with one foot on the pavement, instantly froze in place.
Her pale face flushed a vivid furious shade of crimson at the casual assumption.
She slammed the heavy armored door shut with a violent burst of physical strength, glaring fiercely at the tinted windows of the transport.

"Die in a ditch, you overpriced corporate hack!" Evelyn cursed loudly, flipping off the retreating vehicle as it merged seamlessly back into the chaotic flow of city traffic and disappeared around a corner.
Silas stepped fully onto the sidewalk, completely ignoring her aggressive uncalled-for outburst.
He closed his eyes for a brief second and took a long, deep breath, letting the unique atmosphere of the district wash over him.
The air here was an overwhelming experience.
It was thick with the scent of sweet perfumes, deep-fried street meats, roasted spices, and the unmistakable feeling of mana leaking from illegal workshops.
They had arrived in Shogitown.
Silas opened his eyes, looking up at the sprawling magnificent undercity district.

It was widely considered the gritty beating heart of Valoria City’s eastern quadrant, a place where the strict suffocating laws of the World Council blurred into the chaotic gray areas of syndicate rule.
It was undeniably dangerous, but it was also incredibly beautiful.
Towering skyscrapers constructed from dark obsidian glass and rusted steel loomed overhead, their sleek modern surfaces completely covered in massive glowing neon signs.
Holographic advertisements flashed in a dozen different languages, promoting everything from cheap healing potions to black-market cybernetic enhancements.
But nestled directly beneath the imposing oppressive corporate architecture was a sprawling maze of traditional aesthetics.
Ornate wooden eaves with elegantly curved rooftops jutted out precariously over the narrow winding alleyways.
Bright red paper lanterns swayed gently in the evening breeze, strung together by thick black cables.
They cast a warm intimate glow over the damp, rain-slicked cobblestone streets, reflecting beautifully in the shallow puddles left behind by the afternoon drizzle.
And falling softly through the neon-lit air, drifting on the city wind, were thousands of delicate pink petals.
They were not cheap holographic projections or hard-light illusions.
They were real cherry blossoms.

They bloomed vibrantly from massive, magically enhanced trees that had been deliberately and stubbornly cultivated to weave their thick roots directly through the concrete and steel of the city infrastructure.
The petals drifted down gracefully in the fading sunlight, landing on the pavement, resting on the glowing hoods of hovering sports cars, and catching in the hair of the passing pedestrians.
It was a perfect fusion of ancient tradition and modern cyberpunk grit.
’And other cities are more advanced than this...’

As Silas and Evelyn stood near the curb, taking in the bustling shoulder-to-shoulder crowds of masked mercenaries, eager tourists, street vendors, and exhausted corporate workers, a young local boy wearing a traditional tunic over modern streetwear jogged past them.
"Moon Festival tonight!" the boy shouted energetically, his voice cracking slightly with excitement.
Without breaking his stride, the kid shoved a glossy brightly colored paper pamphlet directly into Silas’s chest before disappearing into the flowing crowd.
Silas blinked, his reflexes easily catching the paper before it could fall to the wet pavement.
He looked down at the pamphlet in his large calloused hand.
It featured a beautiful hand-drawn illustration of the Shogitown central plaza illuminated by thousands of floating paper lanterns.

Bold stylized text advertised an array of evening celebrations, including massive street food stalls, local martial arts tournaments, and traditional music performances that were scheduled to run late into the night.
Evelyn leaned over, peering critically at the paper in his hand.
She let out a soft scoff.
"Tourist trash," Evelyn dismissed it instantly, adjusting the baggy sleeves of her oversized gray hoodie.
"Come on, Silas.
His place is located a few blocks deeper into the district, down in the black-market tech sectors.
We need to move right now before the enforcers start their evening patrols and lock down the main thoroughfares."
Silas didn’t move.
He kept his golden-ringed eyes locked firmly on the glossy pamphlet with his thumb gently tracing the edge of the paper.
"We should stay for a bit," Silas suggested, his deep voice carrying a strange uncharacteristic softness that entirely lacked his usual edge.
Evelyn stopped walking.
She turned around, looking at him with her dark eyes narrowed in genuine confusion.
This was the exact same ruthless guy who had just butchered a mobilized army in the Sovereign Realm which was hers without breaking a sweat.
Why on earth was he suddenly interested in a noisy crowded local street fair?
