chapters.title: Chapter 347: Masks And Smoke [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: His mind rapidly analyzed her words, her rigid body language, and the sudden irrational spike in her aggression.
’Fuu... so complicated...’
He didn’t understand why she was so incredibly annoyed about Harper’s presence at his apartment, or why she was suddenly lashing out with such venom over a simple request to get some street food.
Her logic was flawed, built on incorrect assumptions about his relationship with the woman.
But his common sense quickly kicked in, overriding his immediate desire to argue.
Engaging in a screaming match with a stressed girl in the middle of a crowded undercity street was a terrible decision.
It would draw unwanted attention. It was clearly her own deeply personal issue, and pushing her on it would only make things exponentially worse.
Silas let out a slow sigh, deliberately dropping his dominant, intimidating aura.
He shoved his hands into his coat pockets.

"Well, sorry then," Silas told her calmly, keeping his voice neutral and devoid of anger. "I won’t bring it up again... Let’s just go meet him and get this over with so you can go back to your fortress."
He didn’t yell and he didn’t try to defend his honor against her wild accusations.
Would she even listen?
Evelyn stopped walking.
She stood frozen in the exact middle of the sidewalk, letting the dense crowds of masked people part and flow around her like water around a stone.
She slowly turned back to face him as she reached into her pocket with trembling fingers, pulling out her slim silver cigarette case and her trusted plasma lighter.
"Thank you..."
She popped a pristine white cigarette between her lips and struck the flame, taking a desperate drag that burned the paper halfway down in a single breath.
FWOOSH!
She puffed a thick cloud of gray smoke into the neon-lit air, her dark eyes looking up at Silas’s calm completely unaffected face.
He just looked tired.

’It’s not his fault...’ Evelyn thought with a crushing wave of guilt instantly washing over her chest. ’Why did I say that? Why am I acting like such a bitch to the guy who literally saved my best friend’s life?’
She looked down at her battered mud-stained combat boots, her throat tightening with sudden unshed emotion.
The honest ugly truth was that she didn’t care about Harper Whitmore. She didn’t care about his romantic life or how he funded his territory.
The real reason she had snapped, the exact reason she was so irrationally defensive about the Shogitown festival, was born from her own personal failures.
She had desperately wanted to take her younger brother here on several occasions.
For the past three years, ever since she had begun making real money in the Sovereign Realm and secured her position as a top-tier Lord, she had tried to bring him to the Moon Festival.
She wanted to buy him expensive food, win him cheap carnival prizes, and show him that his older sister could finally provide for him.
She wanted to share her success with the only family she had left.
But he had repeatedly refused. He never wanted to come with her for some reason.

He always pushed her away with flimsy excuses, preferring to spend his time studying or hanging out with his normal civilian college friends rather than the sister who was actively bleeding in wars just to pay his tuition fees.
It was something that quietly devastated her soul.

It pissed her off, but mostly, it just broke her heart. And seeing Silas... a good brother who clearly loved his sibling and just wanted to experience a simple nostalgic festival had violently triggered her own deep-seated inadequacies.
Evelyn let out a long shaky sigh with the lingering smoke curling softly around her messy black hair.
She looked up.
Across the narrow cobblestone street, illuminated warmly by a string of bright red paper lanterns, she spotted a small weathered wooden cart.
An elderly man with a kind face and a thick gray beard was actively arranging a vast impressive display of traditional undercity masks.
Evelyn made a rapid decision to mend the bridge she had just tried to burn.
’I’m a dumbass I know...’
She suddenly reached out, grabbing the thick fabric of Silas’s trench coat sleeve in a vice-like grip, and pulled him firmly toward the street crossing.
"We are going over there," Evelyn instructed with her voice completely losing its venomous edge, replaced by a forced neutrality.
"Why?" Silas asked, allowing himself to be dragged through the gap in the bustling traffic without resistance.

"Because we will definitely need masks for this whole thing," Evelyn explained with a whisper, pointing a slender finger at the wooden cart. "Shogitown is beautiful and lively on the main streets, but the underbelly where he operates is incredibly dangerous... There are spies, rival syndicate thugs, and high-tier bounty hunters everywhere. If they recognize us walking together in the open, we might be dragged into something we don’t want to be in."
Silas processed the sound tactical logic and nodded in agreement. "Fair point. Lead the way..."
They walked up to the brightly lit wooden stall.
The cart was covered from edge to edge in an impressive array of beautifully crafted masks.
They ranged from terrifying demonic faces with elongated fangs to elegant painted animal visages.
They were all forged from lightweight durable alloys, designed not just for festival aesthetics, but to withstand minor impacts in a street fight.
The elderly vendor looked up from his polishing cloth.
His wrinkled eyes crinkled into a massive welcoming smile as he took in the tall, devastatingly handsome teenager and the petite dark-haired girl holding onto his sleeve.

"Welcome, welcome!" the old man greeted them warmly, his voice raspy but full of vibrant life. "Please, take a look at my humble shop! I craft all of these by hand using salvaged scrap metal from the northern industrial forges."
He gestured proudly to the sprawling display.
"Pick whichever masks you want, kids," the vendor offered generously, winking conspiratorially at Silas. "It is completely on the house for such a beautiful striking couple like yourselves!"
Silas blinked in genuine surprise.
He reached into his coat pocket, fully intending to pull out his cash and pay the man a fair, generous price for his hard work and craftsmanship.
He had seventy-five million credits sitting in his digital bank account... he was not going to take charity from a hardworking street vendor trying to make a living.
"Thank you, sir, but I can pa—"
BUMP!
Evelyn violently slammed her hip directly into Silas’s side, cutting him off mid-sentence with a sharp bruising impact.
Silas grunted, looking down at her in bewilderment.
Evelyn was staring right back up into his eyes with an expression of intense determination.
’Are you stupid?!’ Evelyn’s dark eyes screamed at him silently, her glare practically piercing his skull. ’It is free stuff!’
Silas stared at her, genuinely struggling to comprehend the absurdity of her mindset.

How the hell could a multi-millionaire, a Lord who commanded an entire mechanical fortress and controlled massive offshore bank accounts, care so deeply about saving fifty credits on a street mask?𝚏𝗿𝗲𝐞𝐰𝚎𝕓𝐧𝚘𝘃𝗲𝐥.𝐜𝚘𝕞
Her unrelenting stinginess was a psychological marvel that defied all known logic.
Evelyn didn’t wait for him to ruin the grift with his noble intentions.
She instantly wrapped her arms tightly around Silas’s muscular bicep, leaning her head affectionately against his broad shoulder.
She looked at the old man with a sickeningly sweet fabricated smile that radiated pure innocent adoration.

"Oh, you are far too kind, sir!" Evelyn chirped, completely altering her vocal pitch to sound like a sweet naive civilian girl. "We would love a pair of masks! We are actually out celebrating our anniversary today, and money has been a bit tight!"
Silas’s jaw tightened, his pride screaming in loud protest as he was dragged forcefully into her shameless petty con.

"Is that so?" the old man beamed, resting his calloused hands on the wooden cart. "Young love is a truly beautiful thing in this harsh unforgiving city. Are you two planning on tying the knot anytime soon?"

"We are eventually going to get married, yes," Evelyn lied flawlessly, squeezing Silas’s arm even tighter to silently warn him not to blow her cover. "He is saving up for a ring working brutal double shifts down at the shipping docks."
Silas felt a massive sweatdrop form on the back of his neck.

He was a Gold Core Lord who had literally just slaughtered an army on live television, and he was currently standing on a street corner pretending to be a broke overworked dockworker just so his companion could score free festival masks.

"Wonderful!" the old man clapped his hands together, his eyes shining with genuine heartfelt happiness. "I truly hope my own granddaughter can find a happy supportive relationship just like yours one day. Go ahead, choose any masks you like, dear. Take your time."
Evelyn instantly dropped the sweet innocent persona.
Her eyes hardened, scanning the vast cart with the ruthless efficiency of a quartermaster surveying an armory.
She selected two specific pieces, examining the alloy density and the strap mechanisms.
For Silas, she chose a dark gunmetal gray Oni mask.
It featured sharp, menacing silver fangs and jagged metallic horns that swept backward, perfectly matching his intimidating broad-shouldered aesthetic.
For herself, she selected a sleek predatory Kitsune mask. It was painted in stark, glossy white and deep crimson, with narrow angled eye slits that projected an unreadable aura.
They both slid the masks over their faces, securing the leather straps behind their heads.
The cool metal instantly conformed to their features, hiding their true identities behind the traditional undercity visages.
"Thank you, sir," Silas muttered through the Oni mask, feeling a deep lingering guilt about the daylight robbery they had just committed. "Have a good night."
They turned to merge back into the crowd, but the old man suddenly raised a weathered hand.

"Hold on a second, young lady," the vendor called out, his eyes narrowing slightly as he looked at the slim silver cigarette clamped tightly between Evelyn’s lips beneath the lower rim of her new mask.
Evelyn paused with her shoulders tensing.
She braced herself for the usual, exhausting lecture about the dangers of smoking and lung cancer that she received from almost every civilian she met on the street.
Instead, the old man leaned over the wooden counter, sniffing the air like a seasoned experienced connoisseur.

"That is a Silver-Leaf imported blend, isn’t it?" the vendor asked, looking thoroughly impressed by the aroma. "You have incredibly good taste for someone so young... But those mass-produced sticks burn a bit too fast in the heavy city humidity."
He reached beneath his wooden counter, rummaging around for a moment before pulling out a small beautifully carved wooden box.
He flipped the brass latch open, revealing a row of thick premium undercity cigars wrapped tightly in dark mana-infused leaves.

"Here," the old man offered generously, pulling one of the thick cigars out and holding it across the cart. "Take one of my personal stock... It’s a Black-Ash root blend. You can only get them down here in the deep sectors of Shogitown. It burns slow, tastes like dark roasted coffee, and calms the nerves instantly."
Evelyn’s dark eyes widened to comical proportions behind her Kitsune mask.
She practically drooled.
The premium sought-after Black-Ash tobacco was a legendary luxury among heavy smokers.
It was incredibly rare, fiercely expensive, and almost impossible to find outside of syndicate-controlled black markets.
Without a single second of hesitation, Evelyn literally opened her mouth and let her current half-smoked cigarette fall directly onto her own stomach.
The lit cherry bounced harmlessly off her heavy gray hoodie and landed with a quiet sizzle on the wet cobblestone pavement.
She lunged forward, grabbing the premium Black-Ash cigar from the old man’s hand with desperate speed, and immediately stuffed it securely into the deep zippered pocket of her cargo pants.
"Thank you!" Evelyn bowed respectfully, her voice filled with genuine, hell almost religious reverence.
Silas watched the entire exchange with absolute, unfiltered disgust.
In this world, smoking was legal as long as you possessed a verified city license, but Silas couldn’t stand the habit.

He possessed a Gold Core so his internal biology was refined to a state of near-perfection, meaning external toxins like nicotine or alcohol would burn out of his system before they could even affect his brain chemistry.
He literally couldn’t get a buzz if he tried.
’Still...’

There are spies, rival syndicate thugs, and high-tier bounty hunters everywhere.
If they recognize us walking together in the open, we might be dragged into something we don’t want to be in."
Silas processed the sound tactical logic and nodded in agreement.
"Fair point.
Lead the way..."
They walked up to the brightly lit wooden stall.
The cart was covered from edge to edge in an impressive array of beautifully crafted masks.
They ranged from terrifying demonic faces with elongated fangs to elegant painted animal visages.
They were all forged from lightweight durable alloys, designed not just for festival aesthetics, but to withstand minor impacts in a street fight.
The elderly vendor looked up from his polishing cloth.
His wrinkled eyes crinkled into a massive welcoming smile as he took in the tall, devastatingly handsome teenager and the petite dark-haired girl holding onto his sleeve.
"Welcome, welcome!" the old man greeted them warmly, his voice raspy but full of vibrant life.
"Please, take a look at my humble shop!
I craft all of these by hand using salvaged scrap metal from the northern industrial forges."
He gestured proudly to the sprawling display.
"Pick whichever masks you want, kids," the vendor offered generously, winking conspiratorially at Silas.
"It is completely on the house for such a beautiful striking couple like yourselves!"
Silas blinked in genuine surprise.
He reached into his coat pocket, fully intending to pull out his cash and pay the man a fair, generous price for his hard work and craftsmanship.
He had seventy-five million credits sitting in his digital bank account... he was not going to take charity from a hardworking street vendor trying to make a living.
"Thank you, sir, but I can pa—"
BUMP!
Evelyn violently slammed her hip directly into Silas’s side, cutting him off mid-sentence with a sharp bruising impact.
Silas grunted, looking down at her in bewilderment.
Evelyn was staring right back up into his eyes with an expression of intense determination.
’Are you stupid?!’ Evelyn’s dark eyes screamed at him silently, her glare practically piercing his skull. ’It is free stuff!’
Silas stared at her, genuinely struggling to comprehend the absurdity of her mindset.

How the hell could a multi-millionaire, a Lord who commanded an entire mechanical fortress and controlled massive offshore bank accounts, care so deeply about saving fifty credits on a street mask?𝚏𝗿𝗲𝐞𝐰𝚎𝕓𝐧𝚘𝘃𝗲𝐥.𝐜𝚘𝕞
Her unrelenting stinginess was a psychological marvel that defied all known logic.
Evelyn didn’t wait for him to ruin the grift with his noble intentions.
She instantly wrapped her arms tightly around Silas’s muscular bicep, leaning her head affectionately against his broad shoulder.
She looked at the old man with a sickeningly sweet fabricated smile that radiated pure innocent adoration.
"Oh, you are far too kind, sir!" Evelyn chirped, completely altering her vocal pitch to sound like a sweet naive civilian girl.
"We would love a pair of masks!
We are actually out celebrating our anniversary today, and money has been a bit tight!"
Silas’s jaw tightened, his pride screaming in loud protest as he was dragged forcefully into her shameless petty con.
"Is that so?" the old man beamed, resting his calloused hands on the wooden cart.
"Young love is a truly beautiful thing in this harsh unforgiving city.
Are you two planning on tying the knot anytime soon?"
"We are eventually going to get married, yes," Evelyn lied flawlessly, squeezing Silas’s arm even tighter to silently warn him not to blow her cover.
"He is saving up for a ring working brutal double shifts down at the shipping docks."
Silas felt a massive sweatdrop form on the back of his neck.

He was a Gold Core Lord who had literally just slaughtered an army on live television, and he was currently standing on a street corner pretending to be a broke overworked dockworker just so his companion could score free festival masks.
"Wonderful!" the old man clapped his hands together, his eyes shining with genuine heartfelt happiness.
"I truly hope my own granddaughter can find a happy supportive relationship just like yours one day.
Go ahead, choose any masks you like, dear.
Take your time."
Evelyn instantly dropped the sweet innocent persona.
Her eyes hardened, scanning the vast cart with the ruthless efficiency of a quartermaster surveying an armory.
She selected two specific pieces, examining the alloy density and the strap mechanisms.
For Silas, she chose a dark gunmetal gray Oni mask.
It featured sharp, menacing silver fangs and jagged metallic horns that swept backward, perfectly matching his intimidating broad-shouldered aesthetic.
For herself, she selected a sleek predatory Kitsune mask.
It was painted in stark, glossy white and deep crimson, with narrow angled eye slits that projected an unreadable aura.
They both slid the masks over their faces, securing the leather straps behind their heads.
The cool metal instantly conformed to their features, hiding their true identities behind the traditional undercity visages.
"Thank you, sir," Silas muttered through the Oni mask, feeling a deep lingering guilt about the daylight robbery they had just committed.
"Have a good night."
They turned to merge back into the crowd, but the old man suddenly raised a weathered hand.

"Hold on a second, young lady," the vendor called out, his eyes narrowing slightly as he looked at the slim silver cigarette clamped tightly between Evelyn’s lips beneath the lower rim of her new mask.
Evelyn paused with her shoulders tensing.
She braced herself for the usual, exhausting lecture about the dangers of smoking and lung cancer that she received from almost every civilian she met on the street.
Instead, the old man leaned over the wooden counter, sniffing the air like a seasoned experienced connoisseur.
"That is a Silver-Leaf imported blend, isn’t it?" the vendor asked, looking thoroughly impressed by the aroma.
"You have incredibly good taste for someone so young...
But those mass-produced sticks burn a bit too fast in the heavy city humidity."
He reached beneath his wooden counter, rummaging around for a moment before pulling out a small beautifully carved wooden box.
He flipped the brass latch open, revealing a row of thick premium undercity cigars wrapped tightly in dark mana-infused leaves.
"Here," the old man offered generously, pulling one of the thick cigars out and holding it across the cart.
"Take one of my personal stock...
It’s a Black-Ash root blend.
You can only get them down here in the deep sectors of Shogitown.
It burns slow, tastes like dark roasted coffee, and calms the nerves instantly."
Evelyn’s dark eyes widened to comical proportions behind her Kitsune mask.
She practically drooled.
The premium sought-after Black-Ash tobacco was a legendary luxury among heavy smokers.
It was incredibly rare, fiercely expensive, and almost impossible to find outside of syndicate-controlled black markets.
Without a single second of hesitation, Evelyn literally opened her mouth and let her current half-smoked cigarette fall directly onto her own stomach.
The lit cherry bounced harmlessly off her heavy gray hoodie and landed with a quiet sizzle on the wet cobblestone pavement.
She lunged forward, grabbing the premium Black-Ash cigar from the old man’s hand with desperate speed, and immediately stuffed it securely into the deep zippered pocket of her cargo pants.
"Thank you!" Evelyn bowed respectfully, her voice filled with genuine, hell almost religious reverence.
Silas watched the entire exchange with absolute, unfiltered disgust.
In this world, smoking was legal as long as you possessed a verified city license, but Silas couldn’t stand the habit.

He possessed a Gold Core so his internal biology was refined to a state of near-perfection, meaning external toxins like nicotine or alcohol would burn out of his system before they could even affect his brain chemistry.
He literally couldn’t get a buzz if he tried.
’Still...’

chapters.title: Chapter 348: Fake Couple Stuff [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: To him, it was an incredibly expensive hobby that did nothing but destroy the lungs and stamina of regular people.
And more importantly, it smelled terrible.
The thought of walking around smelling like a damp ashtray, like Evelyn constantly did, was a massive no-go.
They finally walked away from the wooden stall, wishing the old man well, and merged back into the dense flowing crowds of the neon-lit street.
The exact second they were safely out of the old man’s sight, Evelyn pulled the premium cigar from her pocket.
She placed the thick roll of dark leaves between her lips and ignited the tip with a quick flick of her plasma lighter.
She took a long deep drag, holding the rich smoke in her lungs before exhaling a thick fragrant cloud toward the glowing neon signs above.

"Oh my god," Evelyn groaned aloud in unfiltered bliss with her tense shoulders completely dropping as the premium tobacco worked its magic. "This is so much better. My last pair of expensive cartons finished yesterday, so I have been stuck smoking those cheap Silver-Leaf ones from the corner store."
Silas waved his large hand violently in front of his face, coughing as the thick pungent smoke hit his Oni mask.
"They smell even worse than the cheap ones," Silas roasted her bluntly, glaring at her through the narrow eye slits. "You smell like a burning tire factory mixed with burnt dirt."
Evelyn didn’t even flinch at the insult.
She just took another slow drag, looking up at him with a smug unbothered smirk beneath her Kitsune mask.

"Well, even a random old man running a street cart has better taste than you, Silas," Evelyn struck back flawlessly, puffing the dark smoke in his general direction. "You wouldn’t know real undercity culture if it punched you in your perfect sculpted jaw..."
Silas just shrugged off the insult.
Arguing with a severe addict currently holding a premium stash was a completely losing battle.
"Whatever," Silas dismissed the topic, checking the glowing street signs hanging from the buildings. "We better start looking for your contact now. Have you contacted him on the secure network yet?"
Evelyn reached into her cargo pocket for her phone, fully intending to pull up the coordinates for the cyber-rig.
But as she turned her head, her dark eyes locked onto a brightly lit stall situated just down the street.
It was a massive decorated ice cream stand, featuring glowing magical frost runes that kept the glass display cases perfectly chilled despite the body heat of the crowd.
Evelyn paused mid-step.
She remembered the genuine uncharacteristic excitement that had briefly lit up Silas’s face earlier when he had looked at the festival pamphlet.
She remembered the story of his poverty, and how brutally and unfairly she had shot him down, projecting her own deep-seated family trauma onto his simple innocent request.
The heavy, crushing guilt flared up in her chest again, hotter this time.
She was a Lord. She was supposed to be a leader, better than petty outbursts.
Evelyn suddenly reached out, grabbing the sleeve of Silas’s trench coat in a vice-like grip.
"Come on," Evelyn ordered firmly, pulling him forcefully down the sidewalk toward the glowing stall.
"What are you doing now?" Silas asked, stumbling slightly as she dragged his massive frame through a group of complaining tourists. "I thought we were in a rush to meet him."
"We are," Evelyn stated stubbornly, not looking back at him. "But we will enjoy a little bit of Shogitown before we go find him... Just for a few minutes."
Silas blinked his golden-ringed eyes behind his Oni mask, thoroughly bewildered by the sudden pivot.
He was experiencing severe emotional whiplash from her rapid unpredictable mood swings.
Minutes ago she was screaming at him about wasting valuable time on a festival, and now she was actively dragging him toward a dessert stall?
’So confusing...’
But, leaning into it, he simply let himself be dragged along without further complaint.
If the angry woman wanted ice cream, he wasn’t going to stop her.
They arrived at the glowing frost-warded stall. The display was filled with dozens of exotic and brightly colored flavors, ranging from glowing green matcha to deep purple void-berry.

The stall owner, a cheerful middle-aged woman wearing a pristine white apron over her clothes, looked at the terrifying broad-shouldered teenager in the dark Oni mask and the grumpy girl in the Kitsune mask dragging him by the sleeve.
"Hello there!" the woman greeted them happily, wiping down the counter. "Are you two looking for a sweet treat for the festival? We have a special discount running for couples tonight!"
Evelyn didn’t even hesitate to ruthlessly exploit the system twice in one single evening.
"We will take the couple’s special," Evelyn ordered smoothly, reaching into her pocket and pulling out a crumbled twenty-credit cash bill. She slapped the physical currency onto the metal counter.
The woman smiled brightly, taking the cash.
She grabbed her enchanted scoop and quickly formed an absurdly massive heart-shaped mound of ice cream onto a wide, reinforced waffle cone.
Half of the massive heart was a vibrant, glowing red strawberry flavor, and the other half was a pristine magically chilled white vanilla.
She handed the massive slightly ridiculous dessert directly over the counter to Evelyn.
"Here~ I hope you two enjoy it~"
Evelyn took the heavy cone and walked over to a quiet neon-lit concrete curb located a few feet away from the main flow of heavy foot traffic.
She sat down heavily on the damp curb, patting the empty space next to her.
Silas walked over with his dark trench coat billowing slightly in the evening wind, and sat down on the hard concrete beside her.
He looked at the massive heart-shaped ice cream cone resting in her hands.
Evelyn wordlessly held it out between them.
"Eat," Evelyn commanded bluntly.
Silas didn’t argue.
He leaned forward and took a bite from the white vanilla side.
The magical cold instantly soothed his dry throat, and the rich complex sweetness was genuinely incredible, far better than the mass-produced one sold in the city limits.
"This tastes really good," Silas admitted, nodding in genuine approval.
Evelyn took a bite from the red strawberry side, humming in quiet agreement.
They sat there in silence for a long moment.
They were two powerful Lords in Valoria City, wearing terrifying metal masks and awkwardly sharing a giant romantic ice cream cone on a dirty curb in the slums.
"It’s almost like a date...’ Evelyn thought, it was better than any one she had been on.
Evelyn leaned in to take another bite with her tongue swiping across the middle dividing line of the heart.

"Hey," Silas complained immediately, pulling his head back to avoid the cross-contamination. "Stay on your designated side... Do not touch my vanilla side, or lick my side with your terrible, toxic tobacco tongue."𝑓𝘳𝑒𝑒𝓌𝘦𝘣𝘯ℴ𝑣𝘦𝑙.𝘤𝑜𝑚
Evelyn’s eyes narrowed dangerously behind the slits of her Kitsune mask.
"I will literally cover the entire thing in cigar ash if you don’t shut up," Evelyn threatened fiercely, driving her sharp elbow violently into his ribs.
Silas grunted, chuckling softly at her aggression.
It was a strange unorthodox dynamic, but it was surprisingly comfortable.
They didn’t have to pretend to be perfect, untouchable nobles or ruthless stoic commanders around each other.
They could just be regular people from Earth.
They stood up from the curb, continuing to share the massive ice cream as they walked slowly down the crowded street with the neon lights reflecting beautifully off the polished metal of their masks.
But suddenly, the easy rhythm of their walk shattered.
SPLAT!
The massive half-eaten heart-shaped ice cream slipped completely from Evelyn’s grasp.
It fell heavily onto the wet cobblestone pavement, splattering in a messy puddle of red and white directly across Silas’s dark combat boots.
Silas stopped, looking down at his ruined sticky boots in annoyance.
"What the fuck, Evelyn?" Silas complained, reaching down to wipe a streak of melting vanilla off the hem of his leather trench coat. "You were the one holding it."
Evelyn didn’t reply and she didn’t even blink either.
She was standing completely frozen in the middle of the crowded sidewalk, her entire body rigid as a petrified board.
Her dark eyes, visible through the narrow slits of her Kitsune mask, were wide with a terrifying shattered emotion that Silas had never seen before.
Silas instantly noticed her unnatural paralysis as his instincts flared violently, assuming an ambush, a hidden sniper targeting them from the rooftops, or a strike team closing in.
’For what reason though...?’
He quickly followed her direct line of sight, his golden-ringed eyes scanning across the bustling street.
Standing near a brightly lit skewer stall, completely oblivious to the two masked Lords watching them from the shadows, was a young man.
He was tall, with messy black hair and wire-rimmed glasses.
He was wearing the crisp and incredibly expensive uniform of Valoria College, indicating he was a wealthy scholar, not a combatant.
He was currently smiling warmly, buying a massive plate of grilled kraken skewers and handing them affectionately to a beautiful petite girl with bright pink hair standing next to him.
They looked incredibly happy.
’Huh? Is there anything weird about them?’
They looked untouched by the blood, the crushing trauma, and the brutal reality of the Sovereign Realm.
Silas looked back at Evelyn.
Even with the metal mask covering her face, he could see the undeniable genetic similarities in their sharp jawlines and the exact shade of their dark hair.
Evelyn’s hands trembled violently at her sides with her knuckles turning white.
Her voice cracked, barely a whisper over the deafening noise of the Shogitown crowds.
"Matt..." Evelyn muttered, her heart visibly shattering into a thousand pieces as she watched the scene.
Silas let out a slow empathetic sigh with the tension leaving his shoulders.
He understood it all now.
It seemed that this college scholar, this boy happily buying street food for his girlfriend while his sister bled in the mud, was Evelyn’s younger brother.
’Or a relative or something...?’
Evelyn watched them hold hands through the narrow angled eye slits of her painted Kitsune mask.
She stood completely frozen on the damp cobblestone with the ruined melted ice cream on Silas’s boots completely forgotten.
The bustling crowds of festival-goers flowed around her in a chaotic, neon-lit river, but Evelyn didn’t see any of them.
Her dark eyes were locked onto the tall black-haired boy in the pristine Valoria College uniform and the petite pink-haired girl standing cheerfully at his side.
They were sharing a massive plate of grilled kraken skewers, laughing under the warm, flickering glow of the red paper lanterns strung between the wooden eaves.
Their lips were moving.
Evelyn leaned forward slightly with her chest tightening as she desperately tried to read their expressions.
She could see the casual easy smile on her brother’s face... a genuine, carefree smile that she hadn’t seen directed at her in so many years.
But she couldn’t hear them.
The deafening noise of the Shogitown street vendors, the sizzling grills, and the distant thumping of traditional festival drums made it impossible to pick up a single syllable of their conversation.
Matt threw his head back, laughing at something the pink-haired girl said.
He tossed his empty wooden skewer into a nearby disposal bin, gently taking the girl’s hand in his own.
They turned away from the food stall, starting to weave their way deeper into the vibrant heart of the festival plaza.
Evelyn didn’t even hesitate.

She reached out with trembling frantic fingers, grabbing the thick fabric of Silas’s dark runic trench coat as she aggressively dragged him forward into the dense crowd with her boots stomping against the wet pavement.
"Woah, woah, woah," Silas protested, stumbling slightly as the petite Lord practically hauled his muscled frame down the sidewalk.
He planted his boots, forcing her to a halt near a brightly lit lantern post.
"Aren’t we supposed to be heading to his place? According to you, we need to get that done."
Evelyn whipped her head around to face him.
The neon streetlights reflected sharply off the glossy white and crimson paint of her Kitsune mask.
Her eyes, shining with a desperate intensity through the narrow slits, burned into him.
"It will be an hour," Evelyn promised. "One hour, Silas. Nothing more. We are following them..."
’Isn’t that what I said earlier?’

chapters.title: Chapter 349: Evelyn The Stalker [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: Silas stared down at her.
He could feel the genuine vibrating tension radiating from her grip on his sleeve.
’What am I getting myself into?’
His instincts told him that wasting time on a personal detour while carrying seventy-five million credits in digital assets was a terrible decision.
He wanted Vespera’s identity solidified in the World Council databases before any auditors started sniffing around the Umbral Basin.
But he also remembered the crushing heartbreak in her voice when she had whispered that boy’s name.
Silas let out a long, deeply exhausted sigh, running his free hand through his messy dark hair.
"Fine," Silas agreed, his broad shoulders dropping in quiet surrender. "But before we do this, I need verbal confirmation. Is that guy actually your younger brother?"
"Yes," Evelyn confirmed quietly, her gaze darting frantically through the crowd to keep the young couple in sight. "That is Matt."
Silas nodded, slipping his hands into his deep coat pockets as he went along with it.
Honestly, beneath his stoic exterior, he was quite interested in the entire situation.
He wanted to see exactly how the dynamic between Matt and Evelyn functioned.
How did a multi-millionaire Lord who commanded a literal mechanical fortress interact with her completely normal civilian sibling?

"If we are going to tail them," Silas instructed smoothly, stepping closer to her, "we have to blend in... We can’t just lurk in the shadows wearing combat gear and metal masks. We need to act like the couple you told that mask vendor we were."
Evelyn gritted her teeth, but she knew he was right.
If they acted like creepy stalkers, the undercity enforcers or Matt himself would spot them immediately.
"Just don’t make it weird," Evelyn muttered, wrapping her arm stiffly around his waist and leaning against his side.
They tailed the couple through the dense vibrant heart of the Moon Festival.
The first stop was a brightly lit magical-rifle shooting gallery. Matt and his pink-haired girlfriend stepped up to the wooden counter.
"Step right up, folks!" the burly vendor shouted, waving a crude rifle in the air. "Three credits for five shots! Knock down the mechanized targets, win a prize for your lovely lady!"
Matt paid the vendor, picking up the long wooden rifle.
He aimed carefully at a moving row of mechanical steel ducks, laughing as his girlfriend cheered him on from the sidelines.
Just ten feet away, at the adjacent shooting stall, Evelyn aggressively shoved a handful of physical credits at a terrified sweating vendor and snatched a rifle off the rack.
"Oh, look, honey, a shooting game," Silas deadpanned, playing his role as the supportive boyfriend.
He leaned casually against the wooden counter, throwing an arm around Evelyn’s narrow shoulders.
Evelyn didn’t even look at her own targets.
She leaned sideways, pressing the cheek of her Kitsune mask against the thin wooden divider separating the two stalls.
She squinted her dark eyes, desperately straining to eavesdrop on Matt’s conversation.
She completely ignored the rifle in her hands, holding it limp and pointing it dangerously toward the ground.
"You’re holding it wrong, babe," Silas whispered, trying to suppress a smirk.
’WHY AM I EVEN DOING THIS?’
He reached around her with his hands guiding her arms to lift the heavy rifle.
"You have to actually shoot if we want to look natural."
"Shut up," Evelyn hissed under her breath, pressing her ear harder against the wood. "I think he’s talking about his mid-term finals."
Silas sighed. To maintain their cover, he gently squeezed her finger on the trigger.
CRACK!
The bolt flew wild, obliterating a cheap plastic prize hanging from the ceiling instead of hitting the targets.
The vendor shrieked, ducking behind the counter.
"Oops," Silas said loudly, patting Evelyn’s shoulder. "Better luck next time, sweetheart."
Matt’s girlfriend cheered as he managed to hit two targets, winning a small plush keychain.
The couple moved on, laughing brightly. Evelyn instantly dropped the smoking rifle onto the counter and dragged Silas after them, leaving the vendor trembling in the cordite-scented smoke.
Their second stop was a towering heavy-duty hammer strike machine designed to test raw physical strength.
"Show me those muscles, Matt!" the pink-haired girl giggled, giving him an encouraging shove toward the massive leather strike pad.
Matt rolled up the sleeves of his crisp Valoria College uniform.
He grabbed the oversized wooden mallet, hefting it over his shoulder. He swung it down onto the strike pad with a loud grunt of exertion.
THUD!
The glowing magical indicator shot up the vertical glass pillar, stopping just past the middle mark.
It was a perfectly respectable and average civilian score. A small bell chimed pleasantly.
His girlfriend clapped happily, wrapping her arms tightly around his waist and resting her chin on his chest.
Evelyn scoffed quietly from behind the safety of a nearby roasted chestnut cart, crossing her arms in deep judgment.
"His stance was terrible," Evelyn criticized in a harsh whisper. "He completely failed to do a proper one... I tried to teach him basic martial forms so long ago, and he never practiced."
To avoid looking suspicious while lingering near the machine, Silas stepped up to the adjacent striker pad.
He paid the fee and picked up the heavy wooden mallet. It felt like a cheap toy in his hands.
"Don’t draw attention to us," Evelyn hissed at him, grabbing a paper bag of chestnuts to blend in. "Just act normal."
Silas nodded.
He deliberately suppressed his Gold Core, locking his surging mana deep inside his chest.
He loosened his grip on the handle, fully intending to give the machine a weak pathetic tap just to keep their cover intact.
He swung the mallet down with a fraction of a fraction of his true strength.
THOOOM!
The power of his physical stats transferred violently through the wood.
The heavy leather strike pad cratered deeply inward, the internal springs screaming in protest.

The glowing magical indicator didn’t just shoot up the glass pillar; it launched upward like an artillery shell, smashing directly into the metal bell at the top with enough kinetic force to physically shatter the iron casing.
Sparks rained down over the damp cobblestone.
The machine let out a dying mechanical wheeze and powered down into total darkness.
The surrounding crowd went silent.
Matt and his girlfriend paused their romantic embracing, staring at the masked teenager in the trench coat with wide and thoroughly terrified eyes.
"Wow, you are so strong, honey," Evelyn deadpanned sarcastically, her voice dripping with venomous irritation through her Kitsune mask.
Silas carefully set the cracked wooden mallet back down on the ground, shoved his hands deep into his pockets, and casually walked away as if nothing had happened.
Evelyn quickly scrambled after him, punching him hard in the bicep for completely destroying their stealth.
"You idiot!"
’It’s not my fault... it was just... weaker than I expected.’
The third game was a traditional undercity goldfish scooping stall.
Matt and the pink-haired girl knelt near a shallow glowing pool of blue water.
Matt was gently guiding her hand, showing her how to use the delicate paper net to scoop up the darting mana-infused koi fish without tearing the fragile material.
They were laughing softly, their shoulders pressed closely together in the intimate, romantic atmosphere.
"You’re doing great, babe," Matt encouraged her warmly. "Just wait for them to slow down."
Evelyn knelt at the pool directly across from them, paying the grumpy stall owner for a paper net.

But she wasn’t looking at the swimming fish. Her dark eyes were burning with a potent mixture of intense jealousy, betrayal, and quiet sorrow as she watched her brother shower a complete stranger with the gentle affection he always denied her.
Her grip on her paper scooper tightened as her physical strength leaked subconsciously into her trembling fingers.
SNAP!
Evelyn unknowingly crushed the wooden handle of the scooper into jagged, ruined splinters, obliterating the delicate net before it even touched the water.
Silas sat casually on a wooden crate next to her, resting his chin on his hand.
"You are crushing the equipment, Evelyn," Silas whispered, trying to make it look like they were having a playful couple’s argument.
He picked up a spare paper net from the counter. "You have to relax."
"I am relaxed," Evelyn hissed back with her eyes refusing to leave Matt. "I am just observing. Why is he being so nice to her? He yelled at me the last time I tried to buy him dinner."
Silas sighed.

Using the terrifying flawless hand-eye coordination of a trained Lord, his hand blurred into motion. Within three seconds, he had cleanly scooped five rare glowing mana-koi into a small plastic bag without so much as dampening the paper net.𝗳𝚛𝗲𝕖𝚠𝚎𝚋𝗻𝗼𝕧𝗲𝐥.𝚌𝚘𝐦
He handed the bag of swimming fish to a nearby, completely bewildered civilian child who had been struggling to catch one all night.
"Let’s keep moving," Silas muttered, placing a gentle hand on her shoulder and lifting her up from the pool.
The fourth game was a balloon-popping stall using weighted iron darts.
"Step right up! Three darts for five credits!" the vendor yelled over the music. "Pop the gold balloons for the grand prize!"
Matt stepped up to the line, throwing the heavy darts with concentrated effort.
He managed to pop enough balloons to win his girlfriend a medium-sized, incredibly fluffy stuffed bear.
The pink-haired girl hugged the bear tightly against her chest, giving Matt a quick affectionate kiss on the cheek.
"Thank you, Matty," she giggled, burying her face in the plush fur.
Evelyn watched the kiss from the shadows of the adjacent stall, her shoulders slumping heavily.
She looked miserable, her fierce untouchable Lord persona completely broken down by the mundane happy reality of her brother’s civilian life.
Silas stepped up to the counter of their stall. He paid the fee and picked up a cheap weighted iron dart.
"They look so happy," Silas said quietly, trying to gently gauge her emotional state.
Evelyn snatched a dart from his hand. "They look ridiculous."
She didn’t even aim.
She threw the dart with the explosive velocity of a military-grade railgun slug, fueled by her simmering sibling jealousy.
THWACK!
The dart didn’t just pop the balloon... it completely bypassed the target board, burying itself three inches deep into the solid concrete wall behind the vendor with a shower of dust.
The terrified stall owner shrieked, hurriedly shoving his grand prize directly into Silas’s chest just to get the masked monsters to leave his stall peacefully.
It was a massive life-sized fluffy stuffed kraken. The thick purple tentacles dragged on the floor, and the head was larger than a boulder.
Evelyn immediately snatched the giant kraken out of Silas’s hands.

She hoisted the massive plushie onto her shoulders and actively used it as a stealth barrier, hiding her entire upper body behind the fluffy purple tentacles as she continued to stalk her brother down the street.
Silas walked beside her, his hands buried in his pockets, feeling a wave of secondhand embarrassment.
An hour passed exactly like that.
It was a bizarre chaotic montage of Warlord destruction and pathetic sibling espionage.

They finally reached the tenth or eleventh game, a brightly lit stall situated near the edge of the central plaza where participants had to throw small wooden rings over the necks of glass bottles to win top-tier electronics.
Matt and his girlfriend were standing at the counter, completely focused on the game.
"I really want that new datapad model," the pink-haired girl said, pointing to the grand prize.
"I’ll get it for you," Matt promised, gripping the wooden rings.
Evelyn, blinded by her massive plushie stealth barrier and her hyper-fixation on her brother, completely misjudged the distance.
She shuffled forward in her heavy boots, bumping directly up to the wooden counter right alongside them.
They were standing side-by-side and mere inches apart.
Silas stopped a few feet back, leaning against a thick wooden pillar covered in neon lights.
He crossed his arms over his chest, letting out a long sigh.
He wasn’t going to step in and save her from this one.
With the way she had been constantly closing the distance on the duo for the past hour, a confrontation was entirely inevitable.
Evelyn stood frozen behind the stuffed kraken, gripping the counter, desperately thinking she was a literal ghost.
’He can’t possibly tell that it’s me,’ Evelyn reasoned in her head, holding her breath. ’I have the Kitsune mask on. I am wearing civilian clothes. I am perfectly blended in.’
Matt slowly lowered his wooden rings.
The clinking of the wood against the counter was the only sound he made.
He didn’t look at his girlfriend. He turned his head slowly with his dark eyes locking directly onto the giant purple plushie standing right next to him.
"How did it feel to stalk us for the past hour, Sis?" Matt asked.

chapters.title: Chapter 350: Jax Has Been Compromised [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: His voice wasn’t surprised.
It was dripping with exhausted irritation.
Evelyn stiffened violently.
The giant stuffed kraken slipped from her numb grasp, falling to the wet cobblestone with a soft pathetic thud.
She stood there, fully exposed in her oversized gray hoodie and her painted metal mask.
Panic flooded her veins as her mind short-circuited under the weight of his direct gaze.
"I—I don’t know what you are talking about," Evelyn stuttered, desperately trying to deepen her voice through the mask to sound like a random, aggressive street thug. "I am just playing a game."
Matt let out a heavy bitter sigh. He pushed his wire-rimmed glasses up the bridge of his nose, shaking his head.

"Drop the act, Evelyn," Matt said bluntly, easily piercing through her pathetic disguise. "You walk exactly the same way you always do. Your posture is rigid and nobody else in this entire city wears heavy boots with an oversized gray hoodie to a festive street fair."
Evelyn slowly reached up, unclasping the leather straps and pulling the Kitsune mask off her face.
Her pale cheeks were flushed a deep, embarrassed crimson, and her dark eyes darted nervously between her unimpressed brother and the wide-eyed pink-haired girl.

"You were actively stalking me," Matt continued, his voice rising in volume, drawing the awkward unwanted attention of the stall vendor. "Why? Is it really that surprising that I am out with a girl? Did you seriously have to follow me through five different sectors just to spy on my personal life?"
The pink-haired girl placed a gentle calming hand on Matt’s arm, looking at Evelyn with nervous empathy.
"Matt, calm down," his girlfriend whispered softly, pulling at his sleeve. "People are staring at us. Let’s just talk to her normally."
"No!" Matt interrupted her harshly, pulling his arm away from her grasp.

He glared at Evelyn with burning resentment. "That is just how she is, Sarah. She is always like this... She disappears into the Sovereign Realm for weeks at a time, completely ghosts all of my messages, and then suddenly shows up out of nowhere just to hover over my shoulder like a vulture... She can’t just give me any privacy!"
Evelyn’s chest tightened painfully. The words felt like physical blows against her ribs.

"Is it considered invading your privacy if I am just making sure you are safe?" Evelyn asked defensively, her voice cracking slightly as she tried to justify her actions. "You know how dangerous Valoria City can be, Matt. The syndicates are everywhere... I just wanted to make sure you were protected while you were out."
"Stop."
Matt interrupted her, his dark eyes devoid of any warmth.
He looked at his older sister with a cold piercing gaze that lacked any affection or gratitude for the sacrifices she had made to keep him in that prestigious college.
"Stalking me through a festival isn’t making sure I am safe, Evelyn," Matt delivered the brutal, unyielding truth. "It’s just suffocating. I don’t need a bodyguard. I just want a normal life..."

A crushing silence fell over the brightly lit stall. Even the cheerful vendor stopped moving, awkwardly pretending to organize his glass bottles to avoid the uncomfortable family drama unfolding in front of him.
Silas stood a few feet away, his golden-ringed eyes watching the scene intently from behind his Oni mask.
He felt a sharp pang of sympathy for Evelyn, knowing how fiercely she fought to provide for her family.
But he refused to step in.
He was not going to get involved in their deep-seated family trauma. It wasn’t his place, and defending her as a Warlord would only make Matt more resentful of her dangerous lifestyle.
Evelyn stood frozen for a long moment, fully absorbing the cold stinging rejection.
Her brother didn’t want her protection... He didn’t want her hovering... He didn’t care about the millions of credits she bled for...
He just wanted her gone.
Evelyn quickly pulled the Kitsune mask back down over her face, hiding her tears.
She spun around on her combat boots and immediately ran off, sprinting desperately back into the dense flowing crowds of the Shogitown plaza.
Silas took a half-step forward.
He opened his mouth, almost calling out her name to stop her from running blindly into the dangerous undercity sectors alone.
But he bit his tongue, stopping himself just in time to protect herself from the surrounding crowd.
Matt watched her disappear into the neon-lit sea of people.
He let out another heavy sigh, aggressively rubbing his temples as his girlfriend patted his back.
He finally turned his attention to the towering, imposing young man standing quietly near the pillar.
"Who are you supposed to be?" Matt asked tiredly, gesturing to Silas’s dark trench coat and terrifying demonic mask. "Are you her new boyfriend or something? Or just another one of her guards?"
Silas didn’t reply. He didn’t offer a nod, a threat, or a single word of confirmation.
He simply turned his back on the college student and broke into a steady jog, weaving effortlessly through the dense crowd to chase after Evelyn.
They needed to get to the underground contact, and he couldn’t let her wander the streets without backup.
’Well I can only be thankful that Lia knew she was wrong...’ Silas thought, he couldn’t help but think of this Matt person was an ungrateful person.
Evelyn pressed her back against the damp rusted brick wall of a narrow isolated alleyway.
She had successfully lost them.
She had ducked down three different side streets, taking erratic winding turns until the blaring noise of the central festival faded into a distant muffled hum.
It was too much. All of this was too much to process.
Evelyn slid slowly down the rough brick wall, pulling her knees tightly against her chest and wrapping her arms protectively around her legs.
Her chest heaved with shallow frantic breaths. Hot, stinging tears pooled in her eyes, burning uncomfortably against the cold metal of her Kitsune mask.
She was trying her best to be a good big sister.
That was all she ever wanted to be.
She had wanted to come to Shogitown with him for several years now.
She had asked him every single autumn to attend the Moon Festival with her.
She wanted to buy him the kraken skewers and the massive ice cream cones.
She wanted to share the spoils of her Sovereign Realm conquests with the only family she had left in the world.
And he had just decided to come here with a random civilian girl from his college?
Were they dating? How long had they been together? Why wasn’t she made aware of this whole thing? Did he hide it from her on purpose?
The dark invasive thoughts spiraled violently in her mind, turning her skills against her own deep insecurities.

Was she truly a bad sister? Was her constant absence, necessitated by the grueling demands of running The Unmovable Wall, ruining his life? Was she just a creepy overbearing stalker interfering with his normal, happy existence?
There were so many conflicting, painful thoughts tearing through her head that she had to sit back, close her eyes, and forcefully command her racing heart to calm down.
She focused on the steady dripping of a broken drainage pipe nearby to ground herself in reality.
After a few minutes, Evelyn slowly opened her eyes and stood up on shaky legs.
She looked around the dimly lit trash-strewn alleyway. She had run so fast and taken so many erratic turns that she had apparently lost Silas too.
The rugged dark-haired Lord was nowhere to be seen.

’Let me just go meet Jax first,’ Evelyn reasoned internally with her training finally overriding her emotional breakdown as she popped another Cigarette. ’I know the exact coordinates of the cyber-rig... I will secure the location, make sure the coast is clear, and then I’ll call Silas on the secure network to guide him in.’
She compartmentalized the trauma, forcefully locking the image of Matt’s cold rejection into a dark mental box.
She had a mission to complete.
Evelyn reached back and pulled the heavy hood of her oversized gray sweater firmly up over her head, shadowing the Kitsune mask.
She shoved her hands deep into her pockets, adjusting the hidden daggers strapped to her thighs, and stepped out of the alley.
She took an unorthodox winding direction to reach Jax’s place.

Shogitown was cool, vibrant, and full of life on the outside main streets. But the deeper you walked into the district, past the festival boundaries and into the neglected industrial sectors, the deeper one realized that this place was just rotten to the core.
The real cherry blossom trees vanished, replaced by rusted metal scaffolding and sparking exposed utility cables.
The bright neon signs flickered violently, casting long erratic shadows over the grimy, cracked pavement.
The smell of roasted food was replaced by the overwhelming stench of stagnant water, cheap mechanical oil, and unwashed bodies.
This was syndicate territory.
As Evelyn walked briskly down the narrow, dimly lit streets, several rough-looking men leaning against the walls tried to catcall her.
They eyed her petite frame and her combat boots, completely unaware of the terrifying power housed in her core.
Evelyn didn’t reply to a single word. She kept her head down, subtly projecting a microscopic fraction of her chilling blood-soaked Lord aura.
The men instantly went pale with their survival instincts screaming at them to back away from the hooded girl.
The people in power... the World Council, the Valoria City Mayor, the elite guilds were well aware of these dark dangerous changes in the district.
They knew the syndicates ran illegal chop shops, trafficking rings, and black-market data rigs down here.𝑓𝘳𝑒𝑒𝓌𝘦𝘣𝘯ℴ𝑣𝘦𝑙.𝘤𝑜𝑚
However, they deliberately left it alone, preferring to contain the rot in Shogitown rather than spend resources cleansing the streets.
’It is not my business though,’ Evelyn thought coldly with her dark eyes scanning the rooftops for snipers. ’I just don’t want to get tangled with the local syndicates tonight.’
She finally reached the specific dead-end alleyway where Jax’s place was located.
It was a dilapidated, four-story concrete building that looked like it had survived a minor bombing.
The fire escapes were rusted through, and the windows were boarded up with thick steel plating.
Evelyn walked up to the heavy, reinforced iron door of his ground-floor apartment.
She raised her fist to knock out their pre-arranged security rhythm.
But as her knuckles brushed the metal, the door creaked loudly.
It was already open, sitting an inch ajar.
Evelyn paused with her hand hovering in the damp air.
Her combat instincts flared. For some strange reason, the heavy deadbolts were disengaged.
But she quickly relaxed her shoulders.
That wasn’t necessarily a massive issue, since Jax was exactly like that.
He was a brilliant, capable underground information broker, but he was incredibly sloppy with his own physical security.
He lived in a perpetual state of scattered hardware and empty noodle boxes.
He was very rough around the edges, but he was undeniably helpful.
That was the one thing Evelyn truly liked about him. He always delivered the intel she paid for without asking moral questions...
He was not very dateable, though.
’I would much rather date Silas than him,’ Evelyn thought casually, her mind briefly flashing to the tall Lord she had left behind at the festival.
Evelyn aggressively shook her head, banishing the stray romantic thought.
’Focus on the mission,’ Evelyn scolded herself internally.
She pushed the heavy iron door open with the rusted hinges groaning loudly in the quiet alley, and stepped inside while adjusting her mask.
It was a simple sprawling one-room apartment.

The walls were lined with humming server racks and tangled webs of fiber-optic cables. Multiple glowing monitors illuminated the center of the room, casting a stark blue light over the disorganized mess of mechanical parts and discarded energy drink cans.
Things didn’t look too out of place at first glance as there were no obvious signs of a struggle.
But Evelyn was a veteran Lord of the Sovereign Realm.
She had survived countless dungeon ambushes and assassination attempts so her perception was honed to a razor’s edge.
She could tell something was wrong. Something was seriously wrong with the atmosphere of the room.
Jax wasn’t here. The leather chair in front of the monitors was empty.
But if he wasn’t here, why was the heavy iron security door left open? Jax was sloppy, but he was insanely paranoid about his hardware.
He would never leave his primary rig exposed to the street.
Evelyn slowly, silently reached up and adjusted the straps of her Kitsune mask.
She closed her eyes for a split second, actively expanding her internal mana senses outward, letting the invisible ripples of her perception map the entire apartment.
It was not a very big room, but her senses immediately snagged on a terrifying anomaly.
The mana density near the ceiling was disrupted. Someone was actively suppressing their signature, hiding in the shadows above her.
Evelyn opened her eyes.
She didn’t look up.
She kept her posture relaxed, pretending to be oblivious as she walked slowly toward the center of the room where Jax usually kept his primary computers.
Directly above Evelyn, clinging silently to the rusted steel support beams of the ceiling, was a man wearing an all-black stealth suit.
A stark white mask covering his face bore a single jagged black kanji character painted across the forehead.
The exact second Evelyn stepped into the center of the room, the assassin dropped.

sentences.text: His voice wasn’t surprised.
It was dripping with exhausted irritation.
Evelyn stiffened violently.
The giant stuffed kraken slipped from her numb grasp, falling to the wet cobblestone with a soft pathetic thud.
She stood there, fully exposed in her oversized gray hoodie and her painted metal mask.
Panic flooded her veins as her mind short-circuited under the weight of his direct gaze.
"I—I don’t know what you are talking about," Evelyn stuttered, desperately trying to deepen her voice through the mask to sound like a random, aggressive street thug.
"I am just playing a game."
Matt let out a heavy bitter sigh.
He pushed his wire-rimmed glasses up the bridge of his nose, shaking his head.
"Drop the act, Evelyn," Matt said bluntly, easily piercing through her pathetic disguise.
"You walk exactly the same way you always do.
Your posture is rigid and nobody else in this entire city wears heavy boots with an oversized gray hoodie to a festive street fair."
Evelyn slowly reached up, unclasping the leather straps and pulling the Kitsune mask off her face.
Her pale cheeks were flushed a deep, embarrassed crimson, and her dark eyes darted nervously between her unimpressed brother and the wide-eyed pink-haired girl.
"You were actively stalking me," Matt continued, his voice rising in volume, drawing the awkward unwanted attention of the stall vendor.
"Why?
Is it really that surprising that I am out with a girl?
Did you seriously have to follow me through five different sectors just to spy on my personal life?"
The pink-haired girl placed a gentle calming hand on Matt’s arm, looking at Evelyn with nervous empathy.
"Matt, calm down," his girlfriend whispered softly, pulling at his sleeve.
"People are staring at us.
Let’s just talk to her normally."
"No!" Matt interrupted her harshly, pulling his arm away from her grasp.
He glared at Evelyn with burning resentment.
"That is just how she is, Sarah.
She is always like this...
She disappears into the Sovereign Realm for weeks at a time, completely ghosts all of my messages, and then suddenly shows up out of nowhere just to hover over my shoulder like a vulture...
She can’t just give me any privacy!"
Evelyn’s chest tightened painfully.
The words felt like physical blows against her ribs.
"Is it considered invading your privacy if I am just making sure you are safe?" Evelyn asked defensively, her voice cracking slightly as she tried to justify her actions.
"You know how dangerous Valoria City can be, Matt.
The syndicates are everywhere...
I just wanted to make sure you were protected while you were out."
"Stop."
Matt interrupted her, his dark eyes devoid of any warmth.
He looked at his older sister with a cold piercing gaze that lacked any affection or gratitude for the sacrifices she had made to keep him in that prestigious college.
"Stalking me through a festival isn’t making sure I am safe, Evelyn," Matt delivered the brutal, unyielding truth.
"It’s just suffocating.
I don’t need a bodyguard.
I just want a normal life..."
A crushing silence fell over the brightly lit stall.
Even the cheerful vendor stopped moving, awkwardly pretending to organize his glass bottles to avoid the uncomfortable family drama unfolding in front of him.
Silas stood a few feet away, his golden-ringed eyes watching the scene intently from behind his Oni mask.
He felt a sharp pang of sympathy for Evelyn, knowing how fiercely she fought to provide for her family.
But he refused to step in.
He was not going to get involved in their deep-seated family trauma.
It wasn’t his place, and defending her as a Warlord would only make Matt more resentful of her dangerous lifestyle.
Evelyn stood frozen for a long moment, fully absorbing the cold stinging rejection.
Her brother didn’t want her protection...
He didn’t want her hovering...
He didn’t care about the millions of credits she bled for...
He just wanted her gone.
Evelyn quickly pulled the Kitsune mask back down over her face, hiding her tears.
She spun around on her combat boots and immediately ran off, sprinting desperately back into the dense flowing crowds of the Shogitown plaza.
Silas took a half-step forward.
He opened his mouth, almost calling out her name to stop her from running blindly into the dangerous undercity sectors alone.
But he bit his tongue, stopping himself just in time to protect herself from the surrounding crowd.
Matt watched her disappear into the neon-lit sea of people.
He let out another heavy sigh, aggressively rubbing his temples as his girlfriend patted his back.
He finally turned his attention to the towering, imposing young man standing quietly near the pillar.
"Who are you supposed to be?" Matt asked tiredly, gesturing to Silas’s dark trench coat and terrifying demonic mask.
"Are you her new boyfriend or something?
Or just another one of her guards?"
Silas didn’t reply.
He didn’t offer a nod, a threat, or a single word of confirmation.
He simply turned his back on the college student and broke into a steady jog, weaving effortlessly through the dense crowd to chase after Evelyn.
They needed to get to the underground contact, and he couldn’t let her wander the streets without backup.
’Well I can only be thankful that Lia knew she was wrong...’ Silas thought, he couldn’t help but think of this Matt person was an ungrateful person.
Evelyn pressed her back against the damp rusted brick wall of a narrow isolated alleyway.
She had successfully lost them.
She had ducked down three different side streets, taking erratic winding turns until the blaring noise of the central festival faded into a distant muffled hum.
It was too much.
All of this was too much to process.
Evelyn slid slowly down the rough brick wall, pulling her knees tightly against her chest and wrapping her arms protectively around her legs.
Her chest heaved with shallow frantic breaths.
Hot, stinging tears pooled in her eyes, burning uncomfortably against the cold metal of her Kitsune mask.
She was trying her best to be a good big sister.
That was all she ever wanted to be.
She had wanted to come to Shogitown with him for several years now.
She had asked him every single autumn to attend the Moon Festival with her.
She wanted to buy him the kraken skewers and the massive ice cream cones.
She wanted to share the spoils of her Sovereign Realm conquests with the only family she had left in the world.
And he had just decided to come here with a random civilian girl from his college?
Were they dating?
How long had they been together?
Why wasn’t she made aware of this whole thing?
Did he hide it from her on purpose?
The dark invasive thoughts spiraled violently in her mind, turning her skills against her own deep insecurities.
Was she truly a bad sister?
Was her constant absence, necessitated by the grueling demands of running The Unmovable Wall, ruining his life?
Was she just a creepy overbearing stalker interfering with his normal, happy existence?
There were so many conflicting, painful thoughts tearing through her head that she had to sit back, close her eyes, and forcefully command her racing heart to calm down.
She focused on the steady dripping of a broken drainage pipe nearby to ground herself in reality.
